metadata.source: Ganganatha Jha: Kāvyaprakāśa of Mammaṭa, with English translation, rev. ed., Varanasi : Bharatiya Vidya Prakaśan, 1967 (2 parts). With occasional corrections according to the ed. by N.S. Venkatanathacharya: The Kavyaprakasha of Mammata, with Sanketa of Acharya Manikyachandra, Madhumati of Ravi Bhattacharya and Bhavukapriya tippani, Mysore : Oriental Research Institute, 1974 (2 vols).

children.translated_text: Oṃ. Salutation to <s>Śiva</s>.
The series of verses (<s>kārikāvalī</s>) of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> (Illumination of Poetry):
Free from the constraint imposed by destiny, consisting solely of delight, dependent on nothing else,
relished through the nine <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments), fashioning a creation — the <s>Bhāratī</s> (speech/goddess of learning) of the poet triumphs! // MKpr-K_1 //
Poetry [serves] for fame, for the attainment of wealth, for the knowledge of practical conduct, for the removal of what is inauspicious,
and for immediate supreme delight, through instruction that is like [the words of] a beloved. // MKpr-K_2 //
Innate talent (<s>śakti</s>), proficiency from the observation of the world, <s>śāstras</s> (treatises), poetry, and the like,
and practice through instruction by those learned in poetry — these are the causes for its production. // MKpr-K_3 //
That [poetry consists of] word and meaning, free from faults, possessing qualities, and sometimes even without figures of speech;
this is the best [kind]: when the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) surpasses the expressed (<s>vācya</s>), it is called <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) by the wise. // MKpr-K_4 //
When it is not of that kind, [the poetry] with subordinated suggestion (<s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>) is middling;
verbal figuration (<s>śabdacitra</s>) and figuration of sense (<s>vācyacitra</s>), without suggestion, is considered the lowest. // MKpr-K_5 //
The word here may be denotative (<s>vācaka</s>), indicative (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>), or suggestive (<s>vyañjaka</s>) — threefold;
the denoted and the rest are their [respective] meanings; in some cases there is also an implied meaning (<s>tātparyārtha</s>). // MKpr-K_6 //
The suggestive capacity is accepted for nearly all meanings;
that [word] which conveys the meaning directly agreed upon by convention is the denotative (<s>vācaka</s>). // MKpr-K_7 //
The conventionally established [meaning] is fourfold: universal (<s>jāti</s>) and the rest, or universal alone;
that is the primary meaning, and the primary function pertaining to it is called <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation). // MKpr-K_8 //
When the primary meaning is obstructed, through connection with it, either from established usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) or from purpose (<s>prayojana</s>),

children.text: anyo 'rtho lakṣyate yatsā lakṣaṇāropitā kriyā // MKpr-K_9 //
children.translated_text: another meaning is indicated — that which is [so] indicated is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication); it is an attributed function. // MKpr-K_9 //
The appropriation of another for one's own establishment, the yielding of oneself for the purpose of another,

children.text: upādānaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cetyuktā śuddhaiva sā dvidhā // MKpr-K_10 //
children.translated_text: and the adoption — these are [types of] indication; and that pure [indication] has been stated to be twofold. // MKpr-K_10 //
The other, with superimposition (<s>sāropa</s>): where the subject and the object [of comparison] are stated,
and the subject is subsumed within the other — that is called <s>sādhyavasānikā</s> (deliberative indication). // MKpr-K_11 //
And these two varieties [of indication], from similarity or from another relation,

children.text: gauṇau śuddhau ca vijñeyau lakṣaṇā tena ṣaḍvidhā // MKpr-K_12 //
children.translated_text: are to be understood as figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>) and pure (<s>śuddha</s>); thus indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) is sixfold. // MKpr-K_12 //

children.text: vyaṅgyena rahitā rūḍhau sahitā tu prayojane /
children.translated_text: Without suggestion, it is in established usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>); combined [with suggestion], it is purposive;

children.text: tacca gūḍhamagūḍhaṃ vā tadeṣā kathitā tridhā // MKpr-K_13 //
children.translated_text: and that [purpose] may be hidden or unhidden — thus it is declared to be threefold. // MKpr-K_13 //
In the case of the indicative [word], the function therein, which is of the nature of suggestion,
for the cognition of which indication is employed [as a stepping stone] — // MKpr-K_14 //
when the result is apprehensible only through the word, there is no other function beyond suggestion;
it is not denotation, because of the absence of convention; nor indication, because of the absence of the [required] cause. // MKpr-K_15 //

children.text: lakṣyaṃ na mukhyaṃ nāpyatra bādho yogaḥ phalena no /
children.translated_text: The indicated meaning is not primary, nor is there obstruction here; connection with the result

children.text: na prayojanametasmin na ca śabdaḥ skhaladgatiḥ // MKpr-K_16 //
children.translated_text: is not a purpose; and the word here does not stumble [in reaching the meaning]. // MKpr-K_16 //
Even so, there would be an infinite regress that would destroy the foundation;

children.text: prayojanena sahitaṃ lakṣaṇīyaṃ na yujyate // MKpr-K_17 //
children.translated_text: the indicative meaning combined with a purpose does not fit [as an explanation]. // MKpr-K_17 //
For the object of cognition is one thing, and the result is stated to be another;

children.text: viśiṣṭe lakṣaṇā naivaṃ viśeṣāḥ syustu lakṣite // MKpr-K_18 //
children.translated_text: indication is not of the qualified [whole]; rather, the qualifications would be [merely] of the indicated [meaning]. // MKpr-K_18 //
When the denotation of a word having multiple meanings is restricted,
the function of producing cognition of the unexpressed meaning, through context and the like, is suggestion (<s>añjana</s>). // MKpr-K_19 //
The word endowed with that [function] is the suggestive word (<s>vyañjaka</s>); when it is connected with another meaning,
the meaning too is a suggester, considered therein as an auxiliary. // MKpr-K_20 //
The meanings have been previously stated; their suggestive capacity through meaning is now explained:
from the speaker, the one to be informed, the context; from the tone; from the sentence, the denoted meaning, and the presence of another [element]; // MKpr-K_21 //
from the speciality of the occasion, place, time, and the like — for those endowed with imaginative insight,
the function of one meaning being the cause of the cognition of another meaning — that is suggestion (<s>vyakti</s>). // MKpr-K_22 //
Since meaning, known through the word as a means of knowledge, suggests another meaning,
in the suggestive capacity of meaning, the word has an auxiliary role. // MKpr-K_23 //
When the denoted meaning is not intended, then in <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion), the denoted meaning becomes
either transferred to another meaning or completely set aside. // MKpr-K_24 //
And when the denoted meaning is intended but subordinate to another [meaning], that [poetry] is the other [type of <s>dhvani</s>];
one has suggestion whose sequence is imperceptible (<s>alakṣyakramavyaṅgya</s>); the other has suggestion with perceptible sequence (<s>lakṣyavyaṅgyakrama</s>). // MKpr-K_25 //
<s>Rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), <s>bhāva</s> (emotional state), the absence of <s>bhāva</s>, the <s>bhāva</s> of quiescence, and the like — [this] is the non-sequential [type];
it is different from <s>rasa</s> and the rest, and from figures of speech, by being established as the object of embellishment. // MKpr-K_26 //
Now, the causes, effects, and concomitants

children.text: ratyādeḥ sthāyino loke tāni cennāṭyakāvyayoḥ // MKpr-K_27 //
children.translated_text: of the permanent emotion (<s>sthāyin</s>) such as love (<s>rati</s>) and the rest, in the world, are in drama and poetry: // MKpr-K_27 //
<s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents); those are called <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions);

children.text: vyaktaḥ sa tairvibhāvādyaiḥ sthāyī bhāvo rasaḥ smṛtaḥ // MKpr-K_28 //
children.translated_text: the permanent emotion, manifested by those <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest, is called <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). // MKpr-K_28 //
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>hāsya</s> (comic), <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic), <s>raudra</s> (furious), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrible),

children.text: bībhatsādbhutasaṃjñau cetyaṣṭau nāṭye rasāḥ smṛtāḥ // MKpr-K_29 //
children.translated_text: <s>bībhatsa</s> (odious), and <s>adbhuta</s> (marvelous) — these eight are the <s>rasas</s> recognized in drama. // MKpr-K_29 //
<s>Rati</s> (love), <s>hāsa</s> (laughter), <s>śoka</s> (sorrow), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm), <s>bhaya</s> (fear),
<s>jugupsā</s> (disgust), and <s>vismaya</s> (wonder) — these are declared the permanent emotions (<s>sthāyibhāvas</s>). // MKpr-K_30 //
<s>Nirveda</s> (despondency), <s>glāni</s> (debility), <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), then <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), <s>śrama</s> (fatigue),

children.text: ālasyaṃ caiva dainyaṃ ca cintā mohaḥ smṛtirdhṛtiḥ // MKpr-K_31 //
children.translated_text: <s>ālasya</s> (indolence) and <s>dainya</s> (dejection), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection), <s>dhṛti</s> (fortitude), // MKpr-K_31 //

children.text: vrīḍā capalatā harṣa āvego jaḍatā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>vrīḍā</s> (shame), <s>capalatā</s> (fickleness), <s>harṣa</s> (joy), <s>āvega</s> (agitation), <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupor),

children.text: garvo viṣāda autsukyaṃ nidrāpasmāra eva ca // MKpr-K_32 //
children.translated_text: <s>garva</s> (arrogance), <s>viṣāda</s> (despair), <s>autsukyā</s> (eagerness), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), and <s>apasmāra</s> (epilepsy); // MKpr-K_32 //
<s>supta</s> (dreaming), <s>prabodha</s> (awakening), <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation), and <s>avahittha</s> (dissimulation), then <s>ugratā</s> (ferocity),
<s>mati</s> (discernment), <s>vyādhi</s> (sickness), then <s>unmāda</s> (insanity), and <s>maraṇa</s> (death) as well; // MKpr-K_33 //
and <s>trāsa</s> (fright) and <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation) — these are to be known as the transitory emotions (<s>vyabhicārins</s>);
these thirty-three <s>bhāvas</s> have been enumerated by name. // MKpr-K_34 //
<s>Nirveda</s> (despondency) is also a permanent emotion; <s>śānta</s> (the tranquil) is a ninth <s>rasa</s>;
<s>rati</s> (love) directed toward deities and the like is a transitory emotion, likewise adorned [by the tranquil rasa]. // MKpr-K_35 //
The <s>bhāva</s> has been described; its semblances (<s>ābhāsa</s>) are those produced by impropriety (<s>anaucitya</s>);

children.text: bhāvasya śāntirudayaḥ sandhiḥ śabalatā tathā // MKpr-K_36 //
children.translated_text: the quiescence, the arising, the juncture, and the variegation of <s>bhāva</s> — // MKpr-K_36 //
even the primary <s>rasa</s> sometimes attains subordination through these.
That which is the abiding of what is suggested through a sequence that is non-sequential, resembling an afterglow — // MKpr-K_37 //
that [<s>dhvani</s>] is said to be threefold, arising from the power of word, meaning, or both;
when a figure of speech (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) or a subject matter (<s>vastu</s>) is manifested from the word — // MKpr-K_38 //
it should be known as predominant; [<s>dhvani</s>] arising from the power of the word is twofold;
that arising from the power of meaning — the meaning is also a suggester, either inherent by itself, // MKpr-K_39 //
or established through bold expression alone, or of the poet endowed [with imagination];

children.text: vastu vālaṅkṛtirvety ṣaḍbhedo 'sau vyanakti yat // MKpr-K_40 //
children.translated_text: whether it suggests a subject matter or a figure of speech — thus that [<s>dhvani</s>] has six varieties. // MKpr-K_40 //
Whether it [suggests] a subject matter or a figure of speech — by this, it becomes twelvefold;
being based on word, meaning, or both — the varieties are eighteen. // MKpr-K_41 //
Since <s>rasas</s> and the rest are infinite, only one variety is counted [as a single class];
in the sentence, [<s>dhvani</s>] arises from both; in the word, from others as well; in the extended composition, from the power of meaning. // MKpr-K_42 //
<s>Rasas</s> and the rest [can be suggested] even in parts of words, constructions, and individual syllables;
the varieties are therefore fifty-one; and in their mutual combination, // MKpr-K_43 //
through mixture (<s>saṃkara</s>) of three forms and through blending (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>) of one form,
[the number reaches] 4, 0, 4, 0, 1 [= 40,401 ... i.e., an astronomically large number]. // MKpr-K_44 //
Unhidden, not a subordinate part of something else, a clear component of the establishment of the expressed meaning,
doubtful, of equal prominence, evoked by tone (<s>kāku</s>), and unattractive — // MKpr-K_45 //
the suggested meaning [in these cases] — thus eight varieties of subordinated suggestion (<s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>) are recognized;

children.text: eṣāṃ bhedā yathāyogaṃ veditavyāśca pūrvavat // MKpr-K_46 //
children.translated_text: their further subdivisions should be understood, as appropriate, as before. // MKpr-K_46 //
The combination of <s>dhvani</s> with those [eight types] endowed with figures, through blending and mixture,
from their mutual combination — thus the count of varieties becomes exceedingly great. // MKpr-K_47 //
The two [kinds of] poetry previously mentioned — verbal figuration (<s>śabdacitra</s>) and figuration of sense (<s>arthacitra</s>) —
their status depends on the predominance of qualities; [the status] of figuration of sense and of word [is relative]. // MKpr-K_48 //
Destruction of the primary meaning is a fault; <s>rasa</s> is primary, and based on it, the expressed [meaning];

children.text: ubhayopayoginaḥ syuḥ śabdādyāstena teṣvapi saḥ // MKpr-K_49 //
children.translated_text: word and the rest serve both [rasa and expressed meaning]; therefore in those too, that [fault applies]. // MKpr-K_49 //
A faulty word is: harsh to the ear (<s>śrutikaṭu</s>), lapsed from grammatical usage (<s>cyutasaṃskṛti</s>), not [properly] employed (<s>aprayukta</s>), impotent (<s>asamartha</s>),

destructive of meaning (<s>nihatārtha</s>), of inappropriate meaning (<s>anucitārtha</s>), meaningless (<s>nirarthaka</s>), non-denotative (<s>avācaka</s>), obscene in three ways (<s>tridhā aślīla</s>), // MKpr-K_50 //
ambiguous (<s>sandigdha</s>), unfamiliar (<s>apratīta</s>), vulgar (<s>grāmya</s>), requiring interpretation (<s>neyārtha</s>), and then forced (<s>kliṣṭa</s>),
having an unexamined predicate (<s>avimṛṣṭavidheyāṃśa</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), with an excessively difficult compound (<s>atikṛtasamāsa</s>). // MKpr-K_51 //
Setting aside lapse from grammatical usage, impotence, and meaninglessness,

children.text: vākye 'pi doṣāḥ santyete padasyāṃśe 'pi kecana // MKpr-K_52 //
children.translated_text: these faults exist in the sentence too; and some also in parts of the word. // MKpr-K_52 //
Having discordant syllables, with damaged or lost <s>visarga</s>, with bad <s>sandhi</s> (euphonic junction), having destroyed meter,
with deficient or superfluous stated words, with falling excellence, and completed [meaning] repeated — // MKpr-K_53 //
having a single expression for two halves, having the connection of a nonexistent thought, having an unexpressed denoted [meaning],
having a compound of words not in construction, mixed up, embedded, and contradicting established usage — // MKpr-K_54 //
with broken sequence, without sequence, and with an unintended other meaning — the sentence too [has these faults];
the meaning [has the faults of being]: unsupported, forced, contradicted, redundant, of bad sequence, and vulgar; // MKpr-K_55 //
doubtful, without reason, and contradicting established knowledge or learning;
unreviewed, with the restriction of what is unrestricted and distinctions that are reversible; // MKpr-K_56 //
syntactically incomplete, having an inappropriate supplement, separated from its companion, having a revealed contradiction,
having an improper injunction and restatement, resuming what was abandoned, and obscene. // MKpr-K_57 //
In words like 'ear-ornament' (<s>karṇāvataṃsa</s>), the [initial syllable] 'karṇa' etc. creates the suggestion;
this is the justification for [such words] standing [in usage], for the purpose of conveying proximity and the like. // MKpr-K_58 //
When the meaning is well-known, [there is] no fault even without a reason; and in imitation, none for all [words];
due to the propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) of the speaker and the rest, even a fault may be a quality somewhere, and somewhere neither. // MKpr-K_59 //
The verbal denotation of the transitory emotions, <s>rasas</s>, and permanent emotions —
manifestation through forced construction — of the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) and <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants); // MKpr-K_60 //
the apprehension of contrary <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest; repeated illumination;
untimely expansion and curtailment; and excessive elaboration of a subordinate element; // MKpr-K_61 //
non-connection with the principal [<s>rasa</s>]; reversal of the [emotional] natures;

children.text: anaṅgasyābhidhānaṃ ca rase doṣāḥ syurīdṛśāḥ // MKpr-K_62 //
children.translated_text: and the expression of what is not a component — such are the faults regarding <s>rasa</s>. // MKpr-K_62 //
There is no fault even when a transitory emotion is expressed by its own name in some [contexts];
the expression of a transitory emotion and the like that contradicts [the dominant rasa], or that is [normally] suppressed, can be conducive to qualities. // MKpr-K_63 //

children.text: āśrayaikye viruddho yaḥ sa kāryo bhinnasaṃśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: That which is contradictory in a single locus should be made to have different loci;
a <s>rasa</s> that is intervened by another <s>rasa</s>, or [that follows] in immediate succession, // MKpr-K_64 //
even if contradictory when remembered, [is acceptable] through equality; and when intended,

children.text: aṅginyaṅgatvamāptau yau tau na duṣṭau parasparam // MKpr-K_65 //
children.translated_text: those that attain the relation of principal and subordinate with each other are not faulty. // MKpr-K_65 //
The properties of the dominant <s>rasa</s>, such as valor and the like — like [properties] of the self,
which are causes of its excellence — those that are stable in position are the qualities (<s>guṇas</s>). // MKpr-K_66 //
Those which sometimes assist that [<s>rasa</s>], when present, through being subordinate elements,
like necklaces and the like — are the figures of speech (<s>alaṅkāras</s>); therefore <s>prāsa</s> (alliteration), <s>upamā</s> (simile), and the rest [are figures]. // MKpr-K_67 //
<s>Mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>ojas</s> (vigor), and <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity) — these three [are the qualities], and not ten;
the quality of producing delight is <s>mādhurya</s>; in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic rasa), it causes a melting [of the heart]; // MKpr-K_68 //
in <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos), in <s>vipralambha</s> (separation), and in <s>śānta</s> (tranquil [rasa]), it is endowed with preeminence;
<s>ojas</s> (vigor) is the cause of effulgence and self-expansion; it abides in <s>vīra rasa</s> (heroic sentiment); // MKpr-K_69 //
in <s>bībhatsa</s> (odious) and <s>raudra</s> (furious) <s>rasas</s>, its intensity increases progressively;
like fire with dry fuel, like clear water, that which immediately // MKpr-K_70 //
pervades the other [mind of the reader] is <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity) — it has its place everywhere;
the mode of these [qualities] depends on the mode of the qualities [themselves] regarding word and meaning. // MKpr-K_71 //
Some are included within these [three]; from the removal of faults, others are obtained;

children.text: anye bhajanti doṣatvaṃ kutracinna tato daśa // MKpr-K_72 //
children.translated_text: still others [which some propose] partake of the nature of faults in certain contexts — therefore [the qualities are] not ten. // MKpr-K_72 //

children.text: tena nārthaguṇā vācyāḥ proktāḥ śabdaguṇāśca ye /
children.translated_text: Therefore, what have been called qualities of meaning should not be stated [as separate qualities]; and those that have been called qualities of word —

children.text: varṇāḥ samāso racanā teṣāṃ vyañjakatāmitāḥ // MKpr-K_73 //
children.translated_text: [namely] syllables, compounding, and arrangement — those are accepted as having suggestive capacity [only]. // MKpr-K_73 //

children.text: murdhni vargāntyagāḥ sparśā aṭavargā raṇau laghū /
children.translated_text: At the head [of words], the final consonants of the classes (<s>varga</s>), and the consonants of the <s>ṭa</s>-class, <s>ra</s> and <s>ṇa</s>, are light;
repetition or middle-flowing [style], and combination in sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>) — thus. // MKpr-K_74 //
The conjunction [is] of the first and third with the fifth [of each class], of two identical [consonants] with <s>ra</s>,

children.text: ṭādiḥ śaṣau vṛttidairghyaṃ gumpha uddhṛta ojasi // MKpr-K_75 //
children.translated_text: <s>ṭa</s>-class and <s>śa</s>, <s>ṣa</s> give length of flow; weaving (<s>gumpha</s>) and extraction (<s>uddhṛta</s>) [belong to] vigor (<s>ojas</s>). // MKpr-K_75 //
That quality by which, merely from hearing a word, the comprehension of meaning arises,

children.text: sādhāraṇaḥ samagrāṇāṃ sa prasādo guṇo mataḥ // MKpr-K_76 //
children.translated_text: which is common to all [the qualities] — that is regarded as the quality of <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity). // MKpr-K_76 //
Through the propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) of the speaker, the subject, and the composition,
an alteration of arrangement, style, and phonemes in some cases is also accepted. // MKpr-K_77 //
When a statement made in one way is construed differently by another,

children.text: śleṣeṇa kākvā vā jñeyā sā vaktroktistathā dvidhā // MKpr-K_78 //
children.translated_text: whether through <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) or <s>kāku</s> (intonation) — that is known as <s>vaktrukti</s> (speaker's expression), and is thus twofold. // MKpr-K_78 //
<s>Anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) is the similarity of phonemes, and it is twofold, belonging to the <s>cheka</s> (elegant) style:
the former is the single occurrence of many [identical phonemes], the latter is the multiple occurrence of even one. // MKpr-K_79 //
That which employs phonemes suggestive of sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>) is called <s>upanāgarikā</s> (refined);
that which employs those revealing vigor (<s>ojas</s>) is <s>paruṣā</s> (harsh), and that with the remaining [phonemes] is <s>komalā</s> (soft). // MKpr-K_80 //
According to some, these are regarded as styles (<s>rīti</s>), headed by <s>Vaidarbhī</s>;
but <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s> (Lāṭa-alliteration) pertains to words, [arising] merely from a difference in purport (<s>tātparya</s>). // MKpr-K_81 //

children.text: padānāṃ saḥ padasyāpi vṛttāvanyatra tatra vā /
children.translated_text: It [applies] to words or to a [single] word, in a different passage or in the same one;

children.text: nāmnaḥ sa vṛttyavṛttyośca tadevaṃ pañcadhā mataḥ // MKpr-K_82 //
children.translated_text: to a noun, with or without a suffix — thus it is regarded as fivefold. // MKpr-K_82 //

children.text: arthe satyarthabhinnānāṃ varṇānāṃ sā punaḥ śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: When the meaning exists but the phonemes differ in meaning, that is <s>śruti</s> (homophony);
<s>yamaka</s> (punning repetition) operates in a verse-foot or in a part thereof, and is of many kinds. // MKpr-K_83 //
Differing through difference of the expressed meaning, words that touch upon simultaneous utterance
coalesce — that is <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), and it is eightfold through syllables and the like. // MKpr-K_84 //
From the absence of difference of base (<s>prakṛti</s>) and so forth, a ninth type may also exist;
that which is <s>citra</s> (pictorial) is where phonemes serve as the cause of the shapes of swords and the like. // MKpr-K_85 //
Furthermore, the appearance of unity in words of distinct forms,
or unity of meaning in a word, and likewise [unity] of word and meaning — this [is another type]. // MKpr-K_86 //

children.text: sādharmyamupamā bhede pūrṇā luptā ca sāgrimā /
children.translated_text: <s>Upamā</s> (simile) is similarity in difference; it is full (<s>pūrṇā</s>) or elliptical (<s>luptā</s>), and it is the foremost [figure];

children.text: śrautyārthī ca bhavedvākye samāse taddhite tathā // MKpr-K_87 //
children.translated_text: it may be phonetic (<s>śrautī</s>) or semantic (<s>ārthī</s>), occurring in a sentence, in a compound, or in a <s>taddhita</s> derivative. // MKpr-K_87 //

children.text: tadvad dharmasya lope syānna śrautī taddhite punaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the property [of comparison] is elided, it would not be phonetic; but in a <s>taddhita</s>,
when the standard of comparison is not mentioned, it occurs in a sentence or in a compound. // MKpr-K_88 //
When [the particle of comparison] beginning with <s>vā</s> is elided, in a compound it [occurs in] <s>karmadharāya</s>, <s>kyac</s>, <s>kyaṅ</s>,
or <s>karmakartr</s>, or with <s>ṇamul</s> — with the elision of two [elements], <s>kvip</s> [forms] occur in compounds. // MKpr-K_89 //
When both property and standard are elided, it is seen in derivation and in a sentence;

children.text: kyaci vādyupameyāse trilope ca samāsagā // MKpr-K_90 //
children.translated_text: in <s>kyac</s>, and when the subject of comparison beginning with <s>vā</s> [is elided] — with the elision of three, it occurs in compounds. // MKpr-K_90 //
When one and the same [entity] serves as both standard and subject of comparison in a single sentence,
that is <s>ananvaya</s> (self-comparison); the reverse is <s>upameyopamā</s> (mutual simile). // MKpr-K_91 //
The supposition of the present subject as being equal [to another] is <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy);

children.text: sasaṃdehastu bhedoktau tadanuktau ca saṃśayaḥ // MKpr-K_92 //
children.translated_text: with doubt when the difference is stated, it is <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt) when [the difference is] not stated. // MKpr-K_92 //
When there is non-difference of the standard and subject of comparison, that is <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor);
it applies to the entire object; it is phonetic and imposed — when // MKpr-K_93 //
both phonetic and semantic — and where it operates in a portion, that

children.text: sāṅgametan niraṅgaṃ tu śuddhaṃ mālā tu pūrvavat // MKpr-K_94 //
children.translated_text: is <s>sāṅga</s> (with parts); without parts, it is <s>śuddha</s> (pure); and a garland [of metaphors] is as before. // MKpr-K_94 //
The means of fixed imposition is the <s>āropa</s> (superimposition) of another [entity];

children.text: tatparaṃparitaṃ śliṣṭe vācake bhedabhāji vā // MKpr-K_95 //
children.translated_text: that which pertains to it, occurring in a close [metaphor] or in an explicit one that admits of distinction. // MKpr-K_95 //
When the present [subject] is denied and another is established, that is <s>apahṇuti</s> (concealment);

children.text: śleṣaḥ sa vākya ekasmin yatrānekārthatā bhavet // MKpr-K_96 //
children.translated_text: that <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) is where multiplicity of meaning occurs in a single statement. // MKpr-K_96 //
<s>Parokti</s> (indirect speech) [is made] through distinguishing [words] with double meaning; <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) is <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration) —
a non-existent relation of things that constructs a simile. // MKpr-K_97 //
The statement of the natural connection of one's own [effect with its] cause, and that with action alone, is another [type];

children.text: aprastutapraśaṃsā yā sā saiva prastutāśrayā // MKpr-K_98 //
children.translated_text: <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) is that which rests on the relevant subject. // MKpr-K_98 //

children.text: kārye nimitte sāmānye viśeṣe prastute sati /
children.translated_text: When the relevant is [described] in terms of effect, cause, generality, particularity,

children.text: tadanyasya vacastulye tulyasyeti ca pañcadhā // MKpr-K_99 //
children.translated_text: or speech equal to another's, or of one who is equal — thus it is fivefold. // MKpr-K_99 //
The determination of the present [subject] by another, after swallowing [it up],

children.text: prastutasya yadanyatvaṃ yadyarthoktau ca kalpanam // MKpr-K_100 //
children.translated_text: the otherness of the present [subject], and the imagining in the statement of meaning — // MKpr-K_100 //
and the reversal of the sequence of cause and effect —

children.text: vijñeyātiśayoktiḥ sā prativastūpamā tu sā // MKpr-K_101 //
children.translated_text: that is to be known as <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole); but <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-simile) is that // MKpr-K_101 //
where a single common [property] resides in two sentences;
and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) is the reflection of all of those. // MKpr-K_102 //
The single occurrence of a property belonging to both present and non-present entities,

children.text: saiva kriyāsu bahvīṣu kārakasyeti dīpakam // MKpr-K_103 //
children.translated_text: the same [property] in many actions of a single agent — that is <s>dīpaka</s> (illuminator). // MKpr-K_103 //
<s>Mālādīpaka</s> (garland-illuminator) is the first [type], inasmuch as each succeeding [element] enhances [the previous];
the single [occurrence of a] property of fixed [entities] — that is <s>tulyayogitā</s> (co-application). // MKpr-K_104 //
The differentiation of one thing from the standard of comparison and the like is <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast);
when equality is declared among the three — cause, stated, and unstated — // MKpr-K_105 //
— the implicit, whether by word or meaning, close [or explicit] — it is thus thrice eight;
the denial of what the speaker wishes [to affirm], with the desire to convey a distinction — // MKpr-K_106 //
— concerning what is to be stated or what has been stated — that is <s>ākṣepa</s> (reproach), regarded as twofold.
Even when an action is denied, the manifestation of its result is <s>vibhāvanā</s> (causeless effect). // MKpr-K_107 //
<s>Viśeṣokti</s> (special statement) is the non-statement of the effect when the causes are unimpaired;
<s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration) is the sequential correlation of sequential [items]. // MKpr-K_108 //

children.text: sāmānyaṃ vā viśeṣo vā tadanyena samarthyate /
children.translated_text: When a general [statement] or a particular is corroborated by something else,
that is <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration), whether through similarity or through its opposite. // MKpr-K_109 //
<s>Virodha</s> (contradiction) is speech expressed as contradictory even when there is no [real] contradiction;
<s>jāti</s> (class) may be contradicted by four [things] — class and the rest — by three qualities, // MKpr-K_110 //

children.text: kriyā dvābhyāmapi dravyaṃ dravyeṇaiveti te daśa /
children.translated_text: action by two, and substance by substance alone — thus there are ten [types].
<s>Svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) is the description of the natural action, form, or color of an infant and the like. // MKpr-K_111 //
<s>Vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) is censure on the face [of it], or praise — the conventional [meaning being] otherwise;

children.text: sā sahoktiḥ sahārthasya balādekaṃ dvivācakam // MKpr-K_112 //
children.translated_text: <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression) is where, by force of the co-existing meaning, one [word] expresses two [things]. // MKpr-K_112 //

children.text: vinoktiḥ sā binānyena yatrānyaḥ sanna netaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vinokti</s> (expression of absence) is where, without one [thing], another exists but not the other [associated thing];
<s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange) is the interchange of meanings between equals. // MKpr-K_113 //
When past or future states of being are rendered as if directly perceptible,
that is <s>bhāvika</s> (vivification); <s>kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason) is the expression of a reason as a sentence or word. // MKpr-K_114 //
<s>Paryāyokta</s> (circumlocution) is speech without the direct relation of expressed and expresser;

children.text: udāttaṃ vastunaḥ saṃpat mahatāṃ copalakṣaṇam // MKpr-K_115 //
children.translated_text: <s>udātta</s> (exalted) is the excellence of the subject, and the characteristic of great [persons]. // MKpr-K_115 //
When, in a single cause of establishing something, another [cause] that produces it arises,

children.text: samuccayo 'sau sa tvanyo yugapad yā guṇakriyāḥ // MKpr-K_116 //
children.translated_text: that is <s>samuccaya</s> (aggregation); but another [type] is when qualities and actions are simultaneous. // MKpr-K_116 //
One [thing] in sequence among many is <s>paryāya</s> (alternation); the other is otherwise;
<s>anumāna</s> (inference) is that which is stated of the provable and the means of proof. // MKpr-K_117 //
A statement with purposeful qualifiers is <s>parikara</s> (attendant);
<s>vyājakti</s> (disguise) is the concealment of the true nature of a thing that has emerged from a pretext. // MKpr-K_118 //

children.text: kiñcit pṛṣṭamapṛṣṭaṃ vā kathitaṃ yat prakalpate /
children.translated_text: When something asked or unasked is stated as if imagined,

children.text: tādṛganyavyapohāya parisaṃkhyā tu sā smṛtā // MKpr-K_119 //
children.translated_text: for the exclusion of others of that kind — that is known as <s>parisaṃkhyā</s> (enumeration by exclusion). // MKpr-K_119 //
When each successive [statement] is the cause of the preceding meaning,

children.text: tadā kāraṇamālā syāt kriyayā tu parasparam // MKpr-K_120 //
children.translated_text: then it is <s>kāraṇamālā</s> (chain of causes); but when actions [cause] each other, // MKpr-K_120 //
[and] two things mutually give rise [to each other], merely from hearing the succeeding [statement],

children.text: praśnasyonnayanaṃ yatra kriyate tatra vā sati // MKpr-K_121 //
children.translated_text: or when the raising of a question is performed therein — // MKpr-K_121 //
when there is a repeatedly inconceivable response, that is <s>uttara</s> (response);
when a subtle meaning perceived from some [indication] is revealed to another — // MKpr-K_122 //

children.text: dharmeṇa kenacid yatra tat sūkṣmaṃ paricakṣate /
children.translated_text: through some property — that is called <s>sūkṣma</s> (subtle);
progressively increasing excellence is <s>sāra</s> (essence), [reaching] the ultimate limit. // MKpr-K_123 //
When two properties that are in the relation of cause and effect, being in utterly different locations,
are declared simultaneously — that is <s>asaṃgati</s> (incongruity). // MKpr-K_124 //
<s>Samādhi</s> (resolution) is an easy task through the connection of another cause;

children.text: samaṃ yogyatayā yogo yadi saṃbhāvitaḥ kvacit // MKpr-K_125 //
children.translated_text: when a conjunction, though conceivable on grounds of fitness, // MKpr-K_125 //
somewhere, from excessive dissimilarity, does not reach the point of coalescence —
when the agent's attainment of the fruit of action is not achieved, and yet no calamity ensues — // MKpr-K_126 //
the quality and action of the effect [become] the quality and action of the cause,

children.text: krameṇa ca viruddhe yat sa eṣa viṣamo mataḥ // MKpr-K_127 //
children.translated_text: and also in the reverse — that is regarded as <s>viṣama</s> (disparity). // MKpr-K_127 //
When two great [things], one being the support and the other the supported,

children.text: āśrayāśrayiṇau syātāṃ tanutve 'pyadhikaṃ tu tat // MKpr-K_128 //
children.translated_text: become mutually the support and the supported — even in smallness, that [figure] is enhanced. // MKpr-K_128 //
The concealment, by one unable to counter the opponent,

children.text: yā tadīyasya tatstutyai pratyanīkaṃ taducyate // MKpr-K_129 //
children.translated_text: of what belongs to that [opponent], for the praise of the other — that is called <s>pratyanīka</s> (rivalry). // MKpr-K_129 //
When a thing is concealed by [another] thing with a similar mark,
whether its own or adventitious — that is known as <s>mīlita</s> (closing of eyes). // MKpr-K_130 //
When things are placed and then removed, one after another, progressively,

children.text: viśeṣaṇatayā yatra vastu saikāvalī dvidhā // MKpr-K_131 //
children.translated_text: as qualifiers — that is <s>ekāvalī</s> (single strand), and it is twofold. // MKpr-K_131 //
The recollection of a meaning as experienced, upon seeing something similar —
<s>smaraṇa</s> (reminiscence) is [when], deluded, upon seeing what resembles another known [experience], [one recalls it]. // MKpr-K_132 //
The objection to the standard of comparison is <s>pratīpa</s> (reverse simile), [where] the subject of comparison becomes [the standard];

children.text: tasyaiva yadi vā kalpyā tiraskāranibandhanam // MKpr-K_133 //
children.translated_text: of that very [subject], if imagined — the basis is disparagement. // MKpr-K_133 //
When the identity of the present [subject] with another, through the desire to express equality of properties,
is established through connection — that is known as <s>sāmānya</s> (generalization). // MKpr-K_134 //
The establishment of the supported without its well-known support;
the unified and simultaneous existence of one [entity] with multiple domains — // MKpr-K_135 //
the performance of another's task by one who is doing [his own]; the doing

children.text: tathaiva karaṇaṃ ceti viśeṣastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ // MKpr-K_136 //
children.translated_text: of what is impossible for another entity, in the same way — <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinction) is thus remembered as threefold. // MKpr-K_136 //
When a thing, abandoning its own quality, through connection with one of exceedingly brilliant quality,

children.text: vastu tadguṇatāmeti bhaṇyate sa tu tadguṇaḥ // MKpr-K_137 //
children.translated_text: takes on that quality — that is called <s>tadguṇa</s> (acquiring the other's quality). // MKpr-K_137 //
If there is no imitation of the other's form, that would be <s>atadguṇa</s> (not acquiring the other's quality);
when what was established in one way by someone is [established] differently by another, // MKpr-K_138 //

children.text: tathaiva yadvidhīyeta sa vyāghāta iti smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: and is carried out in just that [contrary] way — that is known as <s>vyāghāta</s> (contradiction).

children.text: seṣṭā saṃsṛṣṭireteṣāṃ bhedena yadiha sthitiḥ // MKpr-K_139 //
children.translated_text: The desired combination of these [figures], when there is separate existence, is <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination). // MKpr-K_139 //
The subordination and superordination among those that do not rest separately — that is <s>saṃkara</s> (intermingling);
and when one cannot be grasped [to the exclusion of] the other, from the absence of a reason or a fault [for choosing] — that is <s>aniścaya</s> (indetermination). // MKpr-K_140 //
When both sound-ornament and sense-ornament are clearly manifest in a single subject,

children.text: vyavasthitaṃ ca tenāsau trirūpaḥ parikīrtitaḥ // MKpr-K_141 //
children.translated_text: and are co-established — for this reason, [<s>saṃkara</s>] is declared to be of three forms. // MKpr-K_141 //
Whatever faults among these may arise in particular cases,
they are included within those already stated, and therefore are not separately expounded. // MKpr-K_142 //
Thus the series of <s>kārikās</s> (verses) of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> is completed.
<s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> (The Light on Poetry)
First <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter):
At the commencement of the work, the author invokes the appropriate chosen deity for the removal of obstacles —
Free from the constraints imposed by fate, consisting solely of delight, not dependent on anything else,
delightful with the nine <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments), presenting a creation [of its own] — the speech (<s>bhāratī</s>) of the poet is victorious! // MKpr-K_1 //

children.text: niyatiśaktyā niyatarūpā sukhaduḥkhamohasvabhāvā paramāṇvādyupādānakarmādisahakārikāraṇaparatantrā ṣaḍrasā na ca hṛdyaiva taiḥ, tādṛśī brahmaṇo nirmitirnirmāṇam / etadvilakṣaṇā tu kavivāṅnirmitiḥ / ata eva jayati / jayatyarthena ca namaskāra ākṣipyate iti tāṃ pratyasmi praṇata iti labhyate //1//
children.translated_text: The creation of <s>Brahman</s> is of a fixed form, determined by the power of destiny, having the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, dependent on cooperative causes such as atoms and <s>karma</s> as the material and efficient causes, [composed of] six <s>rasas</s> — and is not entirely pleasing through those. Such is the creation of <s>Brahman</s>. But the creation of the poet's speech is different from this. Therefore it is 'victorious.' And by the meaning of 'is victorious,' obeisance is implied — thus 'I bow to it' is obtained. //1//
Here, the subject matter along with the purpose is stated —
Poetry (<s>kāvya</s>) serves fame, wealth, knowledge of worldly conduct, the warding off of the inauspicious,
immediate supreme delight, and instruction that is like [the words of] a beloved woman. // MKpr-K_2 //

children.text: kālidāsādīnāmiva yaśaḥ śrīharṣāderdhāvakādīnāmiva dhanam rājādigatocitācāraparijñānam ādityādermayūrādīnāmivānarthanivāraṇam /
children.translated_text: fame, as in the case of <s>Kālidāsa</s> and others; wealth, as in the case of <s>Śrīharṣa</s> and others, or of <s>dhāvakas</s> (runners/performers) and the like; knowledge of proper conduct obtained from kings and the like; and the prevention of calamity, as [the sun prevents calamity] for peacocks and the like, from <s>Āditya</s> and others.

children.text: sakalaprayojanamaulibhūtaṃ samanantarameva rasāsvādana-samudbhūtaṃ vigalitavedyāntaramānandam prabhusaṃmitaśabdapradhānavedādiśāstrebhyaḥ śabdārthayorguṇabhāvena rasāṅgabhūtavyāpārapravaṇatayā vilakṣaṇaṃ yat kāvyaṃ lokottaravarṇanānipuṇakavikarma tat kānteva sarasatāpādanenābhimukhīkṛtya rāmādivadvartitavyaṃ na rāvaṇādivadityupadeśaṃ ca yathāyogaṃ kaveḥ sahṛdayasya ca karotīti sarvathā tatra yatanīyam //2//
children.translated_text: That which is the crown of all purposes — the bliss that arises immediately from the savoring of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), in which awareness of all other objects dissolves — distinct from the <s>Vedas</s> and other authoritative word-centered scriptures in that it is inclined toward the operation that serves as a component of <s>rasa</s>, with <s>guṇa</s> (quality) as the nature of word and meaning; that is <s>kāvya</s> (poetry), the work of a poet skilled in extraordinary description — like a beloved, by producing charm, it makes one receptive, and instructs that one should conduct oneself like <s>Rāma</s> and the others, not like <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and the others — it gives instruction to both the poet and the sympathetic reader (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) as appropriate. Therefore, one should strive in every way toward it. ||2||
Having thus stated its purpose, he states the cause:
<s>Śakti</s> (innate capacity), <s>nipuṇatā</s> (skill) through the examination of the world, <s>śāstras</s>, <s>kāvya</s>, and the rest,
and practice through the instruction of those who know <s>kāvya</s> — these are the causes of its production. || MKpr-K_3 ||

children.text: śaktiḥ kavitvabījarūpaḥ saṃskāraviśeṣaḥ yāṃ vinā kāvyaṃ na prasaret prasṛtaṃ vā upahasanīyaṃ syāt / lokasya sthāvarajaṅgamātmakalokavṛttasya / śāstrāṇāṃ chandovyākaraṇābhidhānakośakalācaturvargagajaturagakhaḍgādilakṣaṇagranthānām / kāvyānāṃ ca mahākavisaṃbandhinām / ādigrahaṇāditihāsānāṃ ca vimarśanādvyutpattiḥ / kāvyaṃ kartuṃ vicārayituṃ ca ye jānanti tadupadeśena karaṇe yojane ca paunaḥpunyena pravṛttiriti / trayaḥ samuditāḥ na tu vyastāḥ tasya kāvyasyodbhave nirmāṇe samullāse ca heturna tu hetavaḥ //3//
children.translated_text: <s>Śakti</s> (innate capacity) is a special <s>saṃskāra</s> (mental impression) in the form of the seed of poetic genius, without which poetry would either not flow forth, or if it did, would be laughable. Of the world — the world consisting of the animate and inanimate, the ways of the world. Of <s>śāstras</s> — treatises on meter, grammar, lexicons, dictionaries, arts, the four aims of life, treatises on the characteristics of elephants, horses, swords, and the like. Of <s>kāvyas</s> — those composed by great poets. The word 'ādi' (etc.) includes <s>itihāsas</s> (epics) as well — proficiency (<s>vyutpatti</s>) comes from their critical examination. Those who know how to compose and evaluate <s>kāvya</s> — through their instruction, repeated engagement in composition and practice. These three combined — not separately — are the cause of the production, creation, and manifestation of <s>kāvya</s>; not multiple independent causes. ||3||
Having thus stated its cause, he states its essential nature:
That [<s>kāvya</s> is] word and meaning free from defects, possessing <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), and unadorned [by figures] in some cases.

children.text:
doṣaguṇālaṅkārāḥ vakṣyante / kvāpītyanenaitadāha yat sarvatra
sālaṅkārau kvacittu sphuṭālaṅkāravirahe 'pi na kāvyatvahāniḥ /
children.translated_text: Defects, <s>guṇas</s>, and <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments) will be discussed. By 'in some cases' he states that although they are always adorned with ornaments, sometimes even in the absence of explicit <s>alaṅkāra</s>, there is no loss of the status of <s>kāvya</s>.
For example:

children.text:
{yaḥ kaumaraharaḥ sa eva hi varastā eva caitrakṣapāste
  conmīlitamālatīsurabhayaḥ prauḍhāḥ kadambānilāḥ /
  sā caivāsmi tathāpi tatra suratavyāpāralīlāvidau
  revārodhasi vetasītarutale cetaḥ samutkaṇṭhate //1//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śīlābhaṭṭārikā</s>, etc.)

{He who stole my youth is indeed the same, those same are the moonlit nights of <s>Caitra</s>, those same are the South winds, fragrant with blossoming <s>mālatī</s>, heavy with <s>kadamba</s> blossoms — and I too am the same; yet my heart longs for the bank of the <s>Revā</s>, beneath the <s>vetasī</s> tree, where we were both skilled in the play of love. ||1||}

children.text: atra sphuṭo na kaścidalaṅkāraḥ / rasasya ca prādhānyānnālaṅkāratā /
children.translated_text: Here there is no explicit <s>alaṅkāra</s>. And because of the predominance of <s>rasa</s>, it is not [classified as] <s>alaṅkāra</s>.
He states the divisions of that in order:

This is the highest — when the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) surpasses [the stated meaning]; the wise have called it <s>dhvani</s> (resonance), distinct from the expressed meaning. || MKpr-K_4 ||

children.text: idamiti kāvyam / budhairvaiyākaraṇaiḥ pradhānabhūtasphoṭarūpavyaṅgyavyañjakasya śabdasya dhvanir iti vyavahāraḥ kṛtaḥ / tatastanmatānusāribhiranyairapi nyagbhāvitavācyavyaṅgyavyañjanakṣamasya śabdārthayugalasya /
children.translated_text: 'This' refers to <s>kāvya</s>. By the wise — the grammarians — the designation <s>dhvani</s> was applied to the word whose nature is the <s>sphoṭa</s> (linguistic essence), which is the principal element that suggests the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>). Following their view, others too [applied the term] to the combination of word and meaning that is capable of suggesting, with the expressed meaning subordinated.
For example:

children.text:
{niḥśeṣacyutacandanaṃ stanataṭaṃ nirmṛṣṭarāgocharo
  netre dūramanañjane pulakitā tanvī tavayaṃ tanuḥ /
  mithyāvādini dūti bāndhavajanasyājñātapīḍāgame
  vāpīṃ snātumito gatāsi na punastasyādhamasyāntikam //2//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 105)

{The breast-region is entirely bereft of sandal paste, the lip-area is wiped clean of cosmetic, the eyes are far from collyrium, and this slender body of yours is thrilling with horripilation — O deceitful messenger-woman! When the kinsmen's unannounced visit of affliction came, you went from here to bathe at the pool — not, surely, to the presence of that scoundrel! ||2||}

children.text: atra tadantikameva rantuṃ gatāsīti prādhānyenādhamapadena vyajyate //4//
children.translated_text: Here, that she went precisely to his presence to make love is principally suggested by the word 'scoundrel' (<s>adhama</s>). ||4||
When [the suggested meaning] is not such [i.e., not predominant], it is <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion) — that is the middle [type of <s>kāvya</s>].
'Not such' means when the suggested meaning does not surpass the expressed meaning. For example:

children.text:
{grāmataruṇaṃ taruṇyā navavañjulamañjarīsanāthakaram /
  paśyantyā bhavati muhurnitarāṃ malinā mukhacchāyā //3//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 7.39)
{As the young woman watches the young man of the village making the hand-wreath of fresh <s>vañjula</s> blossoms, the complexion of her face becomes increasingly pale. ||3||}

children.text:
atra vañjulalatāgṛhe dattasaṃketā na gateti vyaṅgyaṃ guṇībhūtaṃ
tadapekṣayā vācyasyaiva camatkāritvāt //
children.translated_text: Here, the suggested meaning — that she, who had arranged a rendezvous in the <s>vañjula</s> bower, did not come — is subordinated, because the expressed meaning itself is more striking in comparison.
<s>Śabdacitra</s> (verbal artifice) and <s>vācyacitra</s> (content artifice) without suggestion are considered the lowest [type]. || MKpr-K_5 ||

children.text:
citramiti guṇālaṅkārayuktam / avyaṅgyamiti sphuṭapratīyamānārtharahitam /
avaram adhamam / yathā ----
children.translated_text: '<s>Citra</s>' (artifice) means endowed with <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s>. 'Without suggestion' means devoid of a clearly apprehended implicit meaning. 'The lowest' — the inferior [type]. For example:
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{May the <s>Mandākinī</s>, drunk with the roaring, surging, dense spray of waves overflowing from the hollows of the transparent, rising, pure, cascading waterfalls — [the river] at whose bank the great sages, delighted by the intoxicating splendor of the uprising of the destruction of the immense trees of the deep caves of the swelling frogs, performed their ablutions — may she grant you slowness! ||4||}

children.text:
{vinirgataṃ mānadamātmamandirād bhavatyupaśrutya yadṛcchayāpi yam /
  sasaṃbhramendrradrutapātitārgalā nimīlitākṣīva bhiyāmarāvatī //5//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Meṇṭha's</s> composition, <s>Hayagrīvavadha</s>)
{When <s>Amarāvatī</s> heard that he had departed from his own palace by his own pride, even by chance, she hastily dropped her bolts and, as if with eyes closed in fear... ||5||}
is the first <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter). || 1 ||
Thus in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, the determination of the purpose, cause, essential nature, and specific types of <s>kāvya</s>
He states the essential nature of word and meaning in order:
A word in this [<s>kāvya</s>] is threefold: <s>vācaka</s> (denotative), <s>lākṣaṇika</s> (indicative), and <s>vyañjaka</s> (suggestive).
'Here' means in <s>kāvya</s>. Their essential nature will be discussed.
The expressed (<s>vācya</s>) and the rest are their respective meanings...
namely the expressed (<s>vācya</s>), the indicated (<s>lakṣya</s>), and the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>).
... and according to some, <s>tātparyārtha</s> (purport) as well. || MKpr-K_6 ||

children.text: ākāṅkṣāyogyatāsaṃnidhivaśādvakṣyamāṇasvarūpāṇāṃ padārthānāṃ samanvaye tātparyārtho viśeṣavapurapadārtho 'pi vākyaārthaḥ samullasatītyabhihitānvayavādināṃ matam //
children.translated_text: When the meaning of words — whose nature will be discussed — is synthesized through expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), compatibility (<s>yogyatā</s>), and proximity (<s>saṃnidhi</s>), the <s>tātparyārtha</s> (purport) — a distinct entity that is not a word-meaning — also manifests as the sentence-meaning. This is the view of the proponents of <s>abhihitānvayavāda</s> (the theory that denotation precedes connection).
The expressed meaning alone is the sentence-meaning — so say the proponents of <s>anvitābhidhānavāda</s> (the theory of connected denotation). ||6||
The suggestive capacity is also accepted for practically all meanings.
Here, [an example] of the expressed [meaning serving as suggestive]:

children.text:
{mā_e gharova_araṇaṃ ajja hu ṇatthi tti sāhi_aṃ tuma_e /
  tā bhaṇa kiṃ karaṇijjaṃ eme_a ṇa vāsaro ṭhā_i //6//}
[mātaḥ gṛhopakaraṇaṃ adya khalu nāstīti sādhitaṃ tvayā /
children.translated_text: then say, what is to be done — in this way the day cannot just pass! ||6||}

children.text: tadbhaṇa kiṃ karaṇīyaṃ evameva na vāsaraḥ sthīyī //]
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>: Mother, you have contrived that today there are indeed no household provisions; then say, what is to be done — the day cannot just be spent like this!]
(<s>Hāla's</s> <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s>)
{Mother, you have contrived that today there are indeed no household provisions;
Here, that she desires to roam freely is suggested. An example of the indicated [meaning serving as suggestive]:

children.text:
{sāhentī sahi suha_aṃ khaṇe khaṇe dummiāsi majjhaka_e /
  sabbhāvaṇehakaraṇijjasarisa_aṃ dāva vira_i_aṃ tuma_e //7//}

children.translated_text: something befitting the duty of true affection has indeed been devised by you! ||7||}
[Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>: Accomplishing good fortune, O friend, moment by moment you become distressed on my account; something resembling the duty of true affection has indeed been fashioned by you!]
(<s>Hāla's</s> <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s>)
{Accomplishing good fortune, O friend, you grow weary moment by moment on my account;

children.text: atra matpriyaṃ ramayantyā tvayā śatrutvamācaritamiti lakṣyam / tena ca kāmukaviṣayaṃ sāparādhatvaprakāśanaṃ vyaṅgyam / vyaṅgyasya yathā
children.translated_text: Here, the indicated meaning is: 'While you were entertaining my beloved, you have acted as an enemy to me.' And through that, the suggested meaning is the disclosure of guilt regarding the lover. An example of the suggested [meaning serving as suggestive]:

children.text:
{u_a ṇiccalaṇippandā bhisiṇīpattammi rehai valā_ā /
  ṇimmalamaraga_abhā_aṇapariṭṭiā saṃkhasuttivva //8//}

children.translated_text: like a conch-shell set in a vessel of spotless emerald! ||8||}
[Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>: Look — motionless and still, a crane gleams upon a lotus leaf, like a conch-shell placed in a vessel of spotless emerald!]
(<s>Hāla's</s> <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 1.4)
{Look — motionless and still, a crane rests on a lotus leaf,

children.text: atra niṣpandatvena āśvastatvam / tena ca janarahitatvam / ataḥ saṃketasthānametaditi kayācit kañcitpratyucyate / athavā mithyā vadasi na tvamatrāgatobhūriti vyajyate //
children.translated_text: Here, by its motionlessness, [the crane's] sense of security [is suggested]; and by that, the absence of people. Therefore, 'this is a place for a rendezvous' — so someone says to someone else. Or alternatively, it is suggested: 'You speak falsely — you did not come here [as you claim].'
He states the essential nature of the <s>vācaka</s> (denotative word) and the others in order:
That which conveys a meaning directly designated by convention is the <s>vācaka</s> (denotative word). || MKpr-K_7 ||

children.text: ihāgṛhītasaṃketasya śabdasyārthapratīterabhāvātsaṃketasahāya eva śabdo 'rthaviśeṣaṃ pratipādayatīti yasya yatrāvyavadhānena saṃketo gṛhyate sa tasya vācakaḥ //7//
children.translated_text: Since there is no cognition of meaning from a word whose convention has not been grasped, a word conveys a specific meaning only with the aid of convention. That word whose convention with regard to a particular meaning is grasped without intermediary is the <s>vācaka</s> of that meaning. ||7||
The conventionally designated [meaning] has four divisions: <s>jāti</s> (universal) and the rest — or <s>jāti</s> alone [according to some].

children.text:
yadyapyarthakriyākāritayā pravṛttinivṛttiyogyā vyaktireva tathāpyānantyād vyabhicārācca tatra saṃketaḥ kartuṃ na yujyata iti
gauḥ śuklaścalo ḍittha ityādīnāṃ viṣayavibhāgo na prāpnotīti ca / tadupādhāveva saṃketaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although it is the particular (<s>vyakti</s>) alone that, through its capacity for causal efficacy, is fit for practical engagement and disengagement, nevertheless, because of its infinity and because of deviation, convention cannot properly be applied to it — thus the distinction of the domains of [words like] 'cow,' 'white,' 'moving,' '<s>Ḍittha</s>' and so on would not be obtained. Therefore convention is applied to its qualifying condition (<s>upādhi</s>) alone.

children.text:
upādhiśca dvividhaḥ ---- vastudharmo vaktṛyadṛcchāsaṃniveśitaśca / vastudharmo 'pi dvividhaḥ ---- siddhaḥ sādhyaśca / siddho 'pi dvividhaḥ ---- padārthasya prāṇaprado viśeṣādhānahetuśca / tatrādyo jātiḥ / uktaṃ hi vākyapadīye ----
{na hi gauḥ svarūpeṇa gaurnāpyagauḥ / gotvābhisaṃvandhātu gauḥ} iti /
children.translated_text: The qualifying condition (<s>upādhi</s>) is twofold: a property of the thing itself, and one arbitrarily assigned by the speaker. The property of the thing is also twofold: established (<s>siddha</s>) and to-be-accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>). The established is also twofold: that which gives life to the word-meaning, and that which is the cause of attributing distinction. The first of these is <s>jāti</s> (universal). As stated in the <s>Vākyapadīya</s>: 'A cow is not a cow by its own form, nor is it a non-cow; it is a cow by virtue of its connection with cowness.'

children.text:
dvitīyo guṇaḥ / śuklādinā hi labdhasattākaṃ vastu viśiṣyate / sādhyaḥ pūrvāparībhūtāvayavaḥ kriyārūpaḥ /
ḍitthādiśabdānāmantyabuddhinirgrāhyaṃ saṃhṛtakramaṃ svarūpaṃ vaktrā tadṛcchayā ḍitthādiṣvartheṣūpādhitvena saṃniveśyata iti so 'yaṃ saṃjñārūpo yadṛcchātmaka iti /
children.translated_text: The second is <s>guṇa</s> (quality). For a thing that has obtained its existence through whiteness and the like is thereby distinguished. The to-be-accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>) is action (<s>kriyā</s>) in nature, consisting of parts that are prior and subsequent. The own-form of words like '<s>Ḍittha</s>' — grasped by the final cognition, with its sequence collapsed — is arbitrarily assigned by the speaker as the qualifying condition in objects like <s>Ḍittha</s> and the rest; thus this is of the nature of a proper name (<s>saṃjñā</s>), arbitrary in character.

children.text: {gauḥśuklaścalo ḍittha ityādau catuṣṭayī śabdānāṃ pravṛttiḥ} iti mahābhāṣyakāraḥ / paramāṇvādīnāṃ tu guṇamadhyapāṭhāt pāribhāṣikaṃ guṇatvam / guṇakriyāyadṛcchānāṃ vastuta ekarūpāṇām apyāśrayabhedād bheda iva lakṣyate / yathaikasya mukhasya khaḍgamukuratailādyālambanabhedāt /
children.translated_text: The author of the <s>Mahābhāṣya</s> states: {In 'cow,' 'white,' 'moving,' '<s>Ḍittha</s>' and so on, there is a fourfold basis for the application of words.} As for atoms and the like, their <s>guṇa</s>-hood is conventional, from being listed among <s>guṇas</s>. Though <s>guṇa</s>, <s>kriyā</s>, and <s>yadṛcchā</s> (arbitrary designation) are in reality of one form, a distinction is perceived as if real due to the difference of substrata — just as a single face [appears different] due to the difference of reflecting surfaces such as a sword, mirror, oil, and the like.

children.text:
himapayaḥśaṅkhādyāśrayeṣu paramārthato bhinneṣu śuklādiṣu yadvaśena śuklaḥ śukla ityādyabhinnābhidhānapratyayotpattistat śuklatvādi sāmānyam / guḍataṇḍulādipākādiṣvevameva pākatvādi /
bālavṛddhaśukādyudīriteṣu ḍitthādiśabdeṣu ca pratikṣaṇaṃ bhidyamāneṣu ḍitthādya'rtheṣu vā ḍitthatvādyastīti sarveṣāṃ śabdānāṃ jātireva pravṛttinimittamityanye / tadvān apoho vā śabdārthaḥ kaiściduktaṃ iti granthagauravabhayāt prakṛtānupayogācca na darśitam //7//
children.translated_text: In the substrata of whiteness and the like — snow, milk, conch, etc. — which are ultimately distinct, the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) such as 'whiteness' is that by virtue of which there arises an undifferentiated cognition and designation: 'white, white.' Similarly with 'cooking-ness' in the cooking of molasses, rice, and so on. And in words like '<s>Ḍittha</s>' uttered by children, old men, parrots, and so on, or in objects like <s>Ḍittha</s> that change every moment — <s>Ḍittha</s>-ness and the like exist — [hence] <s>jāti</s> (universal) alone is the ground for the application of all words, according to others. That the meaning of a word is the possessor of that [universal], or <s>apoha</s> (exclusion), has been stated by some — but is not presented here, out of fear of prolixity and because it is not useful for the present topic. ||7||
That is the primary meaning; and the primary operation with regard to it is called <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation). || MKpr-K_8 ||
'That' means directly designated by convention. 'Its' means of the word. ||8||
When the primary meaning is blocked, and there is a connection [with another meaning], either from established usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) or from purpose (<s>prayojana</s>),

children.text: anyo 'rtho lakṣyate yatsā lakṣaṇāropitā kriyā // MKpr-K_9 //
children.translated_text: another meaning is indicated — that operation, superimposed, is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication). || MKpr-K_9 ||

children.text: {karmani kuśalaḥ} ityādau darbhagrahaṇādyayogāt {gaṅgaāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ} ityādau ca gaṅgādīnāṃ ghoṣādyādhāratvāsaṃbhavāt mukhyārthasya bādhe vivecakatvādau sāmīpye ca saṃbandhe rūḍhitaḥ prasiddheḥ
children.translated_text: In expressions like '<s>karmani kuśalaḥ</s>' (skilled in action), because of the inapplicability of the primary meaning of grasping <s>darbha</s> grass and the like; and in '<s>Gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ</s>' (the cowherd settlement is in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>), because of the impossibility of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> being the substratum for the cowherd settlement and so on — when there is a blocking of the primary meaning, and a relation such as proximity serves as the distinguishing factor, from established usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>), i.e., from convention,

children.text: tathā gaṅgātaṭe ghoṣa ityādaiḥ prayogāt yeṣāṃ na tathā pratipattiḥ teṣāṃ pāvanatvādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ tathāpratipādanātmanaḥ prayojanācca mukhyena amukhyo 'rtho lakṣyate yat sa āropitaḥ śabdavyāpāraḥ sāntarārthaniṣṭho
children.translated_text: as well as from usage such as '<s>Gaṅgātaṭe ghoṣaḥ</s>' (the cowherd settlement is on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>) — for those properties such as purifying power and the like, for whom the understanding is not thus [directly], from the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) of conveying such properties — a non-primary meaning is indicated by the primary [meaning]. That superimposed verbal operation, which rests upon an intervening meaning,
is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication). ||9||
The appropriation of another for one's own establishment, and the offering of oneself for another's purpose —

children.text: upādānaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cetyuktā śuddhaiva sā dvidhā // MKpr-K_10 //
children.translated_text: these, [called] <s>upādāna</s> (adoption) and <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (characterization), constitute the pure [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>], which is stated to be twofold. || MKpr-K_10 ||

children.text:
{kuntāḥ praviśanti} {yaṣṭayaḥ praviśanti} ityādau kuntādibhirātmanaḥ praveśasiddhyarthaṃ svasaṃyoginaḥ puruṣā ākṣipyante / tata upādānene 'yaṃ lakṣaṇā /
{gauranubandhyaḥ} ityādau śruticoditamanubandhanaṃ kathaṃ me syāditi jātyā vyaktirākṣipyate na tu śabdenocyate
{viśeṣyaṃ nābhidhā gacchet kṣīṇaśaktirviśeṣaṇe} iti nyāyādityupādānalakṣaṇā tu nodāhartavyā /
na hyatra prayojanamasti na vā rūḍhiriyam / vyaktyavinābhāvitvāttu jātyā vyaktirākṣipyate / yathā kriyatāmityatra kartā / kurvityatra karma / praviśa piṇḍīmityādau gṛhaṃ bhakṣayetyādi ca /
children.translated_text:
In [expressions like] 'the spears enter' or 'the staffs enter,' by 'spears' and the like, the persons connected with them are implied (<s>ākṣipyante</s>) for the purpose of establishing [the act of] their own entering. Therefore, this is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) through <s>upādāna</s> (inclusion).
In [expressions like] 'a cow is to be tied up,' the individual [animal] is implied by the universal [genus] — because the tying up enjoined by scripture requires [asking] 'how may [the injunction] apply to me?' — but the individual is not denoted by the word.
According to the principle that 'the qualifier cannot proceed to the qualified when its power is exhausted,' <s>upādāna-lakṣaṇā</s> (inclusion-type secondary signification) should not be illustrated [here].
For here there is no purpose [for lakṣaṇā], nor is this a conventional usage. Rather, since the individual is inseparable from the universal, the individual is implied by the universal — just as in 'let it be done,' the agent [is implied]; in 'do!', the object [is implied]; and in 'enter the ball [of food],' 'consume the house,' and so forth.

children.text:
{pīno devadatto divā na bhuṅkte} ityatra ca rātribhojanaṃ na lakṣyate śrutārthāpatterarthāpattervā tasya viṣayatvāt /
{gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ} ityatra taṭasya ghoṣādhikaraṇatvasiddhaye gaṅgāśabdaḥ svārthamarpayati ityevamādau lakṣaṇenaiṣā lakṣaṇā / ubhayarūpā ceyaṃ śuddhā / upacāreṇāmiśritatvāt /
children.translated_text:
In 'Fat <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat during the day,' the eating at night is not indicated through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — because that is the domain of <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> (implication from what is heard) or <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption).
In 'the settlement on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,' the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' conveys its own meaning in order to establish the bank as the locus of the settlement — and in such cases, this [type of] <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is [established] through [another] <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. And this [type] is pure in both forms — because it is unmixed with <s>upacāra</s> (figurative transfer).

children.text: anayorlakṣyasya lakṣakasya ca na bhedarūpaṃ tāṭasthyam / taṭādīnāṃ gaṅgādiśabdaiḥ pratipādane tattvapratipattau hi pratipipādayiṣitaprayojanasaṃpratyayaḥ / gaṅgāsaṃbandhamātrapratītau tu gaṅgātaṭe ghoṣa iti mukhyaśabdābhidhānāllakṣaṇāyāḥ ko bhedaḥ //10//
children.translated_text: Between the indicated meaning (<s>lakṣya</s>) and the indicator (<s>lakṣaka</s>), there is no distinction amounting to mere extrinsic [separateness]. For when the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' and the like are used to convey [the meaning of] the bank and so forth, it is in the apprehension of their real nature that the intended purpose is understood. But in the mere cognition of a connection with the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, what distinguishes [this] <s>lakṣaṇā</s> from the primary denotation in [the straightforward expression] 'the settlement on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>'? || 10 ||
Another [kind], however, is with superimposition (<s>sāropā</s>), where both the superimposed and the substrate

children.text: āropyamāṇaḥ āropaviṣayaśca yatrānapahnutabhedau sāmānādhikaraṇyena nirdiśyete sā lakṣaṇā sāropā //
children.translated_text: — that is, the one being superimposed [upon] and the substrate of superimposition — are indicated with their difference undenied, through co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is called 'with superimposition' (<s>sāropā</s>).
When the other [i.e., the substrate] is subsumed within the superimposed, that [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] would be through determination (<s>sādhyavasānikā</s>). || Kpr-K_11 ||

children.text: viṣayiṇāropyamāṇenāntaḥkṛte nigīrṇe anyasminnāropaviṣaye sati sādhyavasānā syāt //11//
children.translated_text: When the other — the substrate of superimposition — is subsumed, that is, absorbed within the superimposed entity, that would be [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] through determination (<s>sādhyavasānā</s>). || 11 ||

children.text:
bhedāvimau ca sādṛśyātsambandhāntaratastathā /
gauṇau śuddhau ca vijñeyau ...
children.translated_text: And these two types, based on similarity and based on other relations, should be known as figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>) and pure (<s>śuddha</s>) respectively...

children.text:
imāvāropādhyavasānarūpau sādṛśyahetū bhedau {gaurvāhīkaḥ} ityatra {gaurayam} ityatra ca /
atra hi svārthasahacāriṇo guṇā jāḍyamāndyādayo lakṣyamāṇā api gośabdasya parārthābhidhāne pravṛttinimittatvamupayāntiṃ iti kecit / svārthasahacāriguṇābhedena padārthagatā guṇā eva lakṣyante na
parārtho 'bhidhīyate ityanye / sādhāraṇaguṇāśrayatvena parārtha eva lakṣyate ityapare /
uktaṃ cānyatra
  {abhidheyāvinābhūtapratītirlakṣaṇocyate /
  lakṣyamāṇaguṇairyogādvṛtteriṣṭā tu gauṇatāṃ} iti /

children.translated_text: (<s>Kumārila</s>, <s>Tantravārtika</s> 3.4.12)

These two types — in the forms of superimposition (<s>āropa</s>) and determination (<s>adhyavasāna</s>) — when based on similarity, are the figurative type, [as in] 'the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is an ox' or 'this one is an ox.'
For here, some [hold that] the qualities accompanying the primary meaning — dullness, slowness, and the like — though indicated, serve as the ground for the word 'ox' being applied to another meaning. Others [hold that] through the non-difference with the qualities accompanying the primary meaning, only the qualities inherent in the referent are indicated, and no other meaning is denoted. Still others [hold that] through being the locus of the common qualities, precisely the other meaning is indicated.
And it has been stated elsewhere:
'The cognition inseparable from the denoted [meaning] is called <s>lakṣaṇā</s>;
but [that usage is called] figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>) because the denotative power is accepted on account of the connection with the qualities that are being indicated.'

children.text:
avinābhāvo 'tra saṃbandhamātraṃ na tu nāntarīyakatvam / tattve hi {mañcāḥ krośanti} ityādau na lakṣaṇā syāt /
avinābhāve cākṣepeṇaiva siddherlakṣaṇāyā nopayoga ityuktam /
{āyurdhṛtam} {āyurevedam} ityādau ca sādṛśyādanyat kāryakāraṇabhāvādi saṃbandhāntaram / evamādau ca kāryakāraṇabhāvādilakṣaṇapūrve āropādhyavasāne /
children.translated_text:
'Inseparability' here means mere connection, not invariable concomitance. For if [it meant] the latter, there would be no <s>lakṣaṇā</s> in [expressions like] 'the platforms are shouting' and the like.
And where there is inseparability, since [the meaning] is already established through implication (<s>ākṣepa</s>), there is no need for <s>lakṣaṇā</s> — as was stated.
In [expressions like] 'lifespan is sustained' or 'this is lifespan itself,' the other relation — such as cause-and-effect — is different from similarity. And in such cases, the superimposition and determination are preceded by <s>lakṣaṇā</s> based on the relation of cause and effect.

children.text: atra gauṇabhedayorbhede 'pi tādrūpyapratītiḥ sarvathaivābhedāvagamaśca prayojanam / śuddhabhedayostvanyavailakṣaṇyenāvyabhicāreṇa ca kāryakāritvādi /
children.translated_text: Here, in both figurative subtypes, the purpose is the cognition of resemblance or the comprehension of complete non-difference, respectively. But in both pure subtypes, [the purpose is] the production of an effect through distinction from others and through non-deviation.

children.text: kvacit tādarthyādupacāraḥ / yathā indrārthā sthūṇā indraḥ / kvacit svasvāmibhāvāt / yathā rājakīyaḥ puruṣo rājā / kvacit avayavāvayavibhāvāt / yathā agrahasta ityatrāgramātre 'vayave hastaḥ / kvacit tātkarmyāt / yathā atakṣā takṣā //
children.translated_text: Sometimes <s>upacāra</s> (figurative transfer) is based on purposive relation (<s>tādarthya</s>) — as when a pillar [used] for <s>Indra</s>'s [festival] is called '<s>Indra</s>.' Sometimes based on the relation of possession — as when a man belonging to the king is called 'the king.' Sometimes based on the part-whole relation — as in '<s>agrahastaḥ</s>' (tip of the hand), where 'hand' [is applied to] the mere tip, a part. Sometimes based on functional similarity (<s>tātkarmya</s>) — as when a non-carpenter is called a carpenter.
... thus <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is sixfold. || Kpr-K_12 ||
Together with the first two types. || 12 ||
And it [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>],

children.text: vyaṅgyena rahitā rūḍhau sahitā tu prayojane /
children.translated_text: when devoid of suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), is in conventional usage; when accompanied [by suggested meaning], it has a purpose.
For the purpose is precisely what is apprehended through the operation of suggestion (<s>vyañjana</s>).
And that [suggested meaning] is either concealed or unconcealed...
'That' refers to the suggested meaning. Concealed, as in:

children.text:
{mukhaṃ vikasitasmitaṃ vaśitavakrima prekṣitaṃ
  samucchalitavibhramā gatirapāstasaṃsthā matiḥ /
  uro mukulitastanaṃ jaghanamaṃsavandhoddhuraṃ
  batenduvadanātanau taruṇimodgamo modate //9//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s>)

'Her face blossoms with a smile, her glance is restrained with a curve, her gait surges with coquetry, her composure is abandoned in mind, her breast is in bud upon her chest, her hips are weighed down by the fullness of flesh — alas, in the moon-faced one's body, the rising of womanhood rejoices!' || 9 ||
Unconcealed, as in:

children.text:
{śrīparicayājjaḍā api bhavantyabhijñā vidagdhacaritānām /
  upadiśati kāminīnāṃ yauvanamada eva lalitāni //10//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vallabhadeva</s>'s <s>Subhāṣitāvali</s>)
'Even the dull become knowledgeable of the ways of the sophisticated through familiarity with beauty; for the intoxication of youth itself instructs young women in the arts of grace.' || 10 ||
Here, [the word] 'instructs' [makes the suggestion unconcealed].
... thus this [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] is described as threefold. || Kpr-K_13 ||
Without suggested meaning, with concealed suggested meaning, and with unconcealed suggested meaning. || 13 ||
A word that is based on that [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] is called <s>lākṣaṇika</s> (figurative)...
'Word' is to be connected [with the previous]. 'Based on that' means having that [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] as its basis.
... therein, the operation [of such a word] is of the nature of suggestion (<s>vyañjana</s>).
Why? He says:
That for whose cognition <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is resorted to — || Kpr-K_14 ||
When the result is apprehensible from the word alone, there is here no other operation beyond suggestion.

children.text: prayojanapratipipādayiṣayā yatra lakṣaṇayā śabdaprayogastatra nānyatastatpratītirapi tu tasmādeva śabdāt /
children.translated_text: Where the use of a word is through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> with the desire to convey the purpose, there too the cognition [of the purpose] is not from anything else but from that very word.
And here there is no other operation apart from suggestion.
For indeed:
It is not denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>), because of the absence of convention (<s>samaya</s>)...

children.text: gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityādau ye pāvanatvādayo dharmāstaṭādau pratīyante na tatra gaṅgādiśabdāḥ saṃketitāḥ //
children.translated_text: In [expressions like] 'the settlement on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' and the like, the qualities such as sanctity and the rest that are cognized regarding the bank and so forth — for those, the words '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' and the like are not conventionally designated.
Nor is it <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, because of the absence of the ground. || Kpr-K_15 ||
The ground is the triad [of conditions] beginning with the obstruction of the primary meaning. || 15 ||
And accordingly:

children.text: lakṣyaṃ na mukhyaṃ nāpyatra bādho yogaḥ phalena no /
children.translated_text: The indicated meaning is not the primary one; nor is there here any obstruction; nor any connection with the result;

children.text: na prayojanametasmin na ca śabdaḥ skhaladgatiḥ // MKpr-K_16 //
children.translated_text: nor any purpose in this; nor is the word faltering in [its capacity]. || Kpr-K_16 ||

children.text:
yathā gaṅgāśabdaḥ srotasi sabādha iti taṭaṃ lakṣayati tadvat yadi taṭe 'pi sabādhaḥ syāt tat prayojanaṃ lakṣayet /
na ca taṭaṃ mukhyo 'rthaḥ / nāpyatra bādhaḥ / na ca gaṅgāśabdārthasya taṭasya pāvanatvādyairlakṣaṇīyaiḥ saṃbandhaḥ / nāpi prayojane lakṣye kiñcit prayojanam / nāpi gaṅgāśabdastaṭamiva prayojanaṃ pratipādayitumasamarthaḥ //16//
children.translated_text:
Just as the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>,' being obstructed in [its application to] the stream, indicates the bank — so too, if it were obstructed in [its application to] the bank as well, it would indicate the purpose.
But the bank is not the primary meaning. Nor is there any obstruction here. Nor is there any connection between the bank — the meaning of the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' — and the [qualities] to be indicated, such as sanctity and the rest. Nor is there any [further] purpose in the purpose that is to be indicated. Nor is the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' incapable of conveying the purpose as it [conveys] the bank. || 16 ||
Even so, there would be an infinite regress that destroys the root [meaning].

children.text: evamapi prayojanaṃ cellakṣyate tat prayojanāntareṇeti tadapi prayojanāntareṇeti prakṛtāpratītikṛt anavasthā bhavet //
children.translated_text: Even if the purpose is indicated [by <s>lakṣaṇā</s>], that [would require] another purpose, and that too another purpose — [thus] there would be an infinite regress that prevents the cognition of the matter at hand.

children.text: nanu pāvanatvādidharmayuktameva taṭaṃ lakṣyate / {gaṅgāyāstaṭe ghoṣaḥ} ityato 'dhikasyārthasya pratītiśca prayojanamiti viśiṣṭe lakṣaṇā tatkiṃ vyañjanayetyāha
children.translated_text: Objection: It is the bank endowed with the qualities of sanctity and the like that is indicated [by <s>lakṣaṇā</s>]. And the cognition of a meaning beyond [what is expressed in] 'the settlement on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' is the purpose. Thus the <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is of the qualified [meaning] — so why posit suggestion (<s>vyañjanā</s>)? To this he responds:

children.text: prayojanena sahitaṃ lakṣaṇīyaṃ na yujyate // MKpr-K_17 //
children.translated_text: That the indicable meaning should be accompanied by the purpose is not tenable. || Kpr-K_17 ||
Why? He says:
For the object of cognition is one thing, and the result is stated to be another.
For perception and the like, the object is blue and so forth, but the result is manifestation or awareness.
That <s>lakṣaṇā</s> should be of the qualified [meaning] is not so...
This has been explained.
... rather, the special features would belong to the indicated [meaning]. || Kpr-K_18 ||

children.text: taṭādau viśeṣāḥ pāvanatvādayaste cābhidhātātparyalakṣaṇābhyo vyāpārāntareṇa gamyāḥ / tacca vyañjanadhvananadyotanādiśabdavācyamavaśyameṣitavyam //18//
children.translated_text: The special features such as sanctity and the rest in the bank and so forth — these are apprehensible through a different operation from denotation, implication (<s>tātparya</s>), and <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. And that [operation], designated by the words suggestion (<s>vyañjana</s>), resonance (<s>dhvanana</s>), illumination (<s>dyotana</s>), and the like, must necessarily be accepted. || 18 ||
Thus, the suggestive power based on <s>lakṣaṇā</s> has been stated. Now he states the [suggestive power] based on denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>):
When the denotative power of a word with multiple meanings is restricted,
the operation that produces the cognition of the undenoted meaning is suggestion (<s>añjana</s>). || Kpr-K_19 ||
'Association, dissociation, co-occurrence, opposition,
meaning, context, gender, the proximity of another word,
capability, propriety, place, time, individual, accent, and the like —
these are the causes of the recollection of the specific [meaning] when the meaning of the word is undetermined.'
(<s>Bhartṛhari</s>, <s>Vākyapadīya</s> 2.315-316)

children.text:
ityuktadiśā
saśaṅkhacakro hariḥ aśaṅkhacakro harirityucyate / rāmalakṣmaṇāviti dāśarathau / rāmārjunagatistayoriti bhārgavakārtavīryayoḥ / sthāṇuṃ bhaja bhavacchide, iti hare / sarvaṃ jānāti deva iti yuṣmadarthe /
kupito makaradhvaja iti kāme / devasya purārāteriti śaṃbhau / madhunā mattaḥ kokila iti vasante / pātu vo dayitāmukhamiti sāṃmukhye / bhātyatra parameśvara iti rājadhānīrūpāt deśādrājani / citrabhānurvibhātīti dine ravau rātrau vahnau /
mitraṃ bhātīti suhṛdi mitro bhātīti ravau / indraśatrurityādau vede eva na kāvye svaro viṣeṣapratītikṛt /
children.translated_text:
