In the manner indicated [by this]: '<s>Hari</s> with conch and disc' — [means] <s>Viṣṇu</s>; '<s>Hari</s> without conch and disc' — [means otherwise]. '<s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>' — [means] the sons of <s>Daśaratha</s>; 'the course of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>' — [means] <s>Bhārgava</s> [<s>Paraśurāma</s>] and <s>Kārtavīrya</s> [<s>Arjuna</s>]. 'Worship <s>Sthāṇu</s> for the destruction of existence' — [means] <s>Hara</s> [<s>Śiva</s>]. 'The god knows everything' — in the second person sense. 'Angry is <s>Makaradhvaja</s>' — [means] <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love). 'Of the god, the enemy of cities' — [means] <s>Śambhu</s> [<s>Śiva</s>]. 'Intoxicated by honey, the <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo)' — [means] in spring. 'May the face of the beloved protect you' — in the sense of being present. '<s>Parameśvara</s> shines here' — [means] the king, from the place being a capital. '<s>Citrabhānu</s> shines' — in daytime [means] the sun; at night [means] fire.
'<s>Mitra</s> shines' — [when meaning] a friend, [refers to] a friend; [when meaning] <s>Mitra</s>, [refers to] the sun. In [the Vedic expression] '<s>Indraśatru</s>' and the like, the accent (<s>svara</s>) is the cause of specific cognition only in the <s>Veda</s>, not in poetry.
By the inclusion of 'and the like,'
so much of this state, so many of these days.' || 11 ||
[Sanskrit chāyā of the Prākrit verse]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 973)
'So much of anxious waiting, so much from these sleepless eyes,

children.text:
ityādāvabhinayādayaḥ /
itthaṃ saṃyogādibhirarthāntarābhidhāyakatve nivārite 'pyanekārthasya śabdasya yat kvacidarthāntarapratipādanaṃ tatra nābhidhā niyamanāttasyāḥ / na ca lakṣaṇā mukhyārthabādhādyabhāvāt / api tvañjanaṃ vyañjanameva vyāpāraḥ / yathā
children.translated_text:
In such cases, dramatic gesture (<s>abhinaya</s>) and the like [serve as determinants].
Thus, when the denotation of another meaning is restricted by association and the like for a word with multiple meanings, yet where it [still] conveys another meaning somewhere — there, it is not denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>), because of the restriction of that [denotative function]. Nor is it <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, because of the absence of the obstruction of the primary meaning and the like. Rather, it is only suggestion (<s>añjana</s> = <s>vyañjana</s>) — the operation [of the word]. As in:

children.text:
{bhadrātmano duradhirohatanorviśāla
  vaṃśonnateḥkṛtaśilīmukhavigrahasya /
  yasyānupaplutagateḥ paravāraṇasya
  dānāmbusekasubhagaḥ satataṃ karobhūt //12//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śivasvāmin</s>'s <s>Kapphinābhyudaya</s> 1.38)

'Of the noble one, of high and expansive lineage, difficult to mount [or: difficult to assault], who had made arrows his weapon [or: who had erected his bow], whose gait was unimpeded, the hand of this lord of enemy elephants [or: this great lord] was always graced by a stream of rut-water [or: a flow of gifts].' || 12 ||
A word endowed with that [suggestion] is suggestive (<s>vyañjaka</s>)...
'Endowed with that' means endowed with suggestion.
... and likewise when it [a meaning] is connected with another meaning,
the meaning too is considered suggestive therein, in a co-operative capacity. || Kpr-K_20 ||
'Likewise' means suggestive. || 20 ||

children.text: iti kāvyaprakāśe śabdārthasvarūpanirṇayo nāma dvitīya ullāsaḥ ||2||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, the second <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter), named 'The Determination of the Nature of Word-Meaning.' || 2 ||
Third <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter).
The meanings stated previously — of those...
The 'meanings' are the denoted (<s>vācya</s>), the indicated (<s>lakṣya</s>), and the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>). 'Of those' — of the denotative, the figurative, and the suggestive [words].
... the suggestiveness of meaning is to be stated.
Of what kind? He says:
From the specialties of the speaker, the addressee, the individual, the tone of voice, the sentence, and the denoted [meaning], and the proximity of another [meaning]; || Kpr-K_21 ||
from the distinction of context, place, time, and the like, for those endowed with intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>),
the operation that is the cause of the cognition of another meaning from a [given] meaning — that is precisely manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>). || Kpr-K_22 ||

children.text:
boddhavyaḥ pratipādyaḥ / kākurdhvanervikāraḥ / prastāvaḥ prakaraṇam /
arthasya vācyalakṣyavyaṅgyātmanaḥ /
krameṇodāharaṇāni /
children.translated_text:
'Addressee' means the one to be informed. 'Tone' (<s>kāku</s>) is the modification of sound. 'Context' (<s>prastāva</s>) means the occasion.
'Of the meaning' — whose nature is denoted, indicated, and suggested.
Examples in order:

children.text:
{a_ipihulaṃ jalakuṃbhaṃ ghettūṇa samāgadahmi sahi turi_aṃ /
  samase_asalilaṇīsāsaṇīsahā vīsamāmi khaṇaṃ //13//}

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā of the Prākrit verse]
[Literal Sanskrit translation of the Prākrit]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 989)
'Having taken a very large water-pot, I have come back quickly, O friend; exhausted by the sweat-water of exertion and gasping, let me rest a moment.' || 13 ||
Here, the concealment of a love-tryst is what is suggested.

children.text:
{oṇṇiddaṃ dobballaṃ cintā alasattaṇaṃ saṇīsasi_aṃ /
  maha mandabhā_iṇī_e keraṃ sahi tuha vi ahaha parihava_i //14//}

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] the drooping, the weakness, the brooding, the listlessness, accompanied by sighing —

children.text: mama mandabhāginyāḥ krṭe sakhi tvāmapyahaha paribhavati //]
children.translated_text: of me, the unfortunate one, on [my] account, O friend, even you, alas, are being disgraced.' || 14 ||
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 956)
'Drooping, weakness, brooding, listlessness, accompanied by sighing —
Here, the messenger-woman's enjoyment by her lover is suggested.

children.text:
{tathābhūtāṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpasadasi pāñcālatanayāṃ
  vane vyādhaiḥ sārdhaṃ suciramuṣitaṃ valkaladharaiḥ /
  virāṭasyāvāse sthitamanucitārambhanibhṛtaṃ
  guruḥ khedaṃ khinne mayi bhajati nādyāpi kuruṣu //15 [=220]//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>'s <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 1.11)

{Having seen <s>Pāñcālī</s> (Draupadī) in such a state in the royal assembly, having dwelt long in the forest with hunters clad in bark garments, having stayed in <s>Virāṭa</s>'s abode concealed in unsuitable occupations — the grief does not even now visit me, O teacher, who am already afflicted, but rather visits the <s>Kurus</s>. //15 [=220]//}

children.text:
atra mayi na yogyaḥ khedaḥ kuruṣu tu yogya iti kākvā prakāśyate /
na ca vācyasiddhyaṅgamatra kākuriti guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatvaṃ śaṅgyam /
praśnamātreṇāpi kākorviśrānteḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, through the <s>kāku</s> (tone of voice), it is revealed: 'The grief is not fitting for me, but is fitting for the <s>Kurus</s>.' Nor should it be suspected that this is a case of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinate suggestion) because the <s>kāku</s> here is an accessory to the expressed meaning — for the <s>kāku</s> comes to rest even through a mere question.

children.text:
{ta_i_ā maha gaṇḍatthalaṇimiaṃ diṭṭhiṃ ṇa ṇesi aṇṇatto /
  eṇhiṃ sacce_a ahaṃ te a kavālā ṇa sā diṭṭhī //16//}

children.translated_text: [Then my gaze, sunken into [your] cheek, you did not divert elsewhere;

children.text: idānīṃ saivāhaṃ tau ca kapolau na ca sā dṛṣṭiḥ //]
children.translated_text: now I am the very same, and those are the same cheeks, but that gaze is no more.]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 939)
{Then my gaze sunk into [your] cheek — you did not draw it elsewhere; now truly I am the same, and those are the same cheeks, but that gaze is no more. //16//}

children.text: atra matsakhīṃ kapolapratibimbitāṃ paśyataste dṛṣṭiranyaivābhūt calitāyāṃ tu tasyāmanyaiva jātetyaho pracchannakāmukatvaṃ te iti vyajyate /
children.translated_text: Here it is suggested: 'Your gaze, while seeing my friend reflected in [your] cheek, was one thing; but when she moved away, it became another — ah, what hidden desire you have!'

children.text:
{uddeśo 'yaṃ sarasakadalīśreṇiśobhātiśāyī
kuñjotkarṣāṅkuritaramaṇīvibhramo narmadāyāḥ /
kiṃ caitasmin suratasuhṛdastanvi te vānti vātā
yeṣāmagre sarati kalitākāṇḍakopo manobhūḥ //17//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kuntaka</s>'s <s>Vakroktijīvita</s> 1.93)

{This region, surpassing the beauty of rows of lush banana trees, with the charm of lovely women blossoming from the excellence of bowers, belongs to the <s>Narmadā</s>; and moreover, O slender one, in this [place] blow breezes — friends of love — before whom the god of love (<s>Manobhū</s>) advances with sudden, causeless agitation. //17//}
Here the suggested meaning is 'enter for the purpose of lovemaking.'

children.text:
{ṇolle_i aṇollamaṇā attā maṃ gharabharammi sa_alammi /
  khaṇamettaṃ ja_i saṃjhā_i ho_i ṇa va ho_i vīsāmo //18//}

children.translated_text: [The hard-hearted mother-in-law drives me to all the household chores;

children.text: kṣaṇamātraṃ yadi saṃdhyāyāṃ bhavati na vā bhavati viśrāmaḥ //]
children.translated_text: if for a moment at twilight there is — or perhaps there is not — any rest.]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 875)
{My mother-in-law, hard-hearted, drives me to all the household chores; if for a moment at twilight there is — or perhaps there is not — any rest. //18//}

children.text: atra saṃdhyā saṃketakāla iti taṭasthaṃ prati kayāciddyotyate /
children.translated_text: Here, 'twilight' means the time of the tryst — this is indicated by one [woman] to a bystander.

children.text:
{suvva_i samāgamissadi tujjha pi_o añjaṃ paharametteṇa /
  eme a kitti ciṭṭhasi tā sahi sañjesu karaṇijjaṃ //19//}

children.translated_text: [It is heard that your beloved will arrive today within a mere watch;

children.text: evameva kimiti tiṣṭhasi tat sakhi sajjaya karaṇīyam //]
children.translated_text: why then do you just stand like this? So, friend, prepare what needs to be done!]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 962)
{It is heard that your beloved will arrive today within a mere watch; why then do you just stand like this? So, friend, prepare what needs to be done! //19//}

children.text: atropapatiṃ pratyabhisartuṃ prastutā na yuktamiti kayācinnivāryate /
children.translated_text: Here, a woman who has set out to meet her paramour is dissuaded by someone [saying] 'it is not proper.'

children.text:
{anyatra yūyaṃ kusumāvacāyaṃ kurudhvamatrāsmi karomi sakhyaḥ /
  nāhaṃ hi dūraṃ bhramituṃ samarthā prasīdatāyaṃ racitoñjalirvaḥ //20//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{Go elsewhere, friends, and gather flowers; I shall do so here. For I am not able to wander far — please be gracious; here is my joined-palms salutation to you. //20//}

children.text: atra vivikto 'yaṃ deśa iti pracchannakāmukastvayābhisāryatāmiti āśvastāṃ prati kayācinnivedyate /
children.translated_text: Here, 'this is a secluded place — let your secret lover come here for the tryst' — this is communicated by one [woman] to another who has been reassured.

children.text:
{guru_aṇaparavasa pi_a kiṃ bhaṇāmi tu_i mandabhāiṇī aha_aṃ /
  ajja pavāsaṃ vaccasi vacca sa_aṃ jevva suṇasi karaṇijjaṃ //21//}
[gurujanaparavaśa priya kiṃ bhaṇāmi tava mandabhāginī ahakam /
children.translated_text: [O beloved, subject to the authority of elders, what shall I say to you — I, the unfortunate one?

children.text: adya pravāsaṃ vrajasi vraja svayameva śroṣyasi karaṇīyam //]
children.translated_text: Today you depart on a journey — go then; you yourself will hear what needs to be done.]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 851)
{O beloved, subject to the authority of elders, what shall I say to you — I, the unfortunate one? Today you depart on a journey — go then; you yourself will hear what needs to be done. //21//}

children.text:
atrādya madhusamaye yadi vrajasi tadāhaṃ tāvat na bhavāmi
tava tu na jānāmi gatimiti vyajyate / //
children.translated_text: Here it is suggested: 'If you depart today during the spring season, then I at least shall not survive; but your own fate I do not know.'
By the word 'and so forth' [in the initial statement], gesture (<s>ceṣṭā</s>) and the like are included. Among those, an example of gesture:

children.text:
{dvāropāntanirantare mayi tayā saundaryasāraśriyā
  prollāsyoruyugaṃ parasparasamāsaktaṃ samāsāditam /
  ānītaṃ purataḥ śiroṃśukamadhaḥ kṣipte cale locane
  vācastatra nivāritaṃ prasaraṇaṃ saṃkocite dorlate //22//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{When I stood in the gap beside the door, she — with the supreme splendor of beauty — brought into view her pair of thighs pressed close together; she drew her headcloth forward, cast down her restless eyes, and there the movement of her vine-like arms was restrained into stillness. //22//}

children.text:
atra ceṣṭayā pracchannakāntaviṣaya ākūtaviśeṣo dhvanyate /
nirākāṅkṣapratipattaye prāptāvasaratayā ca punaḥ punarudāhriyate / vaktrādīnāṃ mithaḥsaṃyoge dvikādibhedena /

children.translated_text: In this manner, the suggestive capacity of both <s>lakṣya</s> (indicated) and <s>vyaṅgya</s> (suggested) should be illustrated. //21-22//

Here, through gesture, a particular intention regarding a hidden lover is suggested. It is cited repeatedly because of the need for complete understanding and because the occasion demands it — in the mutual combination of face and the like, with the distinction of pairs and so on.
A meaning known through verbal testimony suggests another meaning; hence,
when the meaning is the suggestor, the word has a co-operative role. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_23 //
'Known through verbal testimony' — for indeed, a meaning known through another means of knowledge is not a suggestor. //23//
Thus, in the illustrious <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, the third <s>ullāsa</s>, named 'The Determination of Suggestion through Meaning,' [is completed]. //3//
Fourth <s>ullāsa</s>

children.text: yadyapi śabdārthayornirṇaye kṛte doṣaguṇāla.amkārāṇāṃ svarūpamabhidhānīyaṃ tathāpi dharmiṇi pradarśite dharmāṇāṃ heyopādeyatā jñāyata iti prathamaṃ kāvyabhedāt āha ----
children.translated_text: Although, once the examination of word and meaning is completed, the nature of faults (<s>doṣa</s>), qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), and figures of speech (<s>alaṃkāra</s>) should be described, nevertheless, since when the qualified entity (<s>dharmin</s>) is demonstrated, the properties (<s>dharma</s>) to be rejected and adopted become known, he first speaks about the classification of poetry:
That [poetry] in which the expressed meaning is not intended — in such <s>dhvani</s>, the expressed meaning may be
transferred to another meaning, or completely concealed. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_24 //

children.text:
lakṣaṇāmūlagūḍhavyaṅgyaprādhānye satyeva avivakṣitaṃ vācyaṃ yatra sa 'dhvanau'; ityanuvādāt dhvaniriti jñeyaḥ /
tatra ca vācyaṃ kvacidanupayujyamānatvādarthāntare pariṇamitam / yathā
children.translated_text: Where the predominance of <s>gūḍhavyaṅgya</s> (hidden suggestion) based on <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) obtains, and the expressed meaning is not intended — that is '<s>dhvani</s>'; from the continuation [of the word <s>dhvani</s>], it should be understood as <s>dhvani</s>. Therein, the expressed meaning is in some cases, being inapplicable, transformed into another meaning. For example:

children.text:
{tvāmasmi vacmi viduṣāṃ samavāyo 'tra tiṣṭhati /
  ātmīyāṃ matimāsthāya sthitimatra vidhehi tat //23//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 6.15)
{I am telling you — an assembly of the learned is gathered here; holding to your own judgment, establish your position here accordingly. //23//}

children.text:
atra vacanādi upadeśādirūpatayā pariṇamati /
kvacidanupapadyamānatayā atyantaṃ tiraskṛtam / yathā ----
children.translated_text: Here, 'telling' and the like are transformed into the form of 'instructing' and the like. In some cases, the expressed meaning is completely concealed because it is contradicted. For example:

children.text:
{upakṛtaṃ bahu tatra kimucyate sujanatā prathitā bhavatā param /
  vidadhadīdṛśameva sadā sakhe sukhitamāssva tataḥ śaradāṃ śatam //24//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s>)
{Much has been done by you — what more can be said? Your good character, sir, is well-renowned. Continuing to do just so always, friend, may you live happily for a hundred autumns! //24//}
This is spoken by someone to an offender through <s>viparītalakṣaṇā</s> (ironic secondary signification). //24//
And that [<s>dhvani</s>] in which the expressed meaning is intended but directed toward something else — that is the other [type].
'Directed toward something else' means culminating in the suggested meaning. And this [type] is:
one in which the sequence of suggestion is imperceptible, and another in which the sequence of suggestion is perceptible. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_25 //

children.text: alakṣyeti / na khalu vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicāriṇa eva rasaḥ / api tu rasastaiḥ ityasti kramaḥ / sa tu lāghavānna lakṣyate //25//
children.translated_text: 'Imperceptible' — for <s>rasa</s> does not [arise from] <s>vibhāva</s>, <s>anubhāva</s>, and <s>vyabhicārin</s> alone; rather, <s>rasa</s> [arises] through them — thus there is a sequence, but it is not perceived due to its swiftness. //25//
Here:
<s>Rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, the absence thereof, <s>bhāvaśānti</s> (quiescence of emotion) and the like — the imperceptible [sequence];
[this type] is distinct from <s>rasa</s> and the like [serving as] <s>alaṃkāra</s>, and is established as the thing to be ornamented (<s>alaṃkārya</s>). // <s>MKpr-K</s>_26 //

children.text:
ādigrahaṇād bhāvodayabhāvasaṃdhibhāvaśabalatvāni / pradhānatayā yatra sthito rasādistatrālaṅkāryaḥ yathodāhariṣyate / anyatra tu pradhāne vākyārthe yatrāṅgabhūto rasādistatra guṇībhūtavyaṅgye
rasavatpreyaūrjasvisamāhitādayo 'laṅkārāḥ / te ca guṇībhūtavyaṅgyābhidhāne udāhariṣyante //26//
children.translated_text: By the word 'and the like,' the arising of <s>bhāva</s>, the juncture of <s>bhāvas</s> (<s>bhāvasaṃdhi</s>), and the variegation of <s>bhāvas</s> (<s>bhāvaśabalatva</s>) are included. Where <s>rasa</s> and the like are established as predominant — there they are the thing to be ornamented (<s>alaṃkārya</s>), as will be illustrated. Elsewhere, where the predominant sentence-meaning is something else and <s>rasa</s> and the like are subordinate — there, in <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinate suggestion), <s>rasavat</s>, <s>preyas</s>, <s>ūrjasvin</s>, <s>samāhita</s>, and the like are the <s>alaṃkāras</s> (figures). These will be illustrated in the section on <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>. //26//
Now he states the nature of <s>rasa</s>:
The causes, the effects, and the co-operating factors

children.text: ratyādeḥ sthāyino loke tāni cennāṭyakāvyayoḥ // MKpr-K_27 //
children.translated_text: of the enduring mental state (<s>sthāyin</s>) such as <s>rati</s> (love) and the rest in ordinary life — these same, in drama and poetry, // <s>MKpr-K</s>_27 //
are called <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), and <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions);

children.text: vyaktaḥ sa tairvibhāvādyaiḥ sthāyī bhāvo rasaḥ smṛtaḥ // MKpr-K_28 //
children.translated_text: the enduring emotion, manifested by those <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest, is called <s>rasa</s>. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_28 //
For <s>Bharata</s> has said: '<s>Rasa</s> arises from the combination of <s>vibhāva</s>, <s>anubhāva</s>, and <s>vyabhicārin</s>.'

children.text: etadvivṛṇvate ---- {vibhāvairlalanodyānādibhirālambanoddīpanakāraṇaiḥ ratyādiko bhāvo janitaḥ anubhāvaiḥ kaṭākṣabhujākṣepaprabhṛtibhiḥ kāryaiḥ pratītiyogyaḥ kṛtaḥ vyabhicāribhirnirvedādibhiḥ sahakāribhirupacito mukhyayā vṛttyā rāmādāvanukārye tadrūpasaṃdhānānnartake 'pi pratīyamāno rasaḥ} iti bhaṭṭalollaṭaprabhṛtayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Expounding this, [some say]: 'The enduring emotion such as <s>rati</s> and the rest, generated by <s>vibhāvas</s> — excitant causes such as women and gardens, both <s>ālambana</s> (foundational) and <s>uddīpana</s> (stimulating) — made fit for apprehension through <s>anubhāvas</s> — effects such as side-glances, arm-movements, and the like — and intensified by <s>vyabhicārins</s> — co-operating factors such as <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness) and the like — being apprehended in the actor too, who imitates <s>Rāma</s> and the like, through the identification with that form by the primary function [of words] — that is <s>rasa</s>.' Thus [say] <s>Bhaṭṭa Lollaṭa</s> and others.

children.text: rāma evāyam ayameva rāma iti {na rāmo 'yam} ityauttarakālike bādhe rāmo 'yam iti rāmaḥ syādvā na vāyam iti rāmasadṛśyo 'yam iti ca samyaṅmithyāsaṃśayasādṛśyapratītibhyo vilakṣaṇayā citraturagādinyāyena rāmo 'yamiti pratipattyā grāhye naṭe
children.translated_text: [The question arises:] 'This is <s>Rāma</s> himself' or 'this very one is <s>Rāma</s>' — [but] given the subsequent sublation 'this is not <s>Rāma</s>,' through cognitions that are distinct from correct cognition ('this is <s>Rāma</s>'), erroneous cognition ('this might or might not be <s>Rāma</s>'), doubt, and similarity-cognition ('this one resembles <s>Rāma</s>') — the actor is apprehended through a cognition of the type 'this is <s>Rāma</s>,' following the principle of a painted horse (<s>citraturaganyāya</s>);

children.text:
{seyaṃ mamāṅgeṣu sudhārasacchaṭā supūrakarpūraśalākikā dṛśoḥ /
  manorathaśrīrmanasaḥ śarīriṇī prāṇeśvarī locanagocaraṃ gatā //25//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Subhāṣitaratnabhāṇḍāgāra</s> 273/6)

{She is this — a stream of nectar-essence upon my limbs, a stick of finest camphor for my eyes, the embodied fortune of my heart's desire, my life's sovereign who has come within the range of sight. //25//}

children.text:
{daivādahamadya tayā capalāyatanetrayā viyuktaśca /
  aciralavilolajaladaḥ kālaḥ samupāgataścāyam //26//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 7.29)
{By fate I am today separated from her of restless, wide eyes; and this season has arrived — with clouds that are fresh, quivering, and moving. //26//}

children.text: ityādikāvyānusaṃdhānabalācchikṣābhyāsanirvartitasvakāryaprakaṭanena ca naṭenaiva prakāśitaiḥ kāraṇakāryasahakāribhiḥ kṛtrimairapi tathānabhimanyamānairvibhāvādiśabdavyapadeśyaiḥ {saṃyogāt}, gamyagamakabhāvarūpāt anumīyamāno 'pi vastusaudaryabalādrasanīyatvenānyānumīyamānavilakṣaṇaḥ sthāyitvena saṃbhāvyamāno ratyādirbhāvastatrāsannapi sāmājikānāṃ vāsanayā carvyamāṇo rasa iti śrīśaṅkukaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the force of contemplating such poetry, and through the actor's making manifest his own effects, accomplished through training and practice — even though the causes, effects, and co-operating factors are artificial and not regarded as real — being designated by the terms <s>vibhāva</s> and the rest through their 'combination' (<s>saṃyoga</s>), which is the relation of thing-to-be-known and indicator — the enduring emotion such as <s>rati</s>, though inferred, is distinct from other inferred things by virtue of the power of the beauty of the subject-matter and is accepted as enduring — and though not present in the spectators themselves, being savored through their latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) — that is <s>rasa</s>. Thus [says] the illustrious <s>Śaṅkuka</s>.

children.text: na tāṭasthyena nātmagatatvena rasaḥ pratīyate notpadyate nābhivyajyate api tu kāvye nāṭye cābhidhāto dvitīyena vibhāvādisādhāraṇīkaraṇātmanā bhāvakatvavyāpāreṇa bhāvyamānaḥ sthāyī sattvodrekaprakāśānandamayasaṃvidviśrāntisatattvena bhogena bhujyate iti bhaṭṭanāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> is neither cognized with detachment nor as belonging to oneself; it is neither produced nor manifested — rather, in poetry and drama, the enduring emotion, being processed through a second operation of <s>bhāvakatva</s> (the power of making one experience), which consists in the universalization (<s>sādhāraṇīkaraṇa</s>) of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest beyond the expressed meaning, is enjoyed through an experience (<s>bhoga</s>) whose nature is the repose of consciousness pervaded by the luminosity and bliss arising from the predominance of <s>sattva</s>. Thus [says] <s>Bhaṭṭa Nāyaka</s>.

children.text:
loke pramadābhiḥ sthāyyanumāne 'bhyāsapāṭavavatāṃ kāvye nāṭye ca taireva kāraṇatvādiparihāreṇa vibhāvanādivyāpāravattvādalaukikavibhāvādiśabdavyavahāryairmamaivaite śatrorevaite taṭasthasyaivaite na mamaivaite
na śatrorevaite na taṭasthasyaivaite iti saṃbandhaviśeṣasvīkāraparihāraniyamānadhyavasāyāt sādhāraṇyena pratītairabhivyaktaḥ sāmājikānāṃ vāsanātmatayā sthitaḥ sthāyī ratyādiko niyatapramātṛgatatvena sthito 'pi
sādhāraṇopāyabalāt tatkālavigalitaparimitapramātṛbhāvavaśonmiṣitavedyāntarasaṃparkaśūnyāparimitabhāvena pramātrā sakalasahṛdayasaṃvādabhājā sādhāraṇyena svākāra ivābhinno 'pi gocarīkṛtaścarvyamāṇataikaprāṇovibhāvādijīvitāvadhiḥ pānakarasanyāyena carvyamāṇaḥ pura iva parisphuran hṛdayamiva praviśan sarvāṅgīṇamivāliṅgan anyat
sarvamiva tirodadhat brahmāsvādamivānubhāvayan alaukikacamatkārakārī śṛṅgārādiko rasaḥ / sa ca na kāryaḥ / vibhāvādivināṃśe 'pi tasya saṃbhavaprasaṅgāt / nāpi jñāpyaḥ siddhasya tasyāsaṃbhavāt /
api tu vibhāvādibhirvyañjitaścarvaṇīyaḥ / kārakajñāpakābhyāmanyat kva dṛṣṭamiti cet na kvaciddṛṣṭamityalaukikasiddherbhūṣaṇametanna dūṣaṇam / carvaṇāniṣpattyā tasya niṣpattirupacariteti kāryo 'pyucyatām /
laukikapratyakṣādipramāṇatāṭasthyāvabodhaśālimitayogijñānavedyāntarasaṃsparśarahitasvātmamātraparyavasitaparimitetarayogisaṃvedanavilakṣaṇalokottarasvasaṃvedanagocara iti pratyeyo 'pyabhidhīyatām / tadgrāhakaṃ ca na nirvikalpakaṃ vibhāvādiparāmarśapradhānatvāt / nāpi savikalpakaṃ carvyamāṇasyālaukikānandamayasya svasaṃvedanasiddhatvāt / ubhayābhāvasvarūpasya cobhayātmakatvamapi pūrvavallokottaratāmeva gamayati na tu
virodhamiti śrīmadācāryābhinavaguptapādāḥ //
children.translated_text: In the world, by women, the permanent [emotion is experienced]; in inference, by those expert through practice. In poetry and drama, by those very [vibhāvas and the like], through the removal of [literal] causation and the rest, possessing the function of <s>vibhāvana</s> (evoking) and the like, being denoted by the extraordinary terms <s>vibhāva</s> and the rest — 'these belong to me alone, these belong to the enemy alone, these belong to the bystander alone; these do not belong to me, these do not belong to the enemy, these do not belong to the bystander' — because there is no definitive determination of adopting or rejecting a particular relation, through universalization (<s>sādhāraṇya</s>), the permanent emotion of love (<s>rati</s>) and the rest, situated in the audience members as the essence of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), though established as belonging to a particular experiencer, through the power of the universal means, at that moment with the dissolution of the bounded experiencer-condition, manifested with an unlimited nature devoid of contact with any other object of experience — by the experiencer who shares the consensus of all sensitive spectators (<s>sahṛdaya</s>), through universalization, as if identical with one's own form though undifferentiated — is experienced, having its very life-breath in being savored (<s>carvyamāṇatā</s>), sustained through <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest until their [presence], relished like the rasa of a beverage, shining forth as before, as if entering the heart, as if embracing all limbs, as if concealing everything else, as if producing the experience of <s>Brahman</s>-bliss, causing extraordinary wonder — this is <s>rasa</s> such as <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and the rest. And it is not a product; for even in the absence of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest, its occurrence would absurdly follow. Nor is it something to be made known; for it is impossible as something already established. Rather, it is manifested (<s>vyañjita</s>) by the <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest, and is to be savored (<s>carvaṇīya</s>). 'Where else is something seen that is neither a product nor an object of knowledge?' — [The answer is:] 'It is not seen anywhere' — this being an unprecedented establishment is an ornament [of the theory], not a defect. Since its production consists in the production of savoring, let it also be called a product. Being beyond the scope of ordinary direct perception and other means of valid knowledge, devoid of contact with any other object of experience like the cognition of yogins — whose scope is limited to the self alone and differs from the delimited cognition of other yogins — being within the scope of extraordinary self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), let it also be called an object of experience. And the cognition that apprehends it is not non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>), because of the predominance of the awareness of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest. Nor is it conceptual (<s>savikalpaka</s>), because the savored [rasa], being of the nature of extraordinary bliss, is established through self-awareness. And the being of both natures, for something whose nature is the absence of both, indicates its extraordinary nature as before, not a contradiction — thus the revered master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>.

children.text:
vyāghrādayo vibhāvā bhayānakasyeva vīrādbhutaraudrāṇām aśrupātādayo 'nubhāvāḥ śṛṅgārasyeva karuṇabhayānakayoḥ
cintādayo vyabhicāriṇaḥ śṛṅgārasyaeva vīrakaruṇabhayānakānām iti pṛthaganaikāntikatvāt sūtre militā nirdiṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Tigers and the like are <s>vibhāvas</s> of the terrible (<s>bhayānaka</s>) as well as the heroic (<s>vīra</s>), marvelous (<s>adbhuta</s>), and furious (<s>raudra</s>). Shedding tears and the like are <s>anubhāvas</s> of the erotic (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) as well as the pathetic (<s>karuṇa</s>) and terrible (<s>bhayānaka</s>). Anxiety and the like are transitory emotions (<s>vyabhicārins</s>) of the erotic (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) as well as the heroic (<s>vīra</s>), pathetic (<s>karuṇa</s>), and terrible (<s>bhayānaka</s>). Because they are separately non-exclusive [to a single rasa], they are listed together in the sūtra.

children.text:
{viyadalimalināmbugarbhameghaṃ
  madhukarakokilakūjitairdiśāṃ śrīḥ /
  dharaṇirabhinavāṅkurāṅkaṭaṅkā
  praṇatipare dayite prasīda mugdhe //27//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
In such [verses as] this,

{A cloud pregnant with rain-water darkened by bees,
the beauty of the directions with the humming of bees and cuckoos,
the earth marked with the imprint of fresh sprouts —
O timid one, be gracious to your beloved who bows before you! //27//}

children.text:
{parimṛditamṛṇālīmlānamaṅgaṃ pravṛttiḥ
  kathamapi parivāraprārthanābhiḥ kriyāsu /
  kalayati ca himāṃśorniṣkalaṅkasya lakṣmīṃ
  abhinavakaridantacchedakāntaḥ kapolaḥ //28//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> 1.22)
In such [verses as] this,

children.text:
{durādutsukamāgate vivalitaṃ saṃbhāṣiṇi sphāritaṃ
  saṃśliṣyatyaruṇaṃ gṛhītavasane kiñcāñcitabhrūlatam /
  māninyāścaraṇānativyatikare bāṣpāmbupūrṇekṣaṇaṃ
  cakṣurjātamaho prapañcacaturaṃ jātāgasi preyasi //29//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 44)

children.text: yadyapi vibhāvānāmanubhāvānāmautsukyavrīḍāharṣakopāsūyāprasādānāṃ ca vyabhicāriṇāṃ kevalānāmatra sthitiḥ, tathāpyeteṣāmasādhāraṇatvamityanyatamadvayākṣepakatve sati nānaikāntikatvamiti //28//
children.translated_text: Although here there is the presence of <s>vibhāvas</s> alone, of <s>anubhāvas</s> alone, and of transitory emotions alone such as eagerness, shame, joy, anger, envy, and graciousness, nevertheless, because these are non-common [to other rasas], since they imply one or two of the other [components], there is no non-exclusiveness. //28//
And in such [verses as] this:
He states the particular [rasas]:
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>hāsya</s> (comic), <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic), <s>raudra</s> (furious), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrible),

children.text: bībhatsādbhutasaṃjñau cetyaṣṭau nāṭye rasāḥ smṛtāḥ // MKpr-K_29 //
children.translated_text: <s>bībhatsa</s> (odious), and <s>adbhuta</s> (marvelous) — these eight are the <s>rasas</s> recognized in drama. // MKpr-K_29 //

children.text:
tatra śṛṅgārasya dvau bhedau / saṃbhogo vipralambhaśca / tatrādyaḥ parasparāvalokanāliṅganādharapānaparicumbanādyanantatvādaparicchedya
eka eva gaṇyate / yathā
children.translated_text: Therein, <s>śṛṅgāra</s> has two divisions: union (<s>saṃbhoga</s>) and separation (<s>vipralambha</s>). Of these, the first — because of the infinitude of mutual gazing, embracing, lip-drinking, kissing, and the rest — is counted as just one, being undeterminable. For example:

children.text:
{śūnyaṃ vāsagṛhaṃ vilokya śayanādutthāya kiñcicchanair-
  nidrāvyājamupāgatasya suciraṃ nirvarṇya patyurmukham /
  viśrabdhaṃ paricumbya jātapulakāmālokya gaṇḍasthalīṃ
  lajjānamramukhī priyeṇa hasatā bālā ciraṃ cumbitā //30//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 77)
Likewise:

children.text:
{tvaṃ mugdhākṣi vinaiva kañculikayā dhatse manohāriṇīṃ
  lakṣmīmityabhidhāyini priyatame tadvīṭikāsaṃspṛśi /
  śayyopāntaniviṣṭasasmitasakhīnetrotsavānandito
  niryātaḥ śanakairalīkavacanopanyāsamālījanaḥ //31//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 23)

{As the beloved says 'O doe-eyed one, even without a bodice you bear
charming beauty,' and touches the betel-leaf [on her lips],
the man, delighted by the eye-festival of the smiling friend seated at the bedside,
slowly goes out, [being] a crowd devoted to the pretext of false words. //31//}
The other [type, separation,] is fivefold — caused by longing, by separation, by jealousy, by departure, and by a curse. Examples in order:

children.text:
{premārdrāḥ praṇayaspṛśaḥ paricayādudgāḍharāgodayāḥ
  tāstā mugdhadṛśo nisargamadhurāśceṣṭā bhaveyurmayi /
  yāsvantaḥkaraṇasya bāhyakaraṇavyāpārarodhī kṣaṇāt
  āśaṃsāparikalpitāsvapi bhavatyānandasāndro layaḥ //32//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> 5.7)

{Those gestures of the doe-eyed one — tender with love, touching with affection,
deep with passion arising from intimacy, naturally sweet —
in which the inner faculty momentarily blocks the activity of the outer faculties,
even in those [gestures] that are imagined with hope, there is a dense dissolution of bliss. //32//}

children.text:
{anyatra vrajatīti kā khalu kathā nāpyasya tādṛk suhṛd
  yo māṃ necchati nāgataśca hahahā ko 'yaṃ vidheḥprakramaḥ /
  ityalpetarakalpanākavalitasvāntā niśāntāntare
  bālā vṛttavivartanavyatikarā nāpnoti nidrāṃ niśi //33//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{What talk is there that he goes elsewhere? Nor does he have such a friend
who does not want me, nor has he come — alas, alas, what is this course of fate?
Thus the young woman, her mind consumed by small imaginings,
at the end of the night, tossing and turning, does not obtain sleep at night. //33//}
This illustrates separation due to the anguish of separation (<s>virahotkaṇṭhitā</s>).

children.text:
{sā patyuḥ prathamāparādhasamaye sakhyopadeśaṃ vinā
  no jānāti savibhramāṅgavalanāvakroktisaṃsūcanam /
  svacchairacchakapolamūlagalitaiḥ paryastanetrotpalā
  bālā kevalameva roditi luṭhallolālakairaśrubhiḥ //34//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 29)

children.text:
{prasthānaṃ valayaiḥ kṛtaṃ priyasakhairasrairajasraṃ gataṃ
  dhṛtyā na kṣaṇamāsitaṃ vyavasitaṃ cittena gantuṃ puraḥ /
  yātuṃ niścitacetasi priyatame sarve samaṃ prasthitā
  gantavye sati jīvita priyasuhṛtsārthaḥ kimu tyajyate //35//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 35)

children.text:
{tvāmālikhya praṇayakupitāṃ dhāturāgaiḥ śilāyā-
  mātmānaṃ te caraṇapatitaṃ yāvadicchāmi kartum /
  asraistāvanmuhurupacitairdṛṣṭirālupyate me
  krūrastasminnapi na sahate saṃgamaṃ nau kṛtāntaḥ //36//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Meghadūta</s>, <s>Uttaramegha</s> 44)

children.text:
{ākuñcya pāṇimaśucñci mama mūrdhni veśyā
  mantrābhasāṃ pratipadaṃ pṛṣataiḥ pavitre /
  tārasvaraṃ prathitathūtkamadātprahāraṃ
  hāhā hato 'hamiti roditi viṣṇuśarmā //37//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

children.text:
{hā mātastvaritāsi kutra kimidaṃ hā devatāḥ kvāśiṣaḥ
  dhik prāṇān patito 'śanirhutavahaste 'ṅgeṣu dagdhe dṛśau /
  itthaṃ ghargharamadhyaruddhakaruṇāḥ paurāṅganānāṃ gira-
  ścitrasthānapi rodayanti śatadhā kurvanti bhittīrapi //38//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Nārāyaṇabhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Jayantabhaṭṭollekha</s>)

{'Ah mother, where are you hastening? What is this? Ah gods, where are your blessings?
Curse these lives — a thunderbolt has fallen, fire upon those limbs, my eyes are burnt!'
Thus, the voices of the townswomen, their compassion choked midway in their throats,
make even those [painted] on walls weep and split the walls themselves a hundredfold! //38//}

children.text:
{kṛtamanumataṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vā yairidaṃ gurupātakaṃ
  manujapaśubhirnirmaryādairbhavadbhirudāyudhaiḥ /
  narakaripuṇā sārdha teṣāṃ sabhīmakirīṭinā-
  mayamaha[ma]sṛṅmedomāṃsaiḥ karomi diśāṃ balim //39//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>'s <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 3.24)

{'Those human beasts, boundaryless and armed,
by whom this great sin was done, approved, or witnessed —
together with <s>Narakāri</s> [Kṛṣṇa], and with <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> among them,
I shall offer oblation to the quarters with their blood, marrow, and flesh!' //39//}

children.text:
{kṣudrā saṃtrāsamete vijahita harayaḥ kṣuṇṇaśakrebhakumbhā
  yuṣmaddeheṣu lajjāṃ dadhati paramamī sāyakā niṣpatantaḥ /
  saumitre tiṣṭha pātraṃ tvamasi na hi ruṣāṃ nanvahaṃ meghanādaḥ
  kiñcidbhrūbhaṅgalīlāniyamitajaladhiṃ rāmamanveṣayāmi //40//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Harṣa</s>'s <s>Nāgānanda</s> 11.2)

{'O petty ones, be frightened! Abandon your weapons, [you] whose elephant-fronted Indra-vessels are crushed!
These arrows flying forth feel ashamed of your bodies!
O <s>Saumitra</s> [Lakṣmaṇa], stop — you are not the [worthy] target. Am I not <s>Meghanāda</s> [Indrajit]?
I seek <s>Rāma</s>, who restrained the ocean with a mere play of his brow!' //40//}

children.text:
{grīvābhaṅgābhirāmaṃ muhuranupatati syandane baddhadṛṣṭiḥ
  paścārdhena praviṣṭaḥ śarapatanabhayādbhūyasā pūrvakāyam /
  darbhairardhāvalīḍhaiḥ śramavivṛtamukhabhraṃśibhiḥ kīrṇavartmā
  paśyodagraplutatvādviyati bahutaraṃ stokamurvyāṃ prayāti //41//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Abhijñānaśakuntala</s> 1.7)

children.text:
{utkṛtyotkṛtya kṛttiṃ prathamamatha pṛthūtsedhabhūyāṃsi māṃsā-
  nyaṃsasphikpṛṣṭhapiṇḍyādyavayavasulabhānyugrapūtīni jagdhvā /
  ārttaḥ paryastanetraḥ prakaṭitadaśanaḥ pretaraṅkaḥ karaṅkā-
  daṅkasthādasthisaṃsthaṃ sthapuṭagatamapi kravyamavyagramatti //42//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> 5.16)

{Tearing off the hide piece by piece, first, then eating the thick, tall pieces of flesh
from the shoulder, buttock, back, and calf — easily obtained, terribly putrid —
the tormented <s>pretaraṅka</s> (ghoul), with eyes rolled back and teeth bared,
eagerly eats even the morsel lodged in the skull, stuck to the bones in the hollow of the skull! //42//}

children.text:
{citraṃ mahāneṣa batāvatāraḥ kva kāntireṣābhinavaiva bhaṅgiḥ /
  lokottaraṃ dhairyamaho prabhāvaḥ kāpyākṛtirnūtana eṣa sargaḥ //43//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 29)

{'Wonderful! This is a great descent indeed! Where is this beauty, this utterly new style!
Extraordinary is this majesty, oh the power! Some wondrous form, this is a new creation!' //43//}
He states their permanent emotions (<s>sthāyibhāvas</s>):
<s>Rati</s> (love), <s>hāsa</s> (laughter), <s>śoka</s> (sorrow), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm), <s>bhaya</s> (fear),
<s>jugupsā</s> (disgust), and <s>vismaya</s> (wonder) — these are declared the permanent emotions (<s>sthāyibhāvas</s>). // MKpr-K_30 //
This is clear. //30//
He states the transitory emotions (<s>vyabhicārins</s>):
<s>Nirveda</s> (despondency), <s>glāni</s> (debility), <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), then <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), <s>śrama</s> (fatigue),

children.text: ālasyaṃ caiva dainyaṃ ca cintā mohaḥ smṛtirdhṛtiḥ // MKpr-K_31 //
children.translated_text: <s>ālasya</s> (indolence) and <s>dainya</s> (dejection), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection), <s>dhṛti</s> (fortitude), // MKpr-K_31 //

children.text: vrīḍā capalatā harṣa āvego jaḍatā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>vrīḍā</s> (shame), <s>capalatā</s> (fickleness), <s>harṣa</s> (joy), <s>āvega</s> (agitation), <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupor),

children.text: garvo viṣāda autsukyaṃ nidrāpasmāra eva ca // MKpr-K_32 //
children.translated_text: <s>garva</s> (arrogance), <s>viṣāda</s> (despair), <s>autsukyā</s> (eagerness), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), and <s>apasmāra</s> (epilepsy); // MKpr-K_32 //
<s>supta</s> (dreaming), <s>prabodha</s> (awakening), <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation), and <s>avahittha</s> (dissimulation), then <s>ugratā</s> (ferocity),
<s>mati</s> (discernment), <s>vyādhi</s> (sickness), then <s>unmāda</s> (insanity), and <s>maraṇa</s> (death) as well; // MKpr-K_33 //
and <s>trāsa</s> (fright) and <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation) — these are to be known as the transitory emotions (<s>vyabhicārins</s>);
these thirty-three <s>bhāvas</s> have been enumerated by name. // MKpr-K_34 //

Although <s>nirveda</s> (despondency), being mostly inauspicious, is initially not to be accepted [as a sthāyin], its adoption [here] as a transitory emotion is [precisely] for the purpose of declaring [it also as] a permanent emotion (<s>sthāyin</s>). Therefore:
<s>Nirveda</s> is a permanent emotion; <s>śānta</s> (tranquil) too is a ninth <s>rasa</s>.
For example:

children.text:
{ahau vā hāre vā kusumaśayane vā dṛṣadi vā
  maṇau vā loṣṭe vā balavati ripau vā suhṛdi vā /
  tṛṇe vā straiṇe vā mama samadṛśo yānti divasāḥ
  kvacitpuṇyāraṇye śiva śiva śiveti pralapataḥ //44//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Utpalarāja</s>, <s>Utpalarājīya</s>)

{Whether on a serpent or a necklace, on a flower-bed or a stone,
on a jewel or a clod of earth, before a powerful enemy or a friend —
on grass or on a woman — my days pass with equal regard,
somewhere in a meritorious forest, [me] babbling 'Śiva, Śiva, Śiva!' //44//}
Love (<s>rati</s>) directed toward deities and the like is a transitory emotion; likewise adorned [by the tranquil rasa]. // MKpr-K_35 //
The <s>bhāva</s> has been described...

children.text:
ādiśabdānmunigurunṛpaputrādiviṣayā / kāntāviṣayā tu vyaktā śṛṅgāraḥ /
udāharaṇam
children.translated_text: By the word 'and the like,' [love directed] toward sages, teachers, princes, and the like [is meant]. But [love] directed toward a beloved woman, when manifested, is <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. Example:

children.text:
{kaṇṭhakoṇaviniviṣṭamīśa te kālakūṭamapi me mahāmṛtam /
  apyupāttamamṛtaṃ bhavadvapurbhedavṛtti yadi me na rocate //45//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Utpalarāja</s>, <s>Utpalarājīya</s>)

{O Lord, the <s>kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison) lodged in the corner of your throat is great ambrosia to me;
but the ambrosia taken [by you] — if your body acts differently [toward me] — does not please me! //45//}

children.text:
{haratyaghaṃ saṃprati hetureṣyataḥ śubhasya pūrvācaritaiḥ kṛtaṃ śubhaiḥ /
  śarīrabhājāṃ bhavadīyadarśanaṃ vyanakti kālatritaye 'pi yogyatām //46//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Māgha</s>'s <s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 1.26)
Other [examples] too should be cited thus. An example of an adorned transitory emotion is:

children.text:
{jāne kopaparāṅmukhī priyatamā svapnedya dṛṣṭā mayā
  mā māṃ saṃspṛśa pāṇineti rudatī gantuṃ pravṛttā puraḥ /
  no yāvatparirabhya cāṭuśatakairāśvāsayāmi priyāṃ
  bhrātastāvadahaṃ śaṭhena vidhinā nidrādaridrīkṛtaḥ //47//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'I know — my beloved, turned away in anger, was seen by me today in a dream: "Do not touch me with your hand!" she said weeping, and began to walk away. Before I could embrace her and console my beloved with a hundred flattering words, O brother, I was impoverished of sleep by that wicked fate!' //47//
Here there is resentment toward fate.
... Their semblances (<s>ābhāsa</s>) are those prompted by impropriety (<s>anaucitya</s>).

children.text: tadābhāsā rasābhāsā bhāvābhāsāśca / tatra rasābhāso yathā
children.translated_text: Their semblances are <s>rasābhāsa</s> (semblances of aesthetic sentiment) and <s>bhāvābhāsa</s> (semblances of transient emotions). Among these, an example of <s>rasābhāsa</s>:

children.text:
{stumaḥ kaṃ vāmākṣi kṣaṇamapi vinā yaṃ na ramase
  vilebhe kaḥ prāṇān raṇamakhamukhe yaṃ mṛgayase /
  sulagne ko jātaḥ śaśimukhi yamāliṅgasi balāt
  tapaḥśrīḥ kasyaiṣā madananagari dhyāyasi tu yam //48//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 33)

'Whom shall we praise, O side-glancing one, without whom you do not delight even for a moment? Who obtained his life, O one whom you seek on the battlefield? Who was born at an auspicious time, O moon-faced one, whom you embrace by force? Whose is this glory of austerity, O city of the Love-god, the one upon whom you meditate?' //48//

children.text: atrānekakāmukaviṣayamabhilāpaṃ tasyāḥ stuma ityādyanugataṃ bahuvyāpāropādānaṃ vyanakti / bhāvābhāso yathā
children.translated_text: Here, the phrase 'whom shall we praise' and so forth, being applied to her address directed at many lovers, reveals the adoption of many occupations. An example of <s>bhāvābhāsa</s>:

children.text:
{rākāsudhākaramukhī taralāyatākṣī
  sā smerayauvanataraṅgitavibhramāṅgī /
  tat kiṃ karomi vidadhe kathamatra maitrīṃ
  tatsvīkṛtivyatikare ka ivābhyupāyaḥ //49//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 34)

'She whose face is like the full moon, whose eyes are wide and tremulous, whose limbs ripple with the waves of smiling youth — what then shall I do? How shall I form friendship here? What expedient could there be in the venture of accepting her?' //49//
Here, the anxiety is prompted by impropriety. Others too should be illustrated in the same way.

children.text: bhāvasya śāntirudayaḥ sandhiḥ śabalatā tathā // MKpr-K_36 //
children.translated_text: The repose of a <s>bhāva</s> (transient emotion), its arising, its junction, and its variegation (<s>śabalatā</s>) — // MKpr-K_36 //
An illustration of each in order:

children.text:
{tasyāḥ sāndravilepanastanataṭapraśleṣamudrāṅkitaṃ
  kiṃ vakṣaścaraṇānativyatikaravyājena gopāyyate /
  ityukte kva tadityudīrya sahasā tat saṃpramārṣṭuṃ mayā
  sāśliṣṭā(cx: saṃśliṣṭā) rabhasena tatsukhavaśāttanvyā ca tadvismṛtam //50//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 26)

'Why do you conceal your chest, marked with the seal-impressions of her breasts smeared with thick ointment, under the pretense of crossing your feet? When it was said, "Where is that?" and [the lady] quickly tried to wipe it off, she was embraced by me impetuously, and by the power of that pleasure, the slender one forgot all about it.' //50//
Here [we see] the repose of anger.

children.text:
{ekasmiñ śayane vipakṣaramaṇīnāmagrahe mugdhayā
  sadyo mānaparigrahaglapitayā cāṭūni kurvannapi /
  āvegādavadhīritaḥ priyatamastūṣṇīṃ sthitastatkṣaṇaṃ
  mā bhūtsupta ivetyamandavalitagrīvaṃ punarvīkṣitaḥ //51//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 22)

'When a naive woman, even while her beloved was making flattering words, having grown weary from assuming the posture of jealous pride on the same bed [as her rival's] — without mention of the rival's name — rejected her lover impetuously, he stood silent; then at that moment, thinking "perhaps he has fallen asleep," she glanced at him again with her neck gently turned.' //51//
Here [we see] the arising of curiosity (<s>autsukhya</s>).

children.text:
{utsiktasya tapaḥparākramanidherabhyāgamādekataḥ
  satsaṃgapriyatā ca vīrarabhasotphālaśca māṃ karṣataḥ /
  vaidaihīparirambha eṣa ca muhurścaitanyamāmīlayan
  ānandī haricandanenduśiśirasnigdho ruṇaddhyanyataḥ //52//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mahāvīracarita</s> 2.16)

'On the one hand, the arrival of [<s>Rāma</s>], whose ascetic valor is as fierce as a treasure-trove, and the love of the company of the good, and the leap of heroic passion — these pull me; on the other hand, this embrace of <s>Vaidehī</s>, cool as the moon and sandalwood, moist and blissful, repeatedly closing the eyes in consciousness — this blocks me.' //52//
Here [we see] the junction of agitation (<s>āvega</s>) and joy (<s>harṣa</s>).

children.text:
{kvākāryaṃ śaśalakṣaṇaḥ kva ca kulaṃ bhūyo 'pi dṛśyeta sā
  doṣāṇāṃ praśamāya na śrutamaho kope 'pi kāntaṃ mukham /
  kiṃ vakṣyantyapakalmaṣāḥ kṛtadhiyaḥ svapne 'pi sā durlabhā
  cetaḥ svāsthyamupaihi kaḥ khalu yuvā dhanyo 'dharaṃ dhāsyati //53//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 4.4)

'Where the moon-marked [hare]? And where this family? May she be seen again! For the quelling of faults, nothing has been heard! Ah, even in anger, her face is lovely! What will the blameless and wise say? Even in a dream she is unattainable! O heart, be at peace! What fortunate youth will taste her lip?' //53//
Here [we see] the variegation (<s>śabalatā</s>) of deliberation, curiosity, excessive remembrance, apprehension, wretchedness, fortitude, and anxiety.
But the stable state of a <s>bhāva</s> has [already] been stated and illustrated. //36//
Even in the principal <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), they sometimes attain the status of subsidiary [elements].
They — repose of <s>bhāva</s> and the rest — attain subsidiary status, like a servant engaged in the marriage proceedings following the king.
That which has the state of being suggested through resonance, semblance, and imperceptible succession — // MKpr-K_37 //
<s>Dhvani</s> (suggestion) is threefold, declared as arising from the power of word, meaning, or both.
and that whose suggested meaning has the form of resonance, rooted in the power of both — thus it is threefold. //37//
That whose suggested meaning has the form of resonance, rooted in the power of the word; that whose suggested meaning has the form of resonance, rooted in the power of meaning;
Among these:
When an ornament (<s>alaṃkāra</s>) or a mere content (<s>vastu</s>) is manifested by a word — // MKpr-K_38 //
primarily, that should be known as arising from the power of the word, and it is twofold.
'Content' means mere content, without ornament. An example of the first:

children.text:
{ullāsya kālakaravālamahāmbuvāhaṃ
  devena yena jaraṭhorjitagarjitena /
  nirvāpitaḥ sakala eva raṇe ripūṇāṃ
  dhārājalaistrijagati jvalitaḥ pratāpaḥ //54//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śivasvāmin</s>'s <s>Kapphiṇābhyudaya</s> 1.24)

'The one who, having raised up the great cloud as dark as time's black serpent, with its roar fiercer than aged [thunder], extinguished in battle the blazing glory of all enemies with streams of water throughout the three worlds.' //54//

children.text: atra vākyasyāsaṃbaddhārthābhidhāyakatvaṃ mā prasāṅkṣīditi prākaraṇikāprākaraṇikayorupamānopameyabhāvaḥ kalpanīya ityatropamālaṅkāro vyaṅgyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, lest the sentence be understood as conveying an unconnected meaning, the relation of standard and subject of comparison between the contextual and non-contextual [subjects] must be construed — thus the ornament of <s>upamā</s> (simile) is the suggested meaning.
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'O lord, of fierce and beautiful valor, who brings the moon to distress, of sweet grace, wise, of conduct not confined to truth, the foremost partisan at every step — you shine!' //55//
Here, the dual meaning of each word [creates] the semblance of contradiction (<s>virodhābhāsa</s>).

children.text:
{amitaḥ samitaḥ prāptairutkarṣairharṣada prabho /
  ahitaḥ sahitaḥ sādhuyaśobhirasatāmasi //56//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'O joy-giver, O lord, unlimited yet measured, arrived yet with distinctions of excellence, an enemy yet allied — you are the crest-jewel of fame and the glory of the good among the wicked!' //56//
Here too [there is] the semblance of contradiction.
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'He who fashions a wondrous world upon no wall, with materials requiring no material cause — obeisance to that trident-bearer, praiseworthy for his arts!' //57//

children.text:
atra vyatirekaḥ /
alaṅkāryasyāpi brāhmaṇaśramaṇanyāyenālaṅkāratā / vastumātraṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Here [there is] <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast). Even the object of ornament can function as an ornament itself, by the principle of the Brahmin and the ascetic. An example of mere content (<s>vastumātra</s>):

children.text:
{panthi_a ṇa ettha sattharamaitthi maṇaṃ pattharatthale gāme /
  uṇṇa_apa_oharaṃ pekhkhiūṇa ja_i vasasi tā vasasu //58//}

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'O traveler, there is no bed here at all in this village on the stone surface;

children.text: unnatapayodharaṃ praks.ya yadi vasasi tadā vasa //]
children.translated_text: having seen the high breasts, if you stay, then stay.'
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 879)
'O traveler, there is no bed here in this village situated on rocky ground; having seen [her] high breasts, if you [still wish to] stay, then stay!' //58//
Here it is suggested that 'if you are capable of enjoyment, then stay.'

children.text:
{śaniraśaniśca tamuccairnihanti kupyasi narendra yasmai tvam /
  yatra prasīdasi punaḥ sa bhātyudāronudāraśca //59//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'Lightning and thunderbolt — he strikes that one down mightily; you are angry, O king, at the one; the one upon whom you are pleased, he shines, both exalted and generous!' //59//

children.text: aviruddhāvapi tvadanuvartanārthamekaṃ kārya kuruta iti dhvanyate /
children.translated_text: It is suggested that 'though they are not [actually] opposed, for the purpose of conforming to you, [they] perform a single task.'
That whose meaning arises from the power of meaning is also a revealer, either naturally occurring, // MKpr-K_39 //
or established merely from the poet's bold expression, or [arising from a character] constructed by the poet;

children.text: vastu vālaṅkṛtirvety ṣaḍbhedo 'sau vyanakti yat // MKpr-K_40 //
children.translated_text: whether it [reveals] content or ornament — thus it is sixfold in what it suggests. // MKpr-K_40 //
[And what is suggested is] either content or ornament — thus this [type] has twelve varieties.

children.text: svataḥsaṃbhavī na kevalaṃ bhaṇitamātraniṣpanno yāvadbahirapyaucityena saṃbhāvyamānaḥ / kavinā pratibhāmātreṇa bahirasannapi nirmitaḥ kavinibaddhena vaktreti vā dvividhopara iti trividhaḥ / vastu vālaṅkāro vāsāviti ṣoḍhā vyañjakaḥ / tasya vastu vālaṅkāro vā vyaṅgya iti dvādaśabhedo 'rthaśaktyudbhavo dhvaniḥ / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: The 'naturally occurring' [revealer] is not merely one accomplished by statement alone, but is one that is conceivable externally as well, through propriety. [That] constructed by the poet through imagination alone, though not existing externally; or [through speech] bound by the poet, [uttered] by a speaker — thus the latter is twofold, making three kinds. This [revealer] suggests either content or ornament — thus it is sixfold as a revealer. And what is suggested by it is either content or ornament — thus <s>dhvani</s> arising from the power of meaning has twelve varieties. Examples in order —

children.text:
{alasaśiromaṇi dhuttāṇaṃ aggimo putti dhaṇasamiddhima_o /
  i_a bhaṇi_eṇa ṇa_aṅgī papphullavilo_aṇā jā_ā //60//}

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'The crest-jewel of the idle, the foremost among rogues, O daughter, overflowing with wealth —
thus having been told, the girl with bent limbs became one with blossoming eyes.'
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 970)
'O daughter, the foremost among idlers, the crest-jewel of rogues, overflowing with wealth — [thus] having been told, the girl with bent limbs became one with blossoming eyes.' //60//

children.text: atra mamaivopabhogya iti vastunā vastu vyajyate /
children.translated_text: Here, through [one] content, another content is suggested: 'he is fit for my enjoyment alone.'

children.text:
{dhanyāsi yā kathayasi priyasaṃgame 'pi
  viśrabdhacāṭukaśatāni ratāntareṣu /
  nīvīṃ prati praṇihite tu kare priyeṇa
  sakhyaḥ śapāmi yadi kiñcidapi smarāmi //61//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s>)

'You are blessed who speak with confidence hundreds of endearments even during the union with your beloved, during the intervals of love-making; but when the hand of the beloved is directed toward the girdle-knot — O friends, I swear, I do not remember a single thing!' //61//

children.text: atra tvamadhanyā ahaṃ tu dhanyeti vyatirekālaṅkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here [the figure of] <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) — 'you are not blessed; I, however, am blessed' — is [the ornament suggested].

children.text:
{darpāndhagandhagajakumbhakapāṭakūṭa-
  saṃkrāntinighnaghanaśoṇitaśoṇaśociḥ /
  vīrairvyaloki yudhi kopakaṣāyakāntiḥ
  kālīkaṭākṣa iva yasya kare kṛpāṇaḥ //62//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śivasvāmin</s>'s <s>Kapphiṇābhyudaya</s> 1.37)

'Crimson with the dense blood flowing from the cleaving of the temple-lobes of the elephants blinded by the frenzy of their rut, blazing with the passion-red splendor of anger, seen by heroes in battle — the sword in his hand was like the sidelong glance of <s>Kālī</s>.' //62//

children.text: atropamālaṅkāreṇa sakalaripubalakṣayaḥ kṣaṇāt kariṣyate iti vastu /
children.translated_text: Here, through the ornament of <s>upamā</s> (simile), the content is [suggested]: 'he will destroy the entire enemy force in an instant.'
(<s>Viśvanātha</s>'s <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 4.9)
'He who, from the straits of the pain of the deep bite-marks of his beloved, liberated the coral-petal lips of the enemy-women — biting his own lip in battle with fury.' //63//

children.text:
atra virodhālaṅkāreṇādharanirdaśanasamakālameva śatravo vyāpāditā iti tulyayogitā mama kṣatyāpyanyasya kṣatirnivartatāmiti tadbuddhirutprekṣyate ityutprekṣā ca /
eṣūdāharaṇeṣu svataḥsaṃbhavī vyañjakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, through the ornament of <s>virodha</s> (contradiction), at the very same time as the biting of his own lip, the enemies were slain — thus <s>tulyayogitā</s> (co-application); and the imagination that 'even though I am hurt, may the hurt of others cease' — thus <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) is also [suggested]. In these examples, the revealer is naturally occurring.

children.text:
{kailāsasya prathamaśikhare veṇusaṃmūrchanābhiḥ
  śrutvā kīrtiṃ vibudharamaṇīgīyamānāṃ yadīyām /
  srastāpāṅgāḥ sarasabisinīkāṇḍasaṃjātaśaṅkāḥ
  diṅmātaṅgāḥ śravaṇapuline hastamāvartayanti //64//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'On the first peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, hearing his fame sung by the divine nymphs to the tunes of bamboo flutes, the elephants of the directions, with drooping eyes, suspecting [the sound to be that of] moist lotus stalks, roll their trunks on the sandy banks of their ears.' //64//

children.text: atra vastunā yeṣāmapyarthādhigamo nāsti teṣāmapyevamādibuddhijananena camatkāraṃ karoti tvatkīrtiriti vastu dhvanyate /
children.translated_text: Here, through [one] content, [another] content is suggested: 'your fame produces wonder even in those who have no comprehension of meaning, by generating such understanding in them.'

children.text:
{kesesu balāmoḍi_a teṇa a samarammi ja_asirī gahi_ā /
  jaha kandarāṃhi vihurā tassa daḍhaṃ kaṇṭha_ammi saṃṭhavi_ā //65//}

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'By force, in battle, seizing her by the hair, the goddess of victory was captured;
just as, distressed in the caves, she was firmly placed upon his neck.'
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 971)
'By force, seizing her by the hair, he captured the goddess of victory in battle; just as, distressed in the caves, she was firmly placed upon his neck.' //65//

children.text: atra keśagrahaṇāvalokanoddīpitamadanā iva kandarāstadvidhurān kaṇṭhe gṛhṇanti ityutprekṣā / ekatra saṃgrāme vijayadarśanāttasyārayaḥ palāyya guhāsu tiṣṭhantīti kāvyaheturalaṅkāraḥ / na palāyya gatāstadvairiṇo 'pi tu tataḥ parābhavaṃ saṃbhāvya tān kandarā na tyajantītyapahnutiśca /
children.translated_text: Here [there is] <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy): 'the women in the caves, their passion inflamed by the sight of hair-pulling, embrace his neck as if distressed.' In one instance, from the sight of victory in battle, his enemies fled and remain in caves — thus the ornament of <s>kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason). [Or:] his enemies too did not flee, but considering the defeat from that, the caves do not release them — thus <s>apahṇuti</s> (concealment) also.

children.text:
{gāḍhāliṅgaṇarahasujja-ammi da-i-e lahu samosara-i /
  māṇaṃsiṇīṇa māṇo pīlaṇabhī-a vva hi-a-āhiṃ //66//}

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'When the beloved rises impetuously in the excitement of a tight embrace,
the pride of the proud woman quickly subsides, as if frightened of being crushed, from the heart.'
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 934)
'When the beloved rises impetuously in the excitement of a tight embrace, the pride of the proud woman quickly subsides, as if frightened of being crushed, from the heart.' //66//

children.text: atrotprekṣayā pratyāliṅganādi tatra vijṛmbhate iti vastu /
children.translated_text: Here, through <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), the content is [suggested]: 'reciprocal embrace and the like blossom forth therein.'

children.text:
{jā ṭheraṃvva hasantī ka-iva-aṇaṃburuhavaddhaviṇivesā /
  dāve-i bhu-aṇamaṇḍalamaṇṇaṃ vi-a ja-a-i sā vāṇī //67//}

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'She who, laughing as if at an elder, established in the lotus of the poet's face,
reveals the circle of the world as if it were another — that Speech (<s>Vāṇī</s>) is victorious!'
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 982)
'She who, laughing as if at an elder, established in the lotus of the poet's face, reveals the circle of the world as if it were another — that Speech (<s>Vāṇī</s>) is victorious!' //67//

children.text: atrotprekṣayā camatkāraikakāraṇaṃ navaṃ navaṃ jagat ajaḍāsanasthā nirmimīte iti vyatirekaḥ / eṣu kaviprauḍhoktimātraniṣpanno vyañjakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, through <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), the sole cause of aesthetic wonder is [suggested]: [<s>Vāṇī</s>], seated in the undeluded [poet], creates ever new worlds — thus <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast). In these [examples], the revealer is one established merely from the poet's bold expression.

children.text:
{je laṅkāgirimehalāse khali-ā saṃbhogakhiṇṇora-i-
  phārupphullaphaṇāvalīkavalaṇe pattā dariddattaṇaṃ /
  te ehṇiṃ mala-ānilā virahiṇīṇīsāsasaṃpakkiṇo
  jādā jhatti sisuttaṇe vi bahalā tāruṇṇapuṇṇā vi-a //68//}

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Those that stumbled on the girdle-slopes of <s>Laṅkā</s>'s mountain, [those winds] that had reached poverty
in swallowing the expanded hoods of serpents exhausted from love-making —
those <s>Malaya</s> breezes, now mingled with the sighs of love-sick women,
have suddenly, even in their infancy, become dense, as if full of youth.'
(<s>Rājaśekhara</s>'s <s>Karpūramañjarī</s> 1.19)

'Those <s>Malaya</s> breezes that stumbled on the girdle-slopes of <s>Laṅkā</s>'s mountain, and that, in swallowing the hoods of serpents exhausted from love-making, which bloomed and expanded, had fallen into poverty — they now, mingled with the sighs of love-sick women, have suddenly, even in their infancy, become dense, as if full of youth!' //68//

children.text: atra niḥśvāsaiḥ prāptaiśvaryā vāyavaḥ kiṃ kiṃ na kurvantīti vastunā vastu vyajyate /
children.translated_text: Here, through [one] content, [another] content is suggested: 'the winds, having gained prosperity through [the women's] sighs, what will they not do?'

children.text:
{sahi vira-i-ūṇa māṇassa majjha dhīrattaṇeṇa āsāsaṃ /
  pi-adaṃsaṇavihaṅkhalelakkhaṇammi sahasatti teṇa osari-aṃ //69//}

children.translated_text: [O friend, having fashioned a consolation for my pride through fortitude,
at the sign that was the unfettered sight of the beloved, he suddenly withdrew.]
(<s>Hāla's</s> <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 936)
{O friend, having devised for my pride a consolation through fortitude, he suddenly withdrew, at the sign that was the unfettered viewing of the beloved. ||69||}

children.text: atra vastunākṛte 'pi prārthane prasanneti vibhāvanā priyadarśanasya saubhāgyabalaṃ dhairyeṇa soḍhuṃ na śakyate ityutprekṣā vā /
children.translated_text: Here, although no entreaty was made in words, she became pleased — this is <s>vibhāvanā</s> (poetic fancy). Or, [it suggests that] the charm of seeing the beloved cannot be endured through fortitude — this is <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic imagination).

children.text:
{ollollakara-ara-akhkha-ehi tuha lo-aṇesu maha diṇṇaṃ /
  rattaṃsu-aṃ pasā-o koveṇa puṇo ime ṇa akkami-ā //70//}

children.translated_text: [With your eyes scratched by moist, moist, fresh nail-marks, given by me,
the red cloth is a favor — but in anger, these [eyes] have not been assailed again.]
(<s>Hāla's</s> <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 971)
{With your eyes that are moist, moist, scratched by nails still fresh —

children.text: atra kimiti locane kupite vahasi iti uttarālaṅkāreṇa na kevalamārdranakhakṣatāni gopāyasi yāvatteṣāmahaṃ prasādapātraṃ jāteti vastu /
children.translated_text: Here, by the subsequent ornament [addressing] 'Why do you bear angry eyes?' — the meaning (<s>vastu</s>) is: you are not merely concealing the fresh nail-marks, but I have become an object of [your] favor on account of them.

children.text:
{mahilāsahassabhari-e tuha hi-a-e suha-a sā amā-antī /
  aṇudiṇamaṇaṇṇakammā aṅgaṃ taṇu-aṃ vi taṇu-e-i //71//}

children.translated_text: [O handsome one, she who dwells in your heart filled with a thousand women,
with no other occupation day after day, makes even her slender body still more slender.]
(<s>Hāla's</s> <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 2.82)
{O handsome one, she who dwells in your heart, which is filled with a thousand women —

children.text: atra hetvalaṅkāreṇa tanostanūkaraṇepi tava hṛdaye na vartate iti viśeṣoktiḥ / eṣu kavinibaddhavaktṛprauḍhoktimātraniṣpannaśarīro vyañjakaḥ / evaṃ dvādaśa bhedāḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, through the figure of <s>hetu</s> (reason), the <s>viśeṣokti</s> (distinctive statement) is: even while making her body thinner, she does not dwell in your heart. In these [examples], the suggestive element has its body constituted solely by the bold expression of the speaker as fashioned by the poet. Thus there are twelve varieties.
Based on word, meaning, and both — one [more variety]...

children.text:
{atandracandrābharaṇā samuddīpitamanmathā /
  tārakātaralā śyāmā sānandaṃ na karoti kam //72//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{Wearing the moon as an ornament without weariness, with <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) fully kindled, with trembling stars, the dark [night] — who does she not fill with delight? ||72||}
Here, <s>upamā</s> (simile) is the suggested meaning.
... the varieties of this [<s>dhvani</s>] are eighteen. || MKpr-K_41 ||
'Of this' means of <s>dhvani</s>. ||41||
Now, since <s>rasa</s> and the rest have many subdivisions, how can there be [only] eighteen? To this he says:
Because of the infinity of <s>rasa</s> and the rest, each is counted as one division.

children.text:
anantatvāditi / tathāhi ---- nava rasāḥ / tatra śṛṅgārasya dvau bhedau / saṃbhogo vipralambhaśca / saṃbhogasyāpi parasparāvalokanāliṅganaparicumbanādikusumoccayajalakelisūryāstamayacandrodayaṣaḍṛtuvarṇanādayo bahavo bhedāḥ / vipralambhasyābhilāṣādaya uktāḥ / tayorapi vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicārivaicitryam / tatrāpi nāyakayoruttamamadhyamādhamaprakṛtitvam / tatrāpi deśakālāvasthādibhedā ityekasyaiva rasasyānantyam /
kā gaṇanā tvanyeṣāṃ / kramatvaṃ tu sāmānyamāśritya rasādidhvanibheda eka eva gaṇyate //
children.translated_text: 'Because of infinity' — that is to say: there are nine <s>rasas</s>. Of these, <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) has two divisions: <s>saṃbhoga</s> (union) and <s>vipralambha</s> (separation). <s>Saṃbhoga</s> too has many subdivisions: mutual gazing, embracing, kissing, flower-gathering, water-sports, descriptions of sunset, moonrise, the six seasons, and so on. Of <s>vipralambha</s>, <s>abhilāṣa</s> (longing) and the rest have been stated. Both of those have further variety through the diversity of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), and <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions). Within those too, the hero and heroine may be of superior, middling, or inferior disposition. Within those too, there are distinctions of place, time, condition, and so on. Thus, even a single <s>rasa</s> is infinite — what to speak of counting the others? The sequential ordering, however, relies on the general [category], and so <s>rasa</s> and other types of <s>dhvani</s> are each counted as one division.
In a sentence, arising from two [sources]...
'Arising from two' means rooted in the power of both word and meaning.
... and in a word as well, according to others...

'Of him whose pair of eyes is blocked by the hand that is a tender shoot, [itself] employed [to serve as] a garment in the sport of love,

children.text:
atha jayatīti na tu śobhate ityādi / samāne 'pi hi sthaganavyāpāre lokottareṇaiva vyāpāreṇāsya pidhānamiti
tadevotkṛṣṭam / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Now, [the root] 'jayati' (is victorious), not 'śobhate' (looks beautiful) and the like — for although the act of concealment [of the eyes] is the same [in both cases], because his [third eye] is concealed only through a supramundane operation, that alone [expressed by 'jayati'] is superior. Or as in:

children.text:
{preyān so 'yamapākṛtaḥ saśapathaṃ pādānataḥ kāntayā
  dvitrāṇyeva padāni vāsabhavanādyāvanna yātyunmanāḥ /
  tāvatpratyuta pāṇisaṃpuṭagalannīvīnibandhaṃ dhṛto
  dhāvitveva kṛtapraṇāmakamaho premṇo vicitrā gatiḥ //98//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vāmana</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 3.2.15)

'That beloved one was dismissed with an oath, and [then], having bowed at her feet — before the distracted one had gone even two or three steps from the house — she herself, having run and performed an obeisance, held him back by the waist-knot slipping through the cup of her palm. Ah, how wondrous is the course of love!' || 98 ||
Here, 'padāni' (steps) [is used], not 'dvārāṇi' (doors/thresholds).
Through verb-endings (<s>tiṅ</s>) and nominal endings (<s>sup</s>), as in:

children.text:
{pathi pathi śukacañcūcārurābhāṅkurāṇāṃ
  diśi diśi pavamāno vīrudhāṃ lāsakaśca /
  nari nari kirati drāk sāyakān puṣpadhanvā
  puri puri vinivṛttā māninīmānacarcā //99//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Subhāṣitaratnabhāṇḍāgāra</s> 333/85)

'On every path, the sprouts reddish as parrot-beaks [emerge]; in every direction, the wind is a dancer of the plants; upon every woman, the Flower-Bowed One [<s>Kāma</s>] rapidly showers arrows; in every city, the quarrel of the proud women's pride has ceased.' || 99 ||

children.text: atra kiratīti kiraṇasya sādhyamānatvaṃ nivṛtteti nivartanasya siddhatvaṃ tiṅā supā ca tatrāpi ktapratyayenātītatvaṃ dyotyate / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, 'kirati' (showers) — through the verb-ending, the state of being in progress is [suggested]; 'nivṛttā' (has ceased) — through the nominal suffix, specifically the <s>kta</s>-suffix, the state of being past is suggested. Or as in:

children.text:
{likhannāste bhūmiṃ bahiravanataḥ prāṇadayito
  nirāhārāḥ sakhyaḥ satataruditocchūnanayanāḥ /
  parityaktaṃ sarvaṃ hasitapaṭhitaṃ pañjaraśukaiḥ
  tavāvasthā ceyaṃ visṛja kaṭhine mānamadhhunā //100//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 6)

'Your beloved sits outside, head bowed, drawing on the ground; your friends are without food, their eyes swollen from constant weeping; all laughter and recitation by the cage-parrots has been abandoned. And this is your state — release, O hard-hearted one, your pride now.' || 100 ||

children.text:
atra likhanniti na tu likhatīti tathā āste iti na tu āsīta iti api tu prasādaparyantamāste iti bhūmimiti na tu
bhūmāviti na hi buddhipūrvakamaparaṃ kiñcillikhatīti tiṅsubvibhaktīnāṃ vyaṅgyam /
saṃbandhasya yathā
children.translated_text:
Here, 'likhan' (drawing) — not 'likhati' (he draws); and 'āste' (sits) — not 'āsīta' (let him sit); rather, 'āste' means 'he sits until you are appeased'; 'bhūmim' (the ground, accusative) — not 'bhūmau' (on the ground, locative); for he does not purposefully draw anything else — the suggestive power of the verb-endings and the nominal case-endings [conveys all this].
Of grammatical relation (<s>saṃbandha</s>), as in:

children.text:
{gāmāruhamhi hāme vasāmi ṇa-araṭṭhi-iṃ ṇa jāṇāmi /
  ṇā-ari-āṇaṃ pa-iṇo haremi jā homi sā homi //101//}

children.translated_text: [Chāyā:] 'I am a village girl; I dwell in a village; I do not know the ways of city life;

children.text: nāgarikāṇāṃ patīn harāmi yā bhavāmi sā bhavāmi //]
children.translated_text: I steal the husbands of city women — what I am, that I am.'
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 705)
'I am a village girl; I dwell in a village; I know nothing of city ways; I steal the husbands of city-women — what I am, that I am.' || 101 ||

children.text:
atra nāgarikāṇāmiti ṣaṣṭhyāḥ /
ramaṇīyaḥ kṣatriyakumāra āsīt iti kālasya / eṣā hi bhagnamaheśvarakārmukaṃ dāśarathiṃ pratikupitasya bhārgavasyokti / vacanasya yathā /
children.translated_text:
Here, [the suggestion is] through the genitive case in 'of city women.'
[Another example:] 'There was a handsome <s>kṣatriya</s> prince' — [the suggestion is] through time [expressed by the past tense]. For this is the speech of <s>Bhārgava</s> [<s>Paraśurāma</s>], who was enraged toward <s>Dāśarathi</s> [<s>Rāma</s>], who had broken the bow of <s>Maheśvara</s> [<s>Śiva</s>].
Of the [suggestive power of a] statement (<s>vacana</s>), as in:

children.text:
{tāṇaṃ guṇaggaaṇāṇaṃ tāṇukkaṇṭhāṇaṃ tassa pemmassa /
  tāṇaṃ bhaṇi-āṇaṃ suṃdara erisi-aṃ jā-amavasāṇaṃ //102//}

children.translated_text: [Chāyā:] 'Of those appreciations of virtues, of those longings, of that love,
of those utterances, O handsome one — such has been the end, born [of karmic consequence].'
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 940)
'Of those appreciations of virtues, of those longings, of that love, of those utterances — O handsome one, such has been the end, born of [karmic] consequence.' || 102 ||
Here, the plurality of 'appreciations of virtues' and the rest, and the singularity of 'love,' are suggested.
Of the interchange of grammatical person, as in:

children.text:
{re re cañcalalocanāñcitaruce cetaḥ pramucya sthira-
  premāṇaṃ mahimānameṇayanāmālokya kiṃ nṛtyasi /
  kiṃ manye vihariṣyase bata hatāṃ muñcāntarāśāmimām
  eṣā kaṇṭhataṭe kṛtā khalu śilā saṃsāravārāṃnidhau //103//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'O heart, O restless-eyed and beautiful one! Abandoning the steadfast love [you bear], observing the greatness of the deer-eyed ones — why do you dance? What do I think — will you truly sport [with them]? Alas, let go this inner hope of another [love], killed as it is; for this stone has been placed at the edge of the throat in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>.' || 103 ||

Here, the <s>prahāsa</s> (comic) [<s>rasa</s> is suggested].
Of the precedence in word-order (<s>pūrvanipāta</s>), as in:

children.text:
{yeṣāṃ dorbalameva durbalatayā te saṃmatāstairapi
  prāyaḥ kevalanītirītiśaraṇaiḥ kāryaṃ kimurvīśvaraiḥ /
  ye kṣmāśakra punaḥ parākramanayasvīkārakāntakramās ----
  te syurnaiva bhavādṛśāstrijagati dvitrāḥ pavitrāḥ param //104//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'Those whose arm-strength alone is held to be weakness through [their actual] weakness — what is to be done by such kings who mostly take refuge in the path of mere statecraft? But those, O lord of the earth, whose graceful method embraces both valor and statecraft — such pure ones as yourself would number only two or three, no more, in the three worlds.' || 104 ||

Here, the predominance of valor [over statecraft] is understood [from the word-order].
Of a specific case-ending (<s>vibhaktiviśeṣa</s>), as in:

children.text:
{pradhanādhvani dhīradhanurdhvanibhṛti vidhurairayodhi tava divasam /
  divasena tu narapa bhavānayuddha vidhisiddhasādhuvādapadam //105//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'On the battlefield, O steadfast one bearing the sound of a strong bow, the battle was fought fiercely for a whole day; but in [just] a [single] day, O lord of men, your lordship fought without battle [i.e., won without effort] — a circumstance worthy of the praise 'well done!' divinely ordained.' || 105 ||
Here, 'in a day' (<s>divasena</s>) — the instrumental of completion (<s>apavarga-tṛtīyā</s>) suggests the attainment of the result [with ease].

children.text:
{bhūyo bhūyaḥ savidhanagarīrathyayā paryaṭantaṃ
  dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā bhavanavalabhītuṅgavātāyanasthā /
  sākṣātkāmaṃ navamiva ratirmālatī mādhavaṃ yat
  gāḍhotkaṇṭhālulitalulitairaṅgakaistāmyatīti //106//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> 1.30)

'Seeing him wandering again and again through the main street near the city, seeing him repeatedly, she — standing at the lofty window on the roof of the house — like <s>Mālatī</s> [seeing] <s>Mādhava</s> as <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) himself made visible — faints with her limbs trembling, swaying with intense longing.' || 106 ||
Here, [the suggestion is] through the <s>taddhita</s> suffix (secondary derivative) having the form of compassion.

children.text:
{paricchedātītaḥ sakalavacanānāmaviṣayaḥ
  punarjanmanyasminnanubhavapathaṃ yo na gatavān /
  vivekapradhvaṃsādupacitamahāmohagahano
  vikāraḥ ko 'pyantarjaḍayati ca tāpaṃ ca kurute //107//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> 1.30)

'Beyond the reach of definition, beyond the scope of all words, one who in this rebirth has not entered the path of experience — a transformation, altogether inner, unknowable, which, from the destruction of discernment, thickens into a dense forest of great delusion, stupefies and causes anguish.' || 107 ||
Here, [the suggestion is] through the prefix (<s>upasarga</s>) 'pra-.'

children.text:
{kṛtaṃ ca garvābhimukhaṃ manastvayā
  kimanyadevaṃ nihatāśca no dviṣaḥ /
  tamāṃsi tiṣṭhanti hi tāvadaṃśumān
  na yāvadāyātyudayādrimaulitām //108//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'Your mind has been turned toward pride — what else? Our enemies have been slain. Darkness persists only so long as the radiant one [the sun] has not yet reached the summit of the eastern mountain.' || 108 ||
Here, [the suggestion is] through the particle 'ca,' which indicates <s>tulyayogitā</s> (common applicability).

children.text:
{rāmosau bhuvaneṣu vikramaguṇaiḥ prāptaḥ prasiddhiṃ parā-
  masmadbhāgyaviparyayādyadi paraṃ devo na jānāti tam /
  bandīvaiṣa yaśāṃsi gāyati marudyasyaikabāṇāhati-
  śreṇībhūtaviśālatālavivarodgīrṇaiḥsvaraiḥsaptabhiḥ //109//}

children.translated_text: ([<s>Viśākhadatta</s>])

'That <s>Rāma</s>, who has attained the highest fame in the worlds through his qualities of valor — if, due to the reversal of our fortune, the lord does not know him — here this bard sings his glories with the seven notes issuing from the holes of the broad <s>tāla</s> (palm) trees arranged in a row by the strike of his single arrow.' || 109 ||
