children.text: atrāsāviti bhuvaneṣviti guṇairiti sarvanāmaprātipadikavacanānāṃ na tvaditi na maditi api asmadityasya sarvākṣepiṇaḥ bhāgyaviparyayādityanyathāsaṃpattimukhena na tvabhāvamukhenābhidhānasya /
children.translated_text: Here, [the suggestion is] through the pronouns 'asau' (that one), 'bhuvaneṣu' (in the worlds), 'guṇaiḥ' (by qualities) — that is, the pronominal, the nominal stem, and the number [forms] — not 'tvad' (your) or 'mad' (my), but rather 'asmad' (our), which encompasses all; and through 'bhāgyaviparyayāt' (due to the reversal of fortune), the expression is through the avenue of otherwise-obtaining, not through the avenue of non-existence.

children.text:
{taruṇimani kalayati kalāmanumadanadhanurbhruvoḥ paṭhatyagre /
  adhivasati sakalalalanāmaulimiyaṃ cakitaṃhariṇacalanayanā //110//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Mahimabhaṭṭa</s>'s <s>Vyaktiviveka</s>)

'As she adorns the mark of youth, as she masters the art of the bow of <s>Madana</s> (Love) with her brows, she studies in the presence [of the teacher], she inhabits [the world] — the complete crown of all women — she, with the restless, trembling eyes of a doe.' || 110 ||

children.text:
atra imanijavyayībhāvakarmabhūtādhārāṇāṃ svarūpasya taruṇatve, iti dhanuṣaḥ samīpe, iti maulau vasatīti tvādibhistulye, eṣāṃ vācakatve, asti kaścit svarūpasya viśeṣo yaścamatkārakārī sa eva vyañjakatvaṃ prāpnoti /
evamanyeṣāmapi boddhavyam /
varṇaracanānāṃ vyañjakatvaṃ guṇasvarūpanirūpaṇe udāhariṣyate apiśabdāt prabandheṣu nāṭakādiṣu /
evaṃ rasādīnāṃ pūrvagaṇitabhedābhyāṃ saha ṣaḍ bhedāḥ /
children.translated_text:
Here, regarding the individual intrinsic forms of the demonstratives, compounds, verbal objects, and locative expressions: 'in youth,' 'of the bow,' 'in the presence,' 'she inhabits' — when these, like 'you' and the like, are equivalent in denotative power — there is some special quality of their intrinsic form that causes wonder, and that very quality constitutes their suggestive power.
Thus should be understood for others as well.
The suggestive power of phonemic composition (<s>varṇaracanā</s>) will be illustrated in the section on the determination of the nature of qualities (<s>guṇa</s>). By the word 'also,' [this applies] in extended compositions such as dramas and the like.
Thus, together with the two types previously enumerated, there are six divisions of <s>rasa</s> and the like [as suggested].
The divisions of those are fifty-one...
[This has been] explained.
... and in their mutual combination. || Kpr-K_43 ||
Through <s>saṃkara</s> (intermixture), which is of three kinds, and through <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (blending), which is of one kind.

children.text: na kevalaṃ śuddhā evaikapañcāśadbhedā bhavanti / yāvatteṣāṃ svaprabhedairekapañcāśatā saṃśayāspadatvenānugrāhakatayaikavyañjakānupraveśena ceti trividhena saṃkareṇa parasparanirapekṣarūpayaikaprakārayā saṃsṛṣṭyā ceti catur[bhir]guṇane /
children.translated_text: Not only are there fifty-one pure divisions; rather, their mutual combination is fourfold: through <s>saṃkara</s> (intermixture) of three kinds — as grounds for doubt, as mutual reinforcement, and as the penetration of a single suggestor — and through <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (blending), which is of a single kind, where the forms are mutually independent.
Vedas, sky, ocean, space, and moon...
Together with the pure divisions,
... arrows, yoke, sky, and moon. || Kpr-K_44 ||
Therein, only the general direction is to be illustrated.

children.text:
{kkhaṇapāhuṇi-ā de-ara jā-ā-e suha-a kiṃpi de bhaṇi-ā /
  ru-a-i paḍoharavalahīgharammi aṇuṇiñja-u varā-ī //111//}
[kṣaṇaprāghuṇikā devara jāyayā subhaga kimapi te bhaṇitā /
children.translated_text: [Chāyā:] 'A momentary guest, O brother-in-law — your wife, O good-looking one, has said something to you;
she is weeping in the room behind the house — the poor one, let her be consoled.'
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 963; <s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s> 3)
'A momentary guest, O brother-in-law — your wife has said something, O good-looking one, to you; she is weeping in the room behind the house — the poor one, let her be consoled.' || 111 ||

children.text: atrānunayaḥ kimupabhogalakṣaṇe 'rthāntare saṃkramitaḥ kimanuraṇananyāyenopabhoge eva vyaṅgye vyañjakaḥ iti saṃdehaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, [the question is:] has the consolation been transferred to another meaning, namely sexual enjoyment? Or, by the principle of <s>anuraṇana</s> (resonance), is it suggestive with sexual enjoyment itself as the suggested meaning? — this is the doubt.

children.text:
{snigdhaśyāmalakāntiliptaviyato velladbalākā ghanāḥ
  vātāḥ śīkariṇaḥ payodasuhṛdāmānandakekāḥ kalāḥ /
  kāmaṃ santu dṛḍhaṃ kaṭhorahṛdayo rāmo 'smi sarvaṃ sahe
  vaidehī tu kathaṃ bhaviṣyati ha hā hā devi dhīrā bhava //112//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ānandavardhana</s>'s <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2)

'The clouds, their dark beauty spread across the sky, with waving cranes, the winds sprinkling mist, the calls of the friends of the rain-clouds [peacocks] — their joyful cries! Let them be as they may — I am <s>Rāma</s>, strong-hearted, hard — I can bear everything. But <s>Vaidehī</s> — how will she be? Alas, alas! O goddess, be brave!' || 112 ||

children.text: atra lipteti payodasuhṛdāmiti ca atyantatiraskṛtavācyayoḥ saṃsṛṣṭiḥ / tābhyāṃ saha rāmo 'smītyarthāntarasaṃkramitavācyasyānugrāhakabhāvena rāmapadalakṣaṇaikavyañjakānupraveśena cārthāntarasaṃkramitavācyarasadhvanyoḥ saṃkaraḥ / evamanyadapyudāhāryam //
children.translated_text: Here, [the expressions] 'spread' and 'of the friends of the rain-clouds' represent <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (blending) of two [types of <s>dhvani</s>] where the expressed meaning is completely concealed. Along with those, 'I am <s>Rāma</s>' — where the expressed meaning is transferred to another meaning — [produces] <s>saṃkara</s> (intermixture) of the two [types]: expressed-meaning-transferred and <s>rasa</s>-<s>dhvani</s>, through the role of mutual reinforcement and through the penetration of a single suggestor, namely the word '<s>Rāma</s>,' in the expressed-meaning-transferred type. Thus should other [examples] also be illustrated.

children.text: iti kāvyaprakāśe dhvaninirṇayo nāma caturtha ullāsaḥ ||4||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, the fourth <s>ullāsa</s>, named 'The Determination of <s>Dhvani</s>,' [is completed]. ||4||
Now, the fifth <s>ullāsa</s>.
Having thus determined <s>dhvani</s>, he states the varieties of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinate suggestion):
Not hidden; subordinate to another [meaning]; an accessory to the accomplishment of the expressed meaning; indistinct;
of doubtful [predominance]; of equal predominance; indicated by <s>kāku</s> (tone of voice); and aesthetically unpleasing — // <s>MKpr-K</s>_45 //
such suggested meaning — thus eight varieties of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> are recognized.

children.text: kāminīkucakalaśavat gūḍhaṃ camatkaroti / agūḍhaṃ tu sphuṭatayā vācyāyamānamiti guṇībhūtameva / agūḍhaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Like the pitcher-shaped breasts of a beautiful woman, hidden [suggestion] produces wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>). But the non-hidden (<s>agūḍha</s>), being manifest, is subordinated to the expressed meaning — hence it is indeed <s>guṇībhūta</s> (subordinate). An example of non-hidden:

children.text:
{yasyāsuhṛtkṛtatiraskṛtiretya tapta-
  sūcīvyadhavyatikareṇa yunakti karṇau /
  kāñcīguṇagrathanabhājanameṣa so 'smi
  jīvanna saṃprati bhavāmi kimāvahāmi //113//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{She whose cruel rejection was inflicted by one who was not a friend — [that rejection] pierces the ears with the intensity of heated needles; I am the one worthy of being the receptacle for the tying of the girdle-string — yet living now, I do not [truly] exist — what purpose do I serve? //113//}
Here, 'living' — an instance of the expressed meaning transferred to another meaning (<s>arthāntarasaṃkramitavācya</s>).

children.text:
{unnidrakokanadareṇupiśaṅgitāngā
  gāyanti mañju madhupā gṛhadīrghikāsu /
  etaccakāsti ca ravernavabandhujīva-
  puṣpacchadābhamudayācalacumbi bimbam //114//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kuntaka</s>'s <s>Vakroktijīvita</s> 2.3)

{Golden-limbed from the pollen of fully-bloomed lotuses, bees sing sweetly in the house-ponds; and there gleams the orb of the sun, resembling the petals of fresh <s>bandhujīva</s> flowers, kissing the eastern mountain at its rise. //114//}
Here, 'kissing' — an instance of the expressed meaning completely concealed (<s>atyantatiraskṛtavācya</s>).

children.text:
{atrāsīt phaṇipāśabandhanavidhiḥ śaktyā bhavaddevare
  gāḍhaṃ vakṣasi tāḍite hanumatā droṇādriratrāhṛtaḥ /
  divyairindrajidatra lakṣmaṇaśarairlokāntaraṃ prāpitaḥ
  kenāpyatra mṛgākṣi rākṣasapateḥ kṛttā ca kaṇṭhāṭavī //115// (1)}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rājaśekhara</s>'s <s>Bālarāmāyaṇa</s> 10.20)

{Here there was the device of binding with the serpent-noose by the power of your brother-in-law (<s>Indrajit</s>); here, when the chest was struck hard by <s>Hanumān</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>-mountain was brought in the night; here <s>Indrajit</s> was dispatched to another world by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s divine arrows; and here, O doe-eyed one, by someone the throat-forest of the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s> was severed. //115// (1)}

children.text:
atra kenāpyatretyarthaśaktimūlānuraṇanarūpasya / {tasyāpyatra} iti yuktaḥ pāṭhaḥ /
aparasya rasādervācyasya vā (vākyārthībhūtasya) aṅgaṃ rasādi anuraṇanarūpaṃ vā / yathā
children.translated_text: Here, 'by someone, here' — an instance of <s>anuraṇana</s> (reverberation) based on the power of meaning. The reading '{by him too, here}' is the correct one. [The second type:] subordinate to another — [meaning] <s>rasa</s> and the like, or to the expressed meaning (which has become the sentence-meaning), as a subordinate element in the form of <s>rasa</s> and the like, or in the form of <s>anuraṇana</s> (reverberation). For example:

children.text:
{ayaṃ sa raśanotkarṣī pīnastanavimardanaḥ /
  nābhyūrujaghanasparśī nīvīvisraṃsanaḥ karaḥ //116//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Mahābhārata</s>)
{This is that hand — which lifts the garment-string, which presses the full breasts, which touches the navel, thighs, and buttocks, which loosens the girdle. //116//}
Here, <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment) is subordinate to <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic sentiment).

children.text:
{kailāsālayabhālalocanarucā nirvartitālaktaka-
  vyaktiḥ pādanakhadyutirgiribhuvaḥ sā vaḥ sadā trāyatām /
  spardhābandhasamṛddhayeva sudṛḍhaṃ rūḍhā yayā netrayoḥ
  kāntiḥ kokanadānukārasarasā sadyaḥ samutsāryate //117//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{May the radiance of the toenails of the daughter of the mountain — resembling red lac produced by the lustre of the frontal eye of the dweller on <s>Kailāsa</s> — always protect you; by which the beauty residing in the eyes, lush with the semblance of lotuses, is at once forcefully dispelled, as if through the fullness of a bond of rivalry. //117//}
Here, a <s>bhāva</s> (transitory emotion) is subordinate to <s>rasa</s>.

children.text:
{atyuccāḥ paritaḥ sphuranti girayaḥ sphārāstathābhyodhaya-
  stānetānapi bibhratī kimapi na klāntāsi tubhyaṃ namaḥ /
  āścaryeṇa muhurmuhuḥ stutimiti prastaumi yāvadbhuva-
  stāvadbibhradimāṃ smṛtastava bhujo vācastato mudritāḥ //118//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Pañcākṣarīpraśasti</s>)

{Exceedingly lofty mountains tower all around; vast indeed is the expanse; and yet, bearing even these, you are not in the least weary — salutations to you! In wonder, again and again, just as I begin a hymn of praise of the earth, your arm, O [king], is remembered as bearing her — and thereupon my words are sealed [in silence]. //118//}

children.text: atra bhū.viṣayo ratyākhyo bhāvo rājaviṣayasya ratibhāvasya /
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>bhāva</s> called <s>rati</s> (love) directed toward the earth is subordinate to the <s>bhāva</s> of <s>rati</s> directed toward the king.

children.text:
{bandīkṛtya nṛpa dviṣāṃ mṛgadṛśastāḥ paśyatāṃ preyasāṃ
  śliṣyanti praṇamanti lānti paritaścumbanti te sainikāḥ /
  asmākaṃ sukṛtairdṛśornipatitosyaucityavārāṃnidhe
  vidhvastā vipadokhilāstaditi taiḥ pratyarthibhiḥ stūyase //119//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Subhāṣitaratnabhāṇḍāgāra</s> 112/268)

{O king, having captured the doe-eyed women of the enemies, while their beloved ones look on — your soldiers embrace them, bow to them, coax them gently, and kiss them on all sides. By our good fortune, O ocean of propriety, you have fallen within the range of our sight — all calamities are destroyed — thus they praise you, those very adversaries. //119//}

Here, a <s>bhāva</s> subordinate [to another] — <s>rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>rasa</s>) and <s>bhāvābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>bhāva</s>) are suggested by the first half and the second half, respectively.

children.text:
{aviralakaravālakampanairbhrukuṭītarjanagarjanairmuhuḥ /
  dadṛśe tava vairiṇāṃ madaḥ sa gataḥ kvāpi tavekṣaṇe kṣaṇāt //120//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Viśvanātha</s>'s <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s>)

{Through incessant flashing of swords, furrowed brows, threats, and roars, again and again — the arrogance of your enemies was seen; but at a single glance of yours, it vanished somewhere in an instant. //120//}
Here, a <s>bhāva</s> subordinate [to another] — the quiescence of a <s>bhāva</s> (<s>bhāvapraśama</s>).

children.text:
{sākaṃ kuraṅgakadṛśā madhupānalīlāṃ
  kartuṃ suhṛdbhirapi vairiṇi te pravṛtte /
  anyābhidhāyi tava nāma vibho gṛhītaṃ
  kenāpi tatra viṣamāmakarodavasthām //121//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{When your enemy, together with friends, set about engaging in the sport of wine-drinking with a doe-eyed woman, your name, O lord, was uttered by someone there — and it threw everything into a dreadful state. //121//}
Here, the arising of <s>trāsa</s> (terror).

children.text:
{asoḍhā tatkālollasadasahabhāvasya tapasaḥ
  kathānāṃ viśrambheṣvatha ca rasikaḥ śailaduhituḥ /
  pramodaṃ vo diśyāt kapaṭabaṭuveṣāpanayane
  tvarāśaithilyābhyāṃ yugapadabhiyuktaḥ smaraharaḥ //122//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{He who could not endure the austerity that blazed with the unbearable splendor of [her] simultaneous presence, and yet was a connoisseur (<s>rasika</s>) during intimate conversations with the daughter of the mountain — may <s>Smarahara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>, the destroyer of <s>Kāma</s>) grant you joy, he who was engaged with simultaneous haste and hesitation at the moment of removing the disguise of the deceitful young student. //122//}
Here, the juncture (<s>saṃdhi</s>) of agitation (<s>āvega</s>) and composure (<s>dhairya</s>).

children.text:
{paśyetkaściccala capala re kā tvarāhaṃ kumārī
  hastālambaṃ vitara ha ha hā vyutkramaḥ kvāsi yāsi /
  itthaṃ pṛthvīparivṛḍha bhavadvidviṣoraṇyavṛtteḥ
  kanyā kañcit phalakisalayānyādadānābhidhatte //123//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Someone would say: 'Look!' — [she replies:] 'Restless one, O restless one, what is the hurry? I am a maiden!' — 'Give me your hand to hold!' — 'Ha ha, alas! A transgression! Where are you going?' — Thus, O lord of the earth, a certain maiden, plucking fruits and young shoots, speaks to a forest-dwelling enemy of yours. //123//}

children.text: atra śaṅkāsūyādhṛtismṛtiśramadainyavibodhautsukyānāṃ śabalatā / ete ca rasavadādyalaṅkārāḥ / yadyapi bhāvodayabhāvasaṃdhibhāvaśabalatvāni nālaṅkāratayā uktāni tathāpi kaścit brūyādityevamuktam / yadyapi sa nāsti kaścidviṣayaḥ yatra dhvaniguṇībhūtavyaṅgyayoḥ svaprabhedādibhiḥ saha saṃkaraḥ saṃsṛṣṭirvā nāsti tathāpi prādhānyena vyapadeśā bhavantīti kvacitkenacidvyavahāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the variegation (<s>śabalatva</s>) of apprehension (<s>śaṅkā</s>), jealous reproach (<s>asūyā</s>), courage (<s>dhṛti</s>), recollection (<s>smṛti</s>), fatigue (<s>śrama</s>), wretchedness (<s>dainya</s>), awakening (<s>vibodha</s>), and eagerness (<s>autsukya</s>). And these are the <s>alaṃkāras</s> (figures) such as <s>rasavat</s> and the like. Although the arising of <s>bhāva</s>, the juncture of <s>bhāvas</s>, and the variegation of <s>bhāvas</s> were not stated as <s>alaṃkāras</s>, nevertheless, 'someone might say so' — thus it was stated. Although there is indeed no subject-matter where there is no intermixture (<s>saṃkara</s>) or combination (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>) of <s>dhvani</s> and <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> with their own sub-varieties, still, designations are made according to predominance — hence the usage is sometimes one and sometimes another.

children.text:
{janasthāne bhrāntaṃ kanakamṛgatṛṣṇāndhitadhiyā
  vaco vaidehīti pratipadamudaśru pralapitam /
  kṛtālaṅkābharturvadanaparipāṭīṣughaṭanā
  mayāptaṃ rāmatvaṃ kuśalavasutā na tvadhigatā //124//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 66)

{I wandered in <s>Janasthāna</s>, my mind blinded by the mirage of the golden deer; at every step I cried out 'O <s>Vaidehī</s>!' with tears streaming; I fashioned arrows fitted to the lip-contour of my wife — I obtained <s>Rāma</s>-hood, but the state of being father of <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s> was not attained [by me]. //124//}

children.text:
atra śabdaśaktimūlānuraṇanarūpo rāmeṇa sahopamānopameyabhāvo
vācyāṅgatāṃ nītaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>anuraṇana</s> (reverberation) based on the power of word — the relation of comparison between the speaker and <s>Rāma</s> (<s>upamānopameyabhāva</s>) — has been made subordinate to the expressed meaning.

children.text:
{āgatya saṃprati viyogavisaṃṣṭhulāṅgī
  mambhojinīṃ kvacidapi kṣapitatriyāmaḥ /
  etāṃ prasādayati paśya śanaiḥ prabhāte
  tanvaṅgi pādapatanena sahasraraśmiḥ //125// (2)}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 67)

{Having come now, her limbs wasted by the agony of separation, having spent the three watches of the night somewhere near a lotus pond — see, in the morning, the thousand-rayed sun slowly propitiates her, O slender one, by falling at her feet! //125// (2)}

Here, the account of the hero, based on the power of meaning and of the nature of subject-matter (<s>vastu</s>), is established simply through the superimposition of the account of the sun and the lotus-pond, which is independent [of it].
An example of [suggestion that is] an accessory to the accomplishment of the expressed meaning (<s>vācyasiddhyaṅga</s>):

children.text:
{bhramimaratimalasahṛdayatāṃ pralayaṃ mūrchā tamaḥ śarīrasādam /
  maraṇaṃ jaladabhujagajaṃ prasahya kurute viṣaṃ viyoginīnām //126//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ānandavardhana</s>'s <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.3)
{Giddiness, torpor of the heart, stupor, fainting, darkness, bodily wasting, death — the poison of the cloud-serpent forcibly inflicts [these] upon women in separation. //126//}

children.text: atra hālāhalaṃ vyaṅgyaṃ bhujagarūpasya vācyasya siddhikṛt / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, <s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison) is the suggested meaning, which serves to accomplish the expressed meaning of the serpent-form. Or alternatively:

children.text:
{gacchāmyacyuta darśanena bhavataḥ kiṃ tṛptirutpadyate
  kiṃ tvevaṃ vijanasthayorhatajanaḥsaṃbhāvayatyanyathā /
  ityāmantraṇabhaṅgisūcitavṛthāvasthānakhedālasām
  āśliṣyan pulakotkarāñcitatanurgopīṃ hariḥ pātu vaḥ //127// (3)}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{I am leaving, O <s>Acyuta</s> — for what satisfaction arises from seeing you? But then again, in this state of our being alone together, people free from jealousy will suspect otherwise. — Thus embracing a <s>gopī</s> who was languid with the distress of a vainly feigned departure, as indicated by the manner of her leave-taking, <s>Hari</s>, his body bristling with a rush of horripilation, may he protect you! //127// (3)}

Here, [the meaning] suggested by the words '<s>Acyuta</s>' and the like serves [to accomplish] the expressed meaning of 'the manner of leave-taking' and so forth. The distinction between these two [examples] is that in one case the [suggested and expressed] belong to a single speaker, while in the other they belong to different speakers.
An example of indistinct (<s>asphuṭa</s>) [suggestion]:

children.text:
{adṛṣṭe darśanotkaṇṭhā dṛṣṭe vicchedabhīrutā /
  nādṛṣṭena na dṛṣṭena bhavatā labhyate sukham //128// (4)}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{When you are unseen, there is longing to see you; when seen, there is fear of separation — neither unseen nor seen, O you, can happiness be obtained from you! //128// (4)}

children.text: atrādṛṣṭo yathā na bhavasi viyogabhayaṃ ca yathā notpadyate tathā kuryā iti kliṣṭam //
children.translated_text: Here, [the suggested meaning] is strained (<s>kliṣṭa</s>): 'Act in such a way that you are not unseen and that the fear of separation does not arise.'
An example of doubtful predominance (<s>saṃdigdhaprādhānya</s>):

children.text:
{harastu kiñcitparivṛttadhairyaścandrodayārambha ivāmburāśiḥ /
  umāmukhe bimbaphalādharoṣṭhe vyāpārayāmāsa vilocanāni //129// (5)}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 3.67)

{<s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), his composure somewhat wavering, like the ocean at the onset of moonrise, cast his eyes upon the face of <s>Umā</s>, whose lower lip was like a <s>bimba</s> fruit. //129// (5)}

children.text: atra paricumbitumaicchaditi kiṃ pratīyamānaṃ kiṃ vā vilocanavyāpāraṇaṃ vācyaṃ pradhānamiti saṃdehaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here there is doubt: is the apprehended meaning 'he wished to kiss [her],' or is the expressed meaning — the casting of the eyes — predominant?
An example of equal predominance (<s>tulyaprādhānya</s>):
(<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mahāvīracarita</s> 2.8)
{The abandonment of transgressing <s>brāhmaṇas</s> is for your own welfare; <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) is otherwise a friend — otherwise he becomes ill-disposed. //130// (6)}

children.text: atra jāmadagnyaḥ sarveṣāṃ kṣatriyāṇāmiva rakṣasāṃ kṣaṇāt kṣayaṃ kariṣyatīti vyaṅgyasya vācyasya ca samaṃ prādhānyam //
children.translated_text: Here, [the suggested meaning] '<s>Jāmadagnya</s> will destroy all the <s>kṣatriyas</s> in an instant, just as [he would] the <s>rākṣasas</s>' — the suggested and the expressed meanings have equal predominance.
An example of [suggestion] indicated by <s>kāku</s> (tone of voice):

children.text:
{mathnāmi kauravaśataṃ samare na kopāt
  duḥśāsanasya rudhiraṃ na pbāmyurastaḥ //
children.translated_text: {I shall not churn the hundred <s>Kauravas</s> in battle out of anger; I shall not drink the blood of <s>Duḥśāsana</s> from [his] chest;

children.text:
saṃcūrṇayāmi gadayā na suyodhanorū
  saṃdhiṃ karotu bhavatāṃ nṛpatiḥ paṇena //131// (7)}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>'s <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 1.15)
I shall not crush the thighs of <s>Suyodhana</s> with my mace — let the king make peace with your side through a wager! //131// (7)}
Here, 'I shall indeed churn [them]' and so forth is the suggested meaning, established together with the negation of the expressed meaning.
An example of aesthetically unpleasing (<s>asundara</s>) [suggestion]:
[Hearing the clamor of birds taking flight from the <s>vānīra</s> thickets —
the limbs of the bride, occupied with household chores, waste away.]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 876)
{Hearing the clamor of birds taking flight from the <s>vānīra</s> (cane) thickets — the limbs of the bride, occupied with household chores, begin to waste away. //132// (8)}

children.text: atra dattasaṃketaḥ kaścillatāgahanaṃ praviṣṭa iti vyaṅgyāt sīdantyaṅgānīti vācyaṃ sacamatkāram //
children.translated_text: Here, through the suggested meaning that someone with whom a tryst was arranged has entered the dense bower — the expressed meaning 'her limbs waste away' acquires its aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>).

children.text: eṣāṃ bhedā yathāyogaṃ veditavyāśca pūrvavat // MKpr-K_46 //
children.translated_text: The varieties of these [eight types] should be understood as applicable in combination, as before. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_46 //
'As applicable' means:
{When figures of speech are suggested by subject-matter alone, then
their subordination to <s>dhvani</s> is certain — because the poetic mode depends on that [dhvani]. //}

children.text: iti dhvanikāroktadiśā vastumātreṇa yatrālaṅkāro vyajyate na tatra guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatvam /
children.translated_text: Following the direction indicated by the author of the <s>Dhvani</s> [treatise], where a figure is suggested by subject-matter alone, there is no <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatva</s> (status of subordinate suggestion).
The combination (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>) and intermixture (<s>saṅkara</s>) of <s>dhvani</s> with those [types of subordinate suggestion] accompanied by figures —

children.text: sālaṅkārairiti tairevālaṅkāraiḥ alaṅkārayuktaiśca taiḥ / taduktaṃ dhvanikṛtā

children.translated_text: {That [<s>dhvani</s>], together with [the types of] <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> and [those] accompanied by figures, with its own sub-varieties,
is further illuminated in many ways through <s>saṃkara</s> (intermixture) and <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination). //}
Thus.
'Accompanied by figures' means: with those very figures, and with those [types] that are accompanied by figures. As the author of the <s>Dhvani</s> [treatise] has said:
From the mutual combination in this way, the count of varieties would be exceedingly great. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_47 //

children.text: evamanena prakāreṇa avāntarabhedagaṇanetiprabhūtatarā gaṇanā / tathāhi--śṛṅgasyaiva bhedaprabhedagaṇanāyāmānantyam / kā gaṇanā tu sarveṣām /
children.translated_text: Thus, by this method, through the enumeration of sub-varieties, the count is even more extensive. For indeed, in the enumeration of the varieties and sub-varieties of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> alone, there is infinity. What then of the count of all [rasas]!

children.text:
saṃkalanena punarasya dhvanestrayo bhedāḥ / vyaṅgyasya trirūpatvāt / tathāhi--kiñcidvācyatāṃ sahate kiñcittvanyathā / tatra vācyatāsaham avicitraṃ vicitraṃ ceti / avicitraṃ vastumātraṃ vicitraṃ tvalaṅkārarūpam /
yadyapi prādhānyena tadalaṅkāryaṃ tathāpi brāhmaṇaśramaṇanyāyena tathocyate / rasādilakṣaṇastvarthaḥ svapne 'pi na vācyaḥ / sa hi rasādiśabdena śṛṅgārādiśabdena vābhidhīyeta / na cābhidhīyate tatprayoge 'pi vibhāvādyaprayoge tasyāpratipattestadaprayoge 'pi vibhāvādiprayoge tasya pratipatteścetyanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ vibhāvādyabhidhānadvāreṇaiva pratīyate iti niścīyate /
children.translated_text: By way of summary, this <s>dhvani</s> has three varieties — because the suggested meaning is of three forms. For some [suggestion] tolerates [co-existence with] the expressed meaning; some does otherwise [i.e., supersedes it]. Among those that tolerate the expressed meaning, [there are] the aesthetically unremarkable (<s>avicitra</s>) and the aesthetically remarkable (<s>vicitra</s>). The unremarkable is mere subject-matter (<s>vastumātra</s>); the remarkable is in the form of a figure of speech (<s>alaṃkārarūpa</s>). Although in predominance that [suggested meaning] is the thing to be ornamented (<s>alaṃkārya</s>), nevertheless, following the principle of '<s>brāhmaṇa</s> and <s>śramaṇa</s>' [where the first term governs], it is so designated. But the meaning characterized as <s>rasa</s> and the like is never expressed [directly], even in a dream. For it would have to be denoted by the word '<s>rasa</s>' or by a word like '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>' — but it is not so denoted. Through the positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) — that even when those [words] are employed, without the employment of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest, there is no apprehension [of <s>rasa</s>]; and even without the employment of those [words], when <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest are employed, there is apprehension — it is determined that [<s>rasa</s>] is apprehended only through the medium of the denotation of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest.

children.text: tenāsau vyaṅgya eva / mukhyārthabādhādyabhāvānna punarlakṣaṇīyaḥ / arthāntarasaṃkramitātyantatiraskṛtavācyayorvastumātrarūpaṃ vyaṅgyaṃ vinā lakṣaṇaiva na bhavatīti prāk pratipāditam / śabdaśaktimūle tu abhidhāyā niyantraṇenānabhidheyasyārthāntarasya tena sahopamādera[raṃ]laṅkārasya ca nirvivādaṃ vyaṅgatvam / ([raṃ] is needless)
children.translated_text: Therefore, that [<s>rasa</s>] is indeed suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>). And it is not to be regarded as denoted by secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), because of the absence of obstruction to the primary meaning and the like. That in [the cases of] expressed meaning transferred to another meaning and completely concealed, there is no <s>lakṣaṇā</s> without the suggested meaning of the nature of mere subject-matter — this was established earlier. In the case based on the power of word, since denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>) is restricted [to its own meaning], the suggestive nature of the meaning that is not directly denotable — namely, the comparison (<s>upamā</s>) and the like together with it, and the figure of speech — is beyond dispute.

children.text:
arthaśaktimūle 'pi viśeṣe saṃketaḥ kartu[ṃ] na yujyate iti sāmānyarūpāṇāṃ padārthānāmākāṅkṣā-saṃnidhi-yogyatāvaśātparasparasaṃsargo yatrāpadārtho 'pi viśeṣarūpo vākyārthastatrābhihitānvayavāde
kā vārt[t]ā vyaṅgyasyābhidheyatāyām /
children.translated_text: Even in the case [of meaning] rooted in the power of meaning, convention cannot be made for the particular [composite meaning]. For where the mutual combination of word-meanings — which are of a general form — [occurs] through expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), contiguity (<s>saṃnidhi</s>), and compatibility (<s>yogyatā</s>), the particular composite sentence-meaning is itself a non-word-meaning; according to the <s>abhihitānvayavāda</s> (theory of expressed-then-connected [meanings]), what talk is there of the suggested meaning being expressible [by denotation]?
As for what they say:
{'The word-expert sees, through direct perception, the denoted component;
and that it is understood by the hearer is [known] by inference from [the hearer's] behavior. //1//

children.text:
anyathānupapattyā tu bodhecchaktiṃ dvayātmikām /
  arthāpattyāvabodheta saṃbandhaṃ tripramāṇakam //2//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kumārilabhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Ślokavārtika</s> 141)

Through the impossibility of [explaining it] otherwise, one should understand the twofold power of cognition;
through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>), one should understand the connection [of word and meaning] through three means of knowledge. //2//'}

children.text:
iti pratipāditadiśā devadatta gāmānaya ityādyuttamavṛddhavākyaprayogāddeśāntaraṃ sāsnādimantamarthaṃ madhyamavṛddhe nayati sati anenāsmādvākyādevaṃvidho 'rthaḥ pratipannaḥ iti tacceṣṭayānumāya tayorakhaṇḍavākyavākyārthayorarthāpattyā vācyavācakabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ saṃbandhamavadhārya bālastatra vyutpadyate / parataḥ caitra gāmānaya devadatta aśvamānaya devadatta gāṃ naya ityādivākyaprayoge tasya tasya
śabdasya taṃ tamarthamavadhārayatīti anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ pravṛttinivṛttikāri vākyameva prayogayogyamiti vākyasthitānāmeva padānāmanvitaiḥ padā[r]thairanvitānāmeva saṃketo gṛhyate iti viśiṣṭā eva padārthā vākyārthāḥ /
na tu padārthānāṃ vaiśiṣṭyam /
children.translated_text: In the manner indicated [by this]: when a superior elder uses the sentence 'O <s>Devadatta</s>, bring the cow,' a middling elder leads [the child] to a dewlapped animal in another place; then, [the child thinking] 'From this sentence, such a meaning has been understood by him,' inferring from that [elder's] behavior, and ascertaining through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) that the relation between the undivided sentence and sentence-meaning is of the nature of expressed and expresser — the child learns [the convention] thereby. Subsequently, through the use of sentences like '<s>Caitra</s>, bring the cow,' '<s>Devadatta</s>, bring the horse,' '<s>Devadatta</s>, take the cow,' and the like, he ascertains each word's [connection with] each meaning — thus, through co-presence and co-absence (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>), only the sentence which effects engagement and cessation is fit for usage; and the convention is grasped only for word-meanings of words standing within sentences, [i.e.,] for connected word-meanings that are already connected — thus the qualified word-meanings are the sentence-meaning, not the qualification of the word-meanings [separately]. This is the <s>anvitābhidhānavāda</s> (theory of connected-denotation).

children.text:
yadyapi vākyāntaraprayujyamānānyapi pratyabhijñāpratyayena tānyevaitāni padāni niścīyanta iti padārthāntaramātreṇānvitaḥ padārthaḥ saṃketagocaraḥ / tathāpi sāmānyāvacchādito viśeṣarūpa evāsau
pratipadyate vyatiṣaktānāṃ padārthānāṃ tathābhūtatvādityanvitābhidhānavādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although even words used in other sentences are ascertained through the cognition of recognition to be those very same words — and thus a word-meaning connected with merely another word-meaning is the object of convention — nevertheless, it is always apprehended in a particular form veiled by the universal, because word-meanings in combination are of such a nature. Thus say the proponents of <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> (connected-denotation).

children.text:
teṣāmapi mate sāmānyaviśeṣarūpaḥ padārhaḥ saṃketaviṣaya ityativiśeṣabhūto vākyārthāntargatosaṃketitatvādavācya eva yatra padārthaḥ pratipadyate tatra dūre arthāntarabhūtasya niḥśeṣacyutetyādau vidhyādeścarcā /
ananvito 'rtho 'bhihitānvaye padārthāntaramātreṇānvitastvanvitābhidhāne anvitaviśeṣastvavācya eva ityubhayanaye 'pyapadārtha eva vākyārthaḥ /
yadapyucyate naimittikānusāreṇa nimittāni kalpyante iti /
tatra nimittatvaṃ kārakatvaṃ jñāpakatvaṃ vā śabdasya / prakāśakatvānna kārakatvam / jñāpakatvaṃ tu ajñātasya katham / jñātatvañca saṃketenaiva sa cānvitamātre evaṃ ca nimittasya niyatanimittatvaṃ
yāvanna niścitaṃ tāvannaimittikasya pratītireva katham iti 'naimittikānusāreṇa nimittāni kalpyante '; ityavicāritābhidhānam /
children.translated_text: Even according to their view, the word-meaning that is the object of convention has both universal and particular form; therefore, the excessively particularized sentence-meaning, being unconventionalized, is indeed unexpressed. Where the word-meaning is understood [in its particularity] — there, for the purpose of something entirely different, there is discussion of injunction and the like in [examples like] 'complete cessation' and the like. An unconnected meaning in the <s>abhihitānvaya</s> view, but one connected with merely another word-meaning in the <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> view — the connected particular [meaning] is itself unexpressed. Thus, according to both positions, the sentence-meaning is itself a non-word-meaning. As for what is said — 'causes are posited by following effects' — therein, is the word's being a cause (<s>kārakatva</s>) or a signifier (<s>jñāpakatva</s>) [of meaning]? Being an illuminator, it is not a cause. And how can it be a signifier of what is unknown? And it is known only through convention; and that [convention] is of the connected [meaning] alone. And until the specific nature of the cause is ascertained, how can the cognition of the effect arise? — thus the statement 'causes are posited by following effects' is an unconsidered assertion.

children.text:
ye tvabhidadhati so 'yamiṣoriva dīrghadīrghataro vyāpāraḥ iti yatparaḥ śabdaḥ sa śabdārthaḥ iti vidhirevātra vācya iti / te 'pyatātparyajñāstātparyavācoyukterdevānāṃpriyāḥ / tathāhi {bhūtavyasamuccāraṇe bhūtaṃ bhavyāyopadiśyate} iti kārakapadārthāḥ kriyābhisaṇbandhāt sādhyāmānatāṃ prāpnuvanti / tataścādagdhadahananyāyena yāvadaprāptaṃ tāvadvidhīyate / yathā ṛtvikpracaraṇe pramāṇāntarāt siddhe
{lohitoṣṇīṣā ṛtvijaḥ pracaranti} ityatra lohitoṣṇīṣatvamātraṃ vidheyaṃ havanasyānyataḥ siddheḥ {dadhnā juhoti} ityādau dadhyādeḥ karaṇatvamātraṃ vidheyam //
children.translated_text: As for those who maintain: 'That function [of the word] is, like an arrow, longer and longer; what the word ultimately [reaches], that is the word-meaning; therefore the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) alone is the expressed [meaning] here' — they too, being ignorant of purport (<s>tātparya</s>), through the reasoning of purport being [only] the expressed [meaning], are [like] 'the dear ones of the gods' [i.e., fools]. For thus [in Mīmāṃsā]: 'In the utterance of what was and what will be, the past is taught for the sake of the future' — the meanings of the case-relation words (<s>kārakapadārtha</s>) attain the status of being to be accomplished through relation to the action. And then, by the principle of 'unburnt fire' [i.e., what is not yet established is enjoined], what has not yet been attained is enjoined. Just as, when the officiating priests' movement is established from another means of valid knowledge, in 'The priests move about with red turbans,' only the wearing of red turbans is enjoined, since the offering is already established [otherwise]; in 'He offers with curds' and the like, only the instrumentality of curds and the like is enjoined.

children.text: kvacidubhayavidhiḥ kvacittrividhirapi yathā {raktaṃ paṭaṃ vayaḥ} ityādau ekavidhirdvividhistrividhirvā / tataśca {yadeva vidheyaṃ tatraiva tātparyam} ityupāttasyava śabdasyārthe tātparya na tu pratītamātre evaṃ hi {pūrvo dhāvati} ityādāvaparādyathapi kvacittātparyaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Sometimes there is a double injunction, sometimes even a triple injunction — as in 'A red cloth [for weaving]' and the like, there may be a single injunction, a double, or a triple. And thus, 'The purport lies precisely in what is to be enjoined' — the purport is in the meaning of the word that has been adopted, not merely in what is cognized. For otherwise, in 'The first one runs' and the like, sometimes the purport would apply even to the latter [elements].

children.text: yattu {viṣaṃ bhakṣaya mā cānya gṛhe bhuṅkthāḥ} ityatra {etadgṛhe na bhoktavyam} ityatra tātparyamiti sa eva vākyārtha iti, ucyate tatra cakāra ekavākyatāsūcanārthaḥ na cākhyātavākyayor dvayoraṅgāṅgibhāva iti viṣabhakṣaṇavākyasya suhṛdvākyatvenāṅgatā kalpanīyeti {viṣabhakṣaṇādapi duṣṭametadgṛhe bhojanamiti sarvathā māsya gṛhe bhuṅkthāḥ} iti, upāttaśabdārthe eva tātparyam /
children.translated_text: As for [the objection regarding] 'Eat poison, and do not eat in another's house' — that the purport here is 'One should not eat in that house,' and that is the sentence-meaning — we reply: the particle 'ca' [and] there serves to indicate single-sentence status; and since there is no principal-subordinate relation between the two finite-verb sentences, the poison-eating sentence must be construed as subordinate, being a 'friendly sentence' [i.e., an expression of goodwill]; thus [the meaning is:] 'Eating in that house is worse than eating poison; therefore, in no way eat in his house' — the purport lies precisely in the meaning of the adopted word.

children.text: yadi śabdaśruterantaraṃ yāvānartho labhyate tāvati śabdasyābhidhaiva vyāpāraḥ tataḥ kathaṃ 'brāhmaṇa putraste jātaḥ brāhmaṇa kanyā te garbhiṇī'; ityādau harṣaśokādīnāmapi na vācyatvam / kasmācca lakṣaṇā lakṣaṇīye 'pyarthe dīrghadīrghatarābhidhāvyaāpāreṇaiva pratītisiddheḥ / kimiti ca śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyānāṃ pūrvapūrvabalīyastvam ityanvitābhidhānavāde 'pi vidherapi siddhaṃ vyaṅgyatvam //
children.translated_text: If the scope of the word's function of denotation extends to as much meaning as is obtained from hearing the word — then how, in [sentences like] 'O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a son has been born to you' [or] 'O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, your daughter is pregnant' — would joy, sorrow, and the like not also be expressible? And why should there be indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), when even for the indicated meaning, cognition is established through the ever-extending function of denotation? And why is there the hierarchy of strength — scripture, indicatory sign, sentence, context, position, and designation — [showing that] even in the <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> view, the suggestive nature of injunction and the rest is established?

children.text: kiṃ ca {kuru rucim} iti padayorvaiparītye kāvyāntarvartini kathaṃ duṣṭatvam / na hmatrāsabhyo 'rthaḥ padārthāntarairanvitaḥ ityanabhidheya eveti evamādi aparityājyaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, if the words of 'Do [your] pleasure' are inverted [in a poetic context], how is there faultiness? For here, the vulgar meaning, connected with other word-meanings, is simply inexpressible — such [considerations] would be irresolvable.

children.text:
yadi ca vācyavācakatvavyatirekeṇa vyaṅgyavyañjakabhāvo nābhyupeyate tadāsādhutvādīnāṃ nityadoṣatvaṃ kaṣṭatvādīnāmanityadoṣatvamiti
vibhāgakaraṇamanupapannaṃ syāt / na cānupapannaṃ sarvasyaiva vibhaktatayā pratibhāsāt / vācyavācakabhāvavyatirekeṇa vyaṅgyavyañjakatāśrayaṇe tu vyaṅgyasya bahuvidhatvāt kvacideva kasyacidevaucityenopapadyata eva vibhāgavyavasthā //
children.translated_text: And if the relation of suggested and suggestive is not accepted as distinct from the relation of expressed and expresser, then the classification that faults like bad grammar are permanent faults while faults like forced [expression] are non-permanent faults would be unjustifiable. Nor is it unjustifiable — since everything appears as differentiated. But when the relation of suggested and suggestive is accepted as distinct from the relation of expressed and expresser, then because the suggested [meaning] is manifold, the classification is indeed justified — [only] in certain cases is [each fault] justified by propriety (<s>aucitya</s>).
{'Two things have now become pitiable, through the desire for union, of the skull-bearer [<s>Śiva</s>].'}
In such [verses], why is the use of words like 'skull-bearer' (<s>kapālin</s>) suitable for poetry, unlike [the use of] words like '<s>Pinākin</s>' (bow-bearer)?

children.text:
api ca vācyo 'rthaḥ sarvān pratipattṝn prati ekarūpa eveti niyato 'sau / na hi {gatostamarkaḥ} ityādau vācyo 'rthaḥ kvacidanyathā bhavati / pratīyamānastu tattatprakaraṇavaktṛpratipattrādiviśeṣasahāyatayā nānātvaṃ
bhajate / tathā ca {gato 'stamarkaḥ} ityataḥ sapatnaṃ pratyavaskandanāvasara iti abhisaraṇamupakramyatāmiti prāptaprāyaste preyāniti karmakaraṇānnivartāmaha iti sāṃdhyo vidhirupakramyatāmiti dūraṃ mā gā iti surabhayo gṛhaṃ praveśyantāmiti saṃtāpodhunā na bhavatīti vikreyavastūni saṃhriyantāmiti nāgatodyāpi preyānityādiranavadhirvyaṅgyo 'rthaḥ tatra tatra pratibhāti /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the expressed meaning is uniform for all cognizers — it is fixed. For in 'The sun has set' and the like, the expressed meaning never differs. But the suggested meaning, with the assistance of particular context, speaker, cognizer, and the like, assumes manifoldness. Thus, from 'The sun has set,' [there can be suggested:] 'There is now an opportunity for attacking the co-wife'; 'Let the [secret] rendezvous be commenced'; 'Your beloved has nearly arrived'; 'Let us cease from our work'; 'Let the evening rites be commenced'; 'Do not go far'; 'Let the cows be driven home'; 'The heat is now no more'; 'Let the goods for sale be gathered'; 'The beloved has not come even yet' — and so on, the suggested meaning, without limit, shines forth in each [context].
(<s>Bhartṛhari</s>'s <s>Śṛṅgāraśataka</s> 36)
In such [verses], through a [suggested] determination lying between doubt, the tranquil [rasa], and the erotic [rasa];

children.text:
{kathamavanipa darpo yanniśātāsidhārā-
  dalanagalitamūrdhnā vidviṣāṃ svīkṛtā śrīḥ /
  nanu tava nihatārerapyasau kiṃ na nītā
  tridivamapagatāṅgairvallabhā kīrtirebhiḥ //134//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{'How is it pride, O king, when the glory [of your enemies]
was accepted by cutting off their heads with sharp sword-edges?
Surely, even the beloved fame of your slain enemy —
was she not led to heaven by these dismembered limbs? //134//'}
In such [verses], through the form of censure-praise, [there is suggestion] of the intrinsic nature [of things].

children.text: pūrvapaścādbhāvena pratīteḥ kālasya śabdāśrayatvena śabdatadekadeśatadarthavarṇaghaṭanāśrayatvena ca āśrayasya śabdānuśāsabajñānena prakaraṇādisahāyapratibhānairmalyasahitena tena cāvagama iti nimittasya boddhṛmātravidagdhavyapadeśayoḥ pratītimātracamatkṛtyośca karaṇāt kāryasya "gato 'stamarkaḥ" ityādau pradarśitanayena saṃkhyāyāḥ
children.translated_text: The cognition occurs through prior-and-posterior temporal sequence, through time's being word-dependent, through its being dependent on word, word-part, word-meaning, and syllable-composition as its locus, through the intelligence of grammatical knowledge, accompanied by the clarity of contextual and other auxiliary insights — this is the means. By virtue of the designability as 'one learned in discernment alone' of the cognizer, and by virtue of causing mere cognition and wonder (<s>camatkṛti</s>) — this is the effect. By the method demonstrated in 'The sun has set' and the like, regarding the number —

children.text:
{kassa va ṇa ho-i roso daṭṭhūṇa pi-ā-i savvaṇaṃ aharaṃ /
  sabhamarapaḍamagdhā-iṇi vāri-avāme sahasu eṇhiṃ //135//}
[kasya vā na bhavati roṣo dṛṣṭvā priyāyā savraṇamaṣaram /
children.translated_text: [Whose anger does not arise upon seeing the beloved's face all scratched?
O [woman who] smells lotuses with bees [alighting on them], [now] invited to the bed, stop the prohibition of entry!]
(<s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s>)

children.text:
ityādau sakhītatkāntādigatatvena viṣayasya ca bhede 'pi yadyekatvam tat kvacidapi nīlapītādau bhedo na syāt /
uktaṃ hi {ayameva hi bhedo bhedaheturvā yadviruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ kāraṇabhedaśca} iti /
children.translated_text: In such [verses], even though there is a distinction in the domain — [namely] through [the subject] being a female friend, her particular lover, and the like — if there were unity [of meaning], then even in [distinguishing] blue from yellow and the like, there would be no distinction. For it has been said: 'This itself is the distinction or the cause of distinction — the superimposition of contrary properties, and the difference of causes.'
(<s>Jñānaśrīmitra</s>'s <s>Nibandha</s>, Chapter on Momentary Destruction)

{'Of whom does anger not arise, seeing the beloved's face all scratched?
O [you who smell] lotuses with bees [on them], invited to the bed — [stop] the prohibition of entering now! //135//'}

children.text:
vācakānāmarthāpekṣā vyañjakānāṃ tu na tadapekṣatvamiti na vācakatvameva vyañjakatvam / kiṃ ca {vāṇīrakuḍaṅgu} -- ityādau pratīyamānamarthamabhivyajya vācyaṃ svarūpa eva yatra viśrāmyati tatra
guṇībhūtavyaṅgyetātparybhūto 'pyarthaḥ svaśabdānabhidheyaḥ pratītipathamavataran kasya vyāpārasya viṣayatāmavalambatāmiti /
nanu {rāmo 'smi sarvaṃ sahe} iti {rāmeṇa priyajīvitena tu kṛtaṃ
premṇaḥ priye nocitam} iti {rāmo 'sau bhuvaneṣu vikramaguṇaiḥ prāptaḥ prasiddhiṃ parām} ityādau lakṣaṇīyo 'pyartho nānātvaṃ bhajate viśeṣavyapadeśahetuśca bhavati / tadavagamaśca śabdārthāyattaḥ
prakaraṇādisavyapekṣaśca iti ko 'yaṃ nūtanaḥ pratīyamāno nāma /
children.translated_text: Denotative words depend on [specific] meanings, but suggestive words do not have that dependence — therefore, suggestiveness is not just denotativeness. Moreover, in [Prakrit verses like] 'vāṇīrakuḍaṅgu' and the like, where the suggested meaning is manifested and the expressed [meaning] rests in its own form, in subordinated suggestion (<s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>), even a meaning that is the purport, being inexpressible by its own word, descending into the path of cognition — of which function's domain does it become [the object]? [The objection:] 'But in [examples like] "I am <s>Rāma</s>, I endure all" and "By <s>Rāma</s>, who holds life dear, love has not been properly shown to the beloved" and "That <s>Rāma</s> who has attained supreme fame in the worlds through the quality of valor" — even the indicated meaning assumes manifoldness and becomes the basis for particular designation; and its comprehension depends on word and meaning and requires context and the like as auxiliaries — so what is this new [category] called the suggested meaning?'

children.text: ucyate ---- lakṣaṇīyasyārthasya nānātve 'pi anekārthaśabdābhidheyavanniyatatvameva / na khalu mukhyenārthenāniyatasaṃbandho lakṣayituṃ śakyate / pratīyamānastu prakaraṇādiviśeṣavaśena niyata saṃbandhaḥ aniyatasaṃbandhaḥ saṃbaddhasaṃbandhaśca dyotyate /
children.translated_text: We reply: even though the indicated meaning is manifold, it is fixed, like the denotation of a word with multiple meanings. For one whose relation with the primary meaning is not fixed cannot indicate. But the suggested meaning, through the particularity of context and the like, is sometimes of fixed relation, sometimes of unfixed relation, and sometimes of relation-to-relation — it is evoked.
And not —

children.text:
{attā ettha ṇimajja-i ettha ahaṃ di-aha-e palo-ehi /
  mā pahi-a ratti-andha-a sejjā-e maha ṇimajjahisi //136//}

children.translated_text: [The mother-in-law sinks [in sleep] right there; here am I — look [at me] during the daytime!
O traveler, [though] blind in the night darkness, do not sink into our bed!]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 7.67)

{'The mother-in-law sinks [in sleep] right there; here am I — look at me during the day!
O traveler, [though] blind in the night darkness, do not sink into our bed! //136//'}

children.text:
ityādu vivakṣitānyaparavācye dhvanau mukhyārthabādhaḥ / tatkathamatra lakṣaṇā / lakṣaṇāyāmapi vyañjanamavaśyamāśrayitavyamiti pratipāditam /
yathā ca samayasavyapekṣā abhidhā tathā mukhyārthabādhāditrayasamayaviśeṣasavyapekṣā lakṣaṇā / ata evābhidhāpucchabhūtā setyāhuḥ /
na ca lakṣaṇātmakameva dhvananaṃ tadanugamena tasya darśanāt / na ca tadanugatameva abhidhāvalambanenāpi tasya bhāvāt / na cobhayānusāryeva avācakavarṇānusāreṇāpi tasya dṛṣṭeḥ / na ca śabdānusāryeva aśabdātmakanetratribhāgāvalokanādigatatvenāpi tasya prasiddheḥ iti abhidhātātparyalakṣaṇātmakavyāpāratrayātivartī dhvananādiparyāyo vyāpāronapahnavanīya eva //
children.translated_text: and so on — in <s>dhvani</s> where the intended meaning is other than the apparent secondary meaning (<s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya</s>), the primary meaning is blocked. How then can there be <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) here? It has been demonstrated that even in [the case of] <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, suggestion (<s>vyañjana</s>) must necessarily be resorted to. And just as <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) depends on convention, so <s>lakṣaṇā</s> depends on a particular convention involving the triad of primary-meaning-blockage and the rest. Therefore they say it is the tail-end of <s>abhidhā</s>. But the act of suggesting is not merely of the nature of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, for it is seen to follow that [denotation too]. Nor does it merely follow that, for it occurs even with the support of denotation. Nor does it merely follow both, for it is seen to follow even non-denotative phonemes. Nor does it merely follow words, for it is well-known to pertain even to non-verbal [phenomena] such as glances, a third of the eye, and the like. Therefore, the verbal operation synonymous with 'suggesting' (<s>dhvanana</s>) and the like, which transcends the three operations of denotation, purport, and indication, cannot be denied.

children.text: tatra {attā ettha} ityādau niyatasaṃbandhaḥ {kasya va ṇa ho-i roso} ityādau, aniyatasaṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, in [the verse] '<s>attā ettha</s>' and the like, the relation [between suggestive and suggested] is invariable (<s>niyata</s>); in '<s>kasya va ṇa hoi roso</s>' and the like, it is variable (<s>aniyata</s>).

children.text:
{viparī-ara-e lacchī bamhaṃ daṭaṭhūṇa ṇāhikamalaṭṭhaṃ /
  hariṇo dāhiṇaṇa-aṇaṃ rasā-ulā jhatti ḍhakke-i //137//}

children.translated_text: [In the inverted love-posture, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, seeing <s>Brahmā</s> seated on the navel-lotus,
overwhelmed with passion, hastily covers the right eye of <s>Hari</s>.]
(<s>Hāla's</s> <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 816)
{In the inverted love-posture, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, seeing <s>Brahmā</s> seated on the navel-lotus,

children.text:
ityādau saṃbaddhasaṃbandhaḥ / atra hi haripadena dakṣiṇanayanasya sūryātmakatā vyajyate . tannimīlanena sūryāstamayaḥ / tena padmasya saṃkocaḥ / tato brahmaṇaḥ sthaganam / tatra sati go 'pyāṅgasyādarśanena aniryantraṇaṃ nidhuvanavilasitamiti /
{akhaṇḍabuddhinirgrāhyo vākyārtha eva vācyaḥ vākyameva ca vācakam} //
children.translated_text: In this and similar cases, the relation [between suggestive and suggested] is connected-relation (<s>saṃbaddhasaṃbandha</s>). For here, through the word '<s>Hari</s>,' the sun-nature of the right eye is suggested. From closing that eye, the sunset [is implied]. From that, the closing of the lotus. From that, the concealment of <s>Brahmā</s>. And that being so, from the invisibility of even a limb of the body, uninhibited love-play [is implied]. 'The sentence-meaning, grasped by an undivided cognition, is alone the expressed meaning, and the sentence alone is the expressor.'
(<s>Bṛhaddevī</s>)

children.text: iti ye 'pyāhuḥ tairapyavidyāpadapatitaiḥ padapadārthakalpanā kartavyaiveti tatpakṣe 'pyavaśyamuktodāharaṇādau vidhyādirvyaṅgya eva /
children.translated_text: Even those who say this — even they, having fallen into the state of ignorance, must necessarily posit the construction of word-meanings. Even in their view, in examples such as those cited above, injunctions and the like are necessarily suggested.

children.text: nanu vācyādasaṃbaddhaṃ tāvanna pratīyate yataḥ kutaścit yasya kasyacidarthasya pratīteḥ prasaṅgāt / evaṃ ca saṃbandhāt vyaṅgyavyañjakabhāvopratibandhevaśyaṃ na bhavatīti vyāptatvena niyatadharminiṣṭhatvena ca trirūpālliṅgālliṅgijñānamanumānaṃ yat tadrūpaḥ paryavasyati / tathāhi----
children.translated_text: Now, that which is unconnected with the expressed meaning is not cognized, since there would be the unwanted consequence that any meaning whatsoever would be cognized from anything. And thus, because of the relation, the connection of suggested and suggestive is not invariably blocked — therefore, it terminates in the form of inference (<s>anumāna</s>), which is the knowledge of the inferable from the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) that is triform [i.e., satisfying the triple condition: pervasion, presence in the locus, and absence from contrary cases]. That is to say:

children.text:
{bhama dhammi-a vīsaddho so suṇa-o ajja māri-o teṇa /
  golāṇa-ikacchakuḍaṅgavāsiṇā dari-asīheṇa //138//}

children.translated_text: [Roam about, O righteous one, without fear — that dog has been killed today by him,
the fierce lion dwelling in the thickets on the bank of the <s>Godāvarī</s>.] ||138||}
(<s>Hāla's</s> <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 175 [2.75])
{Roam about, O righteous one, without fear — that dog has been killed today by him,

children.text: atra gṛhe śvanivṛttyā bhramaṇaṃ vihitaṃ godāvarītīre siṃhopalabdherabhramaṇamanumāpayati / yat yata bhīrubhramaṇaṃ tattadbhayakāraṇanivṛttyupalabdhipūrvakaṃ godāvarītīre ca siṃhopalabdhiriti vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the instruction to roam about due to the removal of the dog at home makes one infer the impossibility of roaming on the bank of the <s>Godāvarī</s> due to the existence of a lion there. [The inference would be:] whatever fearful roaming there is, that is preceded by the perception of the removal of its cause of fear; and there is the perception of a lion on the bank of the <s>Godāvarī</s> — this is the apprehension of [something] contradictory to the pervader.

children.text:
atrocyate ---- bhīrurapi guroḥ prabhorvā nideśena priyānurāgeṇa anyena caivaṃbhūtena hetunā satyapi bhayakāraṇe bhramatītyanaikāntiko hetuḥśuno bibhyadapi bīratvena siṃhānna bibhetīti viruddho 'pi godāvarītīre
siṃhasadbhāvaḥ pratyakṣādanumānādvā na niścitaḥ / api tu vacanāt / na ca vacanasya prāmāṇyamasti /
arthenāpratibandhādityaasiddhaśca tatkathamevaṃvidhāddheyoḥ sādhyasiddhiḥ /
tathā {niḥśeṣacyuta- } ityādau gamakatayā yāni candanacyavanādīnyupāttāni tāni kāraṇāntarato 'pi bhavanti / ataścātraiva snānakāryatvenoktānīti nopabhoge eva pratibaddhānītyanaikāntikāni /
vyaktivādinā cādhamapadasahāyānāmeṣāṃ vyañjakatvamuktam / na cātrādhamatvaṃ pramāṇapratipannamiti kathamanumānam / evaṃvidhādarthādevaṃvidho 'rtha upapattyanapekṣatve 'pi prakāśate iti vyaktivādinaḥ punastat adūṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: To this we reply: even a timid person roams about in a place where there is cause for fear, due to the command of a teacher or master, or due to the pull of love for a beloved, or due to some other such cause — thus the inferential mark is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). [Moreover,] although fearing the dog, one may not fear the lion, through courage — thus [the mark] is also contradicted. The existence of a lion on the bank of the <s>Godāvarī</s> has not been ascertained either by perception or by inference, but only through statement. And the statement has no probative authority. And [the mark] is also unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), since it is not established that it is invariably connected with the meaning. How then can the establishment of the thing to be proved proceed from such an inferential mark? Similarly, in [the verse] '<s>niḥśeṣacyuta-</s>' and the like, the items such as the disappearance of sandal paste that are taken up as indicators can arise from other causes too. And precisely here they have been stated as effects of bathing — thus they are not invariably connected with [amorous] enjoyment alone, and are therefore inconclusive. The proponent of <s>vyakti</s> (manifestation) has also stated that the suggestiveness of these belongs to [words] accompanied by the word '<s>adhama</s>' (scoundrel). But the scoundrel-hood here is not established by a means of valid cognition — so how can there be inference? From just such a meaning, just such a meaning shines forth, even without dependence on logical proof — this is the position of the <s>vyaktivādin</s> (proponent of manifestation [theory]). And that [objection] is no refutation [of his view].
Thus in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, the fifth <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter), named 'The Determination of the Distinction between <s>Dhvani</s>, <s>Guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, and Mixed Types.' || 5 ||
The two types of <s>kāvya</s> previously exemplified as verbal artifice (<s>śabdacitra</s>) and content artifice (<s>arthacitra</s>) —
therein, the position of <s>citra</s> (artifice) in content and in word is [determined] by the predominance of <s>guṇa</s> (quality). || MKpr-K_48 ||

children.text: na tu śabdacitre arthasyācitratvamarthacitre vā śabdasya / tathā coktam
children.translated_text: But it is not the case that in verbal artifice the content is without artifice, or that in content artifice the word is [without artifice]. As has been stated:
{Figures of speech such as <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and the rest — stated by others in many ways —
even a beautiful face of a woman does not shine without ornaments.
Others call <s>rūpaka</s> and the rest external ornament,

children.text: supāṃ tiṅāṃ ca vyutpattiṃ vācāṃ vāñchantyalaṅkṛtim //
children.translated_text: and desire the derivation of nominal and verbal forms as the [true] adornment of speech.
This is what they call elegance of expression (<s>sauśabdya</s>); [they say] the derivation of meaning is not of this kind.
The twofold [adornment] — of word and of denoted meaning — has been taught to us as [comprising] <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament) and the rest.}
Thus.
An example of verbal artifice (<s>śabdacitra</s>):

children.text:
{prathamamaruṇacchāyastāvattataḥ kanakaprabha-
  stadanu virahottāmyattanvīkapolataladyutiḥ /
  udayati tato dhvāntadhvaṃsakṣamaḥ kṣaṇadāmukhe
  sarasabisinīkandacchedacchavirmṛgalāñchanaḥ //139//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>, <s>Mālinīmādhava</s>)

{First of a reddish hue, then of a golden radiance, then of the complexion of the cheek of a slender woman fainting in separation — then at the face of the night, capable of destroying darkness, with the lustre of a freshly cut lotus stalk, the moon-marked one rises. ||139||}
An example of content artifice (<s>arthacitra</s>):

children.text:
{te dṛṣṭimātrapatitā api kasya nātra
  kṣobhāya pakṣmaladṛśāmalakāḥ khalāśca /
  nīcāḥ sadaiva savilāsamalīkalagnā
  ye kālatāṃ kuṭilatāmiva na tyajanti //140//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Even at the mere fall of a glance, who is not here disturbed by those with lash-laden eyes — the <s>āmalakas</s> (emblic myrobalans) and the wicked? The lowly, always clinging playfully with deceit, who never give up their blackness and crookedness! ||140||}

children.text: yadyapi sarvatra kāvyentataḥ vibhāvādirūpatayaiva paryavasānaṃ tathāpi sphuṭasya rasasyānupalambhādavyaṅgyametatkāvyadvayamuktam / atra ca śabdārthālaṅkārabhedādbahavo bhedāḥ te cālaṅkāranirṇaye nirṇeṣyante //
children.translated_text: Although in all <s>kāvya</s> the ultimate resolution is in the form of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and the rest, nevertheless, because of the non-apprehension of explicit <s>rasa</s>, these two types of <s>kāvya</s> are called 'without suggestion' (<s>avyaṅgya</s>). And here, there are many subdivisions based on the distinction of figures of word and meaning — and those will be determined in the section on the determination of <s>alaṅkāras</s>.

children.text: iti kāvyaprakāśe śabdārthacitranirūpaṇaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭha ullāsaḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, the sixth <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter), named 'The Examination of Verbal and Content Artifice.' || 6 ||
Now the seventh <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter).
Having determined the essential nature of <s>kāvya</s>, he states the general definition of <s>doṣas</s> (defects):
<s>Doṣa</s> (defect) is the impairment of the primary meaning; and <s>rasa</s> is primary — from dependence on it, the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>) [is primary];

children.text: ubhayopayoginaḥ syuḥ śabdādyāstena teṣvapi saḥ // MKpr-K_49 //
children.translated_text: words and the rest serve both — therefore, [defect applies] in them too. || MKpr-K_49 ||
'Impairment' (<s>hati</s>) means diminishment. 'Words and the rest' — by the inclusion of 'and the rest,' [this includes defects] in the arrangement of phonemes. He states the specific definitions:
A word is defective [when it is]: harsh-sounding (<s>śrutikaṭu</s>), deviating from grammatical rules (<s>cyutasaṃskṛti</s>), unused (<s>aprayukta</s>), incapable (<s>asamartha</s>),

of destroyed meaning (<s>nihatārtha</s>), of inappropriate meaning (<s>anucitārtha</s>), meaningless (<s>nirarthaka</s>), non-denotative (<s>avācaka</s>), and threefold indecent (<s>aślīla</s>). || MKpr-K_50 ||
Ambiguous (<s>sandigdha</s>), unfamiliar (<s>apratīta</s>), vulgar (<s>grāmya</s>), requiring interpretation (<s>neyārtha</s>), and also forced (<s>kliṣṭa</s>),
with the predicate-portion unexamined (<s>avimṛṣṭavidheyāṃśa</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddhamati</s>), and excessively compounded (<s>atikṛtsamāsa</s>). || MKpr-K_51 ||
(1) '<s>Śrutikaṭu</s>' (harsh-sounding) — defective by having the form of harsh phonemes. For example:

children.text:
{anaṅgamangalagṛhāpāṅgabhaṅgitaraṅgitaiḥ /
  āliṅgitaḥ sa tanvaṅgyā kārtārthyaṃ labhate kadā //141//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s>)
{When will he, embraced by the slender-limbed one with the waves of the corner-glances of the auspicious abode of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of love), attain fulfillment? ||141||}
Here, the word '<s>kārtārthyam</s>' [is harsh-sounding].
(2) '<s>Cyutasaṃskṛti</s>' (deviating from grammatical rules) — lacking the characteristics prescribed by grammar. For example:

children.text:
{etanmandavipakvatindukaphalaśyāmodarāpāṇḍara-
  prāntaṃ hanta pulindasundarakarasparśakṣamaṃ labhyate /
  tat pallīpatiputri kuñjarakulaṃ kumbhābhayābhyarthanā-
  dīnaṃ tvāmanunāthate kucayugaṃ patrāvṛtaṃ mā kṛthāḥ //142//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{This [breast], dark on the belly like the fruit of a barely ripened <s>tinduka</s> tree, whitish at the edges — alas! — fit for the touch of the hand of a beautiful <s>Pulinda</s> (tribal) man — therefore, O daughter of the village chief, the herd of elephants, distressed with longing for your pot-like [breasts], entreats you — do not cover your pair of breasts with a leaf! ||142||}

children.text:
atrānunāthate iti / {sarpiṣo nāthate} ityādāvāśiṣyeva nāthaterātmanepadaṃ vihitam / {āśiṣi nāthaḥ} iti /
atra tu yācanamarthaḥ / tasmāt {anunāthati stanayugam} iti paṭhanīyam /
children.translated_text: Here, the [defective form is] '<s>anunāthate</s>.' In [<s>Pāṇini's</s> rule] '<s>sarpiṣo nāthate</s>' and the like, the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) of <s>nāth</s> is prescribed only in the sense of a benediction (<s>āśiṣ</s>). The [rule is] '<s>āśiṣi nāthaḥ</s>.' But here the meaning is entreaty. Therefore, the correct reading should be '<s>anunāthati stanayugam</s>' [with the <s>parasmaipada</s> (active voice)].
(3) '<s>Aprayukta</s>' (unused) — though recorded [in grammar], not employed by poets. For example:

children.text:
{yathāyaṃ dāruṇācāraḥ sarvadaiva vibhāvyate /
  tathā manye daivato 'sya piśāco rākṣaso 'tha vā //143//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{Since this [person] of cruel conduct is always perceived [to be so], I believe that either by fate he is a <s>piśāca</s> (goblin) or a <s>rākṣasa</s> (demon). ||143||}

children.text: atra daivataśabdo {daivatāni puṃsi vā} iti puṃsyāmnāto 'pi na kenacitprayujyate //
children.translated_text: Here, the word '<s>daivata</s>' — though recorded in the masculine by [the rule] '<s>daivatāni puṃsi vā</s>' — is not used by anyone [in that form].

children.text: (4) {asamarthaṃ} yattadarthaṃ paṭhyate na ca tatrāsya śaktiḥ / yathā
children.translated_text: (4) '<s>Asamartha</s>' (incapable) — that which is read in a particular meaning but has no capacity for that [meaning]. For example:

children.text:
{tīrthāntareṣu snānena samupārjitasatkṛtiḥ /
  surasrotasvinīmeṣa hanti saṃprati sādaram //144//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka's</s> <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)
{Having acquired merit through bathing at other <s>tīrthas</s> (pilgrimage sites), this one approaches the celestial river with reverence now. ||144||}
Here, '<s>hanti</s>' is [used] in the sense of 'going' [for which it is incapable].
(5) '<s>Nihatārtha</s>' (of destroyed meaning) — that which, having two meanings, is used in an unfamiliar meaning. For example:

children.text:
{yāvakarasārdrapādaprahāraśoṇitakacena dayitena /
  mugdhā sādhvasataralā vilokya paricumbitā sahasā //145//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 77)
{The innocent one, trembling with modesty, was suddenly kissed, upon seeing her beloved with his hair reddened by the blow of [her] foot moist with <s>yāvaka</s> (lac-dye). ||145||}
Here, the meaning of the word '<s>śoṇita</s>' — whose intended sense is 'reddened' — is blocked by the sense characterized as 'blood.'
(6) '<s>Anucitārtha</s>' (of inappropriate meaning) — for example:

children.text:
{tapasvibhiryā sucireṇa labhyate prayatnataḥ sattribhiriṣyate ca yā /
  prayānti tāmāśu gatiṃ yaśasvino raṇāśvamedhepaśutāmupāgatāḥ //146//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Mahimabhaṭṭa's</s> <s>Vyaktiviveka</s>)

{That state which ascetics attain after a very long time, and which is desired with effort by the virtuous — to that state do the glorious ones quickly proceed, those who have assumed the condition of sacrificial victims in battle and in the <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice). ||146||}
Here, the word '<s>paśu</s>' (animal/victim) connotes cowardice — hence it is of inappropriate meaning.
(7) '<s>Nirarthaka</s>' (meaningless) — a word like '<s>ca</s>' and '<s>ādi</s>' serving merely to fill the metrical foot (<s>pādapūraṇa</s>). For example:

children.text:
{utphullakamalakesaraparāgagauradyute mama hi gauri /
  abhivāñchitaṃ prasiddhyatu bhagavati yuṣmatprasādena //147//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Harṣa's</s> <s>Nāgānanda</s> 1.14)
{O <s>Gaurī</s>, radiant with the lustre of the pollen of blossoming lotus stamens — indeed, O Blessed One, may my desire be fulfilled by your grace! ||147||}
Here, the word '<s>hi</s>' [is meaningless, serving only as a filler].
(8) '<s>Avācaka</s>' (non-denotative) — for example:

children.text:
{avandhyakopasya vihanturāpadāṃ bhavanti vaśyāḥ svayameva dehinaḥ /
  amarṣaśūnyena janasya jantunā na jātahārdena na vidviṣādaraḥ //148//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhāravi's</s> <s>Kirātārjunīya</s> 1.33)

{The beings naturally become obedient to one whose anger is never fruitless, the destroyer of calamities; but by one devoid of indignation, a mere creature, in whom no affection has arisen, the enemy is not respected. ||148||}

children.text: atra jantupadamadātaryarthe vivakṣitaṃ tatra ca nābhidhāyakam / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, the word '<s>jantu</s>' (creature) is intended in the sense of 'ungrateful one,' but it does not denote that meaning. Or alternatively:

children.text:
{hādhika sā kila tāmasī śaśimukhī dṛṣṭā mayā yatra sā
  tadvicchedarujāndhakāritamidaṃ dagdhaṃ dinaṃ kalpitam /
  kiṃ kurmaḥ kuśale sadaiva vidhuro dhātā na cettatkathaṃ
  tādṛgyāmavatīmayo bhavati me no jīvalokodhunā //149//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Alas, too much! It was indeed on that dark night that the moon-faced one was seen by me — in the darkness produced by the agony of separation from her, this accursed day has been devised! What shall we do? Fate is always hostile to the well-being [of lovers] — but if not so, then how does it come about that I have such a disease as the <s>Yamāvatī</s> fever? There is no world of the living for me now! ||149||}
Here, '<s>dina</s>' (day) is [intended to be] denotative in the sense of 'that which consists of light,' [but fails to convey the intended meaning clearly].
And that which, through association with a prefix, has shifted to another meaning — for example:

children.text:
{jaṅghākāṇḍorunālo nakhakiraṇalasatjesarālīkarālaḥ
  pratyagrālaktakābhāprasarakisakayo mañjumañjīrabhṛṅga /
  bharturnṛttānukāre jayati nijatanusvacchalāvaṇyavāpī-
  saṃbhūtāmbhojaśobhāṃ vidadhadabhibavo daṇḍapādo bhavānyāḥ //150//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Mahimabhaṭṭa's</s> <s>Vyaktiviveka</s>)

{With the shank as its stem, the thigh as its stalk, with nails' rays as a row of glittering filaments, with the luster of fresh lac-dye spreading on [her] slender body, with charming anklets as bees — in the imitation of the dance of her lord, surpassing the beauty of a lotus born in the limpid pool of her own body's loveliness — the raised foot of <s>Bhavānī</s> is triumphant! ||150||}
Here, '<s>vidadhat</s>' is [used] where '<s>dadhat</s>' (holding) is the [intended] meaning [but the prefix <s>vi-</s> shifts the sense].
(9) '<s>Aślīla</s>' (indecent) — 'threefold' because of connoting modesty, disgust, or ill-omen. For example:

children.text:
{sādhanaṃ sumahadyasya yannānyasya vilokyate /
  tasya dhīśālinaḥ ko 'nyaḥ sahatārālitāṃ bhruvam //151//(1)}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s>)
{He whose means is very great, which is not seen in another — who else can endure the arching of the brow of that wise one? ||151|| (1)}

children.text:
{līlātāmarasāhato 'nyavanitāniḥśaṅkadaṣṭādharaḥ
  kaścvitkesaradūṣitekṣaṇa iva vyāmīlya netre sthitaḥ /
  mugdhā kuḍmalitānanena dadatī vāyuṃ sthitā tatra sā
  bhrāntyā dhūrtatayātha vānatimṛtetenāniśañcumbitā //152//(2)}
  ([Amaruśataka 72(or 70),or 88)])
children.translated_text: 'Struck by a playful lotus, bitten confidently on the lip by another woman, some [man], as if his eyes were soiled by [her] filaments, remained standing with eyes closed. The naive girl, with her face bud-like, stood offering him air [to cool him]; whether through confusion or through craftiness, she was kissed by him unceasingly, without the bowing down [she expected].' //152// (2) (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 72 or 88)

children.text:
{mṛdupavanavibhinno matptriyāyā vināśād
  ghanarucirakalāpo niḥsapatno 'dya jātaḥ /
  rativigalitabandhe keśapāśe sukeśyāḥ
  sati kusumasanāthe kaṃ haredeṣa barhī //153//(3)}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 4.22)

'Broken by the gentle breeze, the peacock with his thick and beautiful crest of feathers, now unchallenged today through the destruction of my beloved — when the beautiful-haired one's hair-braid, loosened in love-making, is adorned with flowers, whom would this peacock charm?' //153// (3)
In these, the words 'means,' 'wind,' and 'destruction' are suggestive of modesty and the like.
(10) Ambiguous (<s>saṃdigdha</s>) — an example:

children.text:
{āliṅgitastatrabhavān saṃparāye jayaśriyā /
  āśīḥparaṃparāṃ vandyāṃ karṇe kṛtvā kṛpāṃ kuru //154//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s>)
'Your honor was embraced by the goddess of victory in battle; having placed to the ear the venerable succession of blessings, please be gracious!' //154//

children.text: atra vandyāṃ kiṃ haṭhahṛtamahilāyāṃ kiṃ vā namasyāmiti saṃdehaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here [the word] <s>vandyā</s> creates doubt: is it a woman seized by force, or does it mean 'worthy of salutation'?
(11) Unfamiliar (<s>apratīta</s>) — that which is well-known only in [specialized] treatises. An example:
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'For one who abides in the splitting of the storehouses [of karma], endowed with the great light of right knowledge — even this [action], though being performed, does not become the bondage of <s>karma</s>.' //155//
(12) Vulgar (<s>grāmya</s>) — that which is established only in common parlance. An example:

children.text:
{rākāvibhāvarīkāntasaṃkrāntadyuti te mukham /
  tapanīyaśilāśobhā kaṭiśca harate manaḥ //156//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 86)
'Your face, with the radiance transferred from the beloved of the full-moon night, and your waist (<s>kaṭi</s>), with the beauty of golden stone — these steal the mind.' //156//
Here, the word <s>kaṭi</s> (waist/hip) [is vulgar].
(13) Having a secondary meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>):
'Some conventional secondary meanings (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) are well-established and function like primary denotation through capacity;
some are freshly created, and some are not [used] at all, due to incapacity.'
(<s>Kumārila</s>, <s>Tantravārttika</s> Pūrva 700)
Thus, that which is a prohibited secondary meaning. An example:
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'Your face, O slender one, makes the beloved of the full-moon night of the autumn season into a guest of a slap.' //157//
Here, through 'being a guest of a slap,' what is indicated is being defeated [by her face's beauty].

children.text: atha samāsagatameva duṣṭamiti saṃbandhaḥ, anyat kevalaṃ samāsagataṃ ca //
children.translated_text: Now, the connection [is]: that which occurs in a compound alone is faulty; the others [may be faulty] either alone or in a compound.
(14) Strained (<s>kliṣṭa</s>) — where the comprehension of meaning is obstructed. An example:
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'O king, your conduct shines as befitting [those] that are radiant with the rising of the light of [the moon] born from the eye of <s>Atri</s>.' //158//
Here, the meaning is: 'radiant with the light-clusters (kumudas/night-lotuses)' — that is, the radiance of the moonrise of the moon born from the eye of <s>Atri</s>.

children.text: (15) {avimṛṣṭavidheyāṃśam} avimṛṣṭaḥ prādhānyenānirdiṣṭo vidheyāṃśo yatra tat / yathā
children.translated_text: (15) With unexamined predicate (<s>avimṛṣṭavidheyāṃśa</s>) — where the predicate-portion is not stated with prominence. An example:

children.text:
{mūrddhnāmudvṛttakṛttāviralagalagaladraktasaṃsaktadhārā-
  dhauteśāṅghriprasādopanatajayajagajjātamithyāmahimnām /
  kailāsollāsanecchāvyatikarapiśunotsarpidarpoddhurāṇāṃ
  doṣṇāṃ caiṣāṃ kimetat phalamiha nagarīrakṣaṇe yat prayāsaḥ //159//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Harṣa</s>'s <s>Nāgānanda</s> 8)

'From the washing of the feet of <s>Īśa</s> (the Lord) by the unbroken streams of dense, dripping, red blood from the heads severed in battle — these [enemies] whose falsely assumed greatness consists in the world-conquest attained through the grace of those [washed feet], whose swelling pride, revealed by the endeavor of desire for the delight of [shaking] <s>Kailāsa</s>, is subdued — what fruit is this exertion of these arms of theirs in the guarding of the city?' //159//

children.text: atra mithyāmahimatvaṃ nānuvādyam api tu vidheyam / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, 'having false greatness' is not the topic [given] but rather the predicate [to be stated]. Or again:

children.text:
{srastāṃ nitambādavaropayantī punaḥ punaḥ kesaradāmakāñcīm /
  nyāsīkṛtāṃ sthānavidā smareṇa dvitīyamaurvīmiva kārmukasya //160//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 3.55)

'Repeatedly pulling down the girdle of filament-garlands slipping from her hips, [<s>Pārvatī</s> stood] — that [girdle] placed there by <s>Smara</s> (the Love-god), who knows the proper place, as if it were a second bowstring for his bow.' //160//

children.text: atra dvitīyatvamātramutprekṣyam / maurvīṃ dvitīyāmiti yuktaḥ pāṭhaḥ / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, only the 'secondness' is to be fancied [as the predicate]. 'A second bowstring' is the correct reading. Or again:

children.text:
{vapurvirūpākṣamalakṣyajanmatā digambaratvena niveditaṃ vasu /
  vareṣu yadbālamṛgākṣi mṛgyate tadasti kiṃ vyastamapi trilocane //161//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 5.12)

'O <s>Virūpākṣa</s> (the Odd-Eyed One)! Your form — unperceived in birth, sky-clad — [thus] you have displayed your wealth. O fawn-eyed maiden, that which is sought in a suitor — does all that exist even when distributed in the Three-Eyed One?' //161//

children.text: atra {alakṣitā janiḥ} iti vācyam / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, [the predicate] to be stated is 'whose birth is unperceived.' Or again:

children.text:
{ānandasindhuraticāpalaśālicitta-
  saṃdānanaikasadanaṃ kṣaṇamapyamuktā /
  yā sarvadaiva bhavatā tadudantacintā
  tāntiṃ tanoti tava saṃprati dhigdhigasmān //162//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'The thought of your [departure], which is the sole abode for restraining the exceedingly restless and lively mind, [which is] an ocean of bliss, and which was never released even for a moment by you always — that thought now produces weariness in you. Shame, shame upon us!' //162//

children.text: atra {na muktā} iti saṃnaddho 'yaṃ vidheyaḥ / yathā
children.translated_text: Here, 'was never released' — this is the predicate, [meaning] 'he is prepared.' An example:

children.text:
{navajaladharaḥ saṃnaddho 'yaṃ na dṛptaniśācaraḥ
  suradhanuridaṃ dūrākṛṣṭaṃ na tasya śarāsanam /
  ayamapi paṭurdhārāsāro na bāṇaparaṃparā
  kanakanikaṣasnigdhā vidyut priyā na mamorvaśī //163//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 4.7)

'This is a new rain-cloud that has appeared — not a fierce demon; this is the rainbow stretched from afar — not his bow; this too is a sharp shower of rain — not a volley of arrows; and this golden touchstone-smooth lightning is [my] beloved — not <s>Urvaśī</s>.' //163//
In this verse, through the reiteration of 'not that [thing],' nothing else is predicated beyond [the denial].
(<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 1.21)
