'He guarded himself without fear, he pursued <s>dharma</s> without affliction, he acquired wealth without greed, he experienced pleasure without attachment.' //164//
Here, through the reiteration of 'fearlessness' and the like [as the topic], the guarding of oneself and the rest [are predicated].
(16) Producing a contrary understanding (<s>viruddhamatikṛt</s>) — an example:
(<s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s>)
'Skilled in the conduct of [one whose deeds are] like the rays of the moon, he is a friend without [need for] purpose — that single one. What shall we describe of him?' //165//

children.text: atra {kāryaṃ vinā mitram} iti vivakṣitam {akārye mitram iti} tu pratītiḥ / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, the intended meaning is 'a friend [even] without purpose,' but the understanding produced is 'a friend in a purposeless [i.e. evil] cause.' Or again:
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'The beloved, producing delight to the eyes after a long time, suddenly performs a choking of the throat upon her lover.' //166//
Here, the intended word is 'an embrace of the neck' (<s>kaṇṭhagraha</s>). Or again:

children.text:
{na trastaṃ yadi nāma bhūtakaruṇāsaṃtānaśāntātmanaḥ
  tena vyārujatā dhanurbhagavato devādbhavānīpateḥ /
  tatputrastu madāndhatārakavadhādviśvasya dattotsavaḥ
  skandaḥ skanda iva priyo 'hamatha vā śiṣyaḥ kathaṃ vismṛtaḥ //167//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mahāvīracarita</s> 2.28)

'If indeed the one whose nature is serenity through the continuity of compassion for beings was not frightened, [then why did] he break the bow of the Blessed Lord, the husband of <s>Bhavānī</s>? But his son <s>Skanda</s>, who gave the world a festival through the slaying of the maddened <s>Tāraka</s>, is dear to me like <s>Skanda</s> [himself] — or rather, how is a disciple forgotten?' //167//

children.text: atra bhavānīpatisabdo bhavānyāḥ patyantare pratītiṃ karoti / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, the word <s>bhavānīpati</s> (husband of <s>Bhavānī</s>) produces an understanding toward another meaning of <s>pati</s> [i.e. 'lord' vs. 'husband' in the context of <s>Bhavānī</s>]. Or again:

children.text:
{gorapi yadvāhanatāṃ prāptavataḥ so 'pi girisutāsiṃhaḥ /
  savidhe nirahaṅkāraḥ pāyādvaḥ so 'mbikāramaṇaḥ //168//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'May he who has obtained the status of vehicle even for a bull, that lion of the daughter of the mountain, who is free from ego in the presence [of devotees] — may that lover of <s>Ambikā</s> protect you!' //168//
Here, <s>ambikāramaṇa</s> (lover of <s>Ambikā</s>) produces a contrary understanding [since <s>Ambikā</s> can mean 'mother'].
Harsh to the ear (<s>śrutikaṭu</s>) in a compound — an example:

children.text:
{sā dūre ca sudhāsāndrataraṅgitavilocanā /
  bahirnirhrādanārho 'yaṃ kālaśca samupāgataḥ //169//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 93)
'She with eyes rippling with dense nectar-like [emotion] is far away, and this time worthy of being proclaimed aloud has arrived.' //169//
Thus other [examples] too should be understood.
Setting aside [those already discussed] — the lapsed in formation (<s>cyutasaṃskāra</s>), the inadequate (<s>asamartha</s>), and the meaningless (<s>nirarthaka</s>) —

children.text: vākye 'pi doṣāḥ santyete padasyāṃśe 'pi kecana // MKpr-K_52 //
children.translated_text: these faults exist in a sentence too, and some also in a portion of a word. // MKpr-K_52 //
Some [faults exist in sentences], but not all. Examples in order:
(1) Harsh to the ear (<s>śrutikaṭu</s>):

children.text:
{so 'dhyauṣṭa vedāṃstridaśānayaṣṭa pitṛnatārpsītsamamaṃsta bandhūn /
  vyajeṣṭa ṣaḍavargamaraṃsta nītau samūlaghātaṃ nyavadhīdarīṃśca //170//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭikāvya</s> 1.2)

'He studied the <s>Vedas</s>, worshipped the gods, satisfied the ancestors, equally honored his kinsmen, conquered the six [inner] enemies, was devoted to statecraft, and destroyed his foes utterly, root and all.' //170//
(2) Unused (<s>aprayukta</s>):

children.text:
{sa rātu vo duścyavano bhāvukānāṃ paraṃparām /
  aneḍamūkatādyaiśca dyatu doṣairasaṃmatān //171//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'May that irremovable <s>Indra</s> protect the lineage of the devout, and may he punish with [the faults of] muteness, deafness, and the like those who are disapproved.' //171//
Here, <s>duścyavana</s> means <s>Indra</s>; <s>aneḍamūka</s> means mute and deaf.
(3) With suppressed meaning (<s>nihatārtha</s>):
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'O lord of the earth, your fame, radiant with the brilliance of the lotus-like [splendor], shines all the more — assisted by the arm whose companion is the arrow, belonging to the lord whose command rules the earth, [lord of the] ocean.' //172//

children.text: atra sāyakādayaḥ śabdaḥ khaḍgābdhibhūcandrayaśaḥparyāyāḥ śarādyarthatayā prasiddhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the words <s>sāyaka</s> and the rest, being synonyms of sword, ocean, earth, moon, and fame [respectively], are well-known in the meaning of 'arrow' and the like [only], [thus suppressing the intended meaning].
(4) With inappropriate meaning (<s>anucitārtha</s>):

children.text:
{kuvindastvaṃ tāvatpaṭayasi guṇagrāmamabhito
  yaśo gāyantyete diśi diśi ca nagnāstava vibho /
  śarajjyotsnāgaurasphuṭavikaṭasarvāṅgasubhagā
  tathāpi tvatkīrtirbhramati vigatācchādanamiha //173//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'You are a weaver — to that extent you weave the fabric of your multitude of qualities all around; these naked ones sing your fame in every direction, O lord; your fame, white as the moonlight of autumn, with clearly visible massive beauty of all limbs — still it wanders here without a covering!' //173//
Here, the word 'weaver' and the like, while conveying another meaning, suggests the disparagement of the person being praised — thus it has inappropriate meaning.
(5) Meaningless (<s>nirarthaka</s>):
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'He, having attained the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the excellent cloud-lord, makes the seven horses unsteady, and causes the sleep of a thousand-petaled [lotus] that tends toward flight.' //174//

Here, the words <s>prābhrabhrāṭ</s>, <s>viṣṇudhāma</s>, <s>viṣamāśva</s>, <s>nidrā</s>, and <s>parṇa</s> do not denote 'excellent cloud,' 'sky,' 'the seven horses [of the sun],' 'closing,' and 'petals' [respectively, and are thus meaningless].
(6) Indecent (<s>aślīla</s>), [producing]
embarrassment (<s>vrīḍā</s>):
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'The trembling, side-glancing woman, approaching the king, endowed with the ardor of various weapons, produced bewilderment.' //175//
Here, the words 'approaching,' 'weapons,' and 'bewilderment' are indecent because they produce embarrassment.
Producing
disgust (<s>jugupsā</s>):

children.text:
{tenyairvāntaṃ samaśnanti parotsargaṃ ca bhuñjate /
  itarārthagrahe yeṣāṃ kavīnāṃ syātpravartanam //176//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'They eat what has been vomited, and they consume what has been excreted — those poets whose activity involves the grasping of another's [material].' //176//
Here, the words 'vomited,' 'excreted,' and 'activity' produce disgust.
Producing a sense of
inauspiciousness (<s>amaṅgala</s>):

children.text:
{pitṛvasatimahaṃ vrajāmi tāṃ saha parivārajanena yatra me /
  bhavati sapadi pāvakānvaye hṛdayamaśeṣitaśokaśalyakam //177//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 83)
'I go to the abode of [my] father along with the retinue, where, in the proximity of the fire-lineage, my heart becomes free of all the thorns of grief.' //177//
Here, when the intended meaning is 'father's house' and so forth, the perception of [it as] the cremation ground and the like [makes it] inauspicious in meaning.
(7) Ambiguous (<s>saṃdigdha</s>):
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'Devoted to the delight of the temple of the gods, having attained sufficient trembling, inclined to seeking, of radiant glory — behold this one!' //178//

children.text: atra kiṃ surādiśabdā devasenāśaravibhūtyarthāḥ kiṃ madirādyarthāḥ iti saṃdehaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, there is doubt: do the words <s>surā</s> and the rest mean 'god, army, arrow, and splendor,' or do they mean 'liquor' and the like?
(8) Unfamiliar (<s>apratīta</s>):

children.text:
{tasyādhimātropāyasya tīvrasaṃvegatājuṣaḥ /
  dṛḍhabhūmiḥ priyaprāptau yatnaḥ sa phalitaḥ sakhe //179//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'For him of supreme means and intense passion, possessing firm ground — that effort in attaining the beloved has borne fruit, O friend!' //179//
Here, the words <s>adhimātropāya</s> and the rest are unfamiliar because they are used only in the treatise on <s>Yoga</s>.
(9) Vulgar (<s>grāmya</s>):

children.text:
{tāmbūlabhṛtagalloyaṃ bhallaṃ jalpati mānuṣaḥ /
  karoti khādanaṃ pādaṃ sadaiva tu yathā tathā //180//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'This man with cheeks stuffed with betel talks nonsense, and constantly kicks about, come what may.' //180//
Here, the words <s>galla</s> (cheek) and the rest are vulgar.
(10) Having a secondary meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>):

children.text:
{vastravaidūryacaraṇaiḥ kṣatasattvarajaḥparā /
  niṣkampā racitā netrayuddhaṃ vedaya sāṃpratam //181//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 37)
'With garments, sapphires, and feet, surpassing in wounded beings and [qualities of] passion — immovable, she was fashioned; now declare the battle of the eyes!' //181//

children.text: atrāmbararatnapādaiḥ kṣatatamā acalā bhūḥ kṛtā netradvandvaṃ bodhayeti neyārthatā //
children.translated_text: Here, 'with sky (<s>ambara</s>), jewels (<s>ratna</s>), and feet (<s>pāda</s>),' 'surpassing in wounded (<s>kṣata</s>) and dark (<s>tamā</s>),' 'the immovable earth (<s>acalā bhūḥ</s>) was made — indicate the pair of eyes' — this is the secondary meaning.
(11) Strained (<s>kliṣṭa</s>):

children.text:
{dhammillasya na kasya prekṣya nikāmaṃ kuraṅgaśāvākṣyāḥ /
  rajyatyapūrvabandhavyutpattermānasaṃ śobhām //182//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vāmana</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṃkārasūtravṛtti</s> 2.1.22)
'Whose mind does not become enamored, having fully seen the beauty of the coiffure of the fawn-eyed one, [arising] from the skill in novel arrangement?' //182//

children.text: atra dhammillasya śobhāṃ prekṣya kasya mānasaṃ na rajyatīti saṃbandhe kliṣṭatvam //
children.translated_text: Here, in the construction 'having seen the beauty of the coiffure, whose mind does not become enamored' — there is strainedness.
(12) With unexamined predicate (<s>avimṛṣṭavidheyāṃśa</s>):

children.text:
{nyakkāro hyayameva me yadarayastatrāpyasau tāpasaḥ
  so 'pyatraiva nihanti rākṣasakulaṃ jīvatyaho rāvaṇaḥ /
  dhigdhik śakrajitaṃ prabodhitavatā kiṃ kumbhakarṇena vā
  svargagāmaṭikāviluṇṭhanavṛthocchūnaiḥ kimebhirbhujaiḥ //183//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Harṣa</s>'s <s>Nāgānanda</s> 9.55; <s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s>)

'Indeed this is my very humiliation, that the enemies are even there, and that ascetic too is right here, and he destroys the <s>rākṣasa</s> (demon) clan — and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> lives! Shame, shame upon <s>Śakrajit</s> (Indra's conqueror) who was awakened! What [use] of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>? What [use] of these arms, swollen in vain from the pointless plundering of the roadway to heaven?' //183//

children.text: atra 'ayameva nyakkāraḥ'; iti vācyam / ucchūnatvamātraṃ cānuvādyam, na vṛthātvaviśeṣitam / atra ca śabdaracanā viparītā kṛteti vākyasyaiva doṣo na vākyārthasya / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, 'this itself is the humiliation' is what should be said. And only the swollenness is the stated subject (anuvādya), not [the swollenness] qualified by futility. And here, it is the arrangement of words that has been made contrary — thus it is a fault of the sentence, not of the sentence-meaning. Or as in:

children.text:
{apāṅgasaṃsargi taraṅgitaṃ dṛśorbhruvorarālāntavilāsi vellitam /
  visāri romāñcanakañcukaṃ tanostanoti yo 'sau subhage tavāgataḥ //184//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

The sidelong glance that mingles with the corner of the eyes, the playful curving at the arched tips of the brows, the gooseflesh spreading like a bodice over the body — he who causes all this, O beautiful one, has arrived. || 184 ||
Here, the two words 'yo' and 'asau' produce only the cognition of the stated subject (anuvādya) [and are thus redundant].
For indeed — a 'tat' (that) pronoun, whose object is a well-known, previously introduced, or experienced meaning, does not require the inclusion of a 'yat' (which) pronoun. Examples in order:

children.text:
{kātaryaṃ kevalā nītiḥ śauryaṃ śvāpadaceṣṭitam /
  ataḥ siddhiṃ sametābhyāmubhābhyāmanviyeṣa saḥ //185//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 17.47)
Timidity is mere policy; bravery is the conduct of wild beasts — therefore, from both combined, he sought success. || 185 ||

children.text:
{dvayaṃ gataṃ saṃprati śocanīyatāṃ samāgamaprārthanayā kapālinaḥ /
  kalā ca sā kāntimatī kalāvatastvamasya lokasya ca netrakaumudī //186[=252]//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 5.71)
Two things have now fallen into a pitiable state, due to the Lord of Skulls seeking union — that lovely digit of the moon, and you, the eye-moonlight of this world. || 186 ||

children.text:
{utkampinī bhayapariskhalitāṃśukāntā
  te locane pratidiśaṃ vidhure kṣipantī /
  krūreṇa dāruṇatayā sahasaiva dagdhā
  dhūmāndhitena dahanena na vīkṣitāsi //187//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Harṣa</s>'s <s>Ratnāvali</s>; <s>Ānandavardhana</s>'s <s>Dhvanyāloka</s>)

Trembling, your garment slipping from the disturbance of fear, casting your distressed eyes in every direction — by the cruel one, suddenly with harshness, you were burned by fire blinded with smoke and not even seen! || 187 ||
But the 'yat' pronoun, being employed as following the subsequent sentence, does not, by its capacity, require the employment of a 'tat' pronoun following the previous sentence. As in:

children.text:
{sādhu candramasi puṣkaraiḥ kṛtaṃ mīlitaṃ yadabhirāmatādhike /
  udyatā jayani kāminīmukhe tena sāhasamanuṣṭhitaṃ punaḥ //188//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinanda</s>'s <s>Rāmacarita</s> 2.95)

Well has the moon done with the lotuses — that it closed [them] when surpassed in charm; but now, O victorious one, with the face of a beautiful woman — by that [moon], a further act of boldness has been performed! || 188 ||

children.text: prāgupāttastu yacchabdastacchabdopādānaṃ vinā sākāṅkṣaḥ / yathā atraiva śloke ādyapādayorvyatyāse / dvayorupādāne tu nirākāṅkṣatvaṃ prasiddham / anupādāne 'pi sāmarthyātkutraciddvayamapi gamyate / yathā
children.translated_text: But the 'yat' pronoun employed first, without the 'tat' pronoun, leaves [the sentence] incomplete (sākāṅkṣa). As in the same verse, when the first two quarters are transposed. When both are employed, the completeness is well-known. Even without [the 'tat' pronoun], in some cases both [meanings] are understood through capacity. As in:

children.text:
{ye nāma kecidiha naḥ prathayantyavajñāṃ
  jānanti te kimapi tān prati naiṣa yatnaḥ /
  utpatsyatesti mama ko 'pi samānadharmā
  kālo hyayaṃ niravadhirvipulā ca pṛthvī //189//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> 1.7)

Whatever people there are here who proclaim contempt for us — they know something [about their own worth]; this effort is not directed at them. There will arise some one of like temperament to me — for this time is without limit, and the earth is vast. || 189 ||

children.text:
atra ya utpatsyate taṃ pratīti / evaṃ ca tacchabdānupādāne 'tra sākāṅkṣatvam / na cāsāviti
tacchabdārthamāha /
children.translated_text: Here, [the meaning is:] 'the one who will arise — toward him [this is directed].' And thus, without the employment of the 'tat' pronoun, there is incompleteness here. Nor does 'asau' express the meaning of the 'tat' pronoun [in the following]:
(<s>Harṣa</s>'s <s>Nāgānanda</s> 6.4)

This one, whose beautiful filaments are kissed by the wind, foremost among the circles of the bright lords of stars, regarded with the eager gaze of women in separation — the spring season has arrived, like <s>Hanumān</s>! || 190 ||
For here, the cognition of the meaning of the 'tat' pronoun [referring back to 'yat'] does not occur.
Or, if there were such cognition:

children.text:
{karabālakarāladoḥ sahāyo yudhi yosau vijayārjunaikamallaḥ /
  yadi bhūpatinā sa tatra kārye viniyujyeta tataḥ kṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ syāt //191//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

He who is the companion with terrible, elephant-trunk-like arms, who was the sole champion against <s>Vijaya</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> in battle — if he were employed by the king in that matter, then the deed would be done, truly done. || 191 ||
Here, 'sa' (he) would become purposeless.
Now:

children.text:
{yovikalpamidamarthamaṇḍalaṃ paśyatīśa nikhilaṃ bhavadvapuḥ /
  ātmapakṣaparipūrite jagatyasya nityasukhinaḥ kuto bhayam //192//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Mahimabhaṭṭa</s>'s <s>Vyaktiviveka</s>)
He who sees this entire sphere of objects as non-dual, O Lord, [as] your body — for this eternally happy one, in a world filled by his own faction, whence could there be fear? || 192 ||

children.text: itīdaṃśabdavadadaḥśabdastacchabdārthamabhidhatte iti ucyate / tarhyatraiva vākyāntare upādānamarhati na tatraiva / yacchabdasya hi nikaṭe sthitaḥ prasiddhiṃ parāmṛśati / yathā
children.translated_text: Here it is said that the 'adaḥ' (that) pronoun, like the 'idam' (this) pronoun, expresses the meaning of the 'tat' pronoun. [Reply:] then it should be employed in another sentence of the same [passage], not in the very same [sentence]. For the 'yat' pronoun, being situated nearby, refers to what is well-known. As in:

children.text:
{yattadūrjitamatyugraṃ kṣātraṃ tejosya bhūpateḥ /
  dīvyatākṣaistadānena nūnaṃ tadapiṃ hāritam //193//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>'s <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 1.13)
That formidable and extremely fierce kṣatriya might of this king — by him who gambles with dice, surely even that has been squandered. || 193 ||

Here, [both] the 'tat' pronoun [are properly used].
But how [is this compatible with the following]?

children.text:
{kalyāṇānāṃ tvamasi mahasāṃ bhājanaṃ viśvamūrte
  dhuryāṃ lakṣmīmatha mayi bhṛśaṃ dhehi deva prasīda /
  yadyatpāpaṃ pratijahi jagannātha namrasya tanme
  bhadraṃ bhadraṃ vitara bhagavan bhūyase maṅgalāya //194//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> 1.4)

children.text:
atra yadyadityuktvā tanme ityuktam / ucyate ---- yadyaditi yena kenacidrūpeṇa sthitaṃ sarvātmakaṃ vastvākṣiptaṃ tathābhūtameva tacchabdena parāmṛśyate /
yathā vā
children.translated_text:
Here, having said 'yadyat' (whatever), 'tanme' (that of me) is said. [Reply:] 'yadyat' implies an object that is all-encompassing, existing in whatever form — and that very [object], being of such nature, is referred to by the 'tat' pronoun.
Or as in:

You are the vessel of great auspiciousness, O one of universal form! Then bestow upon me abundantly the chief <s>Lakṣmī</s>, O Lord, be gracious! Whatever sin there be, destroy that of me who bows, O Lord of the world! Bestow blessing upon blessing, O Blessed One, for the sake of greater auspiciousness! || 194 ||

children.text:
{kiṃ lobheba vilaṅghitaḥ sa bharato yenatadevaṃ kṛtaṃ
  mātrā strīlaghutāṃ gatā kimatha vā mātaiva madhyamā /
  mithyaitanmama cintitaṃ dvitayamapyāryānujosau guru-
  rmātā tātakalatramityanucitaṃ manye vidhātrā kṛtaṃ //195//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Dhanañjaya</s>'s <s>Daśarūpaka</s> 3.29; <s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Uttararāmacarita</s>)

Was it out of greed that <s>Bharata</s> was transgressed — by whom that very thing was done? Or did the mother go to the levity of a woman? Or is even the mother [merely] mediocre? This thought of mine regarding both is false — that noble one's younger brother is the guru, the mother, the father's wife — [yet] I consider what was done by Fate to be improper. || 195 ||

children.text: atrāryasyeti tātasyeti ca vācyam / na tvanayoḥ samāse guṇībhāvaḥ kāryaḥ / evaṃ samāsāntare 'pyudāhāryam //
children.translated_text: Here, 'of the noble one' and 'of the father' are what should be said — but the subordination [of these] in a compound should not be made. Thus should other compounds also be illustrated.
An example of creating contradictory understanding (<s>viruddhamatikṛt</s>):
(13) Creating contradictory understanding

children.text:
{śritakṣamā raktabhuvaḥ śivāliṅgitamūrtayaḥ /
  vigrahakṣapaṇenādya śerate te gatāsukhāḥ //196//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 97)
Resorting to forbearance, devoted to the earth, with forms embraced by <s>Śiva</s> — today, through the exhaustion of battle, they lie down, gone to happiness. || 196 ||

children.text: atra kṣamādiguṇayuktāḥ sukhamāsate iti vivakṣite hatā iti viruddhā pratītiḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, when the intended meaning is 'they, endowed with the qualities of forbearance and the like, rest happily,' the contradictory cognition 'they have been killed' [also arises from the same words].
Examples for [faults in] parts of words, in sequence as applicable:
(1) Harsh to the ear (śrutikaṭu)

children.text:
{alamaticapalatvātsvapnamāyopamatvāt
  pariṇativirasatvātsaṃgamenāṅganāyāḥ /
  iti yadi śatakṛtvastattvamālocayāma-
  stadapi na hariṇākṣīṃ vismaratyantarātmā //197//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bilhaṇacarita</s> [or <s>Bilhaṇakāvya</s>] 58)

Enough, because of excessive fickleness — because of being like a dream or an illusion — because of the insipidity at the end — from the company of a woman — thus, even if I contemplate this truth a hundred times, still the inner self does not forget the doe-eyed one. || 197 ||
Here, [the harsh sounds are in] 'tvāt' and the like. Or as in:

children.text:
{tadgaccha siddhyai kuru devakāryamartho 'yamarthāntaralabhya eva /
  apekṣate pratyayamaṅgalabdhyai bījāṅkuraḥ prāgudayādivāmbhaḥ //198//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 3.18)

Then go, for the accomplishment [of your purpose]; perform the work of the gods — this purpose is indeed to be attained through another purpose. The seed-sprout awaits the rain, as it were, before its arising, for the attainment of growth. || 198 ||
Here, 'ddhyai' and 'vdhyai' are harsh.
(<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 1.4)

And [the mountain] that bears upon its peaks the art of the apsaras' coquetry and ornaments — [the mountain] resplendent with mineral-colors distributed by the cleavage of clouds, like an early twilight. || 199 ||
Here, the word 'mattā' [intended in the sense of 'resplendent with minerals'] is repugnant (nihata) because of its [other] meaning of 'intoxicated.'

children.text:
{ādāvañjanapuñjaliptavapuṣāṃ śvāsānillollāsita-
  protsarpaddhirahānalena ca tataḥ saṃtāpitānāṃ dṛśām /
  saṃpratyeva niṣekamaśrupayasā devasya cettobhuvo
  bhallīnāmiva pānakarma kurute kāmaṃ kuraṅgekṣaṇā //200//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

First, of the eyes whose bodies are smeared with masses of collyrium, then heated by the fire of sighs fanned by the wind of breath, and now, at this very moment — the doe-eyed one performs the act of tempering [as if for] the arrows of the god of Love, the Mind-born One, by sprinkling with the water of tears. || 200 ||

children.text: atra dṛśāmiti bahuvacanaṃ nirarthakam kuraṅgekṣaṇāyā ekasyā evopādānāt / na cālasavalitairityādivat vyāpārabhedādbahutvam vyāpārāṇāmanupāttatvāt / na ca vyāpāretra dṛkśabdo vartate / atraiva 'kurute '; ityātmanepadamapyanarthakam / pradhānakriyāphalasya kartrasaṃbandhe kartrabhiprāyakriyāphalābhāvāt //
children.translated_text: Here, 'of the eyes' in the plural is purposeless, since only the one doe-eyed woman is being referred to. Nor can plurality be [justified] through the differentiation of operations, as in 'with lazy, rolling [glances]' and the like — because the operations are not being taken [separately here]. Nor is the word 'dṛś' (eye) here used in the sense of operation. Also in this same [verse], 'kurute' in the ātmanepada (middle voice) is likewise purposeless — because the fruit of the principal action does not belong to the agent, and there is no fruit of an action intended by the agent.

children.text:
{cāpācāryastripuravijayī kārtikeyo vijeyaḥ
  śastravyastaḥ sadanamudadhirbhūriyaṃ hantakāraḥ /
  astyevaitat kimu kṛtavatā reṇukākaṇṭhabādhāṃ
  baddhaspardhastava paraśunā lajjate candrahāsaḥ //201//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rājaśekhara</s>'s <s>Bālarāmāyaṇa</s> 2.37)

The teacher of the bow is the conqueror of <s>Tripura</s>; <s>Kārtikeya</s> is the one to be conquered; the arsenal is the ocean; this earth is the killing-ground. Is even this so? — What has been done by the one who committed the offense against <s>Reṇukā</s>'s neck? Your <s>Candrahāsa</s> sword is put to shame, having entered into rivalry with his battle-axe! || 201 ||
Here, 'vijeya' — the kṛtya (gerundive) suffix expresses the meaning of the kta (past participle) suffix.

children.text:
{atipelavamatiparimitavarṇaṃ laghutaramudāharati śaṭhaḥ /
  paramārthataḥ sa hṛdayaṃ vahati punaḥ kālakūṭaghaṭitamiva //202//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s>)
Very softly, with very few syllables, the deceitful one utters what is lighter [than light]; but in truth, he carries in his heart [something] as if compounded of kālakūṭa poison. || 202 ||
Here, the word 'pelava' [is the problematic word-part].

children.text:
{yaḥ pūyate surasarinmukhatīrthasārtha-
  snānena śāstrapariśīlanakīlanena /
  saujantyamānyajanirūrjitamūrjitānāṃ
  yo 'yaṃ dṛśoḥ patati kasyacideva puṃsaḥ //203//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

He who is purified by bathing at the chief tīrtha at the mouth of the heavenly river, by the nail of thorough study of the scriptures — the esteem that is exalted among the exalted, born of good character — this falls within the range of sight of some rare person alone. || 203 ||
Here, [the problematic element is] the word 'pūya' [which also means 'pus'].

children.text:
{vinayapraṇaaikaketanaṃ satataṃ yobhavadaṅga tādṛśaḥ /
  kathamadya sa tadvadīkṣyataāṃ tadabhipretapadaṃ samāgataḥ //204//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 104)
He who was always the sole banner of humility — O friend of his body, how is it that today, he who was always thus, is seen in such a way, having arrived at the intended destination? || 204 ||
Now, [the problematic element is] the word 'preta' [which also means 'departed spirit/ghost'].
(<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s>)
In what task does his ability not cause [others] extreme distress? Therefore, let an añjali (salutation with joined palms) be offered to this one who conducts himself well. || 205 ||

children.text: atra kiṃ pūrvaṃ sādhuḥ uta sādhuṣu caratīti saṃdehaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the doubt [arises]: is [the compound 'sādhucara'] first 'sādhu' (good/honest) [and then one who 'conducts himself'], or [does it mean] 'one who roams among sādhus (holy men)'?
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
What can be said of this great jewel in the garland of crowns of kings — whose radiance is made manifest by the arrows of his words, which are most difficult to obtain? || 206 ||

children.text: atra vacaḥśabdena gīḥśabdo lakṣyate / atra khalu na kevalaṃ pūrvapadam yāvaduttarapadamapi paryāyaparivartanaṃ na kṣamate / jaladhyādāvuttarapadameva vaḍavānalādau pūrvapadameva //
children.translated_text: Here, by the word 'vacaḥ' (speech), the word 'gīḥ' (speech/voice) is indicated. And here indeed, not only the first member but also the last member of the compound does not tolerate substitution by a synonym. In [compounds like] 'jaladhi' (ocean) and the like, only the last member [is fixed]; in 'vaḍavānala' (submarine fire) and the like, only the first member [is fixed].

children.text: yadyapyasamarthasyaivāprayuktādayaḥ kecana bhedāḥ tathāpyanyairālaṅkārikairvibhāgena pradarśitā iti bhedapradarśanenodāhartavyā iti ca vibhajyoktāḥ //52//
children.translated_text: Although some divisions such as 'aprayukta' (not in use) and the like belong only to those [words] that are incapable [of standard usage], nevertheless, since they have been separately demonstrated by other ālaṃkārikas (rhetoricians), they are to be illustrated through the demonstration of divisions — and thus are stated with classification. || 52 ||
Sentence-faults (vākyadoṣa)
Adverse phonemes, corrupted or lost visarga, faulty sandhi (euphonic combination), violated meter;
deficient or excessive stated words, fallen emphasis, [and] completed [then] restated. || Kpr-K_53 ||
Expressing one meaning in another half-verse, impossible logical connection, and unexpressed intended meaning;
compound of words not in proper relation, mixed [construction], embedded [construction], and violation of established usage. || Kpr-K_54 ||
Broken sequence, disorder, and having a meaning not intended by the author — [these are] likewise [faults] of the sentence itself.

children.text: (1) rasānuguṇatvaṃ varṇānāṃ vakṣyate / tadviparītaṃ pratikūlavarṇam / yathā śṛṅgāre
children.translated_text: (1) The conformity of phonemes to rasa will be discussed [later]. What is contrary to that is 'adverse phonemes.' As in śṛṅgāra (the erotic rasa):

children.text:
{akuṇṭhotkaṇṭhayā pūrṇamākaṇṭhaṃ kalakaṇṭhi mām /
  kambukaṇṭhyāḥ kṣaṇaṃ kaṇṭhe kuru kaṇṭhārtimuddhara //207//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 107, 325)
With unrestrained eagerness, fill me to the throat, O melodious-throated one! Place [yourself] for a moment upon the throat of this conch-throated woman — relieve the anguish of the throat! || 207 ||
In the raudra (furious) [rasa], as in:

children.text:
{deśaḥ so 'yamarātiśoṇitajalairyasmin hradāḥ pūritāḥ
  kṣatrādeva tathāvidhaḥ paribhavastātasya keśagrahaḥ /
  tānyevāhitahetighasmaragurūṇyastrāṇi bhāsvanti me
  yadrāmeṇa kṛtaṃ tadeva kurute droṇātmajaḥ krodhanaḥ //208//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>'s <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 3.33)

This is that land where lakes were filled with the bloody waters of enemies; from the kṣatriya class itself came that kind of humiliation — the seizing of our father's hair. These very weapons of mine are blazing — heavy [and eager] to devour the hostile forces. What <s>Rāma</s> did, that very thing the son of <s>Droṇa</s> does now, wrathful. || 208 ||

children.text: atra hi vikaṭavarṇatvaṃ dīrghasamāsatvaṃ cocitam / yathā
children.translated_text: For here, the harsh phonemes and the long compounds are appropriate. As in:

children.text:
{prāgprāptaniśumbhaśāṃbhavadhanurdvedhāvidhāvirbhavat-
  krodhapreritabhīmabhārgavabhujastambhāpaviddhaḥ ks.aṇāt /
  ujjvālaḥ paraśurbhavatvaśithilastvatkaṇṭhapīṭhātithi-
  ryenānena jagatsu khaṇḍaparaśurdevo haraḥ khyāpyate //209//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mahāvīracarita</s> 2.33)

The battle-axe — which first split the bow of <s>Śambhu</s> obtained [by <s>Niśumbha</s>], which was hurled from the pillar-like arm of the fearsome <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) impelled by the wrath that arose from the splitting into two [of the bow] — may it, blazing, become slack [now as it rests] upon the pedestal of your throat as a guest; by which [axe] this Lord <s>Hara</s> [<s>Śiva</s>] is proclaimed in the worlds as <s>Khaṇḍaparaśu</s> (He of the Broken Axe). || 209 ||

children.text: yatra tu na krodhastatra caturthapādābhidhāne tathaiva śabdaprayogaḥ //
children.translated_text: But where there is no [sentiment of] anger, the same kind of word-usage in expressing the fourth quarter [is a fault].

children.text: (2) upahata utvaṃ prāpto (3) lupto vā visargo yatra tat / yathā
children.translated_text: (2) Where the visarga has been corrupted — changed to the sound 'u' — or (3) dropped, that [is the fault]. As in:

children.text:
{dhīro vinīto nipuṇo varākāro nṛpo 'tra saḥ /
  yasya bhṛtyā balotsiktā bhaktā buddhiprabhāvitāḥ //210//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
Steadfast, modest, skillful, and of noble bearing is that king here — whose servants are proud of their strength, devoted, and empowered by intelligence. || 210 ||

children.text: (4) visaṃdhi saṃdhervairūpyam viśleṣoślīlatvaṃ kaṣṭatvaṃ ca / tatrādyaṃ yahtā
children.translated_text: (4) <s>Visaṃdhi</s> (faulty juncture) is the disfigurement of juncture (<s>saṃdhi</s>). Disjunction (<s>viśleṣa</s>) is offensiveness and harshness. Among those, the first is as follows:

children.text:
{rājanvibhānti bhavataścaritāni tāni
  indordyutiṃ dadhati yāni rasātalentaḥ /
  dhīdorbale atitate ucitānuvṛttī
  ātanvatī vijayasaṃpadametya bhātaḥ //211//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 109)

{O king, your deeds shine — those which bear the radiance of the moon even in the netherworld; the prowess of intellect and arms, having surpassed [all], spreading a fitting course of conduct, having attained the wealth of victory, shines forth! //211//}
Or alternatively:
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Then, having risen, the moon — with its splendid, charming radiance robbing away [all else] — [rises] aloft from the eastern mountain; in his own lineage, of noble and beautiful luster, he gleams like a priceless, liberated pearl! //212//}

children.text: saṃhitāṃ na karomīti svacchayā sakṛdapi doṣaḥ pragṛhyādihetukatve tvasakṛt //
children.translated_text: The intentional omission of <s>saṃhitā</s> (euphonic combination) is a fault even once; but when caused by <s>pragṛhya</s> (a vowel exempt from <s>saṃdhi</s>) and the like, it is not a fault even if repeated.

children.text:
{vegāduḍḍīya gagane calaṇḍāmaraceṣṭitaḥ /
  ayamuttapate pastrī tato 'traiva ruciṅkuru //213//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{Having flown up swiftly into the sky, displaying the gestures of a moving pennant — this bird takes flight; therefore, take delight right here! //213//}
Here, the juncture is offensive.

children.text:
{urvyasāvatra tarvālī marvante cārvavasthitiḥ /
  mātrarju yujyate gantuṃ śiro namaya tanmanāk //214//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 2.10)
{Vast is the earth here, [and] there a row of trees; at its end, a lovely halting-place; one should not travel further, mother — bow your head a little [and rest]. //214//}

children.text: (5) hataṃ lakṣaṇānusaraṇe 'pyaśravyam / aprāptagurubhāvāntalaghu rasānanuguṇaṃ ca vṛttaṃ yatra tat hatavṛttam / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: (5) <s>Hatavṛtta</s> (defective meter) is that which is unpleasant to the ear even when the rules of meter are followed. A meter in which a short syllable has not attained its heavy value, or an internal light [syllable] is incongruent with the <s>rasa</s> — that is <s>hatavṛtta</s>. Examples in order:

children.text:
{amṛtamamṛtaṃ kaḥ saṃdeho madhūnyapi nānyathā
  madhuramadhikaṃ cūtasyāpi prasannarasaṃ phalam /
  sakṛdapi punarmadhyasthaḥ san rasāntaravijjano
  vadatu yadihānyatsvādu syātpriyādaśanacchadāt //215//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vāmana</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 3.2.10)

{Nectar is nectar — what doubt is there? Honeys too are no different; sweeter still and of clear juice is the fruit of the mango; but let anyone, being an impartial judge, a connoisseur of different flavors, declare whether there is anything sweeter here than the lip of the beloved! //215//}
Here, 'whether there is anything sweeter' — this is unpleasant to the ear. Or alternatively:

children.text:
{jaṃ parihari_uṃ tīra_i maṇa_aṃpi ṇa sundarattaṇaguṇeṇa /
  aha ṇavaraṃ jassa doso paḍipakkhehiṃ pi paḍivaṇṇo //216//}

children.translated_text: [That which cannot be transcended even slightly by the quality of beauty —

children.text: atha kevalaṃ yasya doṣaḥ pratipakṣairapi pratipannaḥ //]
children.translated_text: well then, one whose fault is acknowledged even by opponents —]
(<s>Ānandavardhana</s>'s <s>Viṣamabāṇalīlā</s>; <s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s>)
{That which cannot be avoided even slightly by the quality of beauty — well then, one whose fault is acknowledged even by opponents — //216//}
Here, the second and third metrical feet have <s>sa</s>-gaṇa and <s>bha</s>-gaṇa [which produce harshness].
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{The spring — with blooming <s>sahakāra</s> trees, whose captivating fragrance sets abuzz swarms of bees, and with the beautiful splendor of fresh shoots serving as lovely <s>cāmaras</s> — steals the mind even of a sage! //217//}

children.text: atra hāriśabdaḥ / hāripramuditasaurabheti pāṭho yuktaḥ / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, the word '<s>hāri</s>' [is the fault]. The reading '<s>hāripramuditasaurabha</s>' is correct. Or alternatively:

children.text:
{anyāstā guṇaratnarohaṇabhuvo dhanyā mṛdanyaiva sā
  saṃbhārāḥ khalu tenya eva vidhinā yaireṣa sṛṣṭo yuvā /
  śrīmatkāntijuṣāṃ dviṣāṃ karatalāt strīṇāṃ nitambasthalāt
  dṛṣṭe yatra patanti mūḍhamanasāmastrāṇi vastrāṇi ca //218//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Other [lands] are the mines of jewel-like qualities — blessed is the earth herself! Blessed indeed are those materials, by which providence created this youth — before whom, from the palms of resplendent and beautiful enemies fall weapons, and from the hips of women fall garments, their minds bewildered! //218//}

children.text: atra 'vastrāṇyapi'; iti pāṭhe laghurapi gurutāṃ bhajate //
children.translated_text: Here, in the reading 'garments too,' even a light [syllable] takes on heaviness [which is a fault].

children.text:
{hā nṛpa hā budha hā kavibandho viprasahasrasamāśraya deva /
  mugdhavidagdhasabhāntararatna kvāsi gataḥ kva vayaṃ ca tavaite //219//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Alas, O king! Alas, O wise one! Alas, friend of poets! O lord, refuge of a thousand <s>brāhmaṇas</s>! Jewel amidst the assembly of the naive and the learned — where have you gone, and where are we, these [followers] of yours? //219//}
This meter is evocative of the <s>hāsya</s> (comic) <s>rasa</s> [and is therefore incongruent with the pathetic sentiment intended].
(6) <s>Nyūnapada</s> (deficient word) — as follows:

children.text:
{tathābhūtāṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpasadasi pāñcālatanayāṃ
  vane vyādhaiḥ sārdhaṃ suciramuṣitaṃ valkaladharaiḥ /
  virāṭasyāvāse sthitamanucitārambhanibhṛtaṃ
  guruḥ khedaṃ khinne mayi bhajati nādyāpi kuruṣu //220[= 15]//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>'s <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 1.11)

{Having seen <s>Pāñcālī</s> (Draupadī) in such a state in the royal assembly, having dwelt long in the forest with hunters clad in bark garments, having stayed in <s>Virāṭa</s>'s abode concealed in unsuitable occupations — the grief does not even now visit me, O teacher, who am already afflicted, but rather visits the <s>Kurus</s>. //220[=15]//}
Here, 'by us' — [a word needed] before 'afflicted'; and 'in this manner' [is also missing].
(7) <s>Adhikapada</s> (superfluous word) — as follows:

children.text:
{sphaṭikākṛtinirmalaḥ prakāmaṃ pratisaṃkrāntaniśātaśāstratattvaḥ /
  aviruddhasamanvitoktiyuktiḥ pratimallāstamayodayaḥ sa ko 'pi //221//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Crystal-like in form and utterly clear, fully versed in the essence of keen scriptures, his argument endowed with compatible and coherent reasoning — who is this matchless one, [whose] setting and rising [is like the sun's]? //221//}
Here, the word '<s>ākṛti</s>' (form) [is superfluous]. Or alternatively:

children.text:
{idamanucitamakramaśca puṃsāṃ yadiha jarāsvapi mānmathā vikārāḥ /
  yadapi ca na kṛtaṃ nitambinīnāṃ stanapatanāvadhi jīvitaṃ rataṃ vā //222//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhartṛhari</s>'s <s>Śṛṅgāraśataka</s> 27)

{This is unfitting and a transgression for men, that even in old age there should be amorous disturbances; and that women have not been given [either] a life or a love that lasts only until the falling of the breasts — this too [is unfitting]. //222//}

children.text: atra kṛtamiti / kṛtaṃ pratyuta prakramabhaṅgamāvahati / tathā ca 'yadapi ca na kuraṅgalocanānām'; iti pāṭhe nirākāṅkṣaiva pratītiḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the word '<s>kṛtam</s>' (done) [is superfluous]. '<s>Kṛtam</s>' on the contrary introduces a break in the flow. And thus, in the reading 'nor of the doe-eyed women,' the understanding is unimpeded.
(8) <s>Kathitapada</s> (redundantly stated word) — as follows:

children.text:
{adhikaratalatalpaṃ kalpitasvāpalīlā-
  parimilananimīlatpāṇḍimā gaṇḍapālī /
  sutanu kathaya kasya vyañjayatyañjasaiva
  smaranarapatilīlāyauvarājyābhiṣekam //223//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kuntaka</s>'s <s>Vakroktijīvita</s> 1.109)

{With the palm-bed on her hand, the pallor of her cheek — closing in a feigned drowsiness of pretended sleep — O slender one, tell me, whose [sign] does it manifest directly? The coronation ceremony for the role of prince regent in the sport of the lord of love, <s>Smara</s>! //223//}
Here, the word '<s>līlā</s>' (sport) [is redundant, as the idea is already expressed].
(9) <s>Patatprakarṣa</s> (fallen excellence) — as follows:

children.text:
{kaḥ kaḥ kutra na ghurghurāyitaghurīghoro ghuretsūkaraḥ
  kaḥ kaḥ kaṃ kamalākaraṃ vikamakaṃ kartuṃ karī nodyataḥ /
  ke ke kāni vanānyaraṇyamahiṣā nonmūlayeyuryataḥ
  siṃhīsnehavilāsabaddhavasatiḥ pañcānano vartate //224//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 115)

{What boar, what boar, where does it not grunt its terrifying roar? What elephant, what elephant is not eager to trample some lotus pond? What wild buffaloes, which forests would they not uproot? — since the five-faced lion dwells [here], bound to its residence by the affection of a lioness! //224//}
(10) <s>Samāptapunarātta</s> (completed [idea] restated) — as follows:

children.text:
{kreṅkāraḥ smarakārmukasya suratakrīḍāpikīnāṃ ravaḥ
  jhaṅkāro ratimañkarīmadhulihāṃ līlācakorīdhvaniḥ /
  tanvyāḥ kañculikāpasāraṇabhujākṣepaskhalatkaṅkaṇa-
  kvāṇaḥ prema tanotu vo navavayolāsyāya veṇusvanaḥ //225//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 116)

{The <s>kreṅkāra</s> (twanging sound) of the bow of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), the cooing of the <s>kokila</s>-birds in the sport of love, the buzzing of bees — the honey-drinkers of the vine of passion — the call of <s>cakora</s>-birds in play, the jingling of bracelets slipping from the arm-gesture of [her] removing the bodice — may it bestow love in you! — the sound of the flute, for the dance of fresh youth. //225//}
(11) [A verse in which] the first half is the complement of a single [syntactic] indicator located in the second half — as follows:

children.text:
{masṛṇacaraṇapātaṃ gamyatāṃ bhūḥ sadarbhā
  viracaya sicayāntaṃ mūrdhni gharmaḥ kaṭhoraḥ /
  taditi janakaputrī locanairaśrupūrṇaiḥ
  pathi pathikavadhūbhirvīkṣitā śikṣitā ca //226//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rājaśekhara</s>'s <s>Bālarāmāyaṇa</s> 6.36)

{With gentle footfall, let the earth with its <s>darbha</s> grass be traversed; arrange a heap of <s>śicaya</s> grass upon the head — the heat is harsh! — thus, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, with eyes brimming with tears, was beheld and instructed on the path by the wives of wayfarers. //226//}

children.text: (12) abhavan mataḥ (iṣṭaḥ) yogaḥ (saṃbandhaḥ) yatra tat / yathā
children.translated_text: (12) Where the intended connection (<s>yoga</s>) has not materialized — as follows:

children.text:
{yeṣāṃ tāstridaśebhadānasaritaḥ pītāḥ pratāpoṣmabhi-
  rlīlāpānabhuvaśca nandanavanacchāyāsu yaiḥ kalpitāḥ /
  yeṣāṃ huṅkṛtayaḥ kṛtāmarapatikṣobhāḥ kṣapācāriṇāṃ
  kiṃ taistvatparitoṣakāri vihitaṃ kiñcitpravādocitam //227//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Mahimabhaṭṭa</s>'s <s>Vyaktiviveka</s>)

{Those celestial elephant-streams of the gods which were drunk up by the heat of [his] valor; those sports of drinking which were held in the shade of the <s>Nandana</s> grove; those roars of the night-roamers (<s>rākṣasas</s>) which caused the lord of the gods to tremble — what praiseworthy thing, fit to be spoken of, has been accomplished by them that would please you? //227//}

children.text: atra {guṇānāṃ ca parārthatvādasaṃbandhaḥ samatvātsyāt} ityuktanayena yacchabdanidaśyānāmarthānāṃ parasparasamanvayena yair ityatra viśeṣasyāpratītiriti / {kṣapācāribhiḥ} iti pāṭhe yujyate samanvayaḥ / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, following the principle stated as 'because qualities serve another's purpose, there would be no connection, since they are equal' — the meanings pointed to by the relative pronoun 'which' do not yield the apprehension of a specific referent in 'by whom.' In the reading '<s>kṣapācāribhiḥ</s>' (by the night-roamers), the syntactic connection is proper. Or alternatively:

children.text:
{tvamevaṃsaundaryā sa ca ruciratāyāḥ paricitaḥ
  kalānāṃ sīmānaṃ paramiha yuvāmeva bhajathaḥ /
  api dvandvaṃ diṣṭyā taditi subhage saṃvadati vām
  ataḥ śeṣaṃ yatsyājjitamiha tadānīṃ guṇitayā //228//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mālatīmādhava</s>)

{You are of such beauty, and he is versed in the art of charm; you two alone reach the very limit of arts here. Fortunately there is a pair [of you] — thus, O lovely one, it is fitting for you both; hence whatever remains to be conquered here — that has already been won by your multiplication. //228//}

children.text: atra yadityatra taditi tadānīmityatra yadeti vacanaṃ nāsti / {cetsyāt} iti yuktaḥ pāṭhaḥ / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, at 'which' — there is no corresponding 'that'; and at 'then' — there is no corresponding 'which.' The reading '<s>cetsyāt</s>' (if it should be) is correct. Or alternatively:

children.text:
{saṃgrāmāṅgaṇamāgatena bhavatā cāpe samāropite
  devākarṇaya yena yena sahasā yadyatsamāsāditam /
  kodaṇḍena śarāḥ śarairariśirastenāpi bhūmaṇḍalaṃ
  tena tvaṃ bhavatā ca kīrtiratulā kīrtyā ca lokatrayam //229//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{When you arrived at the arena of battle and strung the bow — O god, listen! — whatever was swiftly accomplished, one thing after another: with the bow, arrows; with the arrows, the heads of enemies; with those, the earth; with the earth, you; with you, incomparable fame; and with fame, the three worlds! //229//}

children.text:
atrākarṇanakriyākarmatve kodaṇḍaṃ śarānityādi vākyārthasya
karmatve kodaṇḍaḥ śarā iti prāptam / na ca yacchabdārthastadviśeṣaṇaṃ
vā kodaṇḍādi / na ca kena kenetyādi praśnaḥ / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, if 'bow, arrows,' etc. are the objects of the action of 'listening,' then the expected form would be 'the bow, the arrows'; and if they are the objects of the sentence-meaning, then likewise 'the bow, the arrows' is what would follow. For the meaning of the relative pronoun 'which' is not the specific qualification of 'bow' and the rest. Nor is 'by what, by what' and the like a question [here]. Or alternatively:

children.text:
{"cāpācāryastripuravijayī kārtikeyo vijeyaḥ
  śastravyastaḥ sadanamudadhirbhūriyaṃ hantakāraḥ /
  astyevaitat kimu kṛtavatā reṇukākaṇṭhabādhāṃ
  baddhasparddhastava paraśunā lajjate candrahāsaḥ" //230//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rājaśekhara</s>'s <s>Bālarāmāyaṇa</s> 2.37)

{"The teacher of archery is the conqueror of <s>Tripura</s> (<s>Śiva</s>); <s>Kārtikeya</s> is the one to be conquered; the armory is the ocean; this earth is the arena of slaughter. Granted, all this is so — but does your battle-axe, having vied with the one who severed the throat of <s>Reṇukā</s>, not feel ashamed before the crescent-moon sword (<s>Candrahāsa</s>)?" //230//}

children.text: ityādau bhārgavasya nindāyāṃ tātparyam / kṛtavateti paraśau sā pratīyate / 'kṛtavataḥ'; iti tu pāṭhe matayogo bhavati / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here and in what follows, the purport is the censure of the <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>). 'By the one who did' — that [censure] is apprehended [as referring] to the axe. But in the reading '<s>kṛtavataḥ</s>' (of the one who did), there would be a [proper] intended connection. Or alternatively:

children.text:
{catvāro vayamṛtvijaḥ sa bhagavān karmopadeṣṭā hariḥ
  saṃgrāmādhvaradīkṣito narapatiḥ patnī gṛhītavratā /
  kauravyāḥ paśavaḥ priyāparirabhavakleśopaśāntiḥ phalaṃ
  rājyanyopanimantraṇāya rasati sphītaṃ hato dundubhiḥ //231//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>'s <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 1.25)

{We four are the officiating priests; that blessed <s>Hari</s> is the instructor of the rite; the king is consecrated for the sacrifice that is battle; his wife has taken the vow; the <s>Kauravas</s> are the sacrificial animals; the cessation of the beloved's sorrow is the fruit; the kettledrum resounds abundantly, as if inviting [all] to a royal sacrifice! //231//}

children.text: atrādhvaraśabdaḥsamāse guṇībhūta iti na tadarthaḥ sarvaiḥ saṃyujyate / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, the word '<s>adhvara</s>' (sacrifice), having become subordinate in the compound, does not have its meaning connected with all [the other terms]. Or alternatively:

children.text:
{jaṅghākāṇḍorunālo nakhakiraṇalasatlesarālīkarālaḥ
  pratyagrālaktakābhāprasarakisalayo mañjumañjīrabhṛṅgaḥ /
  bharturnṛttānukāra jayati nijatanusvacchalāvaṇyavāpī-
  saṃbhūtāmbhojaśobhāṃ vidadhavabhinavo daṇḍapādo bhavānyāḥ //232[=150]//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Mahimabhaṭṭa</s>'s <s>Vyaktiviveka</s>)

{With the shank as its stalk, the thigh as its tube, the toenail-rays forming a glistening, terrible <s>lesarālī</s> creeper, fresh lac-color spreading as its tender shoots, and lovely anklets as its bees — the foot of <s>Bhavānī</s>, imitating the dance of her lord, triumphs, producing anew the beauty of a lotus born from the pellucid pool of her own bodily grace! //232[=150]//}

children.text: atra daṇḍapādagatā nijatanuḥpratīyate bhavānyāḥ saṃbandhinī tu vivakṣitā //
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>nijatanu</s>' (one's own body) in connection with '<s>daṇḍapāda</s>' (the foot [of the verse]) is apprehended [in one sense], but is intended in connection with <s>Bhavānī</s>.
(13) Where what necessarily needs to be said has been left unsaid — as follows:

children.text:
{aprākṛtasya caritātiśayaiśca dṛṣṭai-
  ratyadbhutairapahṛtasya tathāpi nāsthā /
  ko 'pyeṣa vīraśiśukākṛtiraprameya-
  saundaryasārasamudāyamayaḥ padārthaḥ //233//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mahāvīracarita</s> 2.39)

{Though captivated by the extraordinary deeds that have been witnessed — deeds most wondrous — yet there is no complacency. This is some entity of indeterminate form, appearing like the child of a hero, unfathomable, constituted of the totality of the essence of beauty. //233//}

children.text: atra 'apahṛto 'smi'; ityapahṛtatvasya vidhirvācyaḥ tathāpītyasya dvitīyavākyagatatvenaivopapatteḥ / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, 'I am captivated' — the affirmative form of 'being captivated' needs to be expressed; [the word] 'yet' is justified only as belonging to the second clause.
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{I am this one — born from the lotus-face of the daughter of the mountain, having reached [a state] that is far from the heart's desires of gods and demons, having been made into one whose beauty and fortune are attained [only] through an arrangement accomplished in a dream — [I have been made into] the daughter of the king of the <s>Asuras</s>. //234//}

children.text: atra manorathānāmapi dūravartītyapyartho vācyaḥ / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, the meaning 'far from their desires as well' also needs to be expressed.

children.text:
{tvayi nibaddharateḥ priyavādinaḥ praṇayabhaṅgaparāṅmukhacetasaḥ /
  kamaparādhalavaṃ mama paśyasi tyajasi mānini dāsajanaṃ yataḥ //235//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 4.55)

{Though your love is fixed on me, and I am sweet-spoken, and though your heart is turned away from a breach of affection — what trace of offense do you see in me, that you abandon [your] servant, O proud one? //235//}
Here, 'even a trace of offense' — [the word 'even'] needs to be expressed.
(14) <s>Asthānasthapada</s> (word placed in the wrong position) — as follows:

children.text:
{priyeṇa saṃgrathya vipakṣasaṃnidhā-
  vupāhitāṃ vakṣasi pīvarastane /
  srajaṃ na kācidvijahau jalāvilāṃ
  vasanti hi premṇi guṇā na vastuṣu //236//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhāravi</s>'s <s>Kirātārjunīya</s> 8.37)

{No woman abandoned the garland — water-stained — that had been strung together by her beloved and placed on the bosom, on the full breast, in the presence of a rival; for virtues reside in love, not in objects. //236//}

children.text: atra 'kācinna vijahau'; iti vācyam / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, 'no woman abandoned' — [the word 'no'] should be expressed [differently, i.e., 'not one woman abandoned']. Or alternatively:

children.text:
{lagnaḥ kelikacagrahaślathajaṭālambena nidrāntare
  mudrāṅkaḥ śitikandharenduśakalenānta.gkappolasthalam /
  pārvatyā nakhalakṣmaśaṅkitasakhīnarmasmitahrītayā
  pronmṛṣṭaḥ karapallavena kuṭilātāmracchaviḥ pātu vaḥ //237//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Clinging [to <s>Śiva</s>'s] cheek through the loosened matted locks seized during love-play, impressed there during slumber, [the mark] — reddish and curved at the edge by the crescent moon resting on <s>Śiva</s>'s blue throat — may the nail-mark, which <s>Pārvatī</s>, ashamed by the teasing smiles of friends who suspected [it was] a nail-mark, wiped away with the sprout of her hand, protect you! //237//}
Here, 'reddish and curved' should be expressed before 'nail-mark' [for proper word order].
(15) <s>Asthānasthasamāsa</s> (compound placed in the wrong position) — as follows:

children.text:
{adyāpi stanaśailadurgaviṣame sīmantinīnāṃ hṛdi
  sthātuṃ vāñchati māna eṣa dhigiti krodhādivālohitaḥ /
  prodyaddūrataraprasāritakaraḥ karṣatyasau tatkṣaṇāt
  phullatkairavakośaniḥsaradaliśreṇīkṛpāṇaṃ śaśī //238//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Harṣa</s>'s <s>Nāgānanda</s> 2.41)

{'Even now, this pride (<s>māna</s>) desires to dwell in the mountain-fortress
of the breasts, [which is] difficult terrain, in the hearts of women — shame!' Thus, reddened with anger,
extending his hand further and further as he rises,
the moon draws its scimitar — a blade-row issuing from the full <s>kairava</s> (white lotus) cup! //238//}

children.text: atra kruddhasyoktau samāso na kṛtaḥ kaveruktau tu kṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, in the speech of the angered [moon], no compound is formed; but in the speech of the poet, [a compound] is formed.

children.text: (16) saṃkīrṇam yatra vākyāntarasya padāni vākyāntaramanupraviśanti / yathā
children.translated_text: (16) Mixed (<s>saṃkīrṇa</s>) — where the words of one sentence enter into another sentence. For example:

children.text:
{kimiti na paśyasi kopaṃ pādagataṃ bahuguṇaṃ gṛhāṇemam /
  nanu muñca hṛdayanāthaṃ kaṇṭhe manasastamorūpam //239//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 6.42)

{'Why do you not see? Abandon anger! [He is] at [your] feet, of many virtues — take this [necklace]!
Come, release the lord of [your] heart! Around the neck — [cast off] the darkness of the mind! //239//'}

children.text: atra pādagataṃ bahuguṇaṃ hṛdayanārthaṃ kimiti na paśyasi / imaṃ kaṇṭhe gṛhāṇa manasastamorūpaṃ kopaṃ muñceti / ekavākyatāyāṃ tu kliṣṭamiti bhedaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, [the proper construction is:] 'at [your] feet, of many virtues, the lord of [your] heart — why do you not see? Take this around the neck; release the anger, which is the darkness of the mind.' But if construed as a single sentence, it would be [the fault of] forced [expression] — that is the difference.

children.text: (17) garbhitam yatra vākyasya madhye vākyāntaramanupraviśati / yathā
children.translated_text: (17) Embedded (<s>garbhita</s>) — where another sentence enters into the middle of a sentence. For example:

children.text:
{parāpakāraniratairdurjanaiḥ saha saṃgatiḥ /
  vadāmi bhavatastattvaṃ na vidheyā kathañcana //240//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{'Association with wicked people who are devoted to harming others —
I tell you the truth — should never be made. //240//'}

children.text: atra tṛtīyapādo vākyāntaramadhye praviṣṭaḥ / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, the third quarter has entered into the middle of another sentence. Or for example:

children.text:
{lagnaṃ rāgāvṛtāṅgyā sudṛḍhamiha yayaivāsiyaṣṭyārikaṇṭhe
  mātaṅgānāmapīhopari parapuruṣairyā ca dṛṣṭā patantī /
  tatsakto 'yaṃ na kiñcidgaṇayati viditaṃ te 'stu tenāsmi dattā
  bhṛtyebhyaḥ śrīniyogādgaditumiva gatetyambudhiṃ yasya kīrtiḥ //241//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Veṇidatta</s>'s <s>Padyaveṇī</s> 2)

{'That which was firmly attached by her, her limbs covered with passion, with a sword-staff to the enemy's throat —
and she who was seen by strangers falling even upon elephants —
he who is attached to that does not consider anything at all; let it be known to you; by him I have been given
to servants; as if gone to speak by the command of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) [she went] to the ocean — whose fame [is thus]! //241//'}

children.text: atra {viditaṃ testu} iti etatkṛtam / pratyuta lakṣmīstatopasaratīti viruddhamatikṛt //
children.translated_text: Here, 'let it be known to you' — this makes it [embedded]. On the contrary, [the meaning] 'Fortune departs from him' makes it [the fault of] producing a contradictory understanding.
{'For anklets and the like, [the term is] mostly "ringing"; for birds, "cooing" and the like;
"thundering," "groaning," and the like in lovemaking; for clouds and the like, "roaring" and such —'}
thus [certain usages are] contradicting established convention. For example:

children.text:
{mahāpralayamārutakṣubhitapuṣkarāvartaka-
  pracaṇḍaghanagarjitapratirutānukārī muhuḥ /
  ravaḥ śravaṇabhairavaḥ sthagitarodasīkandaraḥ
  kuto 'dya samarodadherayambhūtapūrvaḥ puraḥ //242//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>'s <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 3.4)

{'Repeatedly imitating the fierce roar of the dense clouds of the <s>Puṣkarāvartaka</s>
agitated by the winds of the great dissolution —
this fearsome-to-the-ears sound, concealing the cavern of the sky,
from where [does it come] today before us in the battle? It has never existed before! //242//'}

children.text: atra ravo maṇḍūkādiṣu prasiddho na tūktaviśeṣe siṃhanāde //
children.translated_text: Here, 'sound' (<s>rava</s>) is conventionally established for frogs and the like, not for the specified [type] — the lion's roar.
(19) Broken sequence (<s>bhagnaprakrama</s>) — where the progression or flow is disrupted. For example:

children.text:
{nāthe niśāyā niyaterniyogādastaṃ gate hanta niśāpi yātā /
  kulāṅganānāṃ hi daśānurūpaṃ nātaḥparaṃ bhadrataraṃ samasti //243//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 122)

{'When the lord of the night, by the rule of destiny, has set — alas, the night too has passed!
For virtuous women, there is nothing more auspicious than a condition corresponding [to their nature]. //243//'}

children.text: atra {gate} iti prakrānte {yātā} iti prakṛteḥ / {gatā niśāpi} iti tu yuktam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'gone' (<s>gate</s>) was begun [in the progression], and 'passed' (<s>yātā</s>) is from a different root. Rather, 'the night too has gone' (<s>gatā niśāpi</s>) would be correct.

children.text: nanu {naikaṃ padaṃ dviḥ prayojyaṃ prāyeṇa} ityanyatra kathitapadaṃ duṣṭamiti cehaivoktam / tatkathamekasya padasya dviḥprayogaḥ / ucyate / uddeśyapratinirdeśyavyatirikto viṣaya ekapadaprayoganiṣedhasya / tadvati viṣaye pratyuta tasyaiva padasya sarvanāmro vā prayogaṃ vinā doṣaḥ / tathāhi ----
children.translated_text: Now, it was stated elsewhere that 'a single word should generally not be used twice' — [the fault of] repeated word. How then can a single word be used twice? We reply: the domain of the prohibition of single-word usage is [only] where there is no [relation of] subject and predicate. In a domain where that [relation] exists, the use of that very word or a pronoun for it is actually required to avoid [the] fault. For instance:

children.text:
{udeti savitā tāmrastāmra evāstameti ca /
  saṃpattau ca vipattau ca mahatāmekarūpatā //244//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 123)

{'The sun rises red, and red too does it set;
in prosperity and adversity, the great ones maintain a uniform character. //244//'}

children.text: atra rakta evāstametīti yadi kriyeta tadā padāntarapratipāditaḥ sa evārtho 'rthāntaratayeva pratibhāsamānaḥ pratītiṃ sthagayati // yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, if one were to say 'it sets as red,' then the very same meaning conveyed by another word, appearing as if it were a different meaning, would obstruct the cognition. Or for instance:

children.text:
{yaśodhigantuṃ sukhalipsayā vā manuṣyasaṃkhyāmativartituṃ vā /
  nirutsukānāmabhiyogabhājāṃ samutsukevāṅkamupaiti siddhiḥ //245//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhāravi</s>'s <s>Kirātārjunīya</s> 3.40)

{'To attain fame, or out of desire for happiness, or to surpass the count of human [achievements] —
for those who are dispassionate, [yet] who partake of effort, success approaches as if eagerly. //245//'}

children.text: atra pratyayasya / 'sukhamīhituṃ vā'; iti yuktaḥ pāṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, [it is an example] of the suffix. The correct reading is: 'or to desire happiness' (<s>sukhamīhituṃ vā</s>).

children.text:
{te himālayamāmantrya punaḥ prekṣya ca śūlinam /
  siddhaṃ cāsmai nivedyārthaṃ taddhisṛṣṭā kkhamudyayuḥ //246//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 6.94)

{'They, having taken leave of <s>Himālaya</s>, looking once more at the Trident-bearer [<s>Śiva</s>],
and having reported the accomplished purpose to him — released by him, they rose to the sky. //246//'}

children.text: atra sarvanāmnaḥ / 'anena visṛṣṭāḥ'; iti tu vācyam /
children.translated_text: Here, [it is an example] of the pronoun. '[Having been] released by him' (<s>anena visṛṣṭāḥ</s>) is the [correct] expression.

children.text:
{mahībhṛtaḥ putravato 'pi dṛṣṭistasminnapatye na jagāma tṛptim /
  anantapuṣpasya madhorhi cūte dvirephamālā saviśeṣasaṅgā //247//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 1.27)

children.text: atra paryāyasya / {mahībhṛtopatyavato 'pi} iti yuktam / {atra satyapi putre kanyārūpe 'pyapatye sneho 'bhūt} iti kecitsamarthayante /
children.translated_text: Here, [it is an example] of a synonym. '<s>Mahībhṛtopatyavato 'pi</s>' would be correct. Some justify it as: 'even though there was a son, love was [also] toward the daughter-form offspring.'

children.text:
{vipado 'bhibhavantyavikramaṃ rahayatyāpadupetamāyatiḥ /
  niyatā laghutā nirāyateragarīyānna padaṃ nṛpaśriyaḥ //248//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhāravi</s>'s <s>Kirātārjunīya</s> 2.14)

{'Calamities overpower the effortless; the future drives away the one met with misfortune;
diminution is certain for one who lacks breadth; one who is not weighty has no place in royal fortune. //248//'}

children.text: atropasargasya paryāyasya ca / {tadabhibhavaḥ kurute nirāyatim} / laghutāṃ bhajate nirāyatirlaghutāvānna padaṃ nṛpaśriyaḥ // iti yuktam /
children.translated_text: Here, [it is an example] of both the prefix and the synonym. The [correct form would be]: 'That overpowering brings about a lack of breadth; one who takes on diminution, being of diminution, has no place in royal fortune.'

children.text:
{kācitkīrṇā rajobhirdivamanuvidadhau mandavajtrendulakṣmī-
  raśrīkāḥ kāścidantardiśa iva dadhire dāhamudbhrāntasattvāḥ /
  bhremurvātyā ivānyāḥ pratipadamaparā bhūmivatkampamānāḥ
  prasthāne pārthivānāmaśivamiti puro bhāvi nāryaḥ śaśaṃsuḥ //249//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Māgha</s>'s <s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 15.96)

children.text: atra vacanasya / 'kāśicitkīrṇā rajobhirdivamanuvidadhurmandavaktrenduśobhā niḥśrīkāḥ'; iti 'kampamānāḥ'; ityatra 'kampamāpuḥ'; iti ca paṭhanīyam /
children.translated_text: Here, [it is an example] of verbal endings. The reading should be: 'Some, covered with dust, produced (<s>anuvidadhuḥ</s>) in the sky a moon-beauty of faint luster, their glory gone'; and for 'trembling' (<s>kampamānāḥ</s>), '[they] trembled' (<s>kampamāpuḥ</s>) should be read.

children.text:
{gāhantāṃ mahiṣā nipānasalilaṃ śṛṅgairmuhustāḍitaṃ
  chāyābaddhakadambakaṃ mṛgakulaṃ romanthamabhyasyatāṃ /
  viśrabdhaiḥ kriyatāṃ varāhapatibhirmustākṣatiḥ palvale
  viśrāntiṃ labhatāmidaṃ ca śithilajyābandhamasmaddhanuḥ //250//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Abhijñānaśakuntala</s> 2.6)

children.text: atra kārakasya / {viśrabdhā racayantu śūkaravarā mustākṣatim} ityaduṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Here, [it is an example] of the case-relation (<s>kāraka</s>). 'Let the confident boar-chiefs make <s>mustā</s>-scratch marks' would be non-faulty.

children.text:
{akalitatapastejovīryaprathimni yaśonidhā-
  vavitathamadādhmāte roṣānmunāvabhigacchati /
  abhinavadhanurvidyādarpakṣamāya ca karmaṇe
  sphurati rabhasātpāṇiḥ pādopasaṃgrahaṇāya ca //251//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mahāvīracarita</s> 2.30)

{'When the sage, in whom the glory of austerity, power, and prowess is beyond measure,
a treasury of fame, truly inflated with pride, approaches in anger —
the hand quivers impulsively — suited for the pride of new archery skill and for action,
and also for falling at [his] feet! //251//'}

children.text: atra kramasya / pādopasaṃgrahaṇāyati pūrvaṃ vācyam / evamanyadapyanusartavyam //
children.translated_text: Here, [it is an example of faulty] sequence. 'For falling at [his] feet' should be stated first. Other [examples] too should be followed thus.
(20) Without sequence (<s>akrama</s>) — where there is no [proper] sequence. For example:

children.text:
{dvayaṃ gataṃ saṃprati śocanīyatāṃ
  samāgamaprārthanayā kapālinaḥ /
  kalā ca sā kāntimatī kalāvataḥ
  tvamasya lokasya ca netrakaumudī //252[=186]//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 5.71)

{'Two things have now become pitiable,
through the desire for union of the skull-bearer [<s>Śiva</s>]:
that lovely digit of the one who possesses digits,
and you — the moonlight of this world's eye! //252[=186]//'}

children.text: atra tvaṃśabdānantaraṃ cakāro yuktaḥ / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, the particle 'ca' should follow the word 'you' (<s>tvam</s>). Or for example:

children.text:
{śaktirnistriṃśajeyaṃ tava bhujayugale nātha doṣākaraśrī-
  rvaktre pārśve tathaiṣā prativasati mahākuṭṭanī khaḍgayaṣṭiḥ /
  ājñeyaṃ sarvagā te vilasati ca puraḥ kiṃ mayā vṛddhayā te
  procyevetthaṃ prakopācchaśikarasitayā yasya kīrtyā prayātam //253//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Veṇidatta</s>'s <s>Padyaveṇī</s> 2)
Here, 'having said thus' (<s>itthaṃ procyeva</s>) would be the correct [sequence]. Likewise:
{'That which was firmly attached by her, her limbs covered with passion...... //253(a)//'}
In such [verses], 'thus by the command of <s>Śrī</s>' should be the expression.
(21) Unintended other meaning (<s>amataḥ parārthaḥ</s>) — where there is an [unintended meaning] contradictory to the intended [meaning]. For example:

children.text:
{rāmamanmathaśareṇa tāḍitā duḥsahena hṛdaye niśācarī /
  gandhavadrudhiracandanokṣitā jīviteśavasatiṃ jagāma sā //254//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 11.20)

children.text: atra prakṛte rase viruddhasya śṛṅgārasya vyañjakoparo 'rthaḥ //54//
children.translated_text: Here, the meaning suggestive of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment), which contradicts the intended <s>rasa</s>, is an unintended other meaning. //54//
He states the faults of meaning:

The meaning [may be] unsupported (<s>apuṣṭa</s>), forced (<s>kaṣṭa</s>), contradicted (<s>vyāhata</s>), redundant (<s>punarukta</s>), of bad sequence (<s>duṣkrama</s>), and vulgar (<s>grāmya</s>); // MKpr-K_55 //
doubtful (<s>saṃdigdha</s>), without reason (<s>nirhetu</s>), and contradicting established knowledge or learning;
unreviewed (<s>anavīkṛta</s>), with the restriction of what is unrestricted and distinctions that are reversible; // MKpr-K_56 //

syntactically incomplete (<s>sākāṅkṣa</s>), having an inappropriate supplement (<s>apadayukta</s>), separated from its companion (<s>sahacarabhinna</s>), having a revealed contradiction (<s>prakāśitaviruddha</s>),
having an improper injunction and restatement (<s>vidhyanuvādāyukta</s>), resuming what was abandoned (<s>tyaktapunaḥsvīkṛta</s>), and obscene (<s>aślīla</s>). // MKpr-K_57 //
'Faulty' (<s>duṣṭa</s>) should be connected [with all these]. Examples in order:
(1) [Unsupported (<s>apuṣṭa</s>)]
(<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 126)

{'Delighting in the rest obtained from release through the spread of the path across the vast sky,
the sun triumphs, making the lotuses laugh through fragrance wafted by the wind! //255//'}

children.text: atrātivitatatvādayo 'nupādāne 'pi pratipādyamānamarthaṃ na bādhanta ityapuṣṭāḥ na tvasaṃgatāḥ punaruktā vā //
children.translated_text: Here, 'the vastness' and the rest, even if not adopted, do not obstruct the meaning being conveyed — therefore they are unsupported, not however incoherent or redundant.
(2) [Forced meaning (<s>kaṣṭārtha</s>)]

children.text:
{sadā madhye yāsāmiyamamṛtani[ḥ]syandamadhurā
  sarasvatyuddāmā vahati bahumārgā parimalam /
  prasādaṃ tā etā ghanaparicitāḥ kena mahatāṃ
  mahākāvyavyomni sphuritamadhurā yāntu rucayaḥ //256//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 127)

{'That <s>Sarasvatī</s> (speech), always in the midst of which — sweet with the flow of nectar,
untamed, carrying fragrance in many paths —
those poetic modes, intimately acquainted with profundity, 
shining sweetly in the sky of great poetry — may they attain lucidity through what great one? //256//'}

children.text: atra yāsāṃ kavirucīnāṃ madhye sukumāravicitramadhyamātmakatrimārgā bhāratī camatkāraṃ vahati tāḥ gambhīrakāvyaparicitāḥ kathamitarakāvyavat prasannā bhavantu / yāsāmādityaprabhāṇāṃ madhye tripathagā vahati tā meghaparicitāḥ kathaṃ prasannā bhavantīti saṃkṣepārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, [the meaning is:] amid the poetic modes in which the three-pathed <s>Bhāratī</s> (speech) — of the delicate, variegated, and middle types — bears wonder, how can those [modes], intimately acquainted with profound poetry, become lucid like other poetry? [Alternatively:] amid the rays [of the sun] in which the triple-pathed [Gaṅgā] flows, how can those [rays], acquainted with clouds, become clear? — this is the summary meaning.
(3) [Contradicted meaning (<s>vyāhata</s>)]

children.text:
{jagati jayinaste te bhāvā navendukalādayaḥ
  prakṛtimadhurāḥ santyevānye mano madayanti ye /
  mama tu yadiyaṃ yātā loke vilocanacandrikā
  nayanaviṣayaṃ janmanyekaḥ sa eva mahotsavaḥ //257//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> 1.36)

children.text: atrendukalādayo yaṃ prati paspaśaprāyāḥ sa eva candrikātvam utkarṣārthamāropayatīti vyāhatatvam //
children.translated_text: Here, the crescent-moon digit and the rest, toward which [feelings are] mostly indifferent, [yet] he attributes the quality of being moonlight [to those qualities] for the purpose of exaltation — this is the contradiction.
(4) [Redundant (<s>punarukta</s>)]

children.text:
{kṛtamanumatamityādi //258[=39]//}
  [kṛtamanumataṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vā yairidaṃ gurupātakaṃ
  manujapaśubhirnirmaryādairbhavadbhirudāyudhaiḥ /
  narakaripuṇā sārdha teṣāṃ sabhīmakirīṭinā-
  mayamaha[ma]sṛṅmedomāṃsaiḥ karomi diśāṃ balim //39//]

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>'s <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 3.24)

{'"Those who did, approved, or witnessed this great sin..." //258[=39]//'
[Those human beasts, boundaryless and armed, by whom this great sin was done, approved, or witnessed — together with <s>Narakāri</s> [Kṛṣṇa], and with <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> among them — I shall offer oblation to the quarters with their blood, marrow, and flesh! //39//]

children.text: atrārjunārjuneti bhavadbhiriti cokte sabhīmakirīṭināmiti kirīṭipadārthaḥ punaruktaḥ / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, having said '<s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>' and 'by you,' the [phrase] 'together with the one wearing the diadem (<s>Kirīṭin</s>)' — the meaning of the word 'diadem-wearer' is redundant. Or for example:

children.text:
{astrajvālāvalīḍhapratibalajaladherantaraurvāyamāṇe
  senānāthe sthitesminmama pitari gurau sarvadhanvīśvarāṇām /
  karṇālaṃ saṃbhrameṇa vraja kṛpa samaraṃ muñca hārdikya śaṅkāṃ
  tāte cāpaddhitīye vahati raṇadhuraṃ ko bhayasyāvakāśaḥ //259//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>'s <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 3.7)

{'While my father, the chief of all archers, the lord of the army,
stands — his body like the submarine fire (<s>Aurva</s>) in the ocean of the enemy army,
licked by the flames of his missile-garlands —
O <s>Kṛpa</s>, go to <s>Karṇa</s> with agitation; O son of <s>Hārdikya</s>, abandon [your] fear —
when our father, the venerable one, bears the burden of battle, what room is there for fear? //259//'}
Here, the sentence-meaning of the fourth quarter is redundant.
(5) [Bad sequence (<s>duṣkrama</s>)]

children.text:
{bhūpālaratna nirdainyapradānaprathitotsava /
  viśrāṇaya turaṅgaṃ me mātaṅgaṃ vā madālasam //260//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 126)

{'O jewel among kings, whose festival is famed for poverty-dispelling giving!
Grant me a horse, or else an elephant, languid with rut! //260//'}
Here, the mention of the elephant should come first [since it is more valuable].
(6) [Vulgar (<s>grāmya</s>)]

children.text:
{svapiti yāvadayaṃ nikaṭe janaḥ svapimi tāvadahaṃ kimapaiti te /
  tadapi sāṃpratamāhara kūrparaṃ tvaritamūrumudañcaya kuñcitam //261//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s>)
'While these people nearby are asleep, I too shall sleep — do you not know this? Yet even now, quickly draw up the elbow, raise the thigh and bend it!' //261//
This is [an example of] the unsophisticated (<s>avidagdha</s>).
(7) Ambiguous (<s>saṃdigdha</s>):
(<s>Bhartṛhari</s>'s <s>Śṛṅgāraśataka</s>, <s>Subhāṣitatriśatī</s> 36)
'Setting aside jealousy, considering what is proper, let the noble ones declare with propriety — should the slopes be served — those of mountains, or those of women smiling with love?' //262 [=133]//

children.text: atra prakaraṇādyabhāve saṃdehaḥ śāntaśṛṅgāryanyatarābhidhāne tu niścayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, in the absence of context and such [indicators], there is doubt [about whether the sentiment is <s>śānta</s> or <s>śṛṅgāra</s>]; but when either the peaceful (<s>śānta</s>) or the erotic (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) [sentiment] is expressed, there is certainty.
(8) Without cause (<s>nirhetu</s>):

children.text:
{gṛhītaṃ yenāsīḥ paribhavabhayānnocitamapi
  prabhāvādyasyābhūnna khalu tava kaścinna viṣayaḥ /
  parityaktaṃ tena tvamasi sutaśokānna tu bhayā-
  dvimokṣye śastra tvāmahamapi yataḥ svasti bhavate //263//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>'s <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 3.19)

'That for which you were grasped — even though improper, out of fear of humiliation — through whose power indeed nothing was beyond your domain — you have been abandoned by him, out of grief for his son, not out of fear. I shall release this weapon; for from you comes well-being.' //263//
Here, no reason is given for the releasing of the [second] weapon.
(9) Contradiction with established facts (<s>prasiddhivirodha</s>):

children.text:
{idaṃ te kenoktaṃ kathaya kamalātaṅkavadane
  yadetasmin hemnaḥ kaṭakamiti dhatse khalu dhiyam /
  idaṃ tad duḥsādhākramaṇaparamāstraṃ smṛtibhuvā
  tava prītyā cakraṃ karakamalamūle vinihitam //264//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'Who told you this, O one whose face makes the lotus anxious — that upon this [ornament] of gold, you hold the idea that it is a bracelet? This is that supreme weapon against the invincible, [the discus] placed by <s>Smara</s> (the god of Memory/Love), out of affection for you, at the base of your lotus-hand.' //264//

children.text: atra kāmasya cakraṃ loke 'prasiddham / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, the discus (<s>cakra</s>) of <s>Kāma</s> (the Love-god) is not established in the world. Or again:

children.text:
{upaparisaraṃ godāvaryāḥ parityajatādhvagāḥ
  saraṇimaparo mārgastvadbhavadbhirihekṣyatām /
  iha hi vihito raktāśokaḥ kayāpi hatāśayā
  caraṇalinanyāsodañcannavāṅkurakañcukaḥ //265//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'O travelers, abandon the environs of the <s>Godāvarī</s>! Let another road, another path, be looked upon by your honors here! For here, some despairing woman has planted a red <s>aśoka</s> tree, which has a new sprout-sheath rising from the imprint of her foot-lotus.' //265//

children.text: atra pādāghātenāśokasya puṣpodgamaḥ kaviṣu prasiddho na punaraṅkurodgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the blossoming of the <s>aśoka</s> tree from a kick is well-known among poets, but not the sprouting [of new shoots from a kick].

children.text:
({susitavasanālaṅkārāyāṃ kadācana kaumudī-
  mahasi sudṛśi svairaṃ yāntyāṃ gatostamabhūdcidhuḥ /
  tadanu bhavataḥ kīrtiḥ kenāpyagīyata yena sā
  priyagṛhamagānmuktāśaṅkā kva nāsi śubhapradaḥ //266//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 121)

children.text: atrāmūrtāpi kīrtiḥ jyotsnāvatprakāśarūpā kathiteti lokaviruddhamapi kaviprasiddherna duṣṭam //)
children.translated_text: Here, although fame, being formless, is described as luminous like moonlight — [this], though contradicting common experience, is not faulty, because it is established in poetic convention.

'Once, on a [night] adorned with white garments and ornaments, when the beautiful woman was going freely in the moonlight festival, the moon set. Thereafter, your fame was sung by someone, whereby she, freed from doubt, went to her beloved's house — O bestower of auspiciousness, where are you not present?' //266//
(10) Contradiction with learned tradition (<s>vidyāvirodha</s>):

children.text:
{sadā snātvā niśīthinyāṃ sakalaṃ vāsaraṃ budhaḥ /
  nānāvidhāni śāstrāṇi vyācaṣṭe ca śṛṇoti ca //267//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 132)
'Having bathed always at midnight, the learned one, throughout the entire day, expounds and listens to various treatises.' //267//

children.text: grahoparāgādikaṃ vinā rātrau snānaṃ dharmaśāstraṇa viruddham /
children.translated_text: Bathing at night, except during a planetary eclipse and the like, is contrary to the <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (legal tradition).

children.text:
{ananyasadṛśaṃ yasya balaṃ bāhvoḥ samīkṣyate /
  ṣāḍaguṇyānusṛtistasya satyaṃ sā niṣprayojanā //268//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s> 240)
