'For one whose unmatched strength of arms is perceived, the observance of the sixfold policy (<s>ṣāḍguṇya</s>) is indeed truly purposeless.' //268//
This [contradicts] the <s>arthaśāstra</s> (science of statecraft).

children.text:
{vidhāya dūre keyūramanaṅgāṅgaṇamaṅganā /
  babhāra kāntena kṛtāṃ karajollekhamālikām //269//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'Having placed the armlet far away on the battlefield of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless Love-god), the woman wore a garland of nail-marks made by her lover.' //269//

children.text: atra keyūrapade nakhaksaṭaṃ na vihitamiti / etatkāmaśāstreṇa /
children.translated_text: Here, the nail-mark is not made at the [place of the] armlet. This [contradicts] the <s>kāmaśāstra</s> (science of love).

children.text:
{kaṣṭāṅgayogapariśīlanakīlanena
  duḥsādhasiddhisavidhaṃ vidadhadvidūre /
  āsādayannabhimatāmadhunā viveka-
  khyātiṃ samādhidhanamaulimarṇirvimuktaḥ //270//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

'Through the nail of painful <s>aṅgayoga</s> (bodily discipline) and its practice, bringing the difficult-to-attain accomplishment near and making [it] distant, now attaining the desired <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative knowledge), the crest-jewel of <s>samādhi</s>-wealth — the sage is liberated.' //270//

children.text: atra vivekakhyātistataḥ saṃprajñātasamādhiḥ paścādasaṃprajñātastato muktirna tu vivekakhyātau / etat yogaśāstreṇa //
children.translated_text: Here, <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative knowledge), then <s>saṃprajñātasamādhi</s> (cognitive meditation), then <s>asaṃprajñātasamādhi</s> (non-cognitive meditation), then liberation — but not [liberation] at the stage of <s>vivekakhyāti</s>. This [contradicts] the <s>yogaśāstra</s> (science of yoga).
Thus, contradiction with other learned traditions should also be illustrated.
(11) Not renewed (<s>anavīkṛta</s>):

children.text:
{prāptāḥ śriyaḥ sakalakāmadughāstataḥ kim
  dattaṃ padaṃ śirasi vidviṣatāṃ tataḥ kim /
  saṃtarpitāḥ praṇayino vibhavaistataḥ kim
  kalpaṃ sthitaṃ tanubhṛtāṃ tanubhistataḥ kim //271//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhartṛhari</s>'s <s>Vairāgyaśataka</s> 67)

'Wealth has been obtained, fulfilling all desires — then what? A place has been given on the heads of enemies — then what? Dear ones have been gratified with riches — then what? One has endured for an aeon in one's body — then what?' //271//

children.text: atra tataḥ kimiti na navīkṛtam / tattu yathā
children.translated_text: Here, 'then what?' is not renewed [with varying formulation]. But it [is done properly] thus:

children.text:
{yadi dahatyanalotra kimadbhutaṃ yadi ca gauravamadriṣu kiṃ tataḥ /
  lavaṇamambu sadaiva mahodadheḥ prakṛtireva satāmaviṣāditā //272//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ānandavardhana</s>'s <s>Deviśataka</s>)
'If fire burns here, what is wondrous? And if there is gravity in mountains, what of it? The water of the great ocean is always salty — the nature of the good is never depressed.' //272//
(12) With restricted reversal (<s>saniyamaparivṛtta</s>):

children.text:
{yatrānullikhitārthameva nikhilaṃ nirmāṇametadvidher-
  utkarṣapratiyogikalpanamapi nyakkārakoṭiḥ parā /
  yātāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ manorathagatīrullaṅghya yatsaṃpadas
  tasyābhāsamaṇīkṛtāśmasumaṇeraśmatvamevocitam //273//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kuntaka</s>'s <s>Vakroktijīvita</s> 1.29)

'Where this entire creation of the Creator is merely an outline, where even the imagination of a rival in excellence is the ultimate in humiliation, where the prosperities, having surpassed the courses of desire of living beings, have gone beyond — for him who has made a mere shadow-stone into a jewel, the status of a [mere] stone is indeed fitting.' //273//
Here, 'in shadow-stones that are merely made into jewels, the stone-nature of those [genuine] jewels is fitting' — this restriction should be stated.
(13) With unrestricted reversal (<s>aniyamaparivṛtta</s>):

children.text:
{vaktrāmbhojaṃ sarasvatyadhivasati sadā śoṇa evādharaste
  bāhuḥ kākutsthavīryasmṛtikaraṇapaṭurdakṣiṇaste samudraḥ /
  vāhinyaḥ pārśvametāḥ kṣaṇamapi bhavato naiva muñcantyabhīkṣaṇaṃ
  svacchentarmānasesmin kathamavanipate tembupānābhilāṣaḥ //274//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ballāla</s>'s <s>Bhojaprabandha</s> 230)

'The lotus-face is always inhabited by <s>Sarasvatī</s>; your lip is indeed the <s>Śoṇa</s> [river]; your right arm is the ocean, skilled in recalling the valor of <s>Kākutstha's</s> [descendant]; these streams never leave your side for even a moment; in this clear inner lake of yours, O king of the earth, how could there be desire for water-drinking?' //274//

children.text: atra {śoṇa eva} iti niyamo na vācyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the restriction 'the <s>Śoṇa</s> indeed' should not be stated.
(14) With reversed particular (<s>viśeṣaparivṛtta</s>):

children.text:
{śyāmāṃ śyāmalimānamānayata bhoḥ sāndrairmaṣīkūrcakair
  mantraṃ tantramatha prayujya harata śvetotpalānāṃ śriyam /
  candraṃ carṇayata kṣaṇācca kaṇaśaḥ kṛtvā śilāpaṭṭake
  yena draṣṭumahaṃ kṣame daśa diśastadvaktramudrāṅkitāḥ //275//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rājaśekhara</s>'s <s>Viddhaśālabhañjikā</s> 3.1)

'O bring the dark complexion, the darkness, with dense brushes of ink! Then, applying incantation and spell, remove the beauty of the white lotuses! And inscribe the moon in an instant, particle by particle, on a stone slab — so that I may be able to see, with the ten directions stamped with the seal of that face.' //275//
Here, 'moonlight' (<s>jyautsnī</s>) — a particular type of <s>śyāmā</s> (dark complexion) — should be stated.
(15) With reversed general (<s>aviśeṣaparivṛtta</s>):

children.text:
{kallolavellitadṛṣatparuṣaprahārai
  ratnānyamūni makarālaya māvamaṃsthāḥ /
  kiṃ kaustubhena vihito bhavato na nāma
  yā[ñc]āprasāritakaraḥ puruṣottame 'pi //276//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhallaṭaśataka</s> 62)

'O abode of <s>makaras</s> (sea-monsters), do not despise these jewels [cast about] by the rough blows of waves rolling with billows! Was not the <s>Kaustubha</s> [gem] offered by you to <s>Puruṣottama</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) himself, with hand outstretched in supplication?' //276//

children.text: atra {ekena kiṃ na vihito bhavataḥ sa nāma} iti sāmānyaṃ vācyam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'was not a single one offered by you?' — the general [statement] should be stated.
(16) Incomplete (<s>sākāṅkṣa</s>):

children.text:
{arthitve prakaṭīkṛte 'pi na phalaprāptiḥ prabhoḥ pratyuta
  druhyan dāśarathirviruddhacarito yuktastayā kanyayā /
  utkarṣaṃ ca parasya mānayaśasorvisraṃsanaṃ cātmanaḥ
  strīratnaṃ ca jagatpatirdaśamukho devaḥ kathaṃ mṛṣyate //277//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mahāvīracarita</s> 2.9)

'Although the [<s>Sītā's</s>] desire was made manifest, there was no attainment of the fruit from the lord; on the contrary, the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, hostile and of contradictory conduct, was united with that maiden; the exaltation of the other and the collapse of one's own honor and pride — how does <s>Daśamukha</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), the lord of the world, the god, endure the woman-jewel?' //277//

children.text: atra strīratnam 'upeks.itum'; ityākāṅkṣati / nahi parasyetyanena saṃbandho yogyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, 'the woman-jewel' requires [the infinitive] 'to disregard'; for the connection with 'the exaltation of the other' is not appropriate.
(17) With an unfit word (<s>apadayukta</s>):

children.text:
{ājñā śakraśikhāmaṇipraṇayinī śāstrāṇi cakṣurnavaṃ
  bhaktirbhūtapatau pinākini padaṃ laṅketi divyā purī /
  utpattirdruhiṇānvaye ca tadaho nedṛgvaro labhyate
  syāccedeṣa na rāvaṇaḥ kva nu punaḥ sarvatra sarve guṇāḥ //278//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rājaśekhara</s>'s <s>Bālarāmāyaṇa</s> 1.36)

'His command wins the affection of <s>Indra</s>'s crest-jewel; his scriptures are a new eye; his devotion is to the lord of beings, the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>; his abode is <s>Laṅkā</s>, a divine city; his birth is in the lineage of <s>Brahmā</s> — alas, such a bridegroom is not to be found! If only he were not <s>Rāvaṇa</s>! But where indeed are all qualities found in one?' //278//

children.text: atra 'syāccedeṣa na rāvaṇaḥ'; ityatra eva samāpyam //
children.translated_text: Here, 'if only he were not <s>Rāvaṇa</s>' — the sentence should end right there.
(18) With dissimilar companions (<s>sahacarabhinna</s>):

children.text:
{śrutena buddhirvyasanena mūrkhatā madena nārī salilena nimnagā /
  niśā śaśāṅkena dhṛtiḥsamādhinā nayena cālaṅkriyate narendratā //279//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 140)
'Intellect is adorned by learning, foolishness by vice, a woman by intoxication, a river by water, night by the moon, fortitude by meditation, and sovereignty by statecraft.' //279//
Here, vice and foolishness, being inferior, are inconsistent with the excellent companions such as learning and the rest.
(19) With disclosed contradiction (<s>prakāśitaviruddha</s>):

children.text:
{lagnaṃ rāgāvṛtāṅgyā- ....... //280[=241]//}
  [lagnaṃ rāgāvṛtāṅgyā sudṛḍhamiha yayaivāsiyaṣṭyārikaṇṭhe
  mātaṅgānāmapīhopari parapuruṣairyā ca dṛṣṭā patantī /
  tatsakto 'yaṃ na kiñcidgaṇayati viditaṃ testu tenāsmi dattā
  bhṛtyebhyaḥ śrīniyogādgaditumiva gatetyambudhiṃ yasya kīrtiḥ //241//]

children.translated_text: (<s>Veṇidatta</s>'s <s>Padyaveṇī</s> 2)

'[She who] clung firmly to the enemy's throat with her sword-staff, her limbs covered with passion...' //280 [=241]// [She who, with limbs covered in passion, clung firmly with her sword-staff to the enemy's throat; she too was seen falling from atop elephants by other men. Yet he, attached to her, considers nothing — 'Let them know!' — 'By her I have been given to servants through the command of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), as if she has gone, like [going] to the ocean' — whose fame!]

children.text: ityatra viditaṃ testvityanena śrīstasmādapasaratīti viruddhaṃ prakāśyate //
children.translated_text: Here, by the phrase 'let them know,' the contradictory [implication] that <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune/Lakṣmī) departs from him is made manifest.
(20) With unfit injunction (<s>vidhyayukta</s>):

children.text:
{prayatnaparibodhitaḥ stutibhiradya śeṣe niśā-
  makeśavamapāṇḍavaṃ bhuvanamadya niḥsomakam /
  iyaṃ parisamāpyate raṇakathādya doḥśālinā-
  mapaitu ripukānanātigururadya bhāro bhuvaḥ //281//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>'s <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 3.34)

'O you who are awakened with effort through praises! Sleep today! O <s>Keśava</s>! Today the world is without <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, without the moon. Today this tale of the battle of the arm-proud ones reaches its conclusion. Today let the excessive burden of enemies depart from the earth!' //281//

children.text: atra {śayitaḥ prayatnena bodhyase} iti vidheyam / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, the predicate should be 'you who have slept are being awakened with effort.' Or again:

children.text:
{vātāhāratayā jagadviṣadharairāśvāsya niḥśaṣitaṃ
  te grastāḥ punarabhratoyakaṇikātīvravratairbarhibhiḥ /
  te 'pi kruracamūrucarmavasanairnītāḥ kṣayaṃ lubdhakair-
  dambhasya sphuritaṃ vidannapi jano jālmo guṇānīhate //282//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhallaṭaśataka</s> 87)

'The serpents, consoled by the wind-eaters that the world is devoured, are then swallowed by the peacocks with their vow of intense [consumption of] dewdrops and water; those [peacocks] too are brought to destruction by hunters dressed in cruel army skins — and yet people, knowing the manifestation of hypocrisy, [still] desire qualities!' //282//
Here, the three [elements] — 'wind-eaters' and so forth — should be stated in reverse order.
(21) With inappropriate reiteration (<s>anuvādāyukta</s>):

children.text:
{are rāmāhastābharaṇa bhasalaśreṇiśaraṇa
  smarakrīḍāvrīḍāśamana virahiprāṇadamana /
  sarohaṃsottaṃsa pracaladala nīlotpala sakhe
  sakhedo 'haṃ mohaṃ ślathaya kathaya kvenduvadanā //283//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s>)

'O ornament of <s>Rāma's</s> hand! O refuge of the streak of ashes! O pacifier of the shame of the sport of <s>Smara</s> (Love)! O destroyer of the life-breath of the love-sick! O crest-ornament of the lake-swan, O trembling-petaled blue lotus, O friend! I am distressed — dispel [my] delusion — tell me, where is the moon-faced one?' //283//
Here, 'O destroyer of the life-breath of the love-sick' is not [appropriate as] reiteration [of the topic].
(22) Abandoned and then re-adopted (<s>tyaktapunaḥsvīkṛta</s>):

children.text:
{lagnaṃ rāgāvṛtāṅgyetyādi //284=41//}
  [lagnaṃ rāgāvṛtāṅgyā sudṛḍhamiha yayaivāsiyaṣṭyārikaṇṭhe
  mātaṅgānāmapīhopari parapuruṣairyā ca dṛṣṭā patantī /
  tatsakto 'yaṃ na kiñcidgaṇayati viditaṃ testu tenāsmi dattā
  bhṛtyebhyaḥ śrīniyogādgaditumiva gatetyambudhiṃ yasya kīrtiḥ //241//]

children.translated_text: (<s>Veṇidatta</s>'s <s>Padyaveṇī</s> 2)
'[She who] clung firmly to the enemy's throat with her sword-staff, her limbs covered with passion...' //284 [=241]// [same verse as 241]
Here, though concluded with 'let them know,' [the reference to <s>Śrī</s>] is taken up again with 'by her' and so forth.
(23) Indecent (<s>aślīla</s>):

children.text:
{hantumeva pravṛttasya stabdhasya vivaraiṣiṇaḥ /
  yathāsya jāyate pāto na tathā punarunnatiḥ //285//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhāmaha</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṃkāra</s> 1.51)
Here, the perception of the male organ is also [produced].
'Of one engaged in killing, stiff, seeking openings — as his fall occurs, his rising again does not occur in the same way.' //285//

children.text: yatraiko doṣaḥ pradarśitastatra doṣāntarāṇyapi santi tathāpi teṣāṃ tatrāprakṛtatvātprakāśanaṃ na kṛtam //55-57//
children.translated_text: Where a single fault has been demonstrated, other faults too exist; however, since those are not the primary [subject of discussion] there, they have not been made explicit. //55-57//
In words such as 'ear-ornament' (<s>karṇāvataṃsa</s>) and the like, the mention of 'ear' and such [body-parts] is made for the purpose of indicating location...

children.text: avataṃsādīni karṇādyābharaṇānyevocyante / tatra karṇādiśabdāḥ karṇādisthitipratipattaye / yathā
children.translated_text: 'Ear-ornament' and the like refer to ornaments of the ear and such. Therein, words like 'ear' are [used] for the understanding of their location on the ear and such [body-parts]. As in:

children.text:
{asyāḥ karṇāvataṃsena jitaṃ sarvaṃ vibhūṣaṇam /
  tathaiva śobhatetyarthamasyāḥ śravaṇakuṇḍalam //286//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vāmana</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṃkārasūtravṛtti</s> 2.2.14)
'By the ear-ornament of this one, all ornaments are surpassed; in the same way, the ear-ring of this one is beautiful — this is the meaning.' //286//
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
'Then, from the unprecedented sweet fragrance that delighted the directions, there arrived [flowers] buzzing with bees, wearing garlands upon the head.' //287//
Here, the words 'ear' (<s>karṇa</s>), 'hearing' (<s>śravaṇa</s>), and 'head' (<s>śiras</s>) are used for the understanding of their proximity [to the ornament].
(<s>Vāmana's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 2.2.13)
'In the midst of battle, fearsome with [the sight of] enemy fronts shattered, your arm, marked with the callus-sign of the bowstring, quivered.' //288//
Here, the word '<s>dhanus</s>' (bow) is [used] for the purpose of conveying the sense of 'mounted' (<s>ārūḍha</s>).
But elsewhere:

children.text:
{jyābandhaniṣpandabhujena yasya viniśvamadvaktraparaṃpareṇa /
  kārāgṛhe nirjitavāsavane laṅkeśvareṇoṣitamā prasādāt //289//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa's</s> <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 6.20)

{By him, the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, who had conquered <s>Indra</s>, [<s>Rāvaṇa</s>] whose arm was rendered motionless from the binding of the bowstring, whose row of mouths was hissing — imprisonment was endured until [<s>Rāma's</s>] grace. ||289||}
Here, the word '<s>jyā</s>' (bowstring) alone [is used, without the word for bow].
(<s>Vāmana's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 2.2.15)
{With the movements of confusion arising from the embrace of the lord of her life, the pair of breasts, gleaming with a pearl necklace, seem to laugh. ||290||}
Here, the word '<s>muktā</s>' (pearl) is [used] to indicate that [the pearls are] unmixed with other gems.

children.text:
{saundaryasaṃpat tāruṇyaṃ yasyāste te ca vibhramāḥ /
  ṣaṭpadān puṣpamāleva kān nākarṣati sā sakhe //291//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{The wealth of beauty, youth, and those charms of hers — like a flower-garland [attracting] bees, whom does she not attract, O friend? ||291||}

children.text: atrotkṛṣṭapuṣpaviṣaye puṣpaśabdaḥ / nirupapado hi mālāśabdaḥ puṣpasrajamevābhidhatte //
children.translated_text: Here, the word '<s>puṣpa</s>' (flower) is [used] with reference to excellent flowers. For the word '<s>mālā</s>' (garland) without a qualifier denotes only a garland of flowers.
... when [the above conditions] are established, this serves as their justification. || MKpr-K_58 ||

children.text:
{na khalu karṇāvataṃsādivajjaghanakāñcītyādi kriyate /
  jagāda madhurāṃ vācaṃ viśadākṣaraśālinīm //292//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vāmana's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 2.2.18)

{It is not the case that [such usage is made] like ear-ornaments and the like — [but rather,] 'hip-girdle' and such [are legitimate]. She spoke a sweet utterance, graced with clear syllables. ||292||}

children.text: ityādau kriyāviśeṣaṇatve 'pi vivakṣitārthapratītisiddhau {gatārthasyāpi viśeṣyasya viśeṣaṇadānārthaṃ kvacitprayogaḥ kāryaḥ} iti na yuktam / yuktatve vā
children.translated_text: In such cases, even when [the additional word] is a qualifier of an action, since the cognition of the intended meaning is already established, the [maxim that] 'sometimes the use [of a qualifier] for the purpose of attributing a distinction to a referent whose meaning is already known should be made' — is not appropriate. Or if it is held to be appropriate, [then the following would also have to be exemplified]:

children.text:
{caraṇatraparitrāṇarahitābhyāmapi drutam /
  pādābhyāṃ dūramadhvānaṃ vrajanneṣa na khidyate //293//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{Even without the protection of foot-coverings, this one, walking swiftly a long distance on foot, does not become weary. ||293||}
[This] should be cited as an example. ||58||
When the meaning is well-known, [its restatement] without a reason is not a defect...
For example:

children.text:
{candraṃ gatā padmaguṇānna bhuṅkte padmāśritā cāndramasīmabhikhyām /
  umāmukhaṃ tu pratipadya lolā dvisaṃśrayāṃ prītimavāpa lakṣmīḥ //294//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa's</s> <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 1.43)

{<s>Lakṣmī</s>, having gone to the moon, does not enjoy the qualities of the lotus; and dwelling in the lotus, she does not enjoy the moonlike radiance. But having attained the face of <s>Umā</s>, the fickle one obtained a double-based delight. ||294||}

children.text: atra rātrau padmasya saṃkocaḥ divā candramasaśca niṣprabhatvaṃ lokaprasiddhamiti 'na bhuṅkte '; iti hetuṃ nāpekṣate //
children.translated_text: Here, the closing of the lotus at night and the loss of radiance of the moon during the day are well-known to the world, so 'does not enjoy' does not require a reason.
... but in the case of imitation, [a defect applies] to all of them.
'All of them' means all defects beginning with <s>śrutikaṭu</s> (harsh-sounding). For example:

children.text:
{mṛgacakṣuṣamadrākṣamityādi kathayatyayam /
  paśyaiṣa ca gavityāha sūtrāmāṇaṃ yajeta ca //295//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 147)
{This one tells of how 'I saw the doe-eyed one' and so on; and also look, he says '<s>gavi</s>' (like a cow) and 'one should perform the <s>sūtrāmāṇa</s> sacrifice.' ||295||}
By the propriety of the speaker and the like, a defect sometimes becomes a quality; sometimes it is neither. || MKpr-K_59 ||

children.text: vakṛpratipādyavyaṅgavācyaprakaraṇādīnāṃ mahimnā doṣo 'pi kvacidaguṇaḥ kvacinna doṣo na guṇaḥ / tatra vyākaraṇādau vaktari pratipādye ca raudrādau ca rase vyaṅge kaṣṭatvaṃ guṇaḥ / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: By the power of the speaker, the subject being presented, the suggested <s>rasa</s>, the expressed content, the context, and the like, a defect sometimes is not a [real] fault; sometimes it is neither a defect nor a quality. Therein, when the speaker is [characterized as] a grammarian and the like, when the subject being presented [requires it], and when the suggested <s>rasa</s> is <s>raudra</s> (the furious) and the like, harshness becomes a quality. Examples in order:

children.text:
{dīrghīṅvevīṅsamaḥ kaścidguṇavṛddhyorabhājanam /
  kvippratyayanibhaḥ kaścidyatra saṃnihite na te //296//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 43)

{Some [person], equal to <s>dīrgha</s>, <s>iṅ</s>, <s>vevīṅ</s>, not partaking of <s>guṇa</s> and <s>vṛddhi</s>, resembling the <s>kvip</s> suffix — where you are not present, he is not present either. ||296||}

children.text:
{yadā tvāmahamadrākṣaṃ padavidyāviśāradam /
  upādhyāyaṃ tadāsmārṣaṃ samasprākṣaṃ ca saṃmadam //297//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 149)
{When I saw you, learned in the science of words, O teacher, then I remembered, and I touched joy with delight. ||297||}
(<s>Bhavabhūti's</s> <s>Mahāvīracarita</s> 1.35)

{With ornaments consisting mostly of swinging entrails-strung large skull-strings and cruelly clanging bracelets, filling the sky with their clamor; with a body terrifying under the weight of heaving, trembling breasts, dense with the mass of a load of drunk, vomited, blood-and-mud — she runs, swollen with pride! ||298||}
When [harsh sound is appropriate] by the force of the expressed content (<s>vācya</s>):

children.text:
{mātaṅgāḥ kimu vilgitaiḥ kimaphalairāḍambarairjambukāḥ
  sāraṅgā mahiṣā madaṃ vrajatha kiṃ śūnyeṣu śarā na ke /
  kopāṭopasamudbhaṭotkaṭasaṭākoṭeribhāreḥ puraḥ
  sindhudhvānini huṅkṛte sphurati yat tadgarjitaṃ garjitam //299//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{O elephants, what [use] of your prancings? O jackals, what [use] of your fruitless blusterings? O deer, O buffalos, why do you advance in frenzy? In empty [forests], who are these arrows [aimed at]? Before the one whose mane-tips are fierce, bristling, thick, and massive with the fury of rage — in that thundering roar of ocean-sound — what flashes forth is [true] roaring! ||299||}
Here, when the lion is the expressed content, harsh words [are appropriate].
When [harshness is appropriate] by the force of context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>):

children.text:
{raktāśoka kṛśodarī kka nu gatā tyaktvānuraktaṃ janaṃ
  no dṛṣṭeti mudhaiva cālayasi kiṃ vātāvadhūtaṃ śiraḥ /
  utkaṇṭhāghaṭamānaṣaḍpadaghaṭāsaṃghaṭṭadaṣ.ṭacchada-
  statpādāhatimantareṇa bhavataḥ puṣpodgamo 'yaṃ kutaḥ //300//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa's</s> <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 4)

{O red <s>Aśoka</s> tree, where has the slender-waisted one gone, abandoning one who loves her? You have not seen her, yet you shake your head in vain, tossed by the wind — whence this blossoming of yours without the kick of her foot, when your petals are already bitten by the clustering bees pressing together in their longing? ||300||}
Here, in the speech of one who is angry, with the head-shaking [of the tree as context].

children.text: kvacinnīrase na guṇo na doṣaḥ / yathā
children.translated_text: Sometimes, in the absence of <s>rasa</s>, [a defect] is neither a quality nor a fault. For example:

children.text:
{śīrṇaghrāṇāṅghrapāṇīn vraṇibhirapaghanairgharāvyaktaghoṣān
  dīrghāghrātānaghaughaiḥ punarapi ghaṭayatyeka ullāghayan yaḥ /
  gharmāṃśostasya vontardviguṇaghanaghṛṇānighnanirvighnavṛtter
  dattārghāḥ siddhasaṃghairvidadhatu ghṛṇayaḥ śīghramaṃhovighātam //301//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Mayūra's</s> <s>Sūryaśataka</s> 6)

{He who, exulting, reassembles those with severed noses, feet, and hands, with emaciated bodies of indistinct cries and wounds — joining them again with accumulated sins — may the rays of compassion of that [sun], whose inner activity is of doubled dense compassion, destroying obstacles without hindrance, to whom the assemblies of <s>siddhas</s> have offered worship, quickly destroy our darkness! ||301||}
The [defects of] unused (<s>aprayukta</s>) and destroyed meaning (<s>nihatārtha</s>) are not defects in <s>śleṣa</s> (punning) and the like. For example:

children.text:
{yena dhvastamanobhavena balijitkāyaḥ purā strīkṛto
  yaścoddhṛttabhujaṅgahāravalayogaṅgāṃ ca yodhārayat /
  yasyāhuḥ śaśimacchirohara iti syutyaṃ ca nāmāmarāḥ
  pāyātsa svayamandhakakṣayakarastvāṃ sarvadomādhavaḥ //302//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vallabhadeva's</s> <s>Subhāṣitāvali</s>; <s>Abhinavagupta's</s> <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s> [2.21-22])

{By whom [<s>Śiva</s>], having destroyed <s>Manobhava</s> (<s>Kāma</s>), the body of the conqueror of <s>Bali</s> [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] was formerly made feminine [<s>Mohinī</s>]; who bore the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, adorned with the ornamental garland of serpents lifted up; whom the immortals call '<s>Śaśimad</s>' ('moon-bearing') — and that is also a proper name [<s>Śiva</s>] — may that <s>Mādhava</s>, the destroyer of <s>Andhaka</s>, himself protect you, O giver of all! ||302||}

Here, in the interpretation referring to <s>Mādhava</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>/<s>Viṣṇu</s>], the words '<s>śaśimad</s>' and '<s>andhakakṣaya</s>' are [examples of] unused and destroyed meaning [which are not defects in the context of <s>śleṣa</s>].

children.text:
aślīlaṃ kvacidguṇaḥ / yathā suratārambhagoṣṭhyām {dvyartheḥ
padaiḥ piśunayecca rahasyavastu} iti kāmaśāstrasthitau
children.translated_text: The indecent (<s>aślīla</s>) is sometimes a quality. As in the context of the commencement of lovemaking: 'With words of double meaning, one should hint at the secret matter' — according to the precept of the <s>Kāmaśāstra</s>:

children.text:
{karihastena saṃbādhe praviśyāntarviloḍite /
  upasarpan dhvajaḥ puṃsaḥ sādhanāntarvirājate //303//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 154)
{Entering the narrow passage enclosed by the elephant's trunk, stirring within — the banner of a man, approaching, shines with a different instrument. ||303||}
In narratives of renunciation (<s>śama</s>):
(<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 155)
{In the woman's wound — moist, resembling the split belly of an overturned croaking frog — whose attachment, if not a worm's, would arise? ||304||}

children.text:
{nirvāṇavairadahanāḥ praśamādarīṇāṃ
  nandantu pāṇḍutanayā saha mādhavena /
  raktaprasādhitabhuvaḥ kṣatavigrahāśca
  svasthā bhavantu kururājasutāḥ sabhṛtyāḥ //305//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa's</s> <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 1.7)

{May the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, whose fire of enmity is extinguished, and who dwell in the caves of tranquility, rejoice with <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>); and may the sons of the <s>Kuru</s> king, whose earth is adorned with blood, whose bodies are wounded, be well along with their servants! ||305||}
Here, [the words] indicate an auspicious event that is yet to come.

children.text: saṃdigdhamapi vācyamahimnā kvacinniyatārthapratītikṛttvena vyājastutiparyavasāyitve guṇaḥ / yathā
children.translated_text: The ambiguous (<s>saṃdigdha</s>) too, by the force of the expressed content, is sometimes a quality, when it produces the cognition of a determinate meaning and culminates in ironic praise (<s>vyājastuti</s>). For example:

children.text:
{pṛthukārtasvarapātraṃ bhūṣitaniḥśeṣaparijanaṃ deva /
  vilasatkareṇugahanaṃ saṃprati samamāvayoḥ sadanam //306//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Subhāṣitaratnākara</s> 1644)
{O lord, your house now has wide vessels of gold, an entirely adorned retinue, and is dense with shining she-elephants — it is now equal to mine! ||306||}
The unfamiliar (<s>apratīta</s>) is a quality when both the subject being presented and the one presenting are knowledgeable. For example:

children.text:
{ātmārāmā vihitaratayo nirvikalpe samādau
  jñānodrekādvighaṭitatamogranthayaḥ sattvaniṣṭhāḥ /
  yaṃ vīkṣante kamapi tamasāṃ jyotiṣāṃ vā parastāt
  taṃ mohāndhaḥ kathamayamamuṃ vetti devaṃ purāṇaṃ //307//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa's</s> <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 1.23)

{Those who delight in the Self, whose pleasures are established in undifferentiated <s>samādhi</s> (meditation), whose knots of darkness are sundered by the surge of knowledge, who are established in <s>sattva</s> — they behold something beyond both darkness and light. How can this one, blinded by delusion, know that ancient god? ||307||}
Or [the unfamiliar is a quality] when it involves self-contemplation. For example:

children.text:
{ṣaḍadhikadaśanāḍīcakramadhyasthitātmā
  hṛdi vinihitarūpaḥ siddhidastaddhitāṃ yaḥ /
  avicalitamanobhiḥ sādhakairmṛgyamāṇaḥ
  sa jayati pariṇaddhaḥ śaktibhiḥ śaktināthaḥ //308//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti's</s> <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> 5.1)

{The Self, stationed in the middle of the sixteen-plus-six <s>nāḍī</s>-wheels, with form established in the heart, granting <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) and welfare — sought by practitioners with unshaken minds — that Lord of Power, girded with <s>śaktis</s> (powers), is victorious! ||308||}
In the utterances of one of lowly disposition, the vulgar (<s>grāmya</s>) is a quality. For example:

children.text:
{phullukkaraṃ kalamakūraṇihaṃ vahanti
  je sindhuvāraviḍavā maha vallahā de /
  je gālidassa mahisīdahiṇo saricchā
  de kiṃ ca muddhavi_a_illapasūṇapuñjā //309//}

children.translated_text: [Those <s>sindhuvāra</s> shrubs that bear clusters of blossoms resembling rice-pudding are my beloveds;
those that look like buffalo-milk buttermilk strained through cloth;
and those innocent masses of blooming buds with interlocked petals —
what of them too?]
(<s>Rājaśekhara's</s> <s>Karpūramañjarī</s> 1.19)
{Those <s>sindhuvāra</s> shrubs that bear clusters of flowers resembling rice-and-lentil dishes are dear to me, my beloved;
Here, the words 'rice-pudding' (<s>kalamabhakta</s>), 'buffalo-milk buttermilk' (<s>mahiṣīdadhi</s>) and the like, though vulgar, are [appropriate] in the speech of the <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester).
Deficiency of words (<s>nyūnapada</s>) is sometimes a quality. For example:

children.text:
{gāḍhāliṅganavāmanīkṛtakucaprodbhūtaromodgamā
  sāndrasneharasātirekavigalacchrīmannitambāmbarā /
  mā mā mānada māti māmalamiti kṣāmākṣarollāpinī
  suptā kiṃ nu mṛtā nu kiṃ manasi me līnā vilīnā nu kim //310//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 36)
Sometimes [it is] neither a quality nor a defect. For example:

{With the rising of hair on the body from her breasts being flattened by the tight embrace, with the garment slipping from her beautiful hips due to the excess of intense love's moisture, murmuring with languid eyes 'No, no, O bestower of honor, too much, enough, stop!' — is she asleep? Or is she dead? Or is she absorbed in my mind? Or has she dissolved? ||310||}

children.text:
{tiṣṭhetkopavaśātprabhāvapihitā dīrghaṃ na sā kupyati
  svargāyotpatitā bhavenmayi punarbhāvādramasyā manaḥ /
  tāṃ hartuṃ vibudhadviṣo 'pi na ca me śaktāḥ purovartinīṃ
  sā cātyantamagocaraṃ nayanayoryāteti ko 'yaṃ vidhiḥ //311//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa's</s> <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 4.9)

{She might remain, concealed by [her own] power, out of anger — but she does not remain angry for long; having flown up to heaven, her mind might again incline lovingly toward me; even the enemies of the gods cannot seize her when she is before me — yet she has gone utterly beyond the range of my eyes. What is this fate? ||311||}

children.text: atra pihitā ityatonantaraṃ 'naitadyataḥ'; ityetairnyūnaiḥ padairviśeṣabuddherakaraṇānna guṇaḥ / uttarā pratipattiḥ pūrvāṃ pratipattiṃ bādhate iti na doṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, after '<s>pihitā</s>' (concealed), [the words] 'this is not so, because...' — since the non-production of a specific cognition by these deficient words is [neither helpful nor harmful], it is not a quality. [But] since the latter understanding overrides the former understanding, it is not a defect either.
Excess of words (<s>adhikapada</s>) is sometimes a quality. For example:

children.text:
{yadvañcanāhitamatirbahucāṭugarbhaṃ
  kāryonmukhaḥ khalajanaḥ krṭakaṃ bravīti /
  tatsādhavo na na vidanti vidanti kintu
  kartuṃ vṛthā praṇayamasya na pārayanti //312//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinavagupta's</s> <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s> 3.16)

{What the wicked person, with mind set on deception, says in a manner full of much flattery, intent on his purpose, and artificially — the virtuous ones do not not know it; they do know it. But they are not able to render his affection futile. ||312||}
Here, the second '<s>vidanti</s>' (they know) serves to exclude [the possibility of] connection with another [meaning]. Or alternatively:

children.text:
{vada vada jitaḥ sa śatrurna hato jalpaṃśca tava tavāsmīti /
  citraṃ citramarodīddhā heti paraṃ mṛte putre //313//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 6.30)
{Say, say — the enemy is conquered, not killed! Speaking thus, and 'I am yours!' — wonder of wonders — 'Ah!' — [she cries,] upon the death of her son. ||313||}
In such cases and the like, when the speaker is overcome with joy, fear, and the like.

children.text: kathitapadaṃ kvacidguṇaḥ lāṭānuprāse arthāntarasaṃkramitavācye vihitasyānuvādyatve ca / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: Repeated expression (<s>kathitapada</s>) is sometimes a quality — in <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s> (repetition with shifted meaning), when the expressed meaning has been transferred to another meaning, and when what has been ordained becomes the subject of restatement. Examples in order:

children.text:
{sitakarakararuciravibhā vibhākarākāra dharaṇidhara kīrtiḥ /
  pauruṣakamalā kamalā sāpi tavaivāsti nānyasya //314(cf.359)//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 195)

{Your fame, with the radiance of beautiful moonbeams, is splendid like the maker of radiance; <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), the lotus-like fortune of valor, also belongs to you alone and to no other. ||314||}

children.text:
{tālā jā_anti guṇā jālā de sahi_a_eṃhi gheppanti /
  ra_ikiraṇāṇuggahi_ā_iṃ honti kamalā_iṃ kamalā_iṃ //315//}

children.translated_text: [Then qualities are born when they are grasped by the <s>sahṛdayas</s>;
assisted by the sun's rays, lotuses become [truly] lotuses.]
(<s>Hāla's</s> <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 989; <s>Abhinavagupta's</s> <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s>; <s>Ānandavardhana's</s> <s>Viṣamabāṇalīlā</s>)
{Then qualities are born when they are grasped by the sympathetic readers;

children.text:
{jitendriyatvaṃ vinayasya kāraṇaṃ guṇaprakarṣo vinayādavāpyate /
  guṇaprakarṣeṇa janonurajyate janānurāgaprabhavā hi saṃpadaḥ //316//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vallabhadeva's</s> <s>Subhāṣitāvali</s>)

{The mastery of the senses is the cause of humility; excellence of qualities is obtained from humility; through excellence of qualities, people become devoted; and from the devotion of people, prosperity arises. ||316||}
(<s>Bhavabhūti's</s> <s>Mahāvīracarita</s> 2.33)
{Even falling rank (<s>patatprakarṣa</s>) is sometimes a quality. As in the previously cited example '<s>aprāpta</s>-' and the like. ||317||}

children.text: samāptapunarāttaṃ kvacinna guṇo na doṣaḥ / yatra na viśeṣaṇamātradānārthaḥ punargrahaṇam api tu vākyāntarameva kriyate / yathā
children.translated_text: Resumption after completion (<s>samāptapunarātta</s>) is sometimes neither a quality nor a defect — where the resumption is not merely for the purpose of attributing a qualifier, but rather constitutes an entirely new sentence. For example:
{As in the very same [example] previously [cited]: '<s>aprāpta</s>-' and the like. ||318||}
A compound not in its proper place (<s>apadastha-samāsa</s>) is sometimes a quality. For example:
{as illustrated in the example beginning with 'the red <s>aśoka</s>' and so forth. //319//}
The concealed (<s>garbhita</s>) [type] is similar. For example:

children.text:
{humi avahatthi_areho ṇiraṅkuso aha vive_arahi_o vi /
  siviṇe vi tumammi puṇo pattihi bhattiṃ ṇa pasumarāmi //320//}

children.translated_text: [I become one whose [palm-]lines are erased, without a goad, and even bereft of discrimination —

children.text: svapne 'pi tvayi punaḥ pratīhi bhaktiṃ na prasmarāmi //]
children.translated_text: yet believe me, even in a dream I do not forget my devotion to you!]
(<s>Ānandavardhana</s>'s <s>Viṣamabāṇalīlā</s>; <s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s>)
{I become one without [the lines on] the palm, without a goad, and even bereft of discrimination — yet believe me, even in a dream I do not forget my devotion to you! //320//}

children.text: atra pratīhīti madhye dṛḍhapratyayotpādanāya / evamanyadapi lakṣyāllakṣyam //59//
children.translated_text: Here, 'believe me' is inserted in the middle to generate firm conviction. Thus, other [instances] too should be understood from example to example. //59//
The naming of <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions), <s>rasa</s>, and the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (enduring emotion) by their own words;
strained contrivance in the manifestation of <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) and <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants); // <s>MKpr-K</s>_60 //
the inclusion of contradictory <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like; [excessive] brilliance (<s>dīpti</s>) again and again;
untimely expansion or cessation [of a rasa]; excessive elaboration even of a subordinate element; // <s>MKpr-K</s>_61 //
failure to follow through on the principal [rasa]; the reversal of character-types (<s>prakṛti</s>);

children.text: anaṅgasyābhidhānaṃ ca rase doṣāḥ syurīdṛśāḥ // MKpr-K_62 //
children.translated_text: and the description of what is not a constituent part [of the rasa] — such are the faults in <s>rasa</s>. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_62 //

children.text:
(1) svaśabdopādānaṃ vyabhicāriṇo yathā
  {savrīḍā dayitānane sakaruṇā mātaṅgacarmāmbare
  satrāsā bhujage savismayarasā candre 'mṛtasyandini /
  serṣyā jahnusutāvalokanavidhau dīnā kapālodare
  pārvatyā navasaṃgamapraṇayinī dṛṣṭiḥ śivāyāstu vaḥ //321//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 164)

(1) The naming of a <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) by its own word — as follows: {With modesty upon the face of the beloved, with compassion at [<s>Śiva</s>'s] garment of elephant-hide, with terror at the serpent, with the <s>rasa</s> of wonder at the nectar-dripping moon, with jealousy at the sight of the daughter of <s>Jahnu</s> (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), dejected at [the sight of] the skull-bowl — may the gaze of <s>Pārvatī</s>, enamored at the new union, be auspicious for you! //321//}
Here, [the fault lies in naming] modesty and the rest [by their own terms].

{Downcast upon the face of the beloved, half-closed at the elephant-hide garment, trembling at the serpent, unblinking at the nectar-dripping moon, with narrowing eyes at the sight of the celestial river, languid at the skull-bowl —}
and so forth — this would be correct.

children.text: (2) rasasya svaśabdena śṛṅgārādiśabdena vā vācyatvam / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: (2) The expressibility of <s>rasa</s> by its own word or by a word such as '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>' and the like. Examples in order:

children.text:
{tāmanaṅgajayamaṅgalaśriyaṃ kiñciduccabhujamūlalokitām /
  netrayoḥ kṛtavato 'sya gocare ko 'pyajāyata raso nirantaraḥ //322//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 166)

{Having brought within the range of the eyes that auspicious beauty of the victory of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of love), who was gazing slightly upward from the root of her arm — there arose in him some uninterrupted <s>rasa</s>. //322//}

children.text:
{ālokya komalakapolatalābhiṣikta
  vyaktānurāgasubhagāmabhirāmamūrtim /
  paśyaiṣa bālyamativṛtya vivartamānaḥ
  śṛṅgārasīmani taraṅgitamātanoti //323//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Beholding that lovely form, graced with the anointed beauty of tender cheeks, radiant with manifest passion — see, this one, having passed beyond boyhood, is now turning, making waves at the very frontier of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment). //323//}
(3) [Naming] the <s>sthāyin</s> (enduring emotion) [by its own word] — as follows:

children.text:
{saṃprahāre praharaṇaiḥ prahārāṇāṃ parasparam /
  ṭhaṇatkāraiḥ śrutigatairutsāhastasya ko 'pyabhūt //324//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 167)
{In the clash of combat, from the clanging of weapons striking one against another, reaching the ears — there arose in him some <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm). //324//}
Here, [the fault is in naming] <s>utsāha</s> [directly].

children.text:
{karpūradhūlidhavaladyutipūradhauta-
  diṅmaṇḍale śiśirarociṣi tasya yūnaḥ /
  līlāśiro 'ṃśukaniveśaviśeṣakḷ.pti-
  vyaktastanonnatirabhūnnayanāvanau sā //325//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{In the moonlight, whose splendor — purified by the flood of radiance white as camphor-dust — pervaded the quarters, for that youth, the swelling of the breast, made manifest through the particular arrangement of the playful head-veil, occurred in her [who stood] with downcast eyes. //325//}

children.text: atroddīpanālambanarūpāḥ śṛṅgārayogyā vibhāvā anubhāvaparyavasāyinaḥ sthitā iti kaṣṭakalpanā //
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>vibhāvas</s> — in the form of <s>uddīpana</s> (stimulant) and <s>ālambana</s> (foundational) — suitable for <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, culminate in an <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) — this is a strained contrivance.

children.text:
{pariharati ratiṃ matiṃ lunīte skhalati bhṛśaṃ parivartate ca bhūyaḥ /
  iti bata viṣamā daśāsya dehaṃ paribhavati prasabhaṃ kimatra kurmaḥ //326//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{She avoids love, her mind falters, she stumbles badly, and turns about again — alas, this dire condition forcibly overwhelms her body — what can we do here? //326//}

children.text: atra ratiparihārādīnāmanubhāvānāṃ karuṇādāvapi saṃbhavātkāminīrūpo vibhāvo yatnataḥ pratipādyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, since <s>anubhāvas</s> such as the avoidance of love and the like are possible in <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic sentiment) as well, the <s>vibhāva</s> in the form of a beloved woman must be carefully established.

children.text:
(6)
  {prasāde vartasva prakaṭaya mudaṃ saṃtyaja ruṣaṃ
  priye śuṣyantyaṅgānyamṛtamiva te siñcatu vacaḥ /
  nidhānaṃ saukhyānāṃ kṣaṇamabhimukhaṃ sthāpaya mukhaṃ
  na mugdhe pratyetuṃ prabhavati gataḥ kālahariṇaḥ //327//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s>; <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s>)

(6) {Be at ease, reveal your joy, abandon anger, O beloved — your words, like nectar, should sprinkle my withering limbs. Place your face — the treasury of all happinesses — toward me for a moment. O innocent one, the deer of time, once gone, cannot be made to return! //327//}

children.text: atra śṛṅgāre pratikūlasya śāntasyānityatāprakāśanarūpo vibhāvastatprakāśito nirvedaśca vyabhicārī upāttaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, in the context of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, a contradictory <s>vibhāva</s> has been included — namely <s>śānta</s> (the tranquil sentiment), which takes the form of revealing impermanence; and <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness), which is [thereby] revealed, has been adopted as a <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion).

children.text:
{ṇihu_aramaṇammi lo_aṇapahammi paḍi_e guru_aṇamajjhammi /
  sa_alaparihārahi_a_ā vaṇagamaṇaṃ evva maha_i vahū //328//}

children.translated_text: [When the secret lover [appears] in the path of the eyes, having fallen within the midst of the elders —
the bride, whose heart is [set on] complete evasion, desires nothing but going to the forest.]
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{When the secret lover falls within the path of the eyes, in the midst of the elders — the bride whose heart is [set on] complete evasion desires nothing but to go to the forest. //328//}

children.text: atra sakalaparihāravanagamane śāntānubhāvau / indhanādyānayanavyājenopabhogārthaṃ vanagamanaṃ cet na doṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the complete evasion and going to the forest are <s>anubhāvas</s> of <s>śānta</s> (the tranquil sentiment). But if the going to the forest is on the pretext of fetching firewood and the like, for the purpose of enjoyment, then there is no fault.
(7) <s>Dīpti</s> (brilliance/excess) again and again — as in <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s>, in the lament of <s>Rati</s>.

children.text: (8) akāṇḍe prathanaṃ yathā veṇīsaṃhāre dvitīyeṅkenekavīrakṣaye pravṛtte bhānumatyā saha duryodhanasya śṛṅgāravarṇanam /
children.translated_text: (8) Untimely expansion — as in the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s>, in the second act, when the destruction of <s>Ekalavīra</s> is underway, the description of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> of <s>Duryodhana</s> with <s>Bhānumatī</s>.

children.text: (9) akāṇḍe chedo yathā vīracarite dvitīyeṅke rāghavabhārgavayordhārādhirūḍhe vīrarase {kaṅkaṇamocanāya gacchāmi} iti rāghavasyoktau //
children.translated_text: (9) Untimely cessation — as in the <s>Vīracarita</s>, in the second act, when the <s>vīra rasa</s> (heroic sentiment) between <s>Rāghava</s> and <s>Bhārgava</s> has reached its peak, <s>Rāghava</s>'s statement '{I am going to remove [my] bracelets}.'
(10) The excessive elaboration of a subordinate element that is not predominant — as in [the poem] <s>Hayagrīvavadha</s>, [the description] of <s>Hayagrīva</s>.

children.text: (11) aṅgino 'nanusaṃdhānam / yathā ratnāvalyāṃ caturtheṅke bābhravyāgamane sāgarikāyā vismṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: (11) Failure to follow through on the principal [rasa] — as in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, in the fourth act, the forgetting of <s>Sāgarikā</s> upon the arrival of <s>Bābhravya</s>.

children.text:
(12) prakṛtayo divyā adivyā divyādivyāśca vīraraudraśṛṅgāraśāntarasapradhānā
dhīrodāttadhīroddhatadhīralalitadhīrapraśāntāḥ uttamādhamamadhyamāśca / tatra ratihāsaśokādbhutāni adivyottamaprakṛtivat divyeṣvapi / kiṃ tu ratiḥ saṃbhogaśṛṅgārarūpā uttamadevatāviṣayā na varṇanīyā / tadvarṇanaṃ hi pitroḥ saṃbhogavarṇanamivātyantamanucitam /
children.translated_text: (12) The character-types are divine, non-divine, and divine-and-non-divine; they are predominantly of <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>raudra</s> (furious), <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), and <s>śānta</s> (tranquil) <s>rasas</s>, [and are accordingly] <s>dhīrodātta</s> (noble-steadfast), <s>dhīroddhata</s> (bold-steadfast), <s>dhīralalita</s> (graceful-steadfast), and <s>dhīrapraśānta</s> (tranquil-steadfast); and they are superior, inferior, and middling. Among these, <s>rati</s> (love), <s>hāsa</s> (laughter), <s>śoka</s> (grief), and <s>adbhuta</s> (wonder) apply to divine characters of the superior type just as to non-divine ones. However, <s>rati</s> in the form of <s>saṃbhogaśṛṅgāra</s> (love-in-union) directed toward supreme deities should not be described. For describing that would be as utterly improper as describing the sexual union of one's own parents.

children.text:
{krodhaṃ prabho saṃhara saṃhareti yāvad giraḥ khe marutāṃ caranti /
  tāvatsa vahnirbhavanetrajanmā bhasmāvaśeṣaṃ madanaṃ cakāra //329//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 3.32)

{While the words of the wind-gods were still circling in the sky — 'Withdraw your anger, O Lord, withdraw!' — that fire, born from the eye of <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), reduced <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) to a mere residue of ash. //329//}

children.text: ityuktavat bhrukuṭyādivikāravarjitaḥ krodhaḥ sadyaḥphaladaḥ svargapātālagagasamudrollaṅghanādyutsāhaśca divyeṣyeva / adhikaṃ tu nibadhyamānamasatyapratibhāsena 'nāyakavadvartitavyaṃ na pratināyakavat'; ityupadeśe na paryavasyet / divyādivyeṣu ubhayathāpi / evamuktasyaucityasya divyādīnāmiva dhīrodāttādīnāmapyanyathāvarṇanaṃ viparyayaḥ / tatrabhavan bhagavannityuttamena na adhamena muniprabhṛtau na rājādau bhaṭṭāraka-iti nottamena rājādau prakṛtiviparyayāpattervācyam / evaṃ deśakālavayojātyādīnāṃ veṣavyavahārādikamucitamevopanibanddhavyam //
children.translated_text: As stated [in this verse], anger that is free from distortion such as furrowed brows and the like, and that produces immediate results; and enthusiasm such as leaping across heaven, the netherworld, the sky, and the ocean — these pertain to divine characters alone. But what is being composed beyond [these conventions], if it does not appear unreal, would not contravene the instruction 'one should behave like the hero, not like the villain.' In divine-and-non-divine [characters], both ways apply. Just as the character-types — divine and the like — should not be described otherwise than as stated regarding propriety, so too the <s>dhīrodātta</s> (noble-steadfast) and the rest. Therein, 'O Lord' and 'O Blessed One' — [such forms of address are used] for the superior type; one should not address a sage and the like with the inferior [form], nor a king and the like with the superior [form] — because the [inappropriate] reversal of character-types would result. Similarly, the costume, conduct, and the like appropriate to the country, time, age, caste, and so forth should be composed in keeping [with propriety].

children.text: (13) anaṅgasya rasānupakārakasya varṇanam / yathā karpūramañjaryā nāyikayā svātmanā ca kṛtaṃ vasantavarṇanamanādṛtya bandivarṇitasya rājñā praśaṃsanam //
children.translated_text: (13) The description of what is not a constituent part [of the rasa] — that which does not contribute to the rasa. For example, in the <s>Karpūramañjarī</s>, disregarding the description of spring made by the heroine herself, the king praises [instead] a spring-description recited by a bard.

children.text: {īdṛśāḥ} iti / nāyikāpādaprahārādinā nāyakakopādivarṇanam / uktaṃ hi dhvanikṛtā
children.translated_text: 'Such are [the faults]' — [also includes] the description of the hero's anger and the like caused by the heroine's kick and the like. For the author of the <s>Dhvani</s> [treatise] has said:

children.text:
{anaucityādṛtte nānyad rasabhaṅgasya kāraṇam /
  aucityopanibandhastu rasasyopaniṣatparā //} iti //60-62//
children.translated_text: {'There is no other cause of the destruction of <s>rasa</s> than impropriety; and the foundation of <s>rasa</s> depends entirely upon propriety (<s>aucitya</s>).'} //60-62//
Now it is stated that in some cases these are not faults:
The naming of a <s>saṃcārin</s> (transitory emotion) by its own word is in some cases not a fault —
as follows:

children.text:
{autsukyena kṛtatvarā sahabhuvā vyāvartamānā hriyā
  taistairbandhuvadhūjanasya vacanairnītābhimukhyaṃ punaḥ /
  dṛṣṭvāgre varamāttasādhvasarasā gaurī nave saṃgame
  saṃrohatpulakā hareṇa hasatā śliṣṭā śivāyāstu vaḥ //330//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Harṣa</s>'s <s>Ratnāvalī</s> 1.2)

{Hurrying forward with eagerness, yet turning back with modesty as its companion, then led face-to-face again by the various words of the kinswomen — <s>Gaurī</s>, beholding the bridegroom before her, trembling with the <s>rasa</s> of awe, in the new union, with horripilation rising, was embraced by <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) who laughed — may this be auspicious for you! //330//}

children.text: atrautsukyaśabda iva tadanubhāvo na tathā pratītikṛt / ata eva 'dūrādutsukam'; ityādau vrīḍāpremādyanubhāvānāṃ / vivalitatvādīnāmivotsukatvānubhāvasya sahasā prasaraṇādirūpasya tathā pratipattikāritvābhāvādutsukamiti kṛtam //
children.translated_text: Here, the word '<s>autsukya</s>' (eagerness), unlike its <s>anubhāva</s> [which would be directly perceptible], does not produce cognition in the same way. Hence, even in '[she gazed at him] from afar with eagerness' and similar cases — just as the <s>anubhāvas</s> of modesty, love, and the like such as becoming agitated are immediately productive of cognition, the <s>anubhāva</s> of eagerness, being of the nature of sudden rushing forward and the like, does not similarly produce cognition — hence [the word] 'eager' is used [permissibly].
The statement of a contradictory <s>saṃcārin</s> and the like, when it is [presented as] sublated, contributes to poetic quality. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_63 //
The statement [of a contradictory emotion] as sublated is not a fault — provided it nourishes the <s>rasa</s> at hand. For example:

children.text:
{'kvākāryaṃ śaśalakṣmaṇaḥ kva ca kulam'; ityādau //331[=53]//}
  [kvākāryaṃ śaśalakṣaṇaḥ kva ca kulaṃ bhūyo 'pi dṛśyeta sā
  doṣāṇāṃ praśamāya na śrutamaho kope 'pi kāntaṃ mukham /
  kiṃ vakṣyantyapakalmaṣāḥ kṛtadhiyaḥ svapne 'pi sā durlabhā
  cetaḥ svāsthyamupaihi kaḥ khalu yuvā dhanyo 'dharaṃ dhāsyati //53//]

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 4.4)

{'Where is the task, and where is the hare-marked moon, and where is the lineage — might she be seen again? — faults are not quelled by what is heard — ah, even in anger her face is lovely! — what will the pure-minded say? — even in a dream she is unattainable — O heart, be calm! — what fortunate youth will drink from her lip?' //331[=53]//}

children.text: atra vitarkādiṣu udgateṣvapi cintāyāmeva viśrāntiriti prakṛtarasaparipoṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, even though deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>) and the like arise, [the mind] comes to rest in anxiety alone — thus the <s>rasa</s> at hand is nourished.

children.text:
{pāṇḍu kṣāmaṃ vadanaṃ hṛdayaṃ sarasaṃ tavālasaṃ ca vapuḥ /
  āvedayati nitāntaṃ kṣetriyarogaṃ sakhi hṛdantaḥ //332//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s>)
{Your face is pale and thin, your heart is moist, and your body is languid — O friend, it reveals fully an illness of the countryside within the heart! //332//}
Here and in similar cases, since pallor and the like are common [to both love-sickness and regular illness], there is no contradiction.

children.text:
{satyaṃ manoramā rāmāḥ satyaṃ ramyā vibhūtayaḥ /
  kiṃ tu mattāṅganāpāṅgabhaṅgalolaṃ hi jīvitam //333//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s> 3.30)
{True, women are delightful; true, riches are charming; but life is as unsteady as the quivering of the side-glance of an intoxicated woman. //333//}

children.text: ityatrādyamardhaṃ bādhyatvenaivokyam / jīvitādapi adhikamapāṅgabhaṅgasyāsthiratvamiti prasiddhabhaṅguropamānatayopāttaṃ śāntameva puṣṇāti na punaḥ śṛṅgārasyātra pratītistadaṅgāpratipatterḥ / na tu vineyonmukhīkaraṇamatra parihāraḥ śāntaśṛṅgārayornairantaryasyābhāvāt / nāpi kāvyaśobhākaraṇaṃ rasāntarādanuprāsamātrādvā tathābhāvāt //63//
children.translated_text: Here, the first half is stated precisely as something to be sublated. The instability of a side-glance is even greater than [that of] life — being adopted as the well-known and fragile term of comparison, it nourishes the <s>śānta</s> (tranquil) sentiment alone. There is no apprehension of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> here, because of the non-apprehension of its constituent parts. Nor is the 'turning of the disciple toward [renunciation]' the resolution here, since there is no continuity between <s>śānta</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. Nor does [the first half merely] serve to beautify the poetry, since that [function] does not arise from a mere hint of another <s>rasa</s> or from mere cessation. //63//

children.text: āśrayaikye viruddho yaḥ sa kāryo bhinnasaṃśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: A [<s>rasa</s>] that is contradictory when in the same locus should be made to reside in a different locus;
and a <s>rasa</s> [contradictory] through [immediate] contiguity should be separated by an intervening <s>rasa</s>. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_64 //

children.text:
vīrabhayānakayorekāśrayatvena virodha iti pratiprakṣagatatvena bhayānako niveśayitavyaḥ / śāntaśṛṅgārayostu nairantaryeṇa virodha iti rasāntaramantare kāryam yathā nāgānande śāntasya jīmūtavāhanasya 'aho gītam aho vāditram'; ityadbhūtamantarniveśya
malayavatīṃ prati śṛṅgāro nibaddhaḥ / na paraṃ prabandhe yāvadekasminnapi vākye rasāntaravyavadhinā virodho nivartate / yathā
children.translated_text: Since the heroic (<s>vīra</s>) and the terrible (<s>bhayānaka</s>) are contradictory when in the same locus, the terrible should be placed in the opponent's camp. But since the tranquil (<s>śānta</s>) and the erotic (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) are contradictory through contiguity, another <s>rasa</s> should be interposed. As in the <s>Nāgānanda</s>, where for the tranquil <s>Jīmūtavāhana</s>, after interposing <s>adbhuta</s> (the marvelous) with '{Ah, what singing! Ah, what music!},' <s>śṛṅgāra</s> toward <s>Malayavatī</s> is composed. Not only in a work [as a whole], but even in a single sentence, the contradiction is resolved by the intervention of another <s>rasa</s>. As follows:

children.text:
{bhūreṇudigdhān navapārijāta-
  mālārajovāsitabāhumadhyā /
  gāḍhaṃ śivābhiḥ parirabhyamāṇān
  surāṅganāśliṣṭabhujāntarālāḥ //334//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ānandavardhana</s>'s <s>Dhvanyāloka</s>)

{Smeared with abundant dust, their arms fragrant with garlands of fresh <s>pārijāta</s> blossoms, tightly embraced by the wives of <s>Śiva</s> (the Mothers) — [those heroes] whose arm-spaces are clasped by celestial women — //334//}

children.text:
{saśoṇitaiḥ kravyabhujāṃ sphuradbhiḥ
  pakṣaiḥ khagānāmupavījyamānān /
  saṃvījitāścandanavārisekaiḥ
  sugandhibhiḥ kalpalatādukūlaiḥ //334//(a)//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{Fanned by the quivering, bloodied wings of carrion-eating birds — [yet also] cooled by sprinklings of sandalwood-water and [draped with] fragrant garments from wish-fulfilling creepers — //334(a)//}

children.text:
{vimānaparyaṅkatale niṣaṇṇāḥ
  kutūhalāviṣṭitayā tadānīm /
  nirdiśyamānān lalanāṅgulībhir-
  vīrāḥ svadehān patitānapaśyan //335//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ānandavardhana</s>'s <s>Dhvanyāloka</s>)
{Seated upon the couches of celestial chariots, pointed out at that time by the fingers of women, filled with curiosity — those heroes beheld their own fallen bodies. //335//}
Here, between the <s>bībhatsa</s> (the disgusting) and the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic), the <s>vīra rasa</s> (heroic sentiment) has been interposed. //64//
Even a contradictory [<s>rasa</s>], when recalled [rather than directly presented]; or when intentionally stated through similarity;

children.text: aṅginyaṅgatvamāptau yau tau na duṣṭau parasparam // MKpr-K_65 //
children.translated_text: or when one of two [rasas] has attained the status of principal and the other of subordinate — these two are not faulty with respect to each other. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_65 //

children.text:
{ayaṃ sa raśanotkarṣī pīnastanavimardanaḥ /
  nābhyūrujaghanasparśī nīvīvisraṃsanaḥ karaḥ //336//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Mahābhārata</s>, <s>Strīparvan</s> 24.19)
{'This is that very hand — the one that pulled off the girdle-string, that pressed the full breasts, that touched the navel, thighs, and hips, that loosened the undergarment!' ||336||}

children.text: etad bhūriśravasaḥ samarabhuvi patitaṃ hastamālokya tadvadhūrabhidadhau / atra pūrvāvasthāsmaraṇaṃ śṛṅgārāṅgamapi karuṇaṃ paripoṣayati //
children.translated_text: This was said by the wife of <s>Bhūriśravas</s> upon seeing his severed hand [lying] on the battlefield. Here the recollection of a former state, though itself a limb of the erotic sentiment (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>), nourishes the pathetic sentiment (<s>karuṇa</s>).

children.text:
{dantakṣatāni karajaiśca vipāṭitāni
  prodbhinnasāndrapulake bhavataḥ śarīre /
  dattāni raktamanasā mṛgarājavadhvā
  jātaspṛhairmunibhirapyavalokitāni //337//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinavagupta's</s> <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s> 3.43)

{'Tooth-marks and nail-scratches on your body, covered with dense, bristling goose-bumps, inflicted by the doe-eyed wife of the king of beasts with a passionate heart — even the sages looked upon them with longing.' ||337||}

children.text: atra kāmukasya dantakṣatādīni yathā camatkārakārīṇi tathā jinasya / yathā vā paraḥ śṛṅgārī tadalokanātsaspṛhastadvat etaddṛśo munaya iti sāmyavivakṣā //
children.translated_text: Here, just as the tooth-marks and the like of a lover produce <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic rapture), so too [do those] of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor). Or: just as another [observer] becomes desirous from seeing the erotic [marks], so too these sages of that kind — this is the intended expression of similarity.

children.text:
{krāmantyaḥ kṣatakomalalāṅguligaladraktaiḥ sadarbhāḥ sthalīḥ
  pādaiḥ pātitayāvakairiva galadbāṣpāmbudhautānanā /
  bhītā bhartṛkarāvalambitakarāstvacchatrunāryodhunā
  dāvāgniṃ parito bhramanti punarapyudyadvivāhā iva //338//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ānandavardhana's</s> <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 3.20)

{'Treading on thorny ground with feet whose tender toes drip blood, as if stained with lac-dye, their faces washed by streaming tears, frightened, their hands clinging to their husbands' hands — your enemy's women now wander about the forest-fire on all sides, as though going through a second marriage ceremony.' ||338||}

children.text: atra cāṭuke rājaviṣayā ratiḥ pratīyate / tatra karuṇa iva śṛṅgāro 'pyaṅgamiti tayorna virodhaḥ / yathā
children.translated_text: Here, in this flattering address (<s>cāṭuka</s>), the sentiment of love (<s>rati</s>) directed toward the king is suggested. There, <s>śṛṅgāra</s> too, like <s>karuṇa</s>, is a subordinate limb — thus there is no contradiction between the two. For example:

children.text:
{ehi gaccha patottiṣṭha vada maunaṃ samācara /
  evamāśāgrahagrastaiḥ krīḍanti dhanino 'rthibhiḥ //339//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinavagupta's</s> <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s> 3.44)
{'Come! Go! Fall down! Get up! Speak! Observe silence!' — Thus do the wealthy play with supplicants who are seized by the grip of hope. ||339||}

children.text: ityatra ehīti krīḍanti gaccheti krīḍantīti krīḍanāpekṣayoḥ āgamanagamanayorna virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the [pair] 'come!' — [they] play, and 'go!' — [they] play, there is no contradiction between coming and going, since both depend on the single [act of] playing.

children.text:
{kṣipto hastāvalagnaḥ prasabhamabhihato 'pyādadāno 'ṃśukāntaṃ
  gṛhṇan keśeṣvapāstaścaraṇanipatito nekṣitaḥ saṃbhrameṇa /
  āliṅgan yovadhūtastripurayuvatibhiḥ sāśrunetrotpalābhiḥ
  kāmīvārdrāparādhaḥ sa dahatu duritaṃ śābhavo vaḥ śarāgniḥ //340//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 2)

{'Thrown away, he clings to her hand; violently struck, he seizes the border of her garment; grasped by the hair and pushed aside, he falls at her feet; unlooked-at, [yet] with flustered haste; embracing, [yet] shaken off by the women of the Triple City with lotus-eyes brimming with tears — like a lover guilty of a fresh offense, may that fire of <s>Śiva's</s> arrows burn away your sins!' ||340||}

children.text:
ityatra tripuraripuprabhāvātiśayasya karuṇo 'ṅgam / tasya tu śṛṅgāraḥ / tathāpi na karuṇe viśrāntiriti tasyāṅgataiva / athavā prāk yathā kāmuka ācarati sma tathā śarāgniriti śṛṅgārapoṣitena karuṇeṇa mukhya evārtha upodbalyate /
uktāṃ hi
children.translated_text:
Here, the <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic) is subordinate to the surpassing power of the Destroyer of the Three Cities (<s>Tripurāri</s>), while the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) is subordinate to that [<s>karuṇa</s>]. Even so, since the [aesthetic] experience does not come to rest in the <s>karuṇa</s>, it remains only a subordinate element. Alternatively: 'just as a lover formerly acted, so does the fire of [<s>Śiva's</s>] arrows' — thus the primary meaning is strengthened by the <s>karuṇa</s> enriched through <s>śṛṅgāra</s>.
For it has been said:
{'A quality, having undergone refinement of its own,

children.text: pradhānasyopakāre hi tathā bhūyasi vartate //} iti //
children.translated_text: imitates the principal — for it functions mainly in the service of the principal.'} //
(<s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s> 3.22)

children.text: prākpratipāditasya rasasya rasāntareṇa na virodhaḥ nāpyaṅgāṅgibhāvo bhavati iti rasaśabdenātra sthāyibhāva upalakṣyate //65//
children.translated_text: There is no contradiction between a previously established <s>rasa</s> and another <s>rasa</s>, nor does a principal-subordinate (<s>aṅgāṅgibhāva</s>) relationship [necessarily] arise. By the word '<s>rasa</s>' here, the permanent emotion (<s>sthāyibhāva</s>) is indicated. //65//

children.text: iti kāvyaprakāśe doṣadarśano nāma saptama ullāsaḥ //7//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh <s>ullāsa</s> of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, entitled 'The Perception of Faults' (<s>doṣadarśana</s>). //7//
Now the eighth <s>ullāsa</s>.
Having thus stated the faults, he now explains the distinction between <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments) —
Those properties of the principal <s>rasa</s> (sentiment) — like valor and the like of the self —
which are the causes of its excellence and are of stable presence — those are <s>guṇas</s> (poetic qualities). // MKpr-K 66 //

children.text: ātmana eva hi yathā śauryādayo nākārasya tathā rasasyaiva mādhuryādayo guṇā na varṇānām //
children.translated_text: Just as valor and the like are qualities of the self, not of [external] appearance — so <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) and the like are qualities of the <s>rasa</s> alone, not of the phonemes.

children.text:
kvacittu śauryādisamucitasyākāramahattvāderdarśanāt 'ākāra evāsya śūraḥ'; ityādervyavahārādanyatrāśūre 'pi vitatākṛtitvamātreṇa {śūraḥ'; iti kvāpi śūre 'pi mūrtilāghavamātreṇa 'aśūraḥ} iti aviśrāntapratītayo yathā vyavaharanti tadvanmadhurādivyañjakasukumārādivarṇānāṃ madhurādivyavahārapravṛtteramadhurādirasāṅgānāṃ
varṇānāṃ saukumāryādimātreṇa mādhuryādi madhurādirasopakaraṇānāṃ
teṣāmasaukumāryāderamādhuryādi rasaparyantaviśrāntapratītibandhyā
vyavaharanti / ata eva mādhuryādayo rasadharmāḥ samucitairvarṇairvyajyante na tu
varṇamātrāśrayāḥ / yathaiṣāṃ vyañjakatvam tathodāhariṣyate //66//
children.translated_text: But sometimes, because of the perception of bodily grandeur and the like appropriate to valor, from the usage 'his very form is heroic' and so on, even elsewhere, regarding a non-hero, people use '<s>śūra</s>' (hero) merely on account of an extended physique, and sometimes even regarding a hero of slight build, they use '<s>aśūra</s>' (non-hero) — these are usages whose cognitions have not come to rest [in the ultimate referent]. Similarly, from the occurrence of the usage '<s>madhura</s>' (sweet) and the like regarding phonemes such as soft sounds that manifest sweetness and the like, [people] use '<s>mādhurya</s>' (sweetness) merely on the basis of the softness alone of phonemes that are [actually] limbs of non-sweet <s>rasa</s>; and regarding phonemes that serve as auxiliaries of the sweet <s>rasa</s> and the like, because of their lack of softness, [people use] 'non-sweetness' — they make usages whose cognitions are barren of coming to rest in the <s>rasa</s> as their terminus. Therefore, <s>mādhurya</s> and the like, being properties of <s>rasa</s>, are manifested through appropriate phonemes but are not based on phonemes alone. The manner of their manifestation will be illustrated below. //66//
Those which, through the door of being subordinate limbs, sometimes support that [<s>rasa</s>] when it is present —
like necklaces and the like — those are <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments): <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), <s>upamā</s> (simile), and the rest. // MKpr-K 67 //

children.text:
ye vācakavācyalakṣaṇāṅgātiśayamukhena mukhyaṃ rasaṃ saṃbhavinam upakurvanti te kaṇṭhādyaṅgānāmutkarṣādhānadvāreṇa śarīriṇo 'pi upakārakā hārādaya ivālaṅkārāḥ / yatra tu nāsti rasastatroktivaicitryamātraparyavasāyinaḥ / kvacittu santamapi nopakurvanti /
yathākramamudāharaṇāni ----
children.translated_text:
Those which, through the excellence of subordinate limbs characterized by the expressed word and expressed meaning, support the principal <s>rasa</s> when it is possible — those, like necklaces and the like that also enhance the embodied being through the door of adding excellence to the limbs such as the neck — are <s>alaṅkāras</s>. But where there is no <s>rasa</s>, they terminate in mere verbal ingenuity. And sometimes they do not support even what is present.
Examples in order —

children.text:
{apasāraya ghanasāraṃ kuru hāraṃ dūra eva kiṃ kamalaiḥ /
  alamalamāli mṛṇālairiti vadati divāniśaṃ bālā //341//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Dāmodaragupta's</s> <s>Kuṭṭanīmata</s> 102)
{'Set aside the camphor, put the pearl-necklace far away, what use are lotuses? Enough, enough, O friend, of lotus-fiber stalks!' — thus speaks the young woman day and night. ||341||}
In this and similar cases, [the ornament supports the <s>rasa</s>] through the door of the expressed word;

children.text:
{manorāgastīvraṃ viṣamiva visarpatyavirataṃ
  pramāthī nirdhūmaṃ jvalati vidhutaḥ pāvaka iva /
  hinasti pratyaṅgaṃ jvara iva garīyānita ito
  na māṃ trātuṃ tātaḥ prabhavati na cāmbā na bhavatī //342//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti's</s> <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> 2.1)

{'The passion of the mind spreads intensely like poison without cease; it blazes furiously like fire without smoke; it torments every limb, heavier than a fever — here and there — neither father can save me, nor mother, nor you!' ||342||}
In this and similar cases, the ornaments support the <s>rasa</s> through the door of the expressed meaning.

children.text:
{citte cihutṭadi ṇa ṭuṭṭadi sā guṇesuṃ
  sejjāsu loṭṭadi visappadi dimuṃhesuṃ /
  bolammi vaṭṭadi pavaṭṭadi kavvabandhe
  jhāṇeṇa ṭuṭṭadi ciraṃ taruṇī taraṭṭī //343//}

children.translated_text: [In the mind it dissolves, [yet] does not break off from [his] virtues;
on the beds she tosses, [yet] creeps toward the quarters;
in speech she engages, [yet] sets forth in poetic composition;
through meditation she breaks off for a long while — the bold young woman.]
(<s>Rājaśekhara's</s> <s>Karpūramañjarī</s> 2.4)

{'In the mind it dissolves, [yet] does not break off from [his] virtues; on the beds she tosses, [yet] wanders toward the quarters; in speech she engages, [yet] sets forth in poetic composition; through meditation she breaks off for a long while — the bold young woman.' ||343||}
In this and similar cases, [there is] the expressed word alone [as ornament without rasa];

children.text:
{mitre kvāpi gate saroruhavane baddhānane tāmyati
  krandatsu bhramareṣu vīkṣya dayitāsannaṃ puraḥ sārasam /
  cakrāhvena viyoginā bisalatā nāsvāditā nojjhitā
  kaṇṭhe kevalamargaleva nihitā jīvasya nirgacchataḥ //344//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 176)

{'When his friend has gone somewhere to a lotus-pond, and the bees are wailing, their faces trapped [in closing lotuses], a <s>sārasa</s> (crane) close to his beloved is seen before him — by the <s>cakravāka</s> separated [from his mate]: the lotus-fiber stalk is neither savored nor abandoned, but placed across the throat alone like a bolt, of [one whose] life is departing.' ||344||}

children.text: ityādau vācyameva na tu rasam / atra bisalatā na jīvaṃ roddhuṃ kṣameti prakṛtānanuguṇopamā //
children.translated_text: In this and similar cases, [there is] the expressed meaning alone, not the <s>rasa</s>. Here the lotus-fiber stalk is not capable of restraining the life-force — hence the simile is incongruent with the subject matter.

children.text:
eṣa eva ca guṇālaṅkārapravibhāgaḥ / evaṃ ca "samavāyavṛttyā śauryādayaḥ saṃyogavṛttyā tu hārādaya ityastu guṇālaṅkārāṇāṃ bhedaḥ / ojaḥprabhṛtīnāmanuprāsopamādīnāṃ cobhayeṣāmapi samavāyavṛttyā sthitiriti
gaḍḍalikāpravāheṇaivaiṣāṃ bhedaḥ" ityabhidhānamasat //
children.translated_text: And this itself is the division between <s>guṇa</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s>. And thus: 'the difference between <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s> should be that qualities such as valor exist through inherence (<s>samavāyavṛtti</s>), while ornaments such as necklaces exist through conjunction (<s>saṃyogavṛtti</s>); but both <s>ojas</s> and the like and <s>anuprāsa</s> and <s>upamā</s> and the like exist through inherence' — this statement that their distinction runs in a continuous flow [from the same principle] is incorrect.

children.text:
yadapyuktam {kāvyaśobhāyāḥ kartāro dharmā guṇās tadatiśayahetavastvalaṅkārāḥ} iti tadapi na yuktam / yataḥ kiṃ samastairguṇaiḥ kāvyavyavahāraḥ uta katipayaiḥ / yadi samastaiḥ tatkathamasamastaguṇā gauḍī pāñcālī ca rītiḥ kāvyasyātmā /
atha katipayaiḥ tataḥ
children.translated_text: And what has been stated — '<s>guṇas</s> are the qualities that produce the beauty of poetry; <s>alaṅkāras</s> are the causes of the excellence of those [guṇas]' — that too is not correct. For: does the usage 'poetry' arise from all the <s>guṇas</s> [being present], or from some? If from all, then how are the <s>Gauḍī</s> and <s>Pāñcālī</s> styles, which do not possess all <s>guṇas</s>, the soul of poetry? If from some, then:
(<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 114)
{'Here the fire blazes high without moisture; this smoke, arising copiously, gleams brightly!' ||345||}
In such cases, when <s>ojas</s> and the other <s>guṇas</s> are present, the designation 'poetry' is obtained;

children.text:
{svargaprāptiranenaiva dehena varavarṇinī /
  asyā radacchadaraso nyakkarotitarāṃ sudhām //346//}
children.translated_text: {'O woman of excellent complexion, the attainment of heaven is through this very body! The juice of her teeth utterly surpasses ambrosia!' ||346||}
In such cases, <s>viśeṣokti</s> (particularization) and <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), independently of <s>guṇas</s>, are the causes of the designation 'poetry.' //67//
Now he states the classification of the <s>guṇas</s>:
They are three, called <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>ojas</s> (vigor), and <s>prasāda</s> (perspicuity) — not ten.
He states their definitions in order:
The quality of producing delight (<s>āhlādakatva</s>) is <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness); in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, it is the cause of <s>druti</s> (melting). // MKpr-K 68 //

children.text: śṛṅgāre arthāt saṃbhoge / drutirgalitatvamiva / śravyatvaṃ punarojaḥprasādayorapi //68//
children.translated_text: In <s>śṛṅgāra</s> — meaning in love-in-union (<s>saṃbhoga</s>). <s>Druti</s> (melting) is as if a dissolving. Pleasantness-to-the-ear (<s>śravyatva</s>), however, belongs to <s>ojas</s> and <s>prasāda</s> as well. //68//
In the <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic), in love-in-separation (<s>vipralambha</s>), and in the <s>śānta</s> (tranquil) [<s>rasas</s>], it [<s>mādhurya</s>] is endowed with pre-eminence;
Endowed with pre-eminence
because of being the cause of the utmost <s>druti</s> (melting).
<s>Ojas</s> (vigor), whose nature is radiance (<s>dīpti</s>), is the cause of the expansion of the self; it is established in the <s>vīra</s> (heroic) <s>rasa</s>. // MKpr-K 69 //
<s>Ojas</s> is that which produces the radiance-form of expansion of the mind. //69//
In the <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting) and <s>raudra</s> (furious) <s>rasas</s>, its predominance [increases] in that order;
from the <s>vīra</s> to the <s>bībhatsa</s>, thence <s>ojas</s> [increases] with greater intensity.
<s>Prasāda</s> (perspicuity) is that which, like fire in dry fuel, like clear water, instantly // MKpr-K 70 //
pervades something else. It has an established presence in all [<s>rasas</s>].

children.text: anyaditi / vyāpyamiha cittam / sarvatreti / sarveṣu raseṣu sarvāsu racanāsu ca //
children.translated_text: 'Something else' — what is pervaded here is the mind. 'In all' — in all <s>rasas</s> and in all compositions.
The application of those [<s>guṇas</s>] to word and meaning is considered [to be] through the function of <s>guṇa</s> [i.e., figuratively]. // MKpr-K 71 //
'Through the function of <s>guṇa</s>' means: through figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>). 'Of those' — of the <s>guṇas</s>. Just as valor [is attributed figuratively] to appearance. //70-71//
He now states the reason why [there are] only three and not ten:
Some are subsumed within these; others are based on the removal of faults;

children.text: anye bhajanti doṣatvaṃ kutracinna tato daśa // MKpr-K_72 //
children.translated_text: still others assume the nature of faults in certain contexts — therefore [they are] not ten. // MKpr-K 72 //

children.text:
bahunāmapi padānāmekapadavadbhāsanātmā yaḥ śleṣaḥ yaścārohābarohakramarūpaḥ samādhiḥ yā ca vikaṭatvalakṣaṇā udāratā yaścaujomiśritaśaithilyātmā prasādaḥ
teṣāmojastantarbhāvaḥ / pṛthakpadatvarūpaṃ mādhuryaṃ bhaṅgyā sākṣādupāttam / prasādenārthavyaktirgṛhītā / mārgābhedarūpā samatā kvaciddoṣaḥ / tathāhi {mātaṅgāḥ kimu valgataiḥ} ityādau siṃhābhidhāne masṛṇamārgatvāyo guṇaḥ / kaṣṭatvagrāmyatvayorduṣṭābhidhānāttannirākaraṇenāpāruṣyarūpaṃ saukumāryam aujjvalyarūpā kāntiśca svīkṛtā //
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa</s> (compactness), whose nature is the unitary appearance of many words as a single word; <s>samādhi</s> (coherence), whose nature is the sequence of ascending and descending; <s>udāratā</s> (sublimity), characterized by boldness; and <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity) whose nature is <s>ojas</s> mixed with relaxation — these are subsumed within <s>ojas</s>. <s>Mādhurya</s> (sweetness), whose nature is the distinctness of individual words, has been directly adopted through implication. <s>Prasāda</s> subsumes the clarity of meaning (<s>arthavyakti</s>). <s>Samatā</s> (evenness), whose nature is uniformity of path, is in some cases a fault. For instance, in [the verse] '<s>mātaṅgāḥ kimu valgataiḥ</s>' (What of the prancing elephants?) and the like, in the description of a lion, smoothness of path is a quality. Through the removal of the defects of harshness (<s>kaṣṭatva</s>) and vulgarity (<s>grāmyatva</s>), which constitute defective expression, <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy), whose nature is non-roughness (<s>apāruṣya</s>), and <s>kānti</s> (lustre), whose nature is brilliance (<s>aujjvalya</s>), have been accepted.
Thus there are not ten qualities of word.
{'The arrangement of a sentence in the meaning of a word, and the denotation of a word in the meaning of a sentence,
<s>prauḍhi</s> (boldness), conciseness and elaboration, and purposefulness —'}
(<s>Vāmana's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 3.2.2)

children.text:
iti yā prauḍhiḥ oja ityuktaṃ tad vaicitryamātram na guṇaḥ / tadabhāve 'pi kāvyavyavahārapravṛtteḥ / apuṣṭārthatvādhikapadatvānavīkṛtatvāmaṅgalarūpāślīlagrāmyāṇāṃ nirākaraṇena ca
sābhiprāyatvarūpamojaḥ arthavaimalyātmā prasādaḥ uktivaicitryarūpaṃ mādhuryam apāruṣyarūpaṃ saukumāryam agrāmyatvarūpā udāratā ca svīkṛtāni / abhidhāsyamānasvabhāvoktyalaṅkāreṇa rasadhvaniguṇībhūtavyaṅgyābhyāṃ ca vastusvabhāvasphuṭatvarūpā arthavyaktiḥ, dīptarasatvarūpā kāntiśca svīkṛtā / kramakauṭilyānulbaṇatvopapattiyogarūpaghaṭanātmā śleṣo 'pi vicitratvamātram / avaiṣamyasvarūpā samatā doṣābhāvamātraṃ na punarguṇaḥ / kaḥ khalvanunmattonyasya
prastāvenyadabhidadhyāt / arthasyāyoner'nyacchāyāyonervā yadi na bhavati darśanaṃ tatkathaṃ kāvyam ityarthadṛṣṭirūpaḥ samādhirapi na guṇaḥ //72//
children.translated_text: This <s>prauḍhi</s> (boldness) is said to be <s>ojas</s> — but that is mere variety, not a <s>guṇa</s>; because even in its absence, the designation 'poetry' applies.
