And through the removal of defectiveness-of-meaning, excess-of-words, non-selectedness, inauspiciousness, indecency, and vulgarity — <s>ojas</s>, whose nature is purposefulness (<s>sābhiprāyatva</s>); <s>prasāda</s>, whose nature is clarity of meaning (<s>arthavaimalya</s>); <s>mādhurya</s>, whose nature is variety of expression (<s>uktivaicitrya</s>); <s>saukumārya</s>, whose nature is non-roughness (<s>apāruṣya</s>); and <s>udāratā</s>, whose nature is non-vulgarity (<s>agrāmyatva</s>) — have been accepted. And through <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description), to be described later, and through <s>rasadhvani</s> (suggestion of <s>rasa</s>) and <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (suggestion subordinated to the expressed) — <s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning), whose nature is the manifestness of the intrinsic nature of things; and <s>kānti</s> (lustre), whose nature is the vividness of <s>rasa</s> — have been accepted. <s>Śleṣa</s> (compactness), whose nature is arrangement (<s>ghaṭanā</s>) consisting in sequence, non-obtrusiveness, propriety, and fitness — that too is mere variety. <s>Samatā</s> (evenness), whose nature is uniformity, is merely the absence of fault, not a <s>guṇa</s>. For what person not deranged would express one thing in the context of another? And if the perception of the meaning or of its complement of literary flavor does not occur, then how is it poetry? — Thus <s>samādhi</s> (coherence), whose nature is perception of meaning, is also not a <s>guṇa</s>. //72//
Therefore, the [so-called] qualities of meaning are not to be enumerated ...
... are not to be enumerated.
... and those which are said to be qualities of word:

children.text: varṇāḥ samāso racanā teṣāṃ vyañjakatāmitāḥ // MKpr-K_73 //
children.translated_text: phonemes, compounds, and sentence-structure — these are considered as having the [mere] capacity of manifesting those [qualities]. // MKpr-K 73 //
He states which [manifests] which:

children.text: murdhni vargāntyagāḥ sparśā aṭavargā raṇau laghū /
children.translated_text: The head [sounds], the final [consonants] of classes, stops, the <s>aṭ</s>-class [sounds], <s>ra</s> and <s>ṇa</s>, light [syllables],
repetition, or middle [style of] composition — [these conduce to] <s>mādhurya</s>; likewise the arrangement. // MKpr-K 74 //

children.text: ṭaṭhaḍaḍhavarjitāḥ kādayo māntāḥ śirasi nijavargāntyayuktāḥ tathā rephaṇakārau hrasvāntaritāviti varṇāḥ samāsābhāvo madhyamaḥ samāso veti samāsaḥ tathā mādhuryavatī padāntarayogena racanā mādhuryasya vyañjikā // udāharaṇam
children.translated_text: The phonemes [that indicate <s>mādhurya</s>] are: <s>ka</s> to <s>ma</s>, excluding <s>ṭa</s>, <s>ṭha</s>, <s>ḍa</s>, <s>ḍha</s>, with the final [nasal] of their own group at the head, and likewise <s>repha</s> and <s>ṇakāra</s> separated by short [vowels]. Absence of compounds or moderate compounding, and a composition with interval between words that is expressive of <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness). An example:

children.text:
{anaṅgaraṅgapratiaṃ tadaṅgaṃ
  bhaṅgībhraṅgīkṛtamānatāṅgyāḥ /
  kurvanti yūnāṃ sahasā yathaitāḥ
  svāntāni śāntāparacintanāni //347//74///}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 179)

{Her limbs, serving as a stage for the play of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of love), with her graceful body's bending turned into a swaying gait — these suddenly make the hearts of young men free from all other thoughts. ||347||}
The conjunction of the first and third [consonants of a class] with the final [nasal], of two similar [consonants] with <s>repha</s>,

children.text: ṭādiḥ śaṣau vṛttidairghyaṃ gumpha uddhṛta ojasi // MKpr-K_75 //
children.translated_text: the <s>ṭa</s>-class, <s>śa</s> and <s>ṣa</s>, long compounds, and complex construction — [these characterize] <s>ojas</s> (vigor). || MKpr-K_75 ||

children.text:
vargaprathamatṛtīyābhyāmantyayoḥ dvitīyacaturthayoḥ repheṇa adha upari ubhayatra vā yasya kasyacit tulyayoḥ tena tasyaiva saṃbandhaḥ ṭavargo 'rthāt ṇakāravarjaḥ śakāraṣakārau dīrghasamāsaḥ vikaṭā saṃghaṭanā ojasaḥ /
udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: Of the first and third [consonants] of each class with the final [nasal of the class], and of the second and fourth [consonants] with <s>repha</s> — either above, below, or on both sides — the conjunction of whichever two similar ones with that very one; the <s>ṭa</s>-class, naturally excluding <s>ṇakāra</s>; the sibilants <s>śa</s> and <s>ṣa</s>; long compounds; and complex construction (<s>gumpha</s>) — these [characterize] <s>ojas</s>. An example:

children.text:
{mūrdhnāmuddhṛttakrṭta_ityādi //348[=159(incorr.285)]//75//}
  [mūrddhnāmudvṛttakṛttāviralagalagaladraktasaṃsaktadhārā-
  dhauteśāṅghriprasādopanatajayajagajjātamithyāmahimnām /
  kailāsollāsanecchāvyatikarapiśunotsarpidarpoddhurāṇāṃ
  doṣṇāṃ caiṣāṃ kimetat phalamiha nagarīrakṣaṇe yat prayāsaḥ //159//]

children.translated_text: (<s>Harṣa's</s> <s>Nāgānanda</s> 8)

{<s>mūrdhnām</s> etc. — By those whose pride, swollen and betraying the desire to sport on <s>Kailāsa</s>, whose heads, severed and overturned, with streams of blood flowing thickly from them, washed the grace of <s>Śiva's</s> feet — what is the fruit of these arms' labor here in merely guarding the city? ||348||}
That quality by which the cognition of meaning arises from word by mere hearing,

children.text: sādhāraṇaḥ samagrāṇāṃ sa prasādo guṇo mataḥ // MKpr-K_76 //
children.translated_text: common to all [<s>rasas</s>] — that is considered the quality of <s>prasāda</s> (clarity). || MKpr-K_76 ||
'Common to all' means to all <s>rasas</s> and to all compositional styles. An example:

children.text:
{parimlānaṃ pīnastanajaghanasaṃgādubhayatas-
  tanormadhyasyāntaḥ parimilanamaprāpya haritam /
  idaṃ vyastanyāsaṃ ślathabhujalatākṣepavalanaiḥ
  kṛśāṅgyāḥ saṃtāpaṃ vadati bisinīpatraśayanam //349//76//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa's</s> <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 2.12)

{The bed of lotus leaves tells of the suffering of the slender-bodied one: withered on both sides from the contact of her full breasts and hips, the green of the middle portion not having met [each side] within, and with the tossing and twisting motions of her loosened vine-like arms deployed upon it. ||349||}
Although compositional style and the rest are subordinate to <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), nevertheless:
Sometimes, through the propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) of the speaker, the expressed content, and the composition,
a difference in composition, style, and phonemes is also accepted. || MKpr-K_77 ||
Sometimes, regardless of the expressed content and the composition, compositional style and the rest [arise] solely from the propriety of the speaker. For example:
(<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa's</s> <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 1.22)

{Steady as the rumbling of <s>Mandara</s> [mountain] with its hollows inundated by the water of the churned ocean, fierce as the mutual collision of the clouds of dissolution thundering at the blows of the corners [of the mountain], the forerunner of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> anger, the storm-wind of the catastrophe that destroys the <s>Kuru</s> lineage — by whom has this war-drum been struck, whose lion's roar is echoed by our own? ||350||}

children.text: atra hi na vācyaṃ krodhādivyañjakam / abhineyārthaṃ ca ca kāvyamiti tatpratikūlā uddhatā racanādayaḥ / vaktā cātra bhīmasenaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the expressed content does not indicate anger and the like. And since poetry is meant for dramatic performance, the vigorous compositional style and the rest are contrary to that [requirement]. And the speaker here is <s>Bhīmasena</s>.
Sometimes, regardless of the speaker and the composition, compositional style and the rest [arise] solely from the propriety of the expressed content.
For example:

children.text:
{prauḍhacchedānurūpocchalanarayabhavatsaiṃhikeyopaghāta-
  trāsākṛṣṭāśvatiryagvalitaravirathenāruṇenekṣyamāṇam /
  kurvat kākutsthavīryastutimiva marutāṃ kandharārandhrabhājāṃ
  bhāṅkārairbhīmametannipatati viyataḥ kumbhakarṇottamāṅgam //351//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Viewed by <s>Aruṇa</s> (the dawn), who — his chariot of the sun swerving sidewise, its horses pulled in fright from the destruction of <s>Siṃhikā's</s> son [<s>Rāhu</s>], whose onslaught was appropriate to the magnitude of the severance — praised the valor of <s>Kākutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) with resonant cries (<s>bhāṅkāra</s>) from the cavities of the necks of the winds — this terrifying head of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> falls from the sky! ||351||}
Sometimes, regardless of the speaker and the expressed content, they [compositional features] are appropriate solely to the literary genre.

children.text:
tathāhi ----
ākhyāyikāyāṃ śṛṅgāre 'pi na masṛṇavarṇādayaḥ / kathāyāṃ raudre 'pi nātyantamuddhatāḥ / nāṭakādau raudre 'pi na dīrghasamāsādayaḥ //
children.translated_text: That is to say: in an <s>ākhyāyikā</s> (prose narrative), even in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic), soft phonemes and the like [are not used]. In a <s>kathā</s> (tale), even in <s>raudra</s> (the furious), the [composition] is not extremely vigorous. In a <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) and the like, even in <s>raudra</s>, long compounds and the like [are not used].
Thus, other improprieties should also be observed. ||77||

children.text: iti kāvyaprakāśe guṇālaṅkārabhedaniyataguṇanirṇayo nāma aṣṭama ullāsaḥ //8//
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, the eighth <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter), named 'The Determination of <s>Guṇas</s> Fixed by the Distinction of <s>Guṇa</s> and <s>Alaṅkāra</s>.' ||8||
Now the ninth <s>ullāsa</s> (chapter).

children.text: guṇavivecane kṛte 'laṅkārāḥ prāptāvasarāḥ iti saṃprati śabdālaṅkārānāha ----
children.translated_text: Having completed the examination of <s>guṇas</s>, the <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures of speech) have come to their proper occasion; accordingly, he now states the verbal figures (<s>śabdālaṅkāras</s>):
When a statement spoken in one sense is joined with another meaning by another,

children.text: śleṣeṇa kākvā vā jñeyā sā vaktroktistathā dvidhā // MKpr-K_78 //
children.translated_text: through <s>śleṣa</s> (punning) or through <s>kāku</s> (tone) — that should be known as <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression), which is thus twofold. || MKpr-K_78 ||

children.text: tatheti śleṣavakroktiḥ kākuvakroktiśca / tara padabhaṅgaśleṣeṇa yathā
children.translated_text: 'Thus' means <s>śleṣa-vakrokti</s> (oblique expression through punning) and <s>kāku-vakrokti</s> (oblique expression through tone). Of these, [an example] with word-breaking punning (<s>padabhaṅga-śleṣa</s>):

children.text:
{nārīṇāmanukūlamācarasi cejjānāsi kaścetano
  vāmānāṃ priyamādadhāti hitakṛnnaivābalānāṃ bhavān /
  yuktaṃ kiṃ hitakartanaṃ nanu balābhāvaprasiddhātmanaḥ
  sāmarthyaṃ bhavataḥ purandaramatacchedaṃ vidhātuṃ kutaḥ //352//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{If you act favorably toward women — well, you know how, if you are sentient; [but] a benefactor does not bestow what is dear upon the perverse — you are not [a benefactor] of the weak. Is it fitting to cut off benefit? But for one whose powerlessness is self-evident, whence the capacity, O <s>Purandara</s>? — whence the ability to effect destruction? ||352||}
[An example] with unbroken punning (<s>abhaṅga-śleṣa</s>):

children.text:
{aho kenedṛśī buddhirdāruṇā tava nirmitā /
  triguṇā śrūyate buddhirna tu dārumayī kvacit //353//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka's</s> <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)
{Alas, by whom was such a cruel mind fashioned for you? The mind is said to be threefold in <s>guṇas</s> — but never heard of as made of wood! ||353||}
[An example] with tone (<s>kāku</s>):

children.text:
{gurujanaparatantratayā dūrataraṃ deśamudyato gantum /
  alikulakokilalalite naiṣyati sakhi surabhisamaye 'sau //354//78//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 191)
{Being dependent on the elders, he sets out to go to a distant land; O friend, he will not come in the fragrant season — [the one] delightful with the rows of bees and cuckoos. ||354||}
Similarity of phonemes is <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration)...

children.text: svaravaisādṛśye 'pi vyañjanasadṛśatvaṃ varṇasāmyam / rasādyanugataḥ prakṛṣṭo nyāso 'nuprāsaḥ //
children.translated_text: Even when vowels differ, the similarity of consonants constitutes phonemic similarity. <s>Anuprāsa</s> is an excellent arrangement that accompanies <s>rasa</s> and the rest.
... it is twofold, belonging to the <s>cheka</s> (elegant) and <s>vṛtti</s> (style) [varieties].

children.text: chekāḥ vidagdhāḥ / vṛttirniyatavarṇagato rasaviṣayo vyāpāraḥ / gata iti chekānuprāso vṛttyanuprāsaśca //
children.translated_text: '<s>Cheka</s>' means 'the learned/elegant.' '<s>Vṛtti</s>' is an operation concerning <s>rasa</s>, involving fixed phonemes. 'Belonging to' — thus <s>chekānuprāsa</s> and <s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s>.
What is the nature of these two? He says:
The former is the single occurrence [of similarity] of multiple [consonants]...

children.text: anekasya arthāt vyañjanasya sakṛdekavāraṃ sādṛśyaṃ chekānuprāsaḥ / udāharaṇam
children.translated_text: 'Of multiple' — namely of consonants — the similarity occurring once is <s>chekānuprāsa</s>. An example:
(<s>Kuntaka's</s> <s>Vakroktijīvita</s> 1.19)
{Then the moon, with its body made languid by the faintly reddish trembling, assumed the pallor of the cheeks of women emaciated by love. ||355||}
... the latter is the repeated [occurrence] even of a single [consonant]. || MKpr-K_79 ||

children.text: ekasya apiśabdādanekasya vyañjanasya dvirbahukṛtvo vā sādṛśyaṃ vṛttyanuprāsaḥ //79//
children.translated_text: 'Of a single' — and by the word 'also' (api), of multiple consonants — the similarity occurring twice, many times, and so on is <s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s>. ||79||
Therein:
With phonemes that indicate <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), [the style] is called <s>upanāgarikā</s> (urbane); with those that reveal <s>ojas</s> (vigor), it is <s>paruṣā</s> (harsh)...
For both, examples have been given previously.
... with the remaining ones, [it is] <s>komalā</s> (tender). || MKpr-K_80 ||

children.text: paraiḥ śeṣaiḥ / tāmeva kecit grāmyeti vadanti / udāharaṇam
children.translated_text: 'With the remaining ones' — with the remaining [phonemes]. Some call that very one '<s>grāmya</s>' (rustic). An example:

children.text:
{apasārasya ghanasāraṃ kuru hāraṃ dūra eva kiṃ kamalaiḥ /
  alamalamāli mṛṇākairiti vadati divāniśaṃ bālā //356[=341]//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Dāmodaragupta's</s> <s>Kuṭṭanīmata</s> 102)
{Remove the camphor, put away the necklace, why bother with lotuses at all? Enough, enough, O garland-maker, with lotus stalks! — thus speaks the young girl day and night. ||356||}
According to some, these are considered the literary styles (<s>rītis</s>) headed by the <s>Vaidarbhī</s>.

children.text: etāstisro vṛttayaḥ vāmānādīnāṃ mate vaidarbhīgauḍīpāñcālyākhyā rītayo matāḥ //
children.translated_text: These three styles — in the view of <s>Vāmana</s> and others — are called <s>Vaidarbhī</s>, <s>Gauḍī</s>, and <s>Pāñcālī</s> styles.
The verbal one is <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s> (Lāṭa-style repetition) — from mere difference of purport when [words] are distinct. || MKpr-K_81 ||

children.text: śabdagato 'nuprāsaḥ śabdārthayorabhede 'pyanvayamātrabhedāt lāṭajanavallabhatvācca lāṭānuprāsaḥ / eṣa padānuprāsa ityanye //81//
children.translated_text: A word-based <s>anuprāsa</s> — even when there is no difference in word and meaning, from mere difference of syntactic connection, and because it is beloved of the <s>Lāṭa</s> people — is <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s>. Others call this <s>padānuprāsa</s> (word-repetition). ||81||
Of words, it [occurs]...
'It' refers to <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s>. An example:

children.text:
{yasya na savidhe dayitā davadahanastuhinadīdhitistasya /
  yasya ca savidhe dayitā davadahanastuhinadīdhitistasya //357//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 161)

{For one in whose vicinity the beloved is not present, the forest fire is the cool-rayed moon; and for one in whose vicinity the beloved is present, the forest fire is the cool-rayed moon [i.e., a source of pleasure]. ||357||}
... of a word too...
By the word 'also' (<s>api</s>), 'it' is included [i.e., <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s> can occur with a single word too]. An example:

children.text:
{vadanaṃ varavarṇinyāstasyāḥ satyaṃ sudhākaraḥ /
  sudhākaraḥ kva nu punaḥ kalaṅkavikalo bhavet //358//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 194)
{The face of that woman of excellent complexion is truly the moon (<s>sudhākara</s>). But where again would the moon be — deficient in its blemish? ||358||}

children.text:
... vṛttāvanyatra tatra vā /
nāmnaḥ sa vṛttyavṛttyośca ...
children.translated_text: ... in a compound or elsewhere, in that [compound] or [separately]; of a nominal stem, it [occurs] in compound or non-compound form...

children.text: ekasmin samāse bhinne vā samāse samāsāsamāsayorvā nāmnaḥ prātipadikasya na tu padasya sārūpyam / udāharaṇam
children.translated_text: In a single compound or in a divided compound, or in a compound and a non-compound — the formal identity is of the nominal stem (<s>prātipadika</s>), not of the inflected word (<s>pada</s>). An example:

children.text:
{sitakarakararuciravibhā vibhākarākāra dharaṇidhara kīrtiḥ /
  pauruṣakamalā kamalā sāpi tavaivāsti nānyasya //359 [=314]//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 195)

{Your fame, with the radiance of beautiful moonbeams, is splendid like the maker of radiance; <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), the lotus-like fortune of valor, also belongs to you alone and to no other. ||359||}
... thus it is considered fivefold. || MKpr-K_82 ||

children.text:
arthe satyarthabhinnānāṃ varṇānāṃ sā punaḥ śrutiḥ /
yamakaṃ ...
children.translated_text: When the meaning exists, the repetition of phonemes with different meanings — that is <s>yamaka</s> (chiming)...

children.text: samarasamaraso 'yamityādāvekeṣāmarthavattve anyeṣāmanarthakatve bhinnārthānāmiti na yujyate vaktum iti arthe satītyuktam / seti sarorasa ityādivailakṣaṇyena tenaiva krameṇa sthitā /
children.translated_text: In [examples like] '<s>samarasamaraso 'yam</s>' and so on, some [phonemes] are meaningful while others are not — so it is not proper to say 'of different meanings.' Hence the qualification 'when the meaning exists.' 'It' (<s>sā</s>) — stands [as a technical term] distinguished by [examples like] '<s>sarorasa</s>' and the like, in that very order.
... occurring in a quarter-verse, a portion thereof, [or extending across portions] — it admits of many [varieties]. || MKpr-K_83 ||

children.text: prathamo dvitīyādau dvitīyastṛtīyādau tṛtīyaścaturthe prathamastriṣvapīti sapta / prathamo dvitīye tṛtīyaścaturthe prathamaścaturthe dvitīyastṛtīye, iti dve / tadevaṃ pādajaṃ navabhedam / ardhāvṛttiḥ ślokāvṛttiśceti dve /
children.translated_text: The first [in the] second [quarter] and so on; the second [in the] third and so on; the third in the fourth; the first in [all] three — thus seven [varieties]. The first in the second, the third in the fourth, the first in the fourth, the second in the third — thus two [more]. So the varieties arising from [full] quarter-verses are nine. Half-verse repetition and whole-verse repetition make two [more].

children.text: dvidhā vibhakte pāde prathamādipādādibhāgaḥ pūrvavat dvitīyādipādādibhāgeṣu antabhāgo 'nantabhāgeṣviti viṃśatirbhedāḥ ślokāntare hi nāsau bhāgāvṛttiḥ / trikhaṇḍe triṃśat catuḥkhaṇḍe catvāriṃśat /
children.translated_text: In a quarter divided into two, the first portion of the first quarter and so on [repeating] in the second portion of the second quarter and so on, and the final portion in the subsequent portions — twenty varieties. For in the next verse, it is not a portion-repetition. In three divisions, thirty; in four divisions, forty.

children.text:
prathamapādādigatāntyārghādibhāgo dvitīyapādādigate ādyārdhādibhāge yamyate ityādyanvarthatānusaraṇenānekabhedam / antādikam / ādyantikam / tatsamucchayaḥ / madhyādikam / ādimadhyam / antamadhyam / madhyñtikam / teṣāṃ samuccayaḥ / tathā tasminneva pāde
ādyādibhāgānāṃ madhyādibhāge aniyate ca sthāne āvṛttiriti prabhūtatamabhedam / tadetatkāvyāntargaḍubhūtam iti nāsya bhedalakṣaṇaṃ kṛtam / diṅmātramudāhriyate /
children.translated_text: Following the semantic analysis: the final-half portion of the first quarter occurring in the initial-half portion of the second quarter, and so on — many varieties. Final-initial; initial-final; a combination of those; middle-initial; initial-middle; final-middle; middle-final; combinations of those. And similarly, the repetition of the initial portions within the same quarter at the middle portions, and at unfixed positions — thus very many varieties. Since this is submerged within <s>kāvya</s> [as a whole], its varieties and definitions have not been given [in detail]. Only a brief indication is exemplified:
(<s>Rudraṭa's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 10.27)
{Having worshipped the crescent-moon-crested one (<s>Śiva</s>), free of evil, with ornaments of women — then, O one adorned with women's ornaments, free of delusion, conquer the earth! ||360||}

children.text:
{vināyameno nayatāsukhādinā vinā yamenonayatā sukhādinā /
  mahājanodīyata mānasādaraṃ mahājanodī yatamānasādaram //361//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 3.5)

{Without sin, leading with prosperity and the like; without <s>Yama</s> (death), leading with bliss and the like — may the great people give honor to him of devoted mind; may the great people strive with honored and devoted mind! ||361||}
(<s>Rudraṭa's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 3.18)
{He, delighting in undertakings, necessarily subduing the weak, extending his battle-cry, always desired battle, stationed like a forest fire. ||362||}
(<s>Rudraṭa's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 3.19)
{He of true valor, delighting in undertakings, necessarily restraining the extended battle-cry, always desired battle — stationed like a forest fire. ||363||}

children.text:
{anantamahimavyāptaviśvāṃ vedhā na veda yām /
  yā ca māteva bhajate praṇate mānave dayām //364//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ānandavardhana's</s> <s>Devīśataka</s> 1)
{She of infinite greatness, pervading the universe — the Creator does not know her; and she, like a mother, bestows compassion upon a bowing mortal. ||364||}

children.text:
{yadānato 'yadā nato nayātyayaṃ na yātyayam /
  śivehitāṃ śive hitāṃ smarāmitāṃ smarāmi tām //365//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ānandavardhana's</s> <s>Devīśataka</s> 49)
{When he bows, when he does not bow — this one leads, this one does not lead to destruction; the auspicious one, the beneficent one — I remember her, I remember her! ||365||}

children.text:
{sarasvati prasādaṃ me sthitiṃ cittasarasvati /
  sara svati kuru kṣetrakurukṣetrasarasvati //366//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ānandavardhana's</s> <s>Devīśataka</s> 50)
{O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, grant me grace, a steady state of mind, O <s>Sarasvatī</s> of the mind! Flow forth, O Flowing One, make this the sacred field — O <s>Sarasvatī</s> of <s>Kurukṣetra</s>! ||366||}

children.text:
{sasāra sākaṃ darpaṇe kandarpeṇa sasārasā /
  śarannavānā bibhrāṇā nāvibhrāṇā śarannavā //367//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 3.35)
{She wandered together with <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love) in the mirror — she of fluid essence; bearing new autumn, [herself] bearing — not bearing autumn, [yet] new autumn. ||367||}
(<s>Ratnākara</s>'s <s>Haravijaya</s> 3.57)

{The world bore the splendor of the season of bees and blossoming, conquered by love, delightful with flowers and fragrant, forestalling the flooding of lotuses and waters, bursting forth with coppery reddened forests. ||368||}
Thus, [this topic] stands with thousands of varieties, yet is otherwise inferrable. //83//
Words that, [though] differentiated by difference in meaning, touch upon simultaneous utterance,
coalesce — that is <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), eightfold by means of syllable and the rest. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_84 //

children.text:
{arthabhedena śabdabhedaḥ} iti darśane {kāvyamārge svaro na gaṇyate} iti ca naye vācyabhedena bhinnā api śabdā yat yugapaduccāraṇena śliṣyanti bhinnaṃ svarūpamapahnuvate sa śleṣaḥ /
sa ca varṇapadaliṅgabhāṣāprakṛtipratyayavibhaktivacanñanāṃ bhedādaṣṭadhā / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: According to the view that 'difference of meaning entails difference of word,' and the principle that 'in the path of poetry, accent is not counted,' words that, though differentiated by difference of expressed meaning, coalesce through simultaneous utterance — concealing their distinct forms — that is <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia). It is eightfold due to the distinctions of <s>varṇa</s> (syllable), <s>pada</s> (word), <s>liṅga</s> (gender), <s>bhāṣā</s> (language), <s>prakṛti</s> (stem), <s>pratyaya</s> (suffix), <s>vibhakti</s> (case-ending), and <s>vacana</s> (number). Examples in order —
(1) <s>varṇa</s> (syllable)

children.text:
{alaṅkāraḥ śaṅkākaranarakapālaṃ parijano
  viśīrṇāṅgo bhṛṅgī avsu ca vṛṣa eko bahuvayāḥ /
  avastheyaṃ sthāṇor'pi bhavati sarvāmaraguror-
  vidhau vakre mūrdhni sthitavati vayaṃ ke punaramī //369//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Subhāṣitaratnākara</s> 1344)

{'The ornament is one that causes anxiety; the retinue consists of skulls; the limbs are withered — <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>; the vehicle is a bull, singular and aged. This is the condition even of <s>Sthāṇu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the preceptor of all the gods — when fate is perverse, sitting upon [one's] head, who are we then, and who are these?' //369//}
(2) <s>pada</s> (word)

children.text:
{pṛthukārtasvarapātraṃ bhūṣitaniḥśeṣaparijanaṃ deva /
  vilasatkareṇugahanaṃ saṃprati samamāvayoḥ sadanam //370[=306]//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{'O lord, a vessel of pṛthu-gold, with all attendants adorned, abounding with brilliant she-elephants — at present, our two dwellings are equal.' //370[=306]//}
(3) <s>liṅga</s> (gender), (8) <s>vacana</s> (number)

children.text:
{bhaktiprahvavilokanapraṇayinī nīlotpalaspardhinī
  dhyānālambanatāṃ samādhiniratairnītehitaprāptaye /
  lāvaṇyasya mahānidhī rasikatāṃ lakṣmīdṛśostanvatī
  yuṣmākaṃ kurutāṃ bhavārtiśamanaṃ netre tanurvā hareḥ //371//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vallabhadeva</s>'s <s>Subhāṣitāvali</s>)

{'Inclined in devotion, fond of gazing, rivaling blue lotuses, adopted as objects of meditation by those devoted to <s>samādhi</s> for the attainment of desired accomplishments, great treasuries of beauty, imparting aesthetic sensibility — may the eyes, or the slender body, of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) and <s>Lakṣmī</s> effect the cessation of your worldly suffering!' //371//}
This is also a <s>śleṣa</s> of number (<s>vacana</s>).
(4) <s>bhāṣā</s> (language)

children.text: [mama dehi rasaṃ dharme tamoaśām āśāṃ gamāgamāt hara naḥ /
children.translated_text: [In Sanskrit: 'Give me the essence of <s>dharma</s>; remove our fear from the coming and going of darkness;

children.text: haravadhu śaraṇaṃ tvaṃ cittamoho 'pasaratu me sahasā //]
children.translated_text: O wife of <s>Hara</s>, you are our refuge; may the delusion of mind depart from me suddenly!']
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 991; <s>Ānandavardhana</s>'s <s>Deviśataka</s>)

{'[In Prākṛt:] In the great country, in the assembly of the virtuous, in the treatise on darkness and passion, the story of arrivals and departures, many refuges of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), that delusion of mind — O <s>Umā</s>, may it depart from me suddenly!' //372//}
(5) <s>prakṛti</s> (stem)

children.text:
{ayaṃ sarvāṇi śāstrāṇi hṛdi jñeṣu ca vakṣyati /
  sāmarthyakṛdamitrāṇāṃ mitrāṇāṃ ca nṛpātmajaḥ //373//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{'This prince will expound and hear all the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises) in his heart; he creates the power of enemies [or] of friends.' //373//}
(6) <s>pratyaya</s> (suffix)

children.text:
{rajaniramaṇamauleḥ pādapadmāvaloka-
  kṣaṇasamayaparāptāpūrvasaṃsahasram /
  pramathanivahamadhye jātucittvatprasādād
  ahamucitaruciḥ syānnanditā sā tathā me //374//}
children.translated_text: {'At the moment of beholding the lotus-feet of the Lord who is the jewel of the night, through a sudden unprecedented thousandfold thrill, may I, by your grace, in the midst of the host of <s>pramathas</s> (attendants of <s>Śiva</s>), be of fitting splendor — may that one, so delighted, be mine!' //374//}
(7) <s>vibhakti</s> (case-ending)

children.text:
{sarvasvaṃ hara sarvasya tvaṃ bhavacchedatatparaḥ /
  nayopakārasāṃmukhyamāyāsi tanuvartanam //375//84//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{'Take everything of everyone, O you who are intent on severing existence! You approach the employment of statecraft with the demeanor of servility.' //375//84//}
Due to the absence of distinction, the distinction of stem and the like may also constitute a ninth [type].
'A ninth also' — the word 'also' [indicates] a different sequence. Example —
(<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 201)

{'He who is at once capable of clipping the wings of those of other lineage, bearing hundreds of crores of gifts — that lord of the wise shines, [like <s>Indra</s>,] in steadfastness upon the surface of the earth.' //376//}
Here, due to the absence of restriction by context and the like, both meanings are expressed.

children.text: nanu svaritādiguṇabhedād bhinnaprayatnoccāryāṇāṃ tadabhāvādabhinnaprayatnoccāryāṇāṃ ca śabdānāṃ bandhe 'laṅkārāntarapratibhotpattihetuḥ śabdaśleṣo 'rthaśleṣaśceti dvividho 'pyarthālaṅkāramadhye parigaṇito 'nyairiti kathamayaṃ śabdālaṅkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, [one may object:] since words pronounced with different effort — those distinguished by accent differences such as <s>svarita</s> and the like — and those pronounced with the same effort — without such [accent differences] — give rise to the perception of another ornament when combined, <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), both as verbal and as semantic, has been enumerated among the <s>arthālaṅkāras</s> (figures of meaning) by others. So how is this a <s>śabdālaṅkāra</s> (figure of sound)?

children.text: ucyate ---- iha doṣaguṇālaṅkārāṇāṃ śabdārthagatatvena yo vibhāgaḥ saḥ anvayavyatirekābhyāmeva vyavatiṣṭhate / tathāhi ---- kaṣṭavādigāḍhatvādyanuprāsādayaḥ vyarthatvādiprauḍhyādyupamādayastadbhāvatadabhāvānuvidhāyitvādeva śabdārthagatatvena vyavasthāpyante /
children.translated_text: It is replied: Here, the classification of <s>doṣas</s> (faults), <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), and <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures) as pertaining to sound or meaning is established solely through the method of co-presence and co-absence (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>). Thus — <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) and the like, due to harshness and tightly-woven texture; and <s>upamā</s> (simile) and the like, due to maturity of meaning and such — are established as pertaining to sound and meaning respectively, precisely because they follow the presence and absence [of those elements].

children.text:
svayaṃ ca pallavātāmrabhāsvatkaravirājitā / ityabhaṅgaḥ
  {prabhātasaṃdhyevāsvāpaphalalubdhehitapradā //377//}
iti sabhaṅgaḥ iti dvāvapi śabdaikasamāśrayāviti dvayorapi śabdaśleṣatvamupapannaṃ
na tvādyasyārthaśleṣatvam / arthaśleṣasya tu sa viṣayaḥ yatra śabdaparivartane 'pi na śleṣatvakhaṇḍanā / yathā
children.translated_text: 'And she herself, radiant with hands lustrous as coral-tender shoots' — this is without word-division (<s>abhaṅga</s>). {'At dawn, she who gives the desired fruit to those desirous of the rewards of awakening.' //377//} — this is with word-division (<s>sabhaṅga</s>). Thus both rest upon sound alone, and hence the classification of both as <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (verbal paronomasia) is established — but the first is not <s>arthaśleṣa</s> (semantic paronomasia). The domain of <s>arthaśleṣa</s>, however, is where even upon substitution of words, the paronomastic quality is not destroyed. As in:

children.text:
{stokenonnatimāyāti stokenāyātyadhogatim /
  aho susadṛśī vṛttistulākoṭeḥ khalasya ca //378//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Pañcastavī</s> 1.150)
{'By a little it rises upward, by a little it goes downward — oh, how alike are the movements of the tip of a balance and of a wicked person!' //378//}

children.text:
na cāyamupamāpratibhotpattihetuḥ śleṣaḥ api tu śleṣapratibhotpattiheturupamā / tathāpi ---- yathā
{kamalamiva mukhaṃ manojñametatkacatitarām} ityādau guṇasāmye kriyāsāmye ubhayasāmye vā upamā / tathā 'sakalakalaṃ purametajjātaṃ saṃprati sudhāṃśubimbamiva'; ityādau śabdamātrasāmye 'pi sā yuktaiva / tathā hyuktaṃ rudraṭena
children.translated_text: And this <s>śleṣa</s> does not give rise to the perception of <s>upamā</s> (simile); rather, the <s>upamā</s> gives rise to the perception of <s>śleṣa</s>. Nevertheless — just as in 'this face, charming as a lotus' and the like, there is <s>upamā</s> based on similarity of quality, action, or both; so too in 'this city, born just now, complete with all arts, is like the orb of the nectar-rayed [moon]' and similar cases, the <s>upamā</s> is appropriate even when based on mere verbal similarity. For thus <s>Rudraṭa</s> has stated:

children.text:
{sphuṭamarthālaṅkārāvetāvupamāsamuccayau kiṃ tu /
  āśritya śabdamātraṃ sśmānyamihāpi saṃbhavataḥ //} iti /

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>, <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s>)

{'Clearly these two — <s>upamā</s> (simile) and <s>samuccaya</s> (accumulation) — are <s>arthālaṅkāras</s> (figures of meaning); however, resting on mere sound, they can occur here too in a general way.' //}

children.text: na ca {kamalamiva mukham} ityādiḥ sādhāraṇadharmaprayogaśūnya upamāviṣaya iti vaktaṃ yuktaṃ pūrṇopamāyā nirviṣayatvāpatteḥ //
children.translated_text: And it would not be right to say that 'the face like a lotus' and the like, being devoid of the use of a common property, is a domain of <s>upamā</s> — because that would lead to the absurdity that full <s>upamā</s> has no domain at all.

children.text:
{deva tvameva pātālamāśānāṃ tvaṃ nibandhanam /
  tvaṃ cāmaramarudbhūmireko lokatrayātmakaḥ //379//}
children.translated_text: {'O lord, you alone are the netherworld; you are the fastening of the directions; you are the heaven, the wind, and the earth — the one who is the self of the three worlds.' //379//}

children.text:
ityādiḥ śleṣasya copamādyalaṅkāraviviktosti viṣaya iti / dvayoryoge saṃkara eva / upapattiparyālocane tu upamāyā evāyaṃ yukto viṣayaḥ / anyathā viṣayāpahāra eva pūrṇopamāyāḥ syāt /
na ca 'abindusundarī nityaṃ galallāvaṇyabindukā'; ityādau virodhapratibhotpattihetuḥ śleṣaḥ api tu śleṣapratibhotpattiheturvirodhaḥ / na hyatrārthadvayapratipādakaḥ śabdaśleṣaḥ dvitīyārthasya pratibhātamātrasya prarohābhāvāt / na ca virodhābhāsa iva virodhaḥ śleṣābhāsaḥ śleṣaḥ /
tadevamādiṣu vākyeṣu śleṣapratibhotpattiheturalaṅkārāntarameva / tathā ca
children.translated_text: Such examples as this constitute the domain of <s>śleṣa</s> when it is distinct from <s>upamā</s> and other ornaments. When both occur together, it is indeed <s>saṅkara</s> (conflation). But upon careful reflection, this is indeed the proper domain of <s>upamā</s> alone; otherwise, there would be an encroachment upon the domain of full <s>upamā</s>. And in 'she who is always beautiful without a dot, [yet] having a dot of beauty at the throat' and the like — the <s>śleṣa</s> does not give rise to the perception of <s>virodha</s> (contradiction); rather, the <s>virodha</s> gives rise to the perception of <s>śleṣa</s>. For here, the <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (verbal paronomasia) expressing two meanings does not [truly produce two meanings], since the second meaning merely flashes without taking root. And just as in <s>virodhābhāsa</s> (apparent contradiction), the <s>virodha</s> is [merely] apparent, so the <s>śleṣa</s> here is <s>śleṣābhāsa</s> (apparent paronomasia), not [genuine] <s>śleṣa</s>. Thus, in such sentences, it is another ornament entirely that gives rise to the perception of <s>śleṣa</s>. And so:
(<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 10.27)
{'[Born of] a good lineage, [like] a pearl freed [from its shell].' //380//}
{'Not small, like a poet with few verses — O lord, you are great!' //381//}

children.text:
{anurāgavatī saṃdhyā divasastatpuraḥsaraḥ /
  aho daivagatiścitrā tathāpi na samāgamaḥ //382//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ānandavardhana</s>'s <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 1.9)
{'The twilight is full of passion; the day precedes it. Ah, wonderful is the course of fate — yet still there is no union!' //382//}

children.text:
{ādāya cāpamacalaṃ kṛtvāhīnaṃ guṇaṃ viṣamadṛṣṭiḥ /
  yaścitramacyutaśaro lakṣyamabhāṅkṣīnnamastasmai //383//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{'Taking up the bow, making the mountain steady, diminishing the bowstring's quality, he of venomous gaze, whose arrow never missed <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) — wonderful! — he hit the mark. Obeisance to him!' //383//}

In such cases, it is appropriate to call [the figure] partial transformation (<s>rūpaka</s>), <s>śleṣa</s>, <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), <s>samāsokti</s> (compressed expression), or <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) — but not <s>śleṣa</s> [alone].

children.text:
śabdaśleṣa iti cocyate arthālaṅkāramadhye ca lakṣyate iti ko 'yaṃ nayaḥ / kiṃ ca caicitryamalaṅkāra iti ya eva kavipratibhāsaṃrambhagocarastatreva vicitratā iti saivālaṅkārabhūmiḥ / arthamukhaprekṣitvameteṣāṃ śabdānāmiti cet anuprāsādīnāmapi tathaiveti te 'pyarthālaṅkārāḥ kiṃ nocyante / rasādivyañjakasvarūpavācyaviśeṣasavyapekṣatve 'pi hyanuprāsādīnām
alaṅkāratā / śabdaguṇadoṣāṇāmapyarthāpekṣayaiva guṇadoṣatā / arthaguṇadoṣālaṅkārāṇāṃ śabdāpekṣayaiva vyavasthitiriti te 'pi śabdagatatvenocyantām / {vidhau vakre mūrdhni} ityādau ca varṇādiśleṣe ekaprayatnoccāryatve 'rthaśleṣatvaṃ śabdabhede 'pi prasajyatāmityevamādi svayaṃ
vicāryam //
children.translated_text: [If you ask:] it is called <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (verbal paronomasia) and yet enumerated among the <s>arthālaṅkāras</s> (figures of meaning) — what kind of principle is this? Moreover, since 'variety is ornament,' the very domain where the poet's creative power flourishes is where variety resides — and that alone is the ground of ornament. If [you say] these words are considered from the standpoint of meaning — then <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) and the like are also so [considered], so why are they not called <s>arthālaṅkāras</s> too? Even though <s>anuprāsa</s> and the like depend upon a particular expressed meaning that suggests <s>rasa</s> and the rest, they are still ornaments. The <s>guṇas</s> and <s>doṣas</s> of sound also have their quality and defectiveness only in relation to meaning. And the <s>guṇas</s>, <s>doṣas</s>, and <s>alaṅkāras</s> of meaning are established only in relation to sound — so let them too be called pertaining to sound. Furthermore, in 'when fate is perverse, sitting upon the head' and the like, where there is <s>varṇa</s>-level <s>śleṣa</s> (syllabic paronomasia), let <s>arthaśleṣa</s> (semantic paronomasia) follow even despite the difference in sounds, when they are pronounced with a single effort — let such matters be examined by oneself.
<s>Citra</s> (picture-poetry) is that in which the arrangement of syllables creates the shape of a sword and the like. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_85 //

children.text: saṃniveśaviśeṣeṇa yatra nyastā varṇāḥ khaḍgamurajapadmādyākāramullāsayanti taccitraṃ kāvyam / kaṣṭaṃ kāvyametaditi diṅmātraṃ pradarśyate / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: Where syllables, through a particular arrangement, bring forth the form of a sword, a drum, a lotus, and the like — that is <s>citra kāvya</s> (picture-poetry). 'This is labored poetry' — only a brief indication is shown. Example —
(<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 5.6)

{'By the enemies of <s>Māra</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, and elephants, with the speed of a shower, praises always begun with devotion — may she who is capable of removing that suffering [be praised]!' //384//}

children.text:
{mātā natānāṃ saṃghaṭṭaḥśriyāṃ bādhitasaṃbhramā /
  mānyātha sīmā rāmāṇāṃ śaṃ me diśyādumādimā //385//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 5.7)
(Sword-pattern, <s>khaṅgabandha</s>)

{'The mother of the prostrate, the clash of fortunes, one who has overcome agitation, worthy and the boundary of beautiful women — may she who is foremost among the [forms of] <s>Umā</s> bestow well-being upon me!' //385//}
(<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 5.19)
(Drum-pattern, <s>murajabandha</s>)
{'Straight, of many undertakings, trembling with the buzzing of bees, with gusts of wind and many clouds, with abundant rays and purity.' //386//}

children.text:
{bhāsate pratibhāsāra rasābhātāhatāvibhā /
  bhāvitātmā śubhā vāde devābhā bata te sabhā //387//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)
(Lotus-pattern, <s>padmabandha</s>)
{'She shines, the essence of radiance, the brilliance of undiminished luster, she whose soul is purified, auspicious in discourse — O divine splendor! Alas, your assembly!' //387//}
(<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 3.399)
(<s>Sarvatobhadra</s>, auspicious-in-all-directions pattern)
{'O essence of aesthetic delight, O [one of] wide eyes and wounded endurance, O [one of] pleasing wind and cooling breeze, O protector — may you guard this imperishable [being]!' //388//}

children.text: saṃbhavino 'pyanye prabhedāḥ śaktimātraprakāśakā na tu kāvyarūpatāṃ dadhatīti na pradarśyante //85//
children.translated_text: Other possible varieties, which merely demonstrate ingenuity but do not achieve the status of true poetry, are therefore not illustrated. //85//
<s>Punaruktavadābhāsa</s> (semblance of tautology) pertains to words of different form,
The appearance of identity of meaning in purposeful and purposeless words of different form is <s>punaruktavadābhāsa</s> (semblance of tautology). And this —
... of a word ...
pertains to words alone, both with and without word-division. Example —
(<s>Udbhaṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasārasaṅgraha</s> 1)

{'With a body and form [dedicated to] slaying enemies, suddenly [appearing] with charioteer, driver, horses, and infantry, always shining with the [quality of] never-abandoning, an ornament upon the surface of the earth in steadfastness.' //389//}

children.text:
{cakāsatyaṅganārāmāḥ kautukānandahetavaḥ /
  tasya rājñaḥ sumanaso vibudhāḥ pārśvavartinaḥ //390//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 207)
{'The groves of women shine, being causes of curiosity and joy; his flowers, the wise ones, are companions at the side of that king.' //390//}
... likewise, this [pertains] to both sound and meaning. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_86 //
Example —
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{'Slender of body, last among the broad-hipped, his nails red with the blood of enemy elephants, an abode of radiance, great and broad-minded — <s>Indra</s> among men, <s>Hari</s>, the victorious one.' //391//}

children.text: atraikasmin pade parivartite nālaṅkāra iti śabdāśrayaḥ aparasmiṃstu parivartite 'pi sa na hīyate ityarthaniṣṭha ityubhayālaṅkāro 'yam //86//
children.translated_text: Here, when one word is substituted, there is no ornament — hence it pertains to sound; but when another [word] is substituted, [the ornament] is not lost — hence it pertains to meaning. Thus this is an ornament of both [sound and meaning]. //86//

children.text: iti kāvyaprakāśe śabdālaṅkāranirṇayo nāma navama ullāsaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter (<s>ullāsa</s>) of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, entitled 'The Determination of Figures of Sound' (<s>śabdālaṅkāranirṇaya</s>).
Now the tenth chapter (<s>ullāsa</s>).
He states the <s>arthālaṅkāras</s> (figures of meaning):
<s>Upamā</s> (simile) is similarity [between two things] that are distinct ...

children.text: upamānopameyayoreva na tu kāryakāraṇādikayoḥ sādharmyaṃ bhavatīti tayoreva samānena dharmeṇa saṃbandha upamā /
children.translated_text: Similarity exists only between <s>upamāna</s> (the standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (the thing compared) — not between cause and effect and the like. The relation of these two through a common property is <s>upamā</s> (simile).
... it is full (<s>pūrṇā</s>) or elliptical (<s>luptā</s>) ...

children.text: upamānopameyasādhāraṇadharmopamāpratipādakānāmupādāne pūrṇā / ekasya dvayostrayāṇāṃ vā lope luptā //
children.translated_text: When the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison), <s>upameya</s> (thing compared), common property, and the word expressing comparison are all present, it is full (<s>pūrṇā</s>). When one, two, or three of these are omitted, it is elliptical (<s>luptā</s>).
... the foremost [being full] (<s>sāgrimā</s>).

children.text: śrautyārthī ca bhavedvākye samāse taddhite tathā // MKpr-K_87 //
children.translated_text: It may be auditory (<s>śrautī</s>) or inferential (<s>ārthī</s>), occurring in a sentence, in a compound, or in a <s>taddhita</s> [secondary derivative]. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_87 //
The foremost is the full [simile].

children.text: yathevādiśabdā yatparāstasyaivopamānatāpratītiriti yadyapyupamānaviśeṣaṇānyete tathāpi śabdaśaktimahimnā śrutyaiva ṣaṣṭhīvat saṃbandhaṃ pratipādayantīti tatsadbhāve śrautī upamā /
children.translated_text: Words such as 'iva' ('like') and the like — the very thing to which they are attached is understood as the standard of comparison. Although these are technically qualifiers of the standard of comparison, by the power of the word itself they directly convey the relation, just like the genitive case — hence, when they are present, the <s>upamā</s> is auditory (<s>śrautī</s>).
Likewise, by the inclusion of the suffix 'vat' prescribed in the sense indicated by 'tatra tasyeva' (just like that one there).

children.text:
{tena tulyaṃ mukham} ityādāvupameye eva {tattulyamasya} ityādau copamāne eva {idaṃ ca tacca tulyam} ityubhayatrāpi tulyādiśabdānāṃ viśrāntiriti sāmyaparyālocanayā tulyatāpratītiriti sādharmyasyārthatvāttulyādiśandopādāne ārthī tadvat 'tena tulyaṃ kriyā cedvatiḥ'; ityanena
vihitasya vateḥ sthitau /
children.translated_text: In 'tena tulyaṃ mukham' (the face is equal to that) and the like, the words such as 'tulya' and the like find rest only in the upameya (the thing compared); in 'tattulyamasya' (this is equal to that) and the like, [they find rest] only in the upamāna (the standard of comparison); and in 'idaṃ ca tacca tulyam' (both this and that are equal), [they find rest] in both. Through the consideration of equality, the cognition of likeness arises — and since similarity (sādharmya) is the meaning, with the inclusion of words like 'tulya' and the like, it is meaning-based (ārthī). Likewise, the suffix 'vat' prescribed by the rule 'tena tulyaṃ kriyā cedvatiḥ' (the suffix 'vat' when the action is equal to that) remains [in effect].

children.text: {ivena nityasamāso vibhaktyapolaḥ pūrvapadakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca} iti nityasamāse ivaśabdayoge samāsagā // krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: By the rule 'ivena nityasamāso vibhaktyapolaḥ pūrvapadakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca' (with 'iva' there is obligatory compounding, loss of case-ending, and the accent of the first member's derivative), when there is obligatory compounding with the word 'iva,' [the simile] becomes compound-based (samāsagā). Examples in order:

children.text:
{svapne 'pi samareṣu tvāṃ vijayaśrīrna muñchati /
  prabhāvaprabhavaṃ kāntaṃ svādhīnapatikā yathā //392//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
Even in dreams, in battles, the goddess of victory does not abandon you — like a devoted wife (svādhīnapatikā) [who never leaves] her beloved who is born of [her own] power. || 392 ||

children.text:
{cakitahariṇalolalocanāyāḥ krudhi taruṇāruṇatārahārikānti /
  sarasijamidamānanaṃ ca tasyāḥ samamiti cetasi saṃmadaṃ vidhatte //393//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 211)

The face of her — she of the restless eyes of a startled deer — with the reddish beauty of a freshly-reddened necklace of stars — and this lotus [that is her face] — 'they are equal' — this thought creates intoxication in the mind. || 393 ||

children.text:
{atyāyatairniyamakāribhiruddhatānāṃ
  divyaiḥ prabhābhiranapāyamayairupāyaiḥ /
  śaurirbhujairiva caturbhiradaḥ sadā yo
  lakṣmīvilāsabhavanairbhuvanaṃ babhāra //394//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śivasvāmin</s>'s <s>Kapphinābhyudaya</s> 1.39)

With four arms like divine splendors — exceedingly long, imposing of discipline, exalted, imperishable, and purposeful — <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), who always bore the world below with the mansions of <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s sport as his dwellings. || 394 ||

children.text:
{avitathamanorathapathaprathaneṣu praguṇa garimagītaśrīḥ /
  suratarusadṛśaḥ sa bhavān abhilaṣaṇīyaḥ kṣitīśvaro na kasya //395//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

O virtuous one, whose glory is celebrated for its greatness, whose path of true aspirations is unfailing — like a wish-fulfilling tree — your lordship, the king, is one to be desired — by whom not? || 395 ||

children.text:
{gāmbhīryagarimā tasya satyaṅgaṅgābhujaṅgavat /
  durālokaḥ sa samare nidāghāmbararatnavat //396//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
The weight of his gravity, like a serpent of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> upon his body in truth — he is difficult to behold in battle, like a jewel of the summer sky. || 396 ||

children.text: svādhīnapatikā kāntaṃ bhajamānā yathāṃ lokottaracamatkārabhūḥ tathā jayaśrīstvadāsevanenetyādinā pratīyamānena vinā yadyapi noktervaicitryam / vaicitryaṃ cālaṅkāraḥ / tathāpi na dhvaniguṇībhūtavyaṅgyavyavahāraḥ / na khalu vyaṅgyasaṃsparśaparāmarśādatra cārutāpratītiḥ / api tu vācya vaicityapratibhāsādeva //
children.translated_text: The devoted wife (svādhīnapatikā) serving her beloved, like [the figure suggests], is the ground for supramundane aesthetic wonder; likewise, the goddess of victory [serving] through devotion to you — and so forth — without what is thus suggested, there would be no variety of the expression. And variety is a figure of speech (alaṃkāra). Nevertheless, there is no application of the categories of dhvani or guṇībhūtavyaṅgya (subordinate suggestion). For here, the apprehension of beauty does not arise from the contact and consideration of what is suggested; rather, it arises precisely from the appearance of the variety of the expressed meaning.

children.text: rasādistu vyaṅgyor'rthālaṅkārāntaraṃ ca sarvatrāvyabhicārītyagaṇayitvaiva tadalaṅkārā udāhṛtāḥ / tadrahitatvena tu udāhriyamāṇā virasatāmāvahantīti pūrvāparaciruddhābhidhānamiti na codanīyam //87//
children.translated_text: But rasa and the like, being suggested, and other meaning-figures — since these are invariably present everywhere — those figures have been illustrated disregarding [the suggested element]. When illustrated as devoid of that [suggestion], they would bring about insipidity — hence the statement [seems] contradictory to what was said before and after; but this is not a valid objection. || 87 ||

children.text: tadvad dharmasya lope syānna śrautī taddhite punaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the common property (dharma) is elided, [the simile] would not be the Vedic type; but with a secondary suffix (taddhita), [it would be].

children.text: dharmaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ / taddhite kalpavādau tvārthyeva // tena pañca //
children.translated_text: The 'property' is the common [attribute]. With a secondary suffix (taddhita), [the simile is formed] with 'kalpa' and 'vādi' and the like — these are meaning-based (ārthī) alone. Thus there are five [types].
Examples:
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
The speech, mind, and truthfulness of the blessed one — who is distinguished by the excellence of a unique and incomparable goodness — are like nectar for what is to be done. || 397 ||

children.text:
{ākṛṣṭakaravālo 'sau saṃparāye paribhraman /
  pratyarthisenayā dṛṣṭaḥ kṛtāntena samaḥ prabhuḥ //398//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
That lord, with drawn sword, roaming in battle — when seen by the enemy army, [he appeared] equal to <s>Kṛtānta</s> (the god of Death). || 398 ||

children.text:
{karavāla ivācārastasya vāgamṛtopamā /
  viṣakalpaṃ mano vetsi yadi jīvasi tatsakhe //399//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
His conduct is like a sword; his speech is like nectar — if you know that his mind is like poison, then survive, O friend! || 399 ||
When the standard of comparison (upamāna) is not stated, [the simile may be] sentence-based, or Prākrit [verse]-based, or compound-based. || Kpr-K_88 ||

children.text:
{sa_alakaraṇaparavīsāmasiriviaraṇaṃ ṇa sarasakavvassa /
  dīsa_i aha vā ṇisamma_i sarisaṃ aṃsaṃsametteṇa //400//}

children.translated_text: [Chāyā:] The bestowing of the splendor of the exhaustion of all the senses — this is not seen in good poetry,
or rather is perceived only in a fraction of a fraction of its equal.
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 995)

The bestowing of the splendor of the exhaustion of all the senses [upon the audience] — this is not seen in good poetry, or rather is perceived only in a fraction of a fraction of its equal. || 400 ||

children.text: kavvassetryatra kavvasamamiti sarisamityatra ca ṇūṇamiti pāṭhe eṣaiva samāsagā //88//
children.translated_text: 'Kavvassa' here [means] 'equal to poetry'; and in 'sarisam,' with the reading 'ṇūṇam,' this very [simile] is compound-based. || 88 ||

children.text:
vāderlope samāse sā karmādhārakyaci kyaṅi /
karmakartrorṇamuli ...
children.translated_text: With the elision of 'vā' (or = like), in a compound [the simile arises]; with the denominative suffix kyac from the object [of comparison] and adhikaraṇa (locus), with kyaṅ from the agent or object, and with ṇamul...

children.text: vāśabdaḥ upamādyotaka iti / vāderupamāpratipādakasya lope ṣaṭ samāsena karnṇo 'dhikaraṇāccotpannena kyacā kartuḥ kyaṅā karmakartrorupapadayorṇamulā ca bhavet //
children.translated_text: The word 'vā' is an indicator of simile. With the elision of 'vā' (the simile-indicating particle), there are six [types]: through compounding, through the kyac suffix derived from the object or locus, through the kyaṅ suffix from the agent, and through the ṇamul [suffix].
Examples:

children.text:
{tataḥ kumudanāthena kāminīgaṇḍapāṇḍunā /
  netrānandena candreṇa māhendrī digalaṅkṛtā //401//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Mahābhārata</s>, <s>Droṇaparvan</s> [184.46])
Then, by the moon — pale as the cheek of a beautiful woman, the delight of the eyes — the eastern quarter was adorned. || 401 ||
Likewise:
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

With a sword-blade terrible as a black serpent, with swift movement that agitated the mind like a bird of prey, with the beauty of raised cheeks bristling [with excitement] — such was he at the sight of the enemy's valor. || 402 ||

children.text:
{pauraṃ sutīyati janaṃ samarāntaresā-
  vantaḥpurīyati vicitracaritracuñcuḥ /
  nārīyate samarasīmni kṛpāṇapāṇer
  ālokya tasya caritāni sapatnasenā //403//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 217)

The enemy army — cunning in varied exploits — when it sees the deeds of that one with sword in hand at the battle-front, behaves as if they were townspeople, behaves as if they were harem-women, behaves as if they were [mere] women. || 403 ||

children.text:
{mṛdhe nidāghagharmāṃśudarśaṃ paśyanti taṃ pare /
  sa punaḥ pārthasaṃcāraṃ saṃcaratyavanīpatiḥ //404//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 218)
In battle, the enemies see him as [if he were] the scorching rays of the summer sun; but that king himself moves about [as if performing] the movement of <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>). || 404 ||
... with the elision of both of these [dharma and vā], [the simile is] compound-based through kvip. || Kpr-K_89 ||
Of both of these — dharma (the common property) and vā (the simile-particle). Example:

children.text:
{savitā vidhavati vidhurapi savitarati tathā dinanti yāminyaḥ /
  yāminayanti dināni ca sukhaduḥkhavaśīkṛte manasi //405//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 219)

The sun widows [the days], the widowed [day] also suns [i.e., scorches]; likewise the nights day [the days], and the days night [the nights] — when the mind is under the power of happiness and sorrow. || 405 ||
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
Even with hundreds of enemy warriors desirous of combat, he is difficult to assail — when engaged in battle, that royal elephant shines. || 406 ||
With the elision of both the property (dharma) and the standard of comparison (upamāna), [the simile] is seen in both inflected forms (vṛtti) and in sentences.

children.text:
{ṭuṭuṇṇanto marihisi kaṇṭaakaliāiṃ keaivaṇāiṃ /
  mālaikusumasaricchaṃ bhamara bhamanto ṇa pāvihisi //407//}

children.translated_text: [Chāyā:] Buzzing about, you will die, [encountering] the thorn-entangled ketakī groves —
O bee, [even] buzzing, you will not attain [anything] equal to a mālatī blossom.
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 979; <s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s>)
Buzzing about, you will die, [encountering] the thorn-entangled ketakī groves — O bee, [even] buzzing, you will not attain [anything] equal to a mālatī blossom. || 407 ||
With the reading 'kusumeṇa samam' (equal to the blossom), [the simile] is sentence-based.
With the kyac [suffix], when the standard of comparison (upamāna) and the particle 'vā' [are elided], [and applied to] the subject of comparison (upameya)...
'āse' [means] 'without hope' (nirāse).
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
Here, the self [of the king] is the subject of comparison (upameya).

With eyes wide open at the sight of the enemy's valor, with the staff of his arm raised high wielding a sword — he acts as if he were <s>Sahasrāyudha</s> (the thousand-weaponed [<s>Indra</s>]). || 408 ||
... and with the elision of all three, [the simile is] compound-based. || Kpr-K_90 ||
Of the three — 'vā' (the simile-particle), the property (dharma), and the standard of comparison (upamāna). Example:

children.text:
{taruṇamani kṛtāvalokanā lalitavilāsavitīrṇavigrahā /
  smaraśaravisarācitāntarā mṛganayanā harate munermanaḥ //409//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
With a glance cast at youth, with a form extended in graceful coquetry, with the interior filled by the shooting of the arrows of Love — the doe-eyed one steals the sage's mind. || 409 ||

children.text: atra saptamyupamānetyādinā yadā samāsalopau bhavataḥ / tadedamudāharaṇam //
children.translated_text: Here, when through [the rule beginning with] 'saptamyupamāne' and the like, both the compound and the elision occur, this is the example.

children.text: krūrasyācārasyāyaḥśūlatayādhyavasāyād ayaḥśūlenānvicchati {āyaḥśūlikaḥ} ityatiśayoktirna tu krūrācāropameyataikṣṇyadharmavādīnāṃ lope trilope 'yamupamā /
children.translated_text: Through the determination of [his] cruel conduct as being an iron spike — due to the metaphorical identification with an iron spike — 'āyaḥśūlikaḥ' (one who impales) is an instance of atiśayokti (hyperbole), not a simile with the triple elision of the subject of comparison, the common property, and the simile-particle.
Thus, there are nineteen elided [types]; together with the full [types], twenty-five.

children.text:
{anayeneva rājyaśrīrdainyeneva manasvitā /
  mamlau sātha viṣādena padminīva himāmbhasā //410//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 222)
As if by dishonor, the royal glory — as if by baseness, the nobility — withered; and she, by grief, [withered] like a lotus by frost-water. || 410 ||
This is [an example] where the common property is undifferentiated.

children.text:
{jyotsneva nayanānandaḥ sureva madakāraṇam /
  prabhuteva samākṛṣṭasarvalokā nitambinī //411//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
Like moonlight, a delight to the eyes; like liquor, a cause of intoxication; like sovereignty, she attracts the whole world — that broad-hipped woman. || 411 ||

children.text:
ity bhinne ca tasmin ekasyaiva bahūpamānopādāne mālopamā /
yathottaramupameyasyopamānatve pūrvavadabhinnadharmatve
children.translated_text: Where the property is differentiated, and multiple standards of comparison (upamāna) are employed for a single subject (upameya) — that is mālā-upamā (garland-simile). When, successively, the subject of comparison becomes the standard of comparison, with the property undifferentiated as before:
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

His speech is like his intellect, his intellect is like his conduct, his conduct is like his fame — exceedingly pure, with a stream of hands agitated by the wave-like flow of incessant gold-giving, [at the banks of] the river of supplicants. || 412 ||

children.text:
{matiriva mūrtirmadhurā mūrtiriva sabhā prabhāvacitā /
  tasya sabheva jayaśrīḥ śakyā jetuṃ nṛpasya na pareṣām //413//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 223)
His form is sweet like his intellect; his court is resplendent like his form; his victory-glory is like his court — his alone, not that of other kings, can be conquered. || 413 ||

children.text: ityādikā raśanopamā ca na lakṣitā evaṃvidhavaicitryasahasrasaṃbhavāt

children.translated_text: and because of not transgressing the stated categories. || 90 ||
And the chain-simile (raśanopamā) and the like have not been [separately] defined — because of the possibility of thousands of such varieties of aesthetic beauty,
When one and the same [entity], within a single sentence, serves as both the standard of comparison and the subject of comparison — that is ananvaya (self-simile)...
Ananvaya is the absence of connection with another standard of comparison. Example:

children.text:
{na kevalaṃ bhāti nitāntakāntirnitambanī saiva nitambinīva /
  yāvadvilāsāyudhalāsyavāsāste tadvilāsā iva tadvilāsāḥ //414//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

Not only does that broad-hipped woman shine with exceedingly intense beauty, like a broad-hipped woman herself — but also, insofar as her coquetries are the weapons of a play of grace — her graces are like her very graces. || 414 ||
... the reversal [is called] upameyopamā (reverse simile) of the two. || Kpr-K_91 ||

children.text: tayoḥ upamānopameyayoḥ / parivṛttiḥ arthāt vākyadvaye / itaropamānavyavacchedaparā upameyenopamā iti upameyopamā / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: 'Of the two' — of the upamāna and the upameya. The reversal [is] understood as [occurring] in two sentences. [The simile that is] intent upon the exclusion of any other standard of comparison, [employing] the simile with the subject of comparison [as standard] — that is upameyopamā. Example:

children.text: {kamaleva matirmatiriva kamalā tanuriva vibhā vibheva tanuḥ /
children.translated_text: His intellect is like a lotus, and <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) is like his intellect; his body is like splendor, and splendor is like his body;

children.text: dharaṇīva dhṛtirdhṛtiriva dharaṇī satataṃ vibhāti bata yasya //415//
children.translated_text: the earth is like his fortitude, and his fortitude is like the earth — thus he always shines, indeed! || 415 ||
(<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 225)
The supposition (saṃbhāvanā), or rather utprekṣā (poetic fancy), is [the identification] of the given subject with an equal [entity];
'With an equal' — with a standard of comparison (upamāna). Example:

children.text:
{unmeṣaṃ yo mama na sahate jātivairī niśāyām
  indorindīvaradaladṛśā tasya saundaryadarpaḥ /
  nītiḥ śāntiṃ prasabhamanayā vaktrakāntyeti harṣāl
  lagnā manye lalitatanu te pādayoḥ padmalakṣmīḥ //416//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

He who, being the natural enemy of my bloom, cannot endure [it] at night — the arrogance of <s>Indu</s>'s (the moon's) beauty, by her of the blue-lotus-petal eyes — the moonlight of your face, O slender one, rushes to make peace with its radiance; I think the lotus-<s>Lakṣmī</s> has taken refuge at your feet, O graceful one! || 416 ||

children.text:
{limpatīva tamo 'ṅgāni varṣatīvāñjanaṃ nabhaḥ /
  asatpuruṣaseveva dṛṣṭirviphalatāṃ gatā //417//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śūdraka</s>'s <s>Mṛcchakaṭikā</s> 1.32)
It is as if darkness smears the limbs, as if the sky rains collyrium — vision has gone to futility, like the service of wicked men. || 417 ||
In the above and the like, the pervading and the rest are fancied as having the form of smearing and the like.

children.text: sasaṃdehastu bhedoktau tadanuktau ca saṃśayaḥ // MKpr-K_92 //
children.translated_text: But when there is doubt, with the statement of distinction [it is called] saṃdeha (doubt); without such statement, [it is called] saṃśaya (uncertainty). || Kpr-K_92 ||
With the statement of distinction, as in:

children.text:
{ayaṃ mārtaṇḍaḥ kiṃ sa khalu turagaiḥ saptabhiritaḥ
  kṛśānuḥ kiṃ sarvāḥ prasarati diśo naiṣa niyatam /
  kṛtāntaḥ kiṃ sākṣānmahiṣavahano 'sāviti ciraṃ
  samālokyājau tvāṃ vidadhati vikalpān pratibhaṭāḥ //418//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s>)

Is this the sun? — but he has seven horses. Is this fire? — he extends in all directions — no, that is not definite. Is this Death himself? — surely that one rides a buffalo — thus, gazing at you for a long time on the battlefield, the enemies make conjectures. || 418 ||

children.text:
bhedoktāvityanena na kevalamayaṃ niścayagarbho yāvanniścayānto 'pi saṃdehaḥ svīkrṭaḥ /
yathā
children.translated_text: By [the phrase] 'with the statement of distinction,' not only is doubt containing certainty [accepted], but also doubt ending in certainty is accepted. As in:

children.text:
{induḥ kiṃ kva kalaṅkaḥ sarasijametat kimambu kutra gatam /
  lalitasavilāsavacanairmukhamiti hariṇākṣi niścitaṃ parataḥ //419//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s>)

Is this the moon? — but where is the blemish? Is this a lotus? — but where has the water gone? — with graceful and playful words [the verdict is:] 'It is a face, O doe-eyed one' — certainty is established at the end. || 419 ||

children.text:
kiṃ tu niścayagarbha iva nātra niścayaḥ pratīyamāna iti upekṣito
bhaṭṭodbhaṭena / tadanuktau yathā
children.translated_text: However, this [type] — where certainty is cognized only as embedded [within doubt], rather than [being genuinely] cognized — was disregarded by <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s>. Without the statement of distinction, as in:

children.text:
{asyāḥ sargavidhau prajāpatirabhūccandro nu kāntipradaḥ
  śṛṅgāraikarasaḥ svayaṃ nu madano māso nu puṣpākaraḥ /
  vedābhyāsajaḍaḥ kathaṃ nu viṣayavyāvṛttakautūhalo
  nirmātuṃ prabhavenmanoharamidaṃ rūpaṃ purāṇo muniḥ //420//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 1.8)

Was <s>Prajāpati</s> the creator of her form? Or was the moon the bestower of [her] radiance? Or was <s>Madana</s> (Love) himself the sole essence of śṛṅgāra? Or was the flower-season the month [of her creation]? How indeed could the ancient sage, dullened by the study of the <s>Vedas</s>, with his curiosity turned away from sense-objects, have been capable of fashioning this enchanting form? || 420 ||
That is rūpaka (metaphor) — the non-difference between the standard of comparison and the subject of comparison.
Because of extreme similarity, [there is] non-difference between the two whose distinction is not denied.
When the entire subject is to be taught; [or when] a Vedic [rūpaka is] superimposed — || Kpr-K_93 ||

children.text: āropaviṣayā iva āropyamāṇāḥ yadā śabdopāttāḥ tadā samastāni vastūni viṣayosyeti samastavastuviṣayam / āropitā iti bahuvacanamavivakṣitam / yathā
children.translated_text: When the things being superimposed, as if they were the locus of superimposition, are conveyed by words, then all things are the locus of this [superimposition] — hence, 'having all things as its locus' (<s>samastavastuviṣaya</s>). The plural 'superimposed' is not intended [to indicate plurality]. For example:

children.text:
{jyotsnābhasmacchuraṇadhavalā bibhratī tārakāsthī-
  nyantardhānavyasanarasikā rātrikāpālikīyam /
  dvīpād dvīpaṃ bhramati dadhatī candramudrākapāle
  nyastaṃ siddhāñjanaparimalaṃ lāñchanasyacchalena //421//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{The night — a female ascetic of the skull-bearing (<s>kāpālika</s>) order — white with the gleaming of ashes of moonlight, wearing the stars as bones, delighting in the vice of disappearance, wanders from island to island, bearing the moon-marked skull-bowl in which is placed the fragrance of the <s>siddhāñjana</s> (magical collyrium), under the pretext of the [moon's] mark. //421//}

children.text: atra pādatraye, antardhānavyasanarasikatvamāropitadharma eveti rūpakaparigrahe sādhakamastītitatsaṃkarāśaṅkā na kāryā //93//
children.translated_text: Here, in three quarters [of the verse], the 'delight in the vice of disappearance' is indeed a superimposed property — this supports the classification as <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), so the suspicion of intermixture (<s>saṃkara</s>) should not be entertained. //93//
Those [<s>rūpakas</s>] are verbal (<s>śrauta</s>) and meaning-based (<s>ārtha</s>); where [the transformation occurs] in only a part, it is called <s>ekadeśavivartin</s> (partial transformation).

children.text: kevidāropyamāṇāḥ śabdo 'pāttāḥ kecidarthasāmarthyādavaseyāḥ ityekadeśavivartanāt ekadeśavivarti / yathā
children.translated_text: Some [superimposed properties] are conveyed by words, and some must be inferred from the power of the meaning — since the transformation [from the literal to the metaphorical] occurs only in one part, it is <s>ekadeśavivartin</s>. For example:

children.text:
{jassa raṇante_ura_e kare kuṇantassa maṇḍalaggala_aṃ /
  rasasaṃmuhī vi sahasā paramuhī ho_i ri_useṇā //422//}

children.translated_text: [In whose battle-inner chamber, when [he] makes the tip of the arc curve with the hand —
even the enemy army, though facing with passion, suddenly turns away!]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 980)
{In whose battle-<s>antaḥpura</s> (inner chamber), when [the hero] makes the tip of the arc curve with his hand — even the enemy army, though facing him with passion, suddenly turns away! //422//}

children.text: atra raṇasyāntaḥpuratvamāropyamāṇaṃ śabdo 'pāttam maṇḍalāgralatāyāḥ nāyikātvam ripusenāyāśca pratināyikātvam arthasāmarthyādavasīyate iti ekadeśe viśeṣeṇa vartanādekadeśavivarti /
children.translated_text: Here, the 'inner chamber' status of the battle is conveyed by words as something superimposed; but the 'heroine' status of the arc-tip and the 'rival woman' status of the enemy army are inferred from the power of the meaning — thus, since the [metaphorical] operation occurs in one part with particular [detail], it is <s>ekadeśavivartin</s>.
This [type] has component parts (<s>sāṅga</s>) ...
[It is] with components, having the twofold division stated [above].
... but the componentless (<s>niraṅga</s>) one is pure ...
For example:

children.text:
{kuraṅgīvāṅgāni stimitayati gītadhvaniṣu yat
  sakhīṃ kāntodantaṃ śrutamapi punaḥ praśnayati yat /
  anidraṃ yaccāntaḥ svapiti tadaho vedmyabhinavāṃ
  pravṛtto 'syāḥ sektuṃ hṛdi manasijaḥ premalatikām //423//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s>; <s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Abhinavabhāratī</s>)

{That she freezes her limbs like a doe when hearing the sound of song; that she asks her friend again about a report of her lover already heard; that she sleeps without sleep within — ah, I know: the god of love has begun to water a fresh vine of love in her heart! //423//}
... but the garland (<s>mālā</s>) form is as before. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_94 //
As in garland-simile (<s>mālopamā</s>), many [properties] are superimposed upon a single [subject]. For example:

children.text:
{saundaryasya taraṅgiṇī taruṇimotkarṣasya harṣodgamaḥ
  kānteḥ kārmaṇakarma narmarahasāmullāsanāvāsabhūḥ /
  vidyā vakragirāṃ vidheranavadhiprāvīṇyasākṣātkriyā
  vāṇāḥ pañcaśilīmukhasya lalanācūḍāmaṇiḥ sā priyā //424//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{A river of beauty, a surge of joy at the height of youth, the magical charm of loveliness, the dwelling-place for the unfolding of the secret of amorous play, the art of crooked speech of the Creator, the direct realization of his unlimited skill, the five arrows of the flower-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>) — that beloved is the crest-jewel of women! //424//}
That in which the superimposition of the other [subject] has a fixed means of superimposition —

children.text: tatparaṃparitaṃ śliṣṭe vācake bhedabhāji vā // MKpr-K_95 //
children.translated_text: that [operates] through a chain (<s>paraṃparita</s>), through a <s>śliṣṭa</s> (equivocal) indicator, or through a word carrying a different sense (<s>bhedabhāj</s>). // <s>MKpr-K</s>_95 //
For example:

children.text:
{vidvanmānasahaṃsa vairikamalāsaṃkocadīptadyute
  durgāmārgaṇanīlalohita samitsvīkāravaiśvānara /
  satyaprītividhānadakṣa vijayaprāgbhāvabhīma prabho
  sāmrājyaṃ varavīra vatsaraśataṃ vairiñcamuccaiḥ kriyāḥ //425//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{O <s>haṃsa</s> (swan) of the lake of the wise! O <s>Nīlalohita</s> (<s>Śiva</s> / blue-and-red one) whose brilliance causes the closing of the lotus of the enemy! O <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (universal fire) of the acceptance of the assembly of sticks (<s>samit</s>/fuel)! O <s>Bhīma</s> (Terrible One) who is the precedent of victory! O lord, by whose skill the bestowal of true affection [is accomplished] — may you perform the <s>Brahmā</s>-empire for a hundred years with sublime rites! //425//}

children.text:
atra mānasameva mānasam kamalāyāḥ saṃkoca eva kamalānāmasaṃkocaḥ durgāṇāmamārgaṇameva durgāyāḥ mārgaṇam samitāṃ svīkāra eva samidhāṃ svīkāraḥ satye pratītireva satyāmaprītiḥ vijayaḥ paraparābhava eva vijayorjunaḥ evamāropaṇanimitto haṃsāderāropaḥ /
yadyapi śabdārthālaṅkāro 'yamityuktaṃ vakṣyate ca tathāpi prasiddhyanurodhādatroktaḥ / ekadeśavivarti hīdamanyairabhidhīyate //
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>mānasa</s>' (of the mind) is itself '<s>Mānasa</s>' (the lake); the closing of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>/lotus) is itself the non-closing of lotuses; the non-seeking of <s>Durgā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) is itself the seeking of the inaccessible; the acceptance of <s>samit</s> (assemblies) is itself the acceptance of <s>samidh</s> (fuel-sticks); the conviction in <s>satya</s> (truth) is itself the non-affection for <s>Satyā</s> (a name); <s>vijaya</s> (victory), the defeat of the other, is itself <s>Vijaya</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>). Thus, the superimposition of swan and the rest is occasioned by [the equivocality of] the superimposition. Although this is called a figure of both word and meaning, and will be so stated, it is mentioned here in deference to [its] well-known [classification]. For this is indeed called <s>ekadeśavivartin</s> by others.
Through a word carrying a different sense (<s>bhedabhāj</s>) — for example:

children.text:
{ālānaṃ jayakuñjarasya dṛṣadāṃ seturvipadvāridheḥ
  pūrvādriḥ karavālacaṇḍamahaso līlopadhānaṃ śriyaḥ /
  saṃgrāmāmṛtasāgarapramathanakrīḍāvidhau mandaro
  rājan rājati vīravairivanitāvaidhavyadaste bhujaḥ //426//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Mahimabhaṭṭa</s>'s <s>Vyaktiviveka</s>)

{The tethering-post of the elephant of victory, the bridge of stones over the ocean of calamity, the eastern mountain of the fierce-sworded sun, the plaything-cushion of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), the <s>Mandara</s> mountain for the churning-sport of the ocean of nectar of battle — O king, your arm shines forth, the [instrument of] widowhood for the wives of heroic enemies! //426//}

children.text: atra jayāderbhinnaśabdavācyasya kuñjaratvādyārope bhujasya ālānatvādyāropo yujyate /
children.translated_text: Here, when elephant-hood and the like — denoted by different words such as '<s>vijaya</s>' (victory) and the like — are superimposed, the superimposition of tethering-post status and the like onto the arm is justified.
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{O god, illuminator of the three worlds with extraordinary, great light — you, the jewel freed from the conch-like noble lineage — by whom are you not praised? //427//}

children.text:
{niravadhi ca nirāśrayaṃ ca yasya sthitamanivartitakautukaprapñcam /
  prathama iha bhavān sa kūrmamūrtirjayati caturdaśalokavallikandaḥ //428//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vāmana</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 3.4.32)

{Yours, whose situation is without limit and without support, whose display of unending wonder is unsurpassed — you are the first, you of the Tortoise form, the root-bulb of the creeper of the fourteen worlds, you triumph! //428//}
And thus, even a non-garland form should be seen as involving a chain.

children.text:
{kisalayakarairlatānāṃ karakamalaiḥ kāmināṃ mano jayati /
  nalinīnāṃ kamalamukhaiḥ mukhendubhiryoṣitāṃ madanaḥ //429//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 8.50)

{With the tender-shoot hands of creepers, with the lotus-hands of passionate women, with the lotus-faces of lotus-ponds, and with the moon-faces of young women — <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) conquers the mind! //429//}

children.text: ityādi raśanārūpakaṃ na vaicitryavaditi na lakṣitam //95//
children.translated_text: And so forth — the garland-<s>rūpaka</s> (garland-metaphor), since it lacks variety, has not been identified [as a separate type]. //95//
When the subject at hand is denied and something else is established — that is <s>apahnutī</s> (concealment/denial).

children.text: upameyam asatyaṃ kṛtvopamānaṃ satyatayā yat sthāpyate sā tu apahnutiḥ udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: <s>Apahnutī</s> is when the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) is made out to be unreal and the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) is established as real. Example:

children.text:
{avāptaḥ prāgalbhyaṃ pariṇatarucaḥ śailatanaye
  kalaṅko naivāyaṃ vilasati śaśāṅkasya vapuṣi /
  amuṣyeyaṃ manye vigaladamṛtasyandaśiśire
  ratiśrāntā śete rajaniramaṇī gāḍhamurasi //430//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{O daughter of the mountain! This which gleams upon the body of the moon is not at all a blemish that has gained boldness from mature beauty — I think this is the wife of Night, exhausted from lovemaking, sleeping deeply upon the breast of her lover, cool with dripping nectar-streams. //430//}
Or in this manner:

children.text:
{bata sakhi kiyadetat paśya vairaṃ smarasya
  priyavirahakṛśesmin rāgiloke tathā hi /
  upavanasahakārodbhāsibhṛṅgacchalena
  prativiśikhamanenoṭṭaṅkitaṃ kālakūṭam //431//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Alas, friend, see how great is the enmity of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love) — indeed, against this passion-maddened world, emaciated by the separation from the beloved — under the pretext of bees gleaming on the <s>sahakāra</s> (mango) trees of the garden, arrow by arrow he has affixed deadly <s>kālakūṭa</s> (poison)! //431//}

children.text: atra hi na sabhṛṅgāṇi sahakārāṇi api tu sakālakūṭā śarā iti pratītiḥ / evaṃ vā
