children.translated_text: Here, the understanding is: these are not <s>sahakāras</s> with bees, but rather arrows loaded with <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison. Or in this way:

children.text:
{amuṣmiṃllāvaṇyāmṛtasarasi nūnaṃ mṛgadṛśaḥ
  smaraḥ śarvapluṣṭaḥ pṛthujaghanabhāge nipatitaḥ /
  yadaṅgāṅgāraṇāṃ prathamapiśunā nābhikuhare
  śikhā dhūmasyeyaṃ pariṇaṃmati romāvalivapuḥ //432//}
(Vallabhadeva's Subhāṣitāvali, Bombay Sankrit and Prakrit Series. 1558)
children.translated_text: (<s>Vallabhadeva</s>'s <s>Subhāṣitāvali</s>, Bombay Sanskrit and Prakrit Series 1558)

{Surely, <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), burnt by <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), has fallen into the lake of the nectar of charm of this doe-eyed woman, at the region of her ample buttocks — for the flame of smoke whose first sign is in the navel-hollow, this line of body-hair, is the transformation of [his] bodily embers. //432//}
Here, the understanding is: this is not a line of body-hair but a flame of smoke.
Thus this [<s>apahnutī</s>] should be inferred through other modes as well.

children.text: śleṣaḥ sa vākya ekasmin yatrānekārthatā bhavet // MKpr-K_96 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) is where, in a single sentence, there is multiplicity of meaning. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_96 //

children.text: ekārthapratipādakānāmeva śabdānāṃ yatrāneko 'rthaḥ sa śleṣaḥ / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa</s> is where words that convey a single meaning [each] have multiple meanings [simultaneously]. Example:

children.text:
{udayamayate diṅmālinyaṃ nirākurutetarāṃ
  nayati nidhanaṃ nidrāmudrāṃ pravartayati kriyāḥ /
  racayatitarāṃ svairācārapravartanakartanaṃ
  bata bata lasattejaḥpuñjo vibhāti vibhākaraḥ //433//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 237)

{He brings about the rise; he removes the stain (<s>mālinyam</s> / impurity) of the quarters; he brings to an end the seal of slumber; he sets actions into motion; he effects the cutting of rampant wayward conduct — alas, alas, the mass of resplendent radiance, the <s>vibhākara</s> (sun / illuminator), shines forth! //433//}
Here, because denotation is unrestricted, both the sun and the king are the expressed [meanings]. //96//
<s>Parokti</s> (indirect statement) [operates] through distinguishing [features] that are equivocal; <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) ...

children.text: prakṛtārthapratipādakavākyena śliṣṭaviśeṣaṇamāhātmyāt na tu viśeṣyasya sāmarthyādapi yat aprakṛtasyārthasyābhidhānam sā samāsena saṃkṣepeṇārthadvayakathanāt samāsoktiḥ / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: <s>Samāsokti</s> is [the figure] where, through a sentence that conveys the meaning of the subject at hand, by the power of the equivocal qualifiers — not by the power of the qualified noun itself — a meaning that is not at hand is also denoted. [It is called <s>samāsokti</s>] because it states two meanings in condensed form (<s>samāsa</s>). Example:

children.text:
{lahiūṇa tujjha bāhupphaṃsaṃ jīe sa ko vi ullāso /
  jaalacchī tuba virahe ṇa hujjalā dubbalā ṇaṃ sā //434//}

children.translated_text: [Having obtained the touch of your arms, she had some kind of brilliance —

children.text: jayalakṣmīstava virahe na khalūjjvalā durbalā nanu sā //]
children.translated_text: <s>Jayalakṣmī</s> (the goddess of victory), in separation from you, is no longer radiant, [but] is weak indeed!]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s>, Nirnaya Sagar Press 428)

{Having obtained the touch of your arms, she had some kind of brilliance — but <s>Jayalakṣmī</s> (the goddess of victory / your victorious fortune), in separation from you, is no longer radiant, [but] is weak indeed! //434//}
Here, the word '<s>Jayalakṣmī</s>' does not function solely as a designation for a beloved woman.
... <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration) —
is [that figure] where a non-existent connection of things serves to construct a comparison. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_97 //
<s>Nidarśanā</s> is the producing of an illustration. Example:

children.text:
{kva sūryaprabhāvo vaṃśaḥ kva cālpaviṣayā matiḥ /
  titīrṣurdustaraṃ mohāduḍupenāsmi sāgaram //435//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 1.2)
{Where is the lineage of <s>Sūrya</s>'s power, and where is my intellect of limited scope? Out of delusion, I am attempting to cross the uncrossable ocean in a raft! //435//}

children.text: atra uḍupena sāgarataraṇamiva manmatyā sūryavaṃśavarṇanamityupamāyāṃ paryavasyati /
children.translated_text: Here, the crossing of the ocean by a raft is [analogous to] my description of the solar dynasty with my intellect — thus it culminates in a comparison.
Or alternatively:

children.text:
{udayati vitatordhvaraśmirajjāvahimarucau himadhāmni yāti cāstam /
  vahati girirayaṃ vilambighaṇṭādvayaparivāritavāraṇendralīlām //436//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Māgha</s>'s <s>Śiśupālavadha</s>, Nirnaya Sagar Press 4.20)

{When the cold-rayed sun rises with its extended upward ray-ropes, and the cool-rayed moon sets — this mountain carries on the sport of a lordly elephant garlanded by a pair of hanging bells. //436//}

children.text: atra kathmanyasya līlāmanyo vahatīti tatsadṛśīmityupamāyāṃ paryavasānam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'how does one carry the sport of another? — in a manner resembling it' — thus the culmination is in comparison.

children.text:
{dorbhyāṃ titīrṣati taraṅgavatībhujaṅgam
  ādātumicchati kare hariṇāṅkabimbam /
  meruṃlilaṅghayiṣati dhruvameṣa deva
  yaste guṇān gaditumudyamamādadhati //437//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 241)

{He seeks to cross the serpent of the river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>) with his arms; he wishes to seize the disk of the hare-marked [moon] in his hand; he will surely leap over <s>Meru</s> — O god, this one who undertakes the effort to narrate your qualities! //437//}
In such examples, this [<s>nidarśanā</s>] should also be seen in garland form. //97//
The statement of the connection of each [effect] with its own [specific] cause; and another [type] through action alone —

children.text: kriyayaiva svasvarūpasvakāraṇayoḥ saṃbandho yadavagamyate sā aparā nidarśanā / yathā
children.translated_text: The other <s>nidarśanā</s> is that where the connection of each thing's own form with its own cause is understood through action alone. For example:

children.text:
{unnataṃ padamavāpya yo laghuhelayaiva patediti bruvan /
  śailaśekharagato dṛṣatkaṇaścārumārutadhutaḥ patatyadhaḥ //438//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 242)
{Having attained a lofty position, one who would fall through sheer lightness — thus speaking, a pebble atop the mountain-peak, shaken by the charming wind, falls downward. //438//}

children.text: atra pātakriyayā patanasya lāghave sati unnatapadaprāptirūpasya ca saṃbandhaḥ khyāpyate //
children.translated_text: Here, through the action of falling, the connection between the attainment of a lofty position (which is the form [of the cause]) and lightness (which is [the condition for] falling) is made known.

children.text: aprastutapraśaṃsā yā sā saiva prastutāśrayā // MKpr-K_98 //
children.translated_text: <s>Aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) — it is that which rests on the relevant subject. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_98 //
<s>Aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> is the intimation of the relevant subject through the description of the irrelevant. //98//

children.text: kārye nimitte sāmānye viśeṣe prastute sati /
children.translated_text: When the effect, the cause, the general, the particular, or the subject at hand [is presented],

children.text: tadanyasya vacastulye tulyasyeti ca pañcadhā // MKpr-K_99 //
children.translated_text: [it intimates] another of those [categories]; also through verbal equivalence, and through equivalence [of the situations] — thus fivefold. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_99 //
'Another of those' means [another] from among cause, effect, and so forth. Examples in order:

children.text:
{yātā kiṃ na milanti sundari punaścintā tvayā matkṛte
  no kāryā nitarāṃ kṛśāsi kathayatyevaṃ sabāṣpe mayi /
  lajjāmantharatārakeṇa nipatatpītāśruṇā cakṣuṣā
  dṛṣṭvā māṃ hasitena bhāvimaraṇotsāhastayā sūcitaḥ //439//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 10)

{You have gone — will you not return again, O beautiful one? Do not worry on my account — you have grown exceedingly thin' — as he speaks thus with tears, she, with eyes dropping tear-stained glances of shy, languid pupils, having beheld me, with a smile indicated her determination to die [rather than depart]. //439//}

children.text: atra prasthānātkimiti nivṛtto 'sīti kārye pṛṣṭe kāraṇamabhihitam /
children.translated_text: Here, when the effect is asked about — 'why have you returned from your departure?' — the cause is stated [instead].

children.text:
{rājanrājasutā na pāṭhayati māṃ devyo 'pi tūṣṇīṃ sthitāḥ
  kubje bhojaya māṃ kumārasacivairnādyāpi kiṃ bhujyate /
  itthaṃ nātha śukastavāribhavane muktodhvagaiḥ pañjarāc
  citrasthānavalokya śūnyavalabhāvekaikamābhāṣate //440//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{O king, the princess does not give me lessons; the queens too stand silent; O hunchback, feed me! 'Has the prince's retinue not yet eaten today?' — Thus, O lord, your parrot, released upward from the cage in the enemy's palace, beholding the empty perches in the painted chamber, addresses each one in turn. //440//}

children.text: atra prasthānodyataṃ bhavantaṃ jñātvā sahasaiva tvadarayaḥ palāyya gatāḥ iti kāraṇe prastute kāryamuktam /
children.translated_text: Here, when the cause is the subject at hand — 'knowing you to be intent on departure, your enemies have suddenly fled' — the effect is stated.

children.text:
{etattasya mukhātkiyat kamalinīpatre kaṇaṃ vāriṇo
  yanmuktāmaṇirityamaṃsta sa jaḍaḥśṛṇvanyadasmādapi /
  aṅgulyagralaghukriyāpravilayinyādīyamāne śanaiḥ
  kutroḍḍīya gato mametyanudinaṃ nidrāti nāntaḥśucā //441//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhallaṭaśataka</s> 94)

{This — how much is this from his mouth? — a drop of water on a lotus leaf — which that fool thought was a pearl, hearing from this one [an even more fleeting thing]: when something that dissolves through the light action of a fingertip was being slowly taken away — 'Where has it flown to? — it was mine!' — he grieves day after day, not sleeping from his inner sorrow. //441//}

children.text: atrāsthāne jaḍānāṃ mamatvasaṃbhāvanā bhavatīti sāmānye prastute viśeṣaḥ kathitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, when the general [principle] is the subject at hand — 'the attachment of fools arises in inappropriate places' — the particular [instance] is narrated.

children.text:
{suhṛdvadhūbāṣpajalapramārjanaṃ karoti vairapratiyātanena yaḥ /
  sa eva pūjyaḥ sa pumānsa nītimānsujīvitaṃ tasya sa bhājanaṃ śriyaḥ //442//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Udbhaṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasārasaṅgraha</s>)

{He who wipes the tear-water from the eyes of his friend's wife through retribution against the enemy — he alone is worthy of honor, he is a true man, he is a master of policy; his is a life well-lived; he is a vessel of fortune! //442//}

children.text: atra 'kṛṣṇaṃ nihatya narakāsuravadhūnāṃ yadi duḥkham praśamayasi tat tvameva ślāghyaḥ'; iti viśeṣe prakṛte sāmānyamabhihitam / tuye prastute tulyābhidhāne trayaḥ prakārāḥ / śleṣaḥ samāsoktiḥ sādṛśyamātraṃ vā tulyāt tulyasya hyākṣepe hetuḥ / krameṇodāharaṇam --
children.translated_text: Here, 'If, having slain <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, you pacify the grief of the wives of <s>Narakāsura</s>, then you alone are praiseworthy' — when a particular [proposition] is the subject, the general has been stated. When a comparable [proposition] is the subject, there are three kinds of comparable statement: <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre), <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), or mere similarity (<s>sādṛśyamātra</s>) — for similarity is the cause of the imputation from one comparable thing to another. Examples in order —

children.text:
{puṃstvādapi pravicalet yadi yadyadho 'pi
  yāyād yadi praṇayane na mahānapi syāt /
  abhyuddharettadapi viśvamitīdṛśīyaṃ
  kenāpi dik orakaṭitā puruṣottamena //443//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhallaṭaśataka</s> 79)

{Even if he were to swerve from manliness, even if he were to descend below, even if he were not to be great in winning affection — he would still elevate this entire universe: such is the direction laid out by a certain <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person / the city Puruṣottama). //443//}

children.text:
{yeñāsyabhyuditena candra gamitaḥ klāntiṃ ravau tatra te
  yujyeta pratikartumeva na punastasyaiva pādagrahaḥ /
  kṣīṇenaitadanuṣṭhitaṃ yadi tataḥ kiṃ lajjase no manāg
  astvevaṃ jaḍadhāmatā tu bhavato yad vyomni visphūrjase //444//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{O Moon, when weariness was removed from the sun by the rising of your face, it would be fitting for you to reciprocate that very [favor] — not to grovel at his feet. If you have done this while waning, then why are you not in the least ashamed? So be it — but it is mere dull luminosity that you blaze forth in the sky! //444//}

children.text:
{ādāya vāri paritaḥ saritāṃ mukhebhyaḥ
  kiṃ tāvadarjitamanena durarṇavena /
  kṣārīkṛtaṃ ca vaḍavādahane hutaṃ ca
  pātālakukṣikuhare viniveśitaṃ ca //445//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Having taken water from the mouths of rivers on all sides — what has this wretched ocean earned [thereby]? It has been made brackish, fed to the submarine fire (<s>vaḍavāgni</s>), and deposited in the cavity of the netherworld's belly! //445//}

children.text: iyaṃ ca kācit vācye pratīyamānārthānadhyāropeṇaiva bhavati / yathā
children.translated_text: And this [figure], in some cases, arises in relation to the expressed meaning through the non-superimposition of the cognized meaning alone. As follows:

children.text:
{abdherambhaḥ sthagitabhuvanābhogapātālakukṣeḥ
  potopāyā iha hi bahavo laṅghane 'pi kṣamante /
  āho riktaḥ kathamapi bhavedeṣa daivāt tadānīṃ
  ko nāma syādavaṭakuharālokane 'pyasya kalpaḥ //446//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{The waters of the ocean, whose expanse conceals the worlds and the cavity of the netherworld — indeed, there are many boat-like means for crossing it. But if by fate it were somehow emptied, who indeed would be capable even of beholding the cavity of the abyss? //446//}
In some cases, [it arises] through superimposition alone. As follows:

children.text:
{kastvaṃ bhoḥ kathayāmi daivahatakaṃ māṃ viddhi śākhoṭakaṃ
  vairāgyādiva vakṣi sādhu viditaṃ kasmādidaṃ kathyate /
  vāmenātra vaṭastamadhvagajanaḥ sarvātmanā sevate
  na cchāyāpi paropakārakaraṇe mārgasthitasyāpi me//447//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s> 3.51)

{'Who are you, sir?' 'Know me as a wretched <s>śākhoṭaka</s> tree, struck by fate.' 'You speak as if from dispassion!' 'Very well — it is known. Why is this said?' 'To its left here is a fig tree — travelers serve it with all their being, yet not even the shade of me, standing on the road, serves for the benefit of others.' //447//}
In some cases, [it arises] through superimposition in certain parts. As follows:

children.text:
{so 'pūrvo rasanāviparyayavidhiḥ tat karṇayoścāpalaṃ
  dṛṣṭiḥ sā madavismṛtasvaparadik kiṃ bhūyasoktena vā /
  sarvaṃ vismṛtavānasi bhramara he yadvāraṇo 'dyāpyasau
  antaḥśūnyakaro niṣevyata iti bhrātaḥ ka eṣa grahaḥ //448//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhallaṭaśataka</s> 18)

{That unprecedented reversal of the tongue, that restlessness of the ears, that gaze which in intoxication has forgotten the distinction of one's own and others' directions — but what more need be said? O bee, you have forgotten everything! — 'But, friend, even today that elephant is served with empty trunk — what kind of seizure is this?' //448//}

children.text: atra rasanāvaparyāsaḥ śūnyakartvaṃ ca bhramarasyāsevane na hetuḥ karṇacāpalaṃ tu hetuḥ madaḥ pratyuta sevate nimittam //99//
children.translated_text: Here, the reversal of the tongue and the empty-trunkedness are not reasons for the bee's non-attendance; the restlessness of the ears is indeed a reason; and intoxication is rather the occasion for attendance. //99//
But when the subject is absorbed (<s>nigīrya</s>) and resolved into another,

children.text: prastutasya yadanyatvaṃ yadyarthoktau ca kalpanam // MKpr-K_100 //
children.translated_text: when the subject assumes otherness, and when in a factual statement there is poetic invention — // <s>MKpr-K</s>_100 //
and when there is a reversal of the sequence of cause and effect — this should be known as <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) ...
When the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) that is internally absorbed by the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) is resolved [into it] — that is one [type]. As follows:

children.text:
{kamalamanambhasi kamale ca kubalaye tāni kanakalatikāyām /
  sā ca sukumārasubhagetyutpātaparaṃparā keyam //449//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)
{A lotus [rests] upon water, and upon the lotus a blue water-lily, and those upon a golden creeper — and she is delicate and beautiful — what chain of portents is this? //449//}

children.text: atra mukhādi kamalādirūpatayādhyavasitam / yacca tadevānyatvenādhyavasīyate sā aparā / yathā
children.translated_text: Here, the face and the like are resolved as having the form of a lotus and so forth. And when that very [subject] is resolved as something entirely other — that is another [type]. As follows:

children.text:
{aṇṇaṃ laḍahattaṇa_aṃ aṇṇā vi_a kā vi vattaṇacchā_ā /
  sāmā sāmaṇṇapa_āva_iṇo rehacci_a ṇa ho_i //450//}

children.translated_text: [Her delicacy is something else, and her complexion's hue is yet another thing;

children.text: śyāmā sāmānyaprajāpateḥ rekṣaiva ca na bhavati //]
children.translated_text: the dark one is simply not a replica of the common Creator (<s>Prajāpati</s>). //]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 969)
{Her delicacy is something else, her complexion's hue is something else again —
(That is, [when there is invention of] an impossible meaning) — that is the third [type]. As follows:
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{If on a full-moon night the body of the nectar-rayed [moon] were spotless, then her face would attain the humiliation of being equaled [by it]. //451//}

children.text: kāraṇasya śīghrakāritāṃ vaktuṃ kāryasya pūrvamuktau caturthī / yathā
children.translated_text: When, in order to express the swiftness of the cause's operation, the effect is stated first — that is the fourth [type]. As follows:

children.text:
{hṛdayamadhiṣṭhitamādau mālatyāḥ kusumacāpabāṇena /
  caramaṃ ramaṇīvallabha locanaviṣayaṃ tvayā bhajatā //452//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Dāmodaragupta</s>'s <s>Kuṭṭanīmata</s> 96)
{The heart of <s>Mālatī</s> was first pierced by the flower-bow arrow; and subsequently, O lord of the beloved, it entered the range of your eyes. //452//}
... but that [figure] is <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-example simile). // <s>MKpr-K</s>_101 //
When a common property of two [things] resides in two sentences,

children.text: sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ upameyavākye upamānavākye ca kathitapadasya duṣṭatayābhihitatvāt śabdabhedena yat upādīyate sā vastūno vākyārthasyopamānatvāt prativastūpamā / yathā
children.translated_text: a common quality is mentioned in the <s>upameya</s> (comparandum) sentence and in the <s>upamāna</s> (comparans) sentence; since stating it with the same word would be faulty, it is taken up with a different word — because the subject-matter at the sentence-meaning level serves as the standard of comparison, this is <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-example simile). As follows:

children.text:
{devībhāvaṃ gamitā parivārapadaṃ kathaṃ bhajatveṣā /
  na khalu paribhogayogyaṃ daivatarūpāṅkitaṃ ratnam //453//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vāmana</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 4.2.4)

{She has been elevated to the status of a deity — how can she assume the position of an attendant? Indeed, a gem that has been stamped with the form of a divinity is no longer fit for enjoyment. //453//}

children.text:
{yadi dahatyanalo 'tra kimadbhutaṃ yadi ca gauravamadriṣu kiṃ tataḥ /
  lavaṇamambu sadaiva mahodadheḥ prakṛtireva satāmaviṣāditā //454[=272]//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ānandavardhana</s>'s <s>Deviśataka</s>)

{If fire burns here, what is surprising? And if there is weightiness in mountains, what of it? The water of the great ocean is always saline — indeed, the nature of the virtuous is to be undespairing. //454[=272]//}
Such and similar [examples] should be understood as chain-<s>prativastūpamā</s> (<s>mālāprativastūpamā</s>). The same should be applied in other cases as well. //
<s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration) is again the reflection of all of these. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_102 //

children.text: eteṣāṃ sādhāraṇadharmādīnāṃ dṛṣṭo 'nto niścayo yatra sa dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where the common property and the like of these [elements] has a settled conclusion (<s>dṛṣṭa anta</s>) — that is <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration).

children.text:
{tvayi dṛṣṭa eva tasyā nirvāti mano manobhavajvalitam /
  āloke hi himāṃśorvikasati kusumaṃ kumudvatyāḥ //455//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 251)
{At the very sight of you, her mind, burning with love, is extinguished. For indeed, at the light of the cool-rayed [moon], the flower of the <s>kumudvatī</s> (night-lotus plant) blossoms. //455//}
This is [illustration] through similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>). Through dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>):

children.text:
{tavāhave sāhasakarmaśarmaṇaḥ karaṃ kṛpāṇāntikamāninīṣataḥ /
  bhaṭaḥ pareṣāṃ viśarārutāmaguḥ dadhatyavāte sthiratāṃ hi pāṃsavaḥ //456//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{The warriors of the enemies, hearing the fearsome sounds of your hand — daring in bold battle-deeds — reaching toward the sword, turned to flee. Indeed, dust settles only when there is no wind. //456//}
When a single occurrence of a property belonging to the subject and the non-subject

children.text: saiva kriyāsu bahvīṣu kārakasyeti dīpakam // MKpr-K_103 //
children.translated_text: is the same across many actions or agents — that is <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination). // <s>MKpr-K</s>_103 //

children.text: prākaraṇikāprākaraṇikānām arthāt upamānopameyānāṃ dharmaḥ kriyādiḥ ekavārameva yat upādīyate tat ekasthasyaiva samastavākyadīpanād dīpakam / yathā
children.translated_text: Of those that are contextual (<s>prākaraṇika</s>) and those that are non-contextual (<s>aprākaraṇika</s>) — that is, of the <s>upamāna</s> (comparans) and <s>upameya</s> (comparandum) — the property, namely action and the like, is taken up only once; since it illuminates all the sentences from a single locus, it is <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination). As follows:

children.text:
{kivaṇāṇaṃ dhaṇaṃ ṇāgāṇaṃ phaṇamaṇī keśarā_iṃ sīhāṇaṃ /
  kulabāli_āṇaṃ tthaṇa_ā kutto chippanti amu_āṇaṃ //457//}

children.translated_text: [Of misers, wealth; of serpents, the hood-jewel; the mane of lions;
the breasts of well-born maidens — how can they be touched by the dead? //]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s>, Nirnaya Sagar Press, 976)
{Of misers, wealth; of serpents, the crest-jewel; of lions, the mane;

children.text: kārakasya ca bahvīṣu kriyāsu sakṛdvṛttidīrpakam / yathā
children.translated_text: And <s>dīpaka</s> where a single agent occurs once across many actions. As follows:

children.text:
{svidya[t]i kūṇati vellati vicalati nimiṣati vilokayati tiryak /
  antarnandati cumbatumicchati navapariṇayā vadhūḥ śayane //458//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Subhāṣitaratnabhāṇḍāgāra</s> 317/3)
{She perspires, she squints, she sways, she trembles, she blinks, she glances sideways — inwardly she rejoices, she desires to kiss — the newly-wed bride upon the bed. //458//}
<s>Mālādīpaka</s> (chain-illumination) is the first, and the latter enhances the former;

children.text: pūrveṇa pūrveṇa vastunā uttaramuttaraṃ cedupakriyate tat mālādīpakam / yathā
children.translated_text: When each preceding thing enriches the next succeeding thing — that is <s>mālādīpaka</s> (chain-illumination). As follows:

children.text:
{saṃgrāmāṅgaṇamāgatena bhavatā cāpe samāropite
  devākraṇaya yena yena sahasā yadyatsamāsāditam /
  kodaṇḍena śarāḥ śarairariśirastenāpi bhūmaṇḍalaṃ
  tena tvaṃ bhavatā ca kīrtiratulā kīrtyā ca lokatrayam //459//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{When you came to the battle-arena and strung the bow — O gods, marvel! — whatever was instantly seized: by the bow, arrows; by the arrows, the heads of enemies; by those [heads], the earth; by the earth, you; by you, incomparable fame; and by fame, the three worlds! //459//}
When a single property applies to fixed [members] — that is <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction). // <s>MKpr-K</s>_104 //
Of fixed members — either only contextual (<s>prākaraṇika</s>) ones or only non-contextual (<s>aprākaraṇika</s>) ones. Examples in order —

children.text:
{pāṇḍu kṣāmaṃ vadanaṃ hṛdayaṃ sarasaṃ tavālasaṃ ca vapuḥ /
  āvedayati nitāntaṃ kṣetriyarogaṃ sakhi hṛdantaḥ //460//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s>)
{Pale and emaciated is the face, moist is the heart, and languid is the body — O friend, the inner heart fully reveals a disease of the countryside (<s>kṣetriyaroga</s>)! //460//}
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{The night-lily, lotus, and blue water-lily — before the gracefully playful eyes, what [chance have they]? Nectar, the nectar-rayed [moon], the water-born [lotus] — they are all defeated at a single step by your face. //461//}
The <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast/distinction) of another from the <s>upamāna</s> and the rest — that itself is it.
The <s>vyatireka</s> (distinction) of another — namely the <s>upameya</s> (comparandum) — is [its] superiority.

children.text:
{kṣīṇaḥ kṣīṇo 'pi śaśī bhūyo bhūyo vivardhate satyam /
  virama prasīda sundari yauvanamanivarti yātaṃ tu //462//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Amaruśataka</s>)
{The moon, though it wanes and wanes, truly waxes again and again. Cease, be appeased, O beautiful one — but youth, once departed, does not return. //462//}
That is apt. Here, the superiority over the [qualities] that have departed with youth is indeed what is intended.
When, regarding the cause of distinction, three [varieties] of stated and unstated are presented in the context of similarity — // <s>MKpr-K</s>_105 //
and when [comparison] is conveyed by word and meaning, and when imputed, and with <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre) — likewise thrice-eight [= twenty-four varieties] that is.

children.text: vyatirekasya hetuḥ upameyagatamutkarṣanimittam / upamānagatamapakarṣakāraṇam / tayordvayoruktiḥ, ekatarasya dvayorvā anuktirityanuktitrayam / etadbhedacatuṣṭayamupamānopameyabhāve śabdena pratipādite ārthena ca krameṇoktāścatvāra eva bhedāḥ / ākṣipte caupamye tāvanta eva / evaṃ dvādaśa // ete śleṣe 'pi bhavantīti caturviśatirbhedāḥ / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: The cause of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) is: the reason for the superiority located in the <s>upameya</s> (comparandum), and the reason for the inferiority located in the <s>upamāna</s> (comparans). The statement of both, or the non-statement of one or of both — [these constitute] the three [varieties] of non-statement. This fourfold division, when the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation is conveyed by word and by meaning, [gives] four varieties each in sequence. When comparison is imputed, equally many. Thus twelve. These also occur with <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre), making twenty-four varieties. Examples in order —
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{Though his only companion is a sword, in the overthrow of numerous enemies — unlike some lowly person — there is no pride in this greatly resolute one. //463//}

children.text: atraiva tuccheti mahādhṛterityanayoḥ paryāyeṇa yugapadvānapādānenyat bhedatrayam / evamanyeṣvapi draṣṭavyam / atra ivaśabdasya sadbhāvācchābdamaupamyam /
children.translated_text: Here, with 'lowly' and 'greatly resolute' — by alternating or simultaneously omitting these, three further sub-varieties [are obtained]. The same should be observed in the other cases as well. Here, since the word 'iva' (like) is present, the comparison is verbal (<s>śābda</s>).
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{Though his only companion is a sword, in the overthrow of numerous enemies — this greatly resolute one has no pride at all, unlike some lowly person. //464//}
Here, 'vat' [conveys] the sense of similarity — hence the comparison is by meaning (<s>ārtha</s>).
(<s>Udbhaṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasārasaṅgraha</s>)
{This <s>Sunayanā</s>, having made the beauty of the lotus her slave, conquers with her spotless face the blemished moon. //465//}
Here, precisely through the absence of words like 'iva' (like), 'tulya' (equal), and the like, the comparison is only imputed (<s>ākṣipta</s>).
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{Through mastery of the senses, properly serving the elders learned in wisdom — the qualities of this one, deeply rooted in virtue, are not fragile like those of a lotus. //466//}
Here too, 'vat' [conveys] the sense of similarity; the word '<s>guṇa</s>' (quality/string) is used with <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre); the comparison is verbal (<s>śābda</s>). //

children.text:
{akhaṇḍamaṇḍalaḥ śrīmān paśyaiṣa pṛthivīpatiḥ /
  na niśākaravajjātu kalāvaikalyamāgataḥ //467//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{Behold this glorious lord of the earth, complete and full-orbed — unlike the moon, he has never attained diminishment of his digits (<s>kalā</s>). //467//}
Here, 'vat' [conveys] the sense of similarity; the word '<s>kalā</s>' (digit/art) is used with <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre).

children.text: mālāprativastūpamāvat mālāvyatireko 'pi saṃbhavati / tasyāpi bhedā evamūhyāḥ / diṅmātramudāhriyate / yathā
children.translated_text: Just as there is chain-<s>prativastūpamā</s> (<s>mālāprativastūpamā</s>), chain-<s>vyatireka</s> (<s>mālāvyatireka</s>) is also possible. Its varieties should be inferred in the same manner. Only a brief illustration is given. As follows:

children.text:
{haravanna viṣamadṛṣṭirharivanna vibho vidhūtavitatavṛṣaḥ /
  rativanna cātiduḥsahakaratāpitabhūḥ kadācidasi //468//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 256)

{You are not like <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), O Lord, [for you have] no uneven gaze; nor like <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), [for you have] no shaken-off and spread-out bull; nor like <s>Rati</s>'s [lord, <s>Kāma</s>], [for you are] never [one] whose land is scorched by unbearably hot rays. //468//}

children.text: atra tulyārthe vatiḥ / viṣamādayaśca śabdāḥ śliṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, 'vat' [conveys] the sense of similarity; and the words 'viṣama' (uneven/poison) and the like are used with <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre).
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{By this king of ever-risen glory, whose splendor closes the three watches of the night — this <s>Bhāsvān</s> (Sun) has been surpassed. //469//}
Here indeed the comparison is merely imputed; '<s>Bhāsvat</s>' (radiant/the Sun) is used with <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre). And as follows:

children.text:
{svacchātmatāguṇasamullasitendubimbaṃ
  bimbaprabhādharamakṛtrimahṛdyagandham /
  yūnāmatīva pibatāṃ rajanīṣu yatra
  tṛṣṇāṃ jahāra madhu nānanamaṅganānām //470//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{The moon-orb, radiant with the quality of its own crystal-clear nature, with a lip of <s>bimba</s>-fruit radiance and a naturally pleasing fragrance — the face of the women [was such that] as young men drank it deeply on those nights, the nectar did not remove their thirst. ||470||}

children.text: atrevādīnāṃ tulyādīnāṃ ca padānāmabhāve 'pi śliṣṭaviśeṣaṇairākṣiptaivopamā pratīyate / evañjātīyakāḥ śliṣṭoktiyogyasya padasya pṛthagpādāne 'nyepi bhedāḥ saṃbhavanti / te 'pi anayaiva diśā draṣṭavyāḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, even in the absence of words like 'as if' (<s>iva</s>) or 'equal' (<s>tulya</s>), the simile is apprehended as implied by the <s>śliṣṭa</s> (interlocked) qualifiers. In this manner, other varieties too are possible when a word fit for <s>śliṣṭokti</s> (interlocked expression) is separately placed. Those too should be understood in the same direction.
The negation of what one wishes to say, with the desire of expressing a distinction — || MKpr-K_106 ||
that is <s>ākṣepa</s> (feigned denial), pertaining to what is about to be said or to what has been said — it is considered twofold.

children.text:
vivakṣitasya prākaraṇikatvādanupasarjanīkāryasya aśakyavaktavyatvam atiprasiddhatvaṃ vā viśeṣaṃ vaktuṃ niṣedho niṣedha iva yaḥ sa vakṣyamāṇaviṣaya uktaviṣayaśceti dvidhā ākṣepaḥ /
krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: Of what is intended — being contextually relevant and therefore not to be subordinated — the impossibility of expressing it, or its being too well-known, [leads to] a negation, or what resembles negation, for the purpose of stating a distinction. That is <s>ākṣepa</s>, twofold: pertaining to what is about to be said, and pertaining to what has been said. Examples in order:

children.text:
{e ehi kiṃapi kīevi a_eṇa ṇikkiva bhaṇāmi alamaha vā /
  aviāri_akajjārambha_āriṇī marau ṇa bhaṇissaṃ //471//}
[e ehi kimapi kasyā api kṛte niṣkṛpa bhaṇāmi alamatha vā /
children.translated_text: [Come, come — I shall tell something about some woman, O merciless one — enough, or rather —
one who begins actions without deliberation — let her die! I shall not speak! ||471||]
(<s>Hāla's</s> <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 7.2)
{Come, come — I'll tell something to someone, O merciless one — enough, or rather,

children.text:
{jyotsnā mauktikadāma candanarasaḥ śītāṃśukāntadravaḥ
  karpūraṃ kadalī mṛṇālavalayānyambhojinīpallavāḥ /
  antarmānasamāstvayā prabhavatā tasyāḥ sphuliṅgotkara-
  vyāpārāya bhavanti hanta kimanenoktena na brūmahe //472//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Moonlight, a pearl necklace, sandal paste, the liquid of the cool-rayed [moon], camphor, plantain, lotus-stalk bracelets, lotus leaves — O powerful one, for the sparking-fire-operations of her inward pride, all these become — alas, why say more? We shall not speak! ||472||}
<s>Vibhāvanā</s> (poetic fancy) is the manifestation of the result even when the action [that is its cause] is negated. || MKpr-K_107 ||
<s>Vibhāvanā</s> is the manifestation of the result even when the action that is the cause is negated. For example:
(<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s>)
{Though not struck by flowering creepers, she bore pain; though not bitten by clusters of bees, she writhed; though not shaken by waves of the lotus-pond, she whirled about. ||473||}
<s>Viśeṣokti</s> (distinctive statement) is the statement of the absence of the result when the causes are unimpaired.

children.text: militeṣvapi kāraṇeṣu kāryasyākathanaṃ viśeṣoktiḥ / anuktanimittā uktanimittā acintyanimittā ca / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: The non-statement of the effect even when the causes are all present is <s>viśeṣokti</s>. [It is of three kinds:] with unexpressed cause, with expressed cause, and with inconceivable cause. Examples in order:

children.text:
{nidrānivṛttāvudite dyuratne sakhījane dvārapadaṃ parāpte /
  ślathīkṛtāśleṣarase bhujaṅge cacāla nāliṅganatoṅganā sā //474//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{When sleep departed, when the day-jewel (sun) arose, when the company of friends arrived at the doorstep, and when the embrace loosened its hold — still that woman did not stir from the embrace. ||474||}

children.text:
{karpūra iva dagdho 'pi śaktimān yo jane jane /
  namo 'stvavāryavīryāya tasmai makaraketave //475//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rājaśekhara's</s> <s>Bālarāmāyaṇa</s> 3.11)

{Like camphor, though burned, he who is powerful in person after person — obeisance to that <s>Makaraketana</s> (the banner-marked-with-<s>makara</s>, i.e., <s>Kāma</s>), of irresistible valor! ||475||}

children.text:
{sa ekastrīṇi jayati jaganti kusumāyudhaḥ /
  haratāpi tanuṃ yasya śambhunā na balaṃ hṛtam //476//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhāmaha's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 3.24)
{He, the flower-weaponed one (<s>Kāma</s>), alone conquers the three worlds; even when <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) destroyed his body, his power was not taken away. ||476||}
<s>Yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration in order) is the sequential correlation of items in the same order. || MKpr-K_108 ||
For example:

children.text:
{ekastridhā vasasi cetasi citramatra
  deva dviṣāṃ ca viduṣāṃ ca mṛgīdṛśāṃ ca /
  tāpaṃ ca saṃmadarasaṃ ca ratiṃ ca puṣṇan
  śauryoṣmaṇā ca vinayena ca līlayā ca //477//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Subhāṣitaratnākara</s> 1438)

{O lord, you dwell threefold in the minds — wonderfully — of enemies, of the learned, and of the doe-eyed women, fostering torment, delight, and love respectively, through the heat of valor, through modesty, and through grace. ||477||}

children.text: sāmānyaṃ vā viśeṣo vā tadanyena samarthyate /
children.translated_text: When a general [statement] or a particular [instance] is corroborated by another —
that is <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration by another matter), whether through similarity or through contrast. || MKpr-K_109 ||

children.text: sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa vā sāmānyaṃ viśeṣeṇa yat samarthyate viśeṣo vā sāmānyena so 'rthāntaranyāsaḥ / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: <s>Arthāntaranyāsa</s> is when a general [statement] is corroborated by a particular, or a particular by a general — through similarity or dissimilarity. Examples in order:

children.text:
{nijadoṣāvṛtamanasāmatisundarameva bhāti viparītam /
  paśyati pittopahataḥ śaśiśubhraṃ śaṅkhamapi pītam //478//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 265)
{For those whose minds are covered by their own faults, even what is supremely beautiful appears as the opposite; one afflicted with bile sees even a conch white as the moon as yellow. ||478||}

children.text:
{susitavasanālaṅkārāyāṃ kadācana kaumudī-
  mahasi sudṛśi svairaṃ yāntyāṃ gato 'stamabhūdvidhuḥ /
  tadanu bhavataḥ kīrtiḥ kenāpyagīyata yena sā
  priyagṛhamagānmuktāśaṅkā kva nāsi śubhapradaḥ //479[=266]//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 121)

{Once, when the beautiful-eyed one, adorned with white garments and ornaments, was freely wandering in the splendor of the moonlit night, the moon set. Then your fame was sung by someone, and she — freed from suspicion — went to her beloved's house. Where were you not a bestower of good? ||479||}

children.text:
{guṇānāmeva daurātmyād dhuri dhuryo niyujyate /
  asaṃjātakiṇaskandhaḥ sukhaṃ svapiti gaurgaliḥ //480//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhoja's</s> <s>Sarasvatīkaṇṭhābharaṇa</s> 4.125)

{It is precisely because of the wickedness of [having] qualities that the foremost [bull] is yoked to the yoke; the bull <s>Gali</s>, whose shoulders have not yet developed calluses, sleeps comfortably. ||480||}

children.text:
{aho hi me bahvaparāddhamāyuṣā yadapriyaṃ vācyamidaṃ mayedṛśam /
  ta eva dhanyāḥ suhṛdaḥ parābhavaṃ jagatyadṛṣṭvaiva hi ye kṣayaṃ gatāḥ //481//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka's</s> <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{Alas, much has been wronged by my long life, in that I must speak such unpleasant words! Those friends are truly fortunate who departed this world without having witnessed [this] humiliation. ||481||}
<s>Virodha</s> (contradiction) is a statement in the form of contradiction even when there is no [real] contradiction.
When there is no contradiction in the actual course of events, yet the expression is as if of contradictory things — that is <s>virodha</s>.
<s>Jāti</s> (genus) may be contradicted by four [types]: genus and the rest; by three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities); || MKpr-K_110 ||

children.text: kriyā dvābhyāmapi dravyaṃ dravyeṇaiveti te daśa /
children.translated_text: <s>Kriyā</s> (action) by two; and <s>dravya</s> (substance) by substance alone — thus ten [types].
Examples in order:
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s> 267)

{Fresh lotus buds, lotus-stalk bracelets, and the like — [all become] a mass of forest fire for that doe-eyed one of yours, O handsome one, by the power of fate, in the calamity of separation from you. ||482||}
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{Mountains are without elevation, the wind is without motion, the oceans are without depth, and the earth-bearer is exceedingly light — certainly, O lord of men, in your presence. ||483||}

children.text:
{yeṣāṃ kaṇṭhaparigrahapraṇayitāṃ saṃprāpya dhārādharas
  tīkṣṇaḥ so 'pyanurajyate ca kamapi snehaṃ parāpnoti ca /
  teṣāṃ saṃgarasaṅgasaktamanasāṃ rājñāṃ tvayā bhūpate
  pāṃsūnāṃ paṭalaiḥ prasādhanavidhirnirvartyate kautukam //484//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{When swords, attaining the state of being lovingly embraced around the neck, [become soft] — even that fierce one becomes enamored and attains a certain affection; for those kings whose minds are attached to the passion of battle, O king, by you the grooming ritual is performed with layers of dust — what a marvel! ||484||}

children.text:
{sṛjati ca jagadidamavati ca saṃharati ca helayaiva yo niyatam /
  avasaravaśataḥ śapharo janārdanaḥ so 'pi citramidam //485//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{He who certainly creates, preserves, and destroys this world with mere play — and yet [he is also] a <s>Śaphara</s> fish depending on the occasion — that is <s>Janārdana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) — how wonderful this is! ||485||}

children.text:
{satataṃ musalāsaktā bahutaragṛhakarmaghaṭanayā nṛpate /
  dvijapatnīnāṃ kaṭhināḥ sati bhavati karāḥ sarojasukumārāḥ //486//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{O king, the hands of the wives of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, constantly busy with pestles and with much domestic work, though hard, are [also] soft as lotuses when present [before you]. ||486||}

children.text:
{peśalamapi khalavacanaṃ dahatitarāṃ mānasaṃ sattattvavidām /
  paruṣamapi sujanavākyaṃ malayajarasavat pramodayati //487//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{Even elegant speech of the wicked burns the minds of the knowers of truth all the more; even harsh speech of the good, like sandal-wood paste, brings delight. ||487||}
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{He, <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>), who in the shower of arrows at the adamant <s>Krauñca</s> mountain — that truly unprecedented creation — became [soft as] a fresh lotus petal! ||488||}

children.text:
{paricchedātītaḥ sakalavacanānāmaviṣayaḥ
  punarjanmanyasminnanubhavapathaṃ yo na gatavān /
  vivekapradhvaṃsādupacitamahāmohagahano
  vikāraḥ ko 'pyantarjaḍayati ca tāpaṃ ca kurute //489//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti's</s> <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> 1.30)

{Beyond all measure, beyond the domain of all words, not having come within the path of experience in this birth again — through the destruction of discernment, dense with accumulated great delusion, some inexplicable inner transformation both numbs and causes anguish. ||489||}

children.text:
{ayaṃ vārāmeko nilaya ita ratnākara iti
  śritosmābhistṛṣṇātaralitamanobhirjalanidhiḥ /
  ka evaṃ jānīte nijakarapuṭīkoṭaragataṃ
  kṣaṇādenaṃ tāmyattimimakaramāpāsyati muniḥ //490//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhallaṭaśataka</s> 108)

{This ocean — 'a single abode of water,' 'a mine of gems' — has been resorted to by us whose minds are agitated by thirst. Who indeed knows that in an instant, the sage will drink him up — this one [ocean] with its gasping fish and sea-monsters — holding it in the hollow of his own palm? ||490||}
(<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{O ornament of the earth, when you are stationed on the bank, even the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>) [becomes like] the river on <s>Śaṅkara's</s> (<s>Śiva's</s>) head (<s>Gaṅgā</s>) — from the embrace of waves of rut-water streaming from the temples of maddened elephants of equal pride. ||491||}
<s>Svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) is the description of the natural action, form, or appearance of an infant and the like. || MKpr-K_111 ||

children.text: svayostadekāśrayoḥ / rūpaṃ varṇaḥ saṃsthānaṃ ca / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: 'Natural' (<s>sva</s>) — their own; and [the description of] these two [action and form] having a single locus. 'Form' (<s>rūpa</s>) means appearance and configuration. An example:

children.text:
{paścādaṅghrī prasārya trikanativitataṃ drāghayitvāṅgamuccair
  āsajyābhugnakaṇṭho mukhamurasi saṭāṃ dhūlidhūbhrāṃ vidhūya /
  ghāsagrāsābhilāṣādanavaratacalatprothatuṇḍasturaṅgo
  mandaṃ śabdāyamāno vilikhati śayanādutthitaḥ kṣmāṃ khureṇa //492//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bāṇa's</s> <s>Harṣacarita</s> 3.5)

{Stretching its hind legs behind, elongating its body far upward with the three bends, fastening its bent neck with its mouth on its chest, shaking its mane thick with dust, its muzzle ceaselessly moving with the desire to seize a mouthful of grass — the horse, having risen from its bed, scrapes the ground with its hoof, neighing softly. ||492||}
<s>Vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) is where, on the surface, there is blame but [in reality] praise, or vice versa.
Praise in the guise [of blame], or through a guise. Examples in order:

children.text:
{hitvā tvāmuparodhabandhyamanasāṃ manye na mauliḥ paro
  lajjāvarjanamantareṇa na ramāmanyatra saṃdṛśyate /
  yastyāgaṃ tanutetarāṃ mukhaśatairetyāśritāyāḥ śriyaḥ
  prāpya tyāgakṛtāvamānanamapi tvayyeva yasyāḥ sthitiḥ //493//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{Having abandoned you, I think no other is a chief — with minds barren from the restraint of suitors. Nor is <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) seen elsewhere without casting off shame. One who extends renunciation all the more through a hundred faces — of such <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) who has taken refuge, even though she has suffered the humiliation wrought by renunciation, her abode remains in you alone. ||493||}

children.text:
{he helājitabodhisattva vacasāṃ kiṃ vistaraistoyadhe
  nāsti tvatsadṛśaḥ paraḥ parahitādhāne gṛhītavrataḥ /
  tṛṣyatpānthajanopakāraghaṭanāvaimukhyalabdhāyaśo-
  bhāraprodvahane karoṣi kṛpayā sāhāyakaṃ yanmaroḥ //494//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kuntaka's</s> <s>Vakroktijīvita</s> 1.90; <s>Puñjarāja</s>, <s>Vākyapadīyaṭīkā</s> 2.249)

{O you who have effortlessly conquered the <s>Bodhisattva</s>! What need of elaborate words, O rain-cloud? There is no other equal to you who has taken a vow of benefiting others. In bearing the burden of the infamy obtained through your aversion to helping thirsty travelers — you render assistance to the desert out of compassion! ||494||}

children.text: sā sahoktiḥ sahārthasya balādekaṃ dvivācakam // MKpr-K_112 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sahokti</s> (co-expression) is when a single expression, by the force of the co-meaning, denotes two [things]. || MKpr-K_112 ||

children.text: ekārthābhidhāyakamapi sahārthabalāt yat ubhayasyāpyavagamakaṃ sā sahoktiḥ / yathā
children.translated_text: That which, though expressing a single meaning, through the force of the co-meaning produces the understanding of both — that is <s>sahokti</s>. For example:

children.text:
{saha diahaṇisāṃhi dīharā sāsadaṇḍā
  saha maṇivalayeṃhi bāhadhārā galanti /
  tuha suhaa vioe tīa ubbiggirīe
  saha a taṇuladāe dubbalā jīvidāsā //495//}

children.translated_text: [Together with the days and nights, long are the rods of sighs;
together with the jeweled bracelets, streams of tears flow down;
in your separation, O handsome one, for her who is distressed,
together with the slender creeper-body, the hope of life grows feeble.] ||495||
(<s>Rājaśekhara's</s> <s>Karpūramañjarī</s> 2.9)
{Together with the days and nights, long are the rods of sighs;

children.text: śvāsadaṇḍādigataṃ dīrghatvādi śābdam divasaniśādigataṃ tu sahārthasāmarthyātpratipadyate //112//
children.translated_text: The 'longness' and the like pertaining to 'rods of sighs' and the rest are verbal [i.e., directly expressed]; but the same pertaining to 'days and nights' and the rest is understood through the force of the co-meaning (<s>sahārtha</s>). ||112||

children.text: vinoktiḥ sā vinānyena yatrānyaḥ sanna netaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vinokti</s> (expression through absence) is where, in the absence of one thing, another exists — and [behaves] not as the other [would].
Sometimes [the absent thing is] unbeautiful, sometimes beautiful. Examples in order:

children.text:
{arucirniśayā vinā śaśī śaśinā sāpi vinā mahattamaḥ /
  ubhayena vinā manobhavasphuritaṃ naiva cakāsti kāminoḥ //496//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

children.text:
{mṛgalocanayā vinā vicitracvyavahārapratibhāprabhāpragalbhaḥ /
  amṛtadyutisundarāśayo 'yaṃ suhṛdā tena vinā narendrasūnuḥ //497//}
children.translated_text: {Without the doe-eyed one, this prince, though masterful in the brilliance of eloquence and varied conduct, beautiful in ambition like the nectar-rayed [moon] — and he without his friend [is likewise diminished]. ||497||}
(<s>Ruyyaka's</s> <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s> 50)

{The night without the moon is charmless; the moon too, without her, is of supreme darkness; without both, the stirring of <s>Manobhava</s> (<s>Kāma</s>, god of love) does not shine at all for lovers. ||496||}
<s>Parivṛtti</s> (exchange) is the mutual interchange of meanings between equals. || MKpr-K_113 ||
<s>Parivṛtti</s> is a figure of speech. An example:

children.text:
{latānāmetāsāmuditakusumānāṃ marudayaṃ
  mataṃ lāsyaṃ dattvā śrayati bhṛśamāmodamasamam /
  latāstvadhvanyānāmahaha dṛśamādaya sahasā
  dadatyādhivyādhibhramiruditamohavyatikaram //498//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{The wind, giving a dance to these creepers with blossomed flowers, acquires an incomparable fragrance from them. But the creepers of travelers — alas! — seizing their sight suddenly, give them a confusion of disease, agitation, tears, and delusion. ||498||}

children.text: atra prathamerghe samena samasya dvitīye uttamene nyūnasya /
children.translated_text: Here, in the first half-verse, equal things exchange with equals; in the second, the superior [exchanges] with the inferior.

children.text:
{nānāvidhapraharaṇairnṛpa saṃprahāre
  svīkṛtya dāruṇaninādavataḥ prahārān /
  dṛptārivīravisareṇa vasuṃdhareyaṃ
  nirvipralambhaparirambhavidhirvitīrṇā //499//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{O king, in battle with various weapons, having received the fierce-sounding blows, this earth has been granted by the mass of proud enemy heroes in the manner of an embrace without deception. ||499||}
Here, [the exchange is] of the inferior with the superior. ||113||

children.text:
pratyakṣā iva yadbhāvāḥ kriyante bhūtabhāvinaḥ /
tadbhāvikaṃ ...
children.translated_text: Past and future states are rendered as if directly perceived —

children.text: bhūtāśca bhāvinaśceti dvandvaḥ / bhāvaḥ kaverabhiprāyo 'trāstīti bhāvikam / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: 'Past and future' is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. <s>Bhāvika</s> [means] the poet's intention is present here. Example —

children.text:
{āsīdañjanamatreti paśyāmi tava locane /
  bhāvibhūṣaṇasaṃbhārāṃ sākṣātkurve tavākṛtim //500//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhallaṭaśataka</s> 69)
{'There was collyrium here' — I see in your eyes; 'the full array of future ornaments' — I behold your form directly! //500//}
In the first [line], there is the perception of the past; in the second, of the future.
... <s>Kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason) is [the figure in which] the reason has the status of a sentence or word-meaning. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_114 //
As a sentence-meaning, for example:

children.text:
{vapuḥprādurbhāvādanumitamidaṃ janmani purā
  purāre na prāyaḥ kvacidapi bhavantaṃ praṇatavān /
  naman muktaḥ saṃpratyahamatanuragre 'pyanatibhāṅ
  maheśa kṣantavyaṃ tadidamaparādhadvayamapi //501//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Subhāṣitaratnākara</s> 36)

{'From the manifestation of [this] body, it is inferred that in a previous birth, O enemy of <s>Pura</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), I probably never bowed to you anywhere. Now, prostrating, I am liberated; yet even before the bodiless one (<s>Kāma</s>), I do not break my bow [of salutation]. O Great Lord, may this twofold offense be forgiven!' //501//}
As multiple word-meanings, for example:

children.text:
{praṇayisakhī salīlaparihāsarasādhigatair
  lalitaśirīṣapuṣpahananairapi tāmyati yat /
  vapuṣi vadhāya tatra tava śastramupakṣipataḥ
  patatu śirasyakāṇḍayamadaṇḍa ivaiṣa bhujaḥ //502//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> 5.31)

{'Since the body, [even] from playful blows with tender <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers, inflicted by a loving friend in jest and sport, grows faint — upon that body, as you cast your weapon to kill, may this arm fall upon your head like the sudden staff of <s>Yama</s> (Death)!' //502//}
As a single word-meaning, for example:

children.text:
{bhasmoddhūlana bhadramastu bhavate rudrākṣamāle śubhaṃ
  hā sopānaparaṃparāṃ girisutākāntālayālaṅkṛtiṃ /
  adyārādhanatoṣitena vibhunā yuṣmatsaparyāsukhā-
  lokocchedini mokṣanāmani mahāmohe nidhīyāmahe //503//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{'O ash-smearing, may it be well with you! O <s>rudrākṣa</s> garland, may there be auspiciousness! Alas, the flights of stairs — the ornaments of the dwelling of the beloved of the Mountain's daughter! Now, by the Lord gratified through worship, we are deposited in the great delusion called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — which destroys the happiness of beholding the joy of your worship!' //503//}

children.text: eṣu aparādhadvaye pūrvāparajanmanoranamanam bhujapāte śastropakṣepaḥ mahāmohe sukhāvalokoccheditvaṃ ca yathākramamuktarūpo hetuḥ //114//
children.translated_text: In these — the twofold offense of not bowing in the previous and present births; in the falling of the arm, the casting of the weapon; and in the great delusion, the destruction of the happiness of beholding — [these are] the reasons stated in the aforementioned manner, respectively. //114//
<s>Paryāyokta</s> (circumlocution) is speech without the [direct] relation of signifier and signified;

children.text: vācyavācakabhāvavyatiriktenāvagamanavyāpāreṇa yat pratipādanaṃ tat paryāyeṇa bhaṅgyantareṇa kathanāt paryāyoktam / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: That expression which conveys [meaning] through a mode of understanding other than the relation of signifier and signified — that is <s>paryāyokta</s> (circumlocution), because it states [the matter] through a turn of phrase, by an indirect route. Example —

children.text:
{yaṃ prekṣya cirarūḍhāpi nivāsaprītirujjhatā /
  madenairāvaṇamukhe mānena hṛdaye hareḥ //504//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Meṇṭha</s>, <s>Hayagrīvavadha</s>)

{'Upon seeing whom, even long-established affection for one's dwelling is abandoned — through intoxication, on the face of <s>Airāvaṇa</s> (Indra's elephant); through pride, in the heart of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>).' //504//}

children.text:
atra airāvaṇaśakrau madamānamuktau jātāviti vyaṅgyamapi śabdenocyate / tena yadevocyate tadeva vyaṅgyam / yathā tu vyaṅgyaṃ na tathocyate / yathā gavi śukle calati dṛṣṭe {gauḥ śuklaścalati} iti vikalpaḥ / yadeva dṛṣṭaṃ tadeva vikalpayati na tu yathā dṛṣṭaṃ tathā /
yato 'bhinnāsaṃsṛṣṭatvena dṛṣṭam bhedasaṃsargābhyāṃ vikalpayati //
children.translated_text: Here, the suggested meaning — that <s>Airāvaṇa</s> and <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) have abandoned their intoxication and pride — is also expressed through words. Thus what is expressed is itself the suggested meaning. However, it is not expressed in the [same] manner as it is suggested. Just as, when a white cow is seen moving, one formulates 'the cow is white and moves' — what is perceived is exactly what is formulated, but not in the manner perceived. For what is seen as undifferentiated and unrelated is formulated through distinction and relation.
<s>Udātta</s> (the exalted) is the prosperity of a thing ...
'Prosperity' means the conjunction of affluence. For example:

children.text:
{muktāḥ kelivisūtrahāragalitāḥ saṃmārjanībhirhṛtāḥ
  prātaḥ prāṅgaṇasīmni mantharacaladbālāṅghrilākṣāruṇāḥ /
  dūrāddāḍimabījaśaṅkitadhiṃyaḥ karṣanti kelīśukāḥ
  yadvidvadbhavaneṣu bhojanṛpatestat tyāgalīlāyitam //505//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{'Pearls fallen from the sport-thread-necklaces, swept up by cleaning women, reddened by the slow-moving lac from infants' feet on the courtyard's edge in the morning — parrot-playthings which the servants, from afar suspecting them to be pomegranate seeds, drag away — such is the display of the munificence of King <s>Bhoja</s> in the houses of the learned!' //505//}
... and the indirect indication of great persons. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_115 //
'Indirect indication' means non-explicit mention — the meaning to be indicated from [another] meaning. Example —

children.text:
{tadidamaraṇyaṃ yasmin daśarathavacanānupālanavyasanī /
  nivasan bāhusahāyaścakāra rakṣaḥkṣayaṃ rāmaḥ //506//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 7.104)

{'This is that forest in which <s>Rāma</s>, devoted to upholding the word of <s>Daśaratha</s>, dwelling with only his arms as companions, accomplished the destruction of the <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons).' //506//}
And here the <s>vīra rasa</s> (heroic sentiment) is not [the principal] <s>rasa</s>, since it functions here as a subordinate element. //115//
When, for the accomplishment of one [result], there is one [cause], and another [cause] that also produces that [same result] —

children.text: tasya prastutasya kāryasya ekasmin sādhake sthite sādhakāntarāṇi yatra saṃbhavanti sa samuccayaḥ / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: When one agent for the accomplishment of the intended effect is present, and additional agents also arise — that is <s>samuccaya</s> (accumulation). Example —

children.text:
{durvārāḥ smaramārgaṇāḥ priyatamo dūre manotyutsukaṃ
  gāḍhaṃ prema navaṃ vayotikaṭhināḥ prāṇāḥ kulaṃ nirmalam /
  strītvaṃ dhairyavirodhi manmathasuhṛt kālaḥ kṛtāntokṣamo
  no sakhyaścaturāḥ kathaṃ nu virahaḥ soḍhavya itthaṃ śaṭhaḥ //507//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s>)

{'The arrows of <s>Smara</s> (Love) are irresistible; the beloved is far away; the mind is restless; love is deep and new; youth [makes one] hard — life is tough; lineage is pure; womanhood opposes fortitude; the season is a friend of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love), equaling Death — and no clever friends! How is separation to be endured? Thus [speaks] the deceiver [Love].' //507//}

children.text: atra virahāsahatvaṃ smaramārgaṇā eva kurvanti / tadupari priyatamadūrasthityādi upāttam //
children.translated_text: Here, the arrows of <s>Smara</s> alone produce the inability to endure separation. On top of that, the beloved's distance and the rest are added.

children.text: eṣa eva samuccayaḥ sadyoge 'sadyoge sadasadyoge ca paryavasyatīti na pṛthak lakṣyate / tathāhi ----
children.translated_text: This very <s>samuccaya</s> resolves into [three types:] conjunction of [all] good [things], conjunction of [all] bad [things], and conjunction of good and bad — hence it is not defined separately. Thus —

children.text:
{kulamamalinaṃ bhadrā mūrtirmatiḥ śrutiśālinī
  bhujabalamalaṃ sphītā lakṣmīḥ prabhutvamakhaṇḍitam /
  prakṛtisubhagā hyete bhāvā amībhirayaṃ jano
  vrajati sutarāṃ darpaṃ rājan ta eva tavāṅkuśāḥ //508//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhoja</s>'s <s>Sarasvatīkaṇṭhābharaṇa</s> 5.368)

{'The lineage is spotless; the form is auspicious; the intellect is adorned with learning; the strength of arms is sufficient; fortune is abundant; sovereignty is unbroken. These qualities are naturally charming — O king, by these very [qualities] this person attains excessive pride; [yet] these same [qualities] are your goads [to restrain him].' //508//}

children.text: atra satāṃ yogaḥ / uktodāharaṇe tvasatāṃ yogaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, there is a conjunction of good [things]. In the previously cited example, however, there is a conjunction of bad [things].

children.text:
{śaśī divasadhūsaro galitayauvanā kāminī
  saro vigatavārikaṃ mukhamanakṣaraṃ svākṛteḥ /
  prabhurdhanaparāyaṇaḥ satatadurgataḥ sajjano
  nṛpāṅgaṇagataḥ khalo manasi sapta śalyāni me //509//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhartṛhari</s>'s <s>Nītiśataka</s> 45)

{'The moon [when] grey by day; a woman [when] past her youth; a lake [when] devoid of water; a face [when] bereft of letters [learning]; a lord [when] devoted to wealth; a good person [when] always impoverished; a scoundrel [when] arrived at the king's courtyard — these seven are thorns in my heart.' //509//}

children.text: atra śaśini dhūsare śalye śalyāntarāṇīti śobhanāśobhanayogaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the grey moon being a thorn, and alongside it other thorns — this is a conjunction of good and bad.

children.text: ... sa tvanyo yugapad yā guṇakriyāḥ // MKpr-K_116 //
children.translated_text: ... but another [type is] that which [involves] simultaneous qualities and actions. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_116 //

children.text: guṇau ca kriye ca guṇakriye ca guṇakriyāḥ / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: Both qualities and actions, and qualities-and-actions [together] — [these are] 'qualities and actions.' Examples in order —

children.text:
{vidalitasakalārikulaṃ tava balamidamabhavadā‘u vimalaṃ ca /
  prakhalamukhāni narādhipa malināni ca tāni jātāni //510//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 7.28)
{'Your army, which shattered all enemy hosts, was once spotless — [but now] its faces are dismayed, O lord of men, and they have become soiled.' //510//}

children.text:
{ayamekapade tayā viyogaḥ prayayā copanataḥ suduḥsaho me /
  navavāridharodayādahobhirbhavitavyaṃ ca nirātapatvaramyaiḥ //511//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 4.10)

{'This separation from her who has departed, and the approach [of the rains], are both unbearable to me — and by these days of new cloud-risings, one must endure the lack of shelter's charm.' //511//}

children.text:
{kaluṣaṃ ca tavāhiteṣvakasmātsitapaṅkeruhasodaraśri cakṣuḥ /
  patitaṃ ca mahīpatīndra teṣāṃ vapuṣi prasphuṭamāpadāṃ kaṭākṣaiḥ //512//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Viśvanātha</s>'s <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 10.85)

{'Your eye, having the beauty of a white lotus's kin, suddenly became turbid toward your enemies, O lord of the earth, and has visibly cast the sidelong glances of misfortune upon their bodies.' //512//}

children.text: {dhunoti cāsiṃ tanute ca kīrtim} ityādeḥ {kṛpāṇapāṇiśca bhavān raṇakṣitau sasādhuvādāśca surāḥ surālaye} ityādeśca darśanāt {vyadhikaraṇe} iti {ekasmin deśe} iti ca na vācyam //116//
children.translated_text: Since [examples like] 'he brandishes his sword and extends his fame' and 'you stand sword-in-hand on the battlefield, and the gods raise cries of approval in the celestial realm' are attested, the qualifications 'in different grammatical subjects' and 'in one place' should not be stipulated. //116//
<s>Paryāya</s> (succession) is one [thing] in many, in sequence ...

children.text: ekaṃ vastu krameṇānekasmin bhavati kriyate vā sa paryāyaḥ / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: One thing exists in or is placed upon many things in sequence — that is <s>paryāya</s> (succession). Examples in order —

children.text:
{nanvāśrayasthitiriyaṃ tava kālakūṭa
  kenottarottaraviśiṣṭapadopadiṣṭā /
  prāgarṇavasya hṛdaye vṛṣalakṣmaṇo 'tha
  kaṇṭhedhunā vasasi vāci punaḥ khalānām //513//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhallaṭaśataka</s> 4)
Or as follows:

{'O <s>Kālakūṭa</s> (poison)! This abode-succession of yours — by whom was it prescribed in progressively higher stations? First in the heart of the ocean-born (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), marked by the bull (<s>Śiva</s>), then on the throat, and now you dwell in the speech of the wicked.' //513//}

children.text:
{bimboṣṭa eva rāgaste tanvi pūrvamadṛśyata /
  adhunā hṛdaye 'pyeṣa mṛgaśāvākṣi lakṣyate //514//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Padmagupta</s> alias <s>Parimala</s>'s <s>Navasāhasāṅkacarita</s> 6.60)
{'O slender one, your redness (<s>rāga</s>, passion) was first seen only on your <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips; now, O fawn-eyed one, it is perceived in the heart as well.' //514//}
Although <s>rāga</s> (redness/passion) is in reality different [in each context], its unity is not contradicted since it is determined as one.

children.text:
{taṃ tāṇa sirisahoararaaṇāharaṇammi hiaamekkarasaṃ /
  bimbāhare piāṇaṃ ṇivesiaṃ kusumabāṇeṇa //515//}

children.translated_text: [In Sanskrit: 'That single-flavored heart of theirs, [placed] in the jewel-ornament that is the sister of <s>Śrī</s>,
was placed by the flower-arrowed one upon the <s>bimba</s>-fruit lip of their beloveds.']
(<s>Ānandavardhana</s>'s <s>Viṣamabāṇalīlā</s>)

{'[In Prākṛt:] That single-flavored heart of theirs, [placed] in the jewel-ornament that is the sister of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), was placed by the flower-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>) upon the <s>bimba</s>-fruit lip of their beloveds.' //515//}
... the other [type] is the reverse of that;

children.text: anekamekasmin krameṇa bhavati kriyate vā so 'nyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Many things in one, in sequence, exist or are placed — that is the other [type].
Examples in order —

children.text:
{madhurimaruciraṃ vacaḥ khalānāmamṛtamaho prathamaṃ pṛthu vyanakti /
  atha kathayati mohahetumantargatamiva hālahalaṃ viṣaṃ tadeva //516//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 286)

{'The speech of the wicked, endowed with the charm of sweetness, at first broadly reveals nectar, as it were; then it discloses the cause of delusion — that very [speech reveals] the poison, the <s>hālāhala</s>, hidden within.' //516//}

children.text:
{tadgehaṃ natabhitti mandiramidaṃ labdhāvakāśaṃ divaḥ
  sā dhenurjaratī nadamti kariṇāmetā ghanābhā ghaṭāḥ /
  sa kṣudro musaladhvaniḥ kalamidaṃ saṃgītakaṃ yoṣitām
  āścaryaṃ divasairdvijoyamiyatīṃ bhūmiṃ samāropitaḥ //517//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s> 3.16)

{'That house with crumbling walls — this is a temple that has obtained access to the sky! That cow, decrepit — these elephants trumpet! Those dark-hued pots — that small pestle-sound — this is the concert of women! Wondrous — in [just a few] days, this twice-born has been elevated to such a station!' //517//}
Here, since the rejection and adoption of the same thing are both unintended, this is not <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange).
<s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is that statement in which the relationship of <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) and <s>sādhana</s> (the means of proof) is expressed. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_117 //

children.text: pakṣadharmānvayavyatirekitvena trirūpo hetuḥ sādhanam / dharmiṇi ayogavyavacchedo vyāpakasya sādhyatvam / yathā
children.translated_text: The <s>hetu</s> (reason), being threefold as a property of the subject, positively concomitant, and negatively concomitant — is the <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof). In the subject, the exclusion of non-connection of the pervader is <s>sādhyatva</s> (the status of being provable). For example:

children.text:
{yatraitā laharīcalācaladṛśo vyāpārayanti bhruvaṃ
  yat tatraiva patanti saṃtatamamī marmaspṛśo mārgaṇāḥ /
  taccakrīkṛtacāpamañcitaśarapreṅkhatkaraḥ krodhano
  dhāvatyagrata eva śāsanadharaḥ satyaṃ sadāsāṃ smaraḥ //518//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{'Where these [women] with wave-flickering, trembling eyes ply their brows, precisely there these arrows, touching the vital spots, fall continuously. That angry one, having made the bow into a wheel, the arrow fitted, his hand swinging — runs ahead as the enforcer of law. Truly, <s>Smara</s> (Love) is the eternal [commander] of that assembly!' //518//}

children.text: sādhyasādhanyoḥ paurvāparyavikalpe ne kiñcidvaicitryamiti na tathā darśitam //117//
children.translated_text: Since there is no particular variety in the reversal of sequence between <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s>, it has not been illustrated thus. //117//
<s>Parikara</s> (attendant expression) is a statement with purposeful qualifiers;
[Qualifiers] of the thing qualified, implicitly. Example —

children.text:
{mahaujaso mānadhanā dhanārcitā
  dhanurbhṛtaḥ saṃyati labdhakīrtayaḥ /
  na saṃhatāstasya na bhedavṛttayah
  priyāṇi vāñchantyasubhiḥ samīhitum //519//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhāravi</s>'s <s>Kirātārjunīya</s> 1.19)

{'Of great might, with honor as their wealth, honored by wealth, bow-bearers who have won fame in battle — they are not allied with him, nor do they practice the ways of division; with their lives they desire to accomplish what is dear [to their lord].' //519//}

children.text: yadyapyuṣṭārthasya doṣatābhidhānāttannirākaraṇena puṣṭārthasvīkāraḥ kṛtaḥ tathāpyekaniṣṭhatvena bahunāṃ viśeṣaṇānāmevamupanyāse vaicitryam ityalaṅkāramadhye gaṇitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Although, by stating the deficiency of the enriched meaning, the enriched meaning is accepted through the negation of that [deficiency] — nevertheless, since many qualifiers are thus marshaled with respect to a single subject, there is variety [in the expression], and hence it has been counted among the ornaments.
<s>Vyājoktī</s> (pretextual speech) is the concealment of the true nature of a thing through a pretext when it has become manifest. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_118 //

children.text:
nigūḍhamapi vastuno rūpaṃ kathamapi prabhinnaṃ kenāpi vyapadeśena yadapahnūyate sā vyājoktiḥ /
na caiṣāpahnutiḥ prakṛtāprakṛto 'bhayaniṣṭhasya sāmyasyehāsaṃbhavāt / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: When the true nature of a thing, though hidden, has somehow become manifest, and is then denied through some pretext — that is <s>vyājoktī</s> (pretextual speech). This is not <s>apahnutī</s> (denial), because the similarity that resides in both the intended and unintended [meanings] is not possible here. Example —

children.text:
{śailendrapratipādyamānagirijāhastopagūḍhollasad-
  romāñcādivisaṃṣṭhulākhilavidhivyāsaṅgabhaṅgākulaḥ /
  hā śaityaṃ tuhinācalasya karayorityūcivān sasmitaṃ
  śailāntaḥpuramātṛmaṇḍalagaṇairdṛṣṭo 'vatādvaḥ śivaḥ //520//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{'When, as the mountain-king was giving away <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), the horripilation and other [signs] that blazed forth upon his hand's embrace were so profuse as to disrupt all the ritual procedures — 'Ah, the coldness of the Snowy Mountain's hands!' he said with a smile, being observed by the hosts of mothers in the mountain's inner chambers. May that <s>Śiva</s> protect you!' //520//}

children.text: kiñcit pṛṣṭamapṛṣṭaṃ vā kathitaṃ yat prakalpate /
children.translated_text: <s>Parisaṃkhyā</s> (enumeration) is that which, whether asked about or unasked,

children.text: tādṛganyavyapohāya parisaṃkhyā tu sā smṛtā // MKpr-K_119 //
children.translated_text: when stated, serves to exclude other similar [things]. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_119 //

children.text:
pramānāntarāvagatamapi vastu śabdena pratipāditaṃ prayojanāntarābhāvāt sadṛśavastvanataravyavacchedāya yat paryavasyati sā bhavetparisaṃkhyā / atra ca kathanaṃ praśnapūrvakaṃ tadanyathā ca paridṛṣṭam /
tathā ubhayatra vyapohyamānasya pratīyamānatā vācyatvaṃ ceti catvāro bhedāḥ // krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: When a thing, even though already known through another means of knowledge, is expressed through words and — in the absence of any other purpose — resolves into the exclusion of other similar things, that is <s>parisaṃkhyā</s> (enumeration). Herein, the statement may be preceded by a question or may be otherwise [unprompted]. Thus, in both cases, [the excluded item] may be implied or may be explicitly stated — hence there are four varieties. Examples in order —

children.text:
{kimāsevyaṃ puṃsāṃ savidhamanavadyaṃ dyusaritaḥ
  kimekānte dhyeyaṃ caraṇayugalaṃ kaustubhabhṛtaḥ /
  kimārādhyaṃ puṇyaṃ kiṃabhilaṣaṇīyaṃ ca karuṇā
  yadāsaktyā ceto niravadhivimuktyai prabha[v]ati //521//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{'What should men attend upon closely? The blameless celestial river. What should be meditated upon in solitude? The pair of feet of the bearer of the <s>Kaustubha</s>. What is the sacred thing to be worshipped? What is to be desired? Compassion — for when the mind is devoted to these, it becomes capable of boundless liberation.' //521//}

children.text:
{kiṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ sudṛḍhamatra yaśo na ratnaṃ
  kiṃ kāryamāryacaritaṃ sukṛtaṃ na doṣaḥ /
  kiṃ cakṣurapratihataṃ dhiṣaṇā na netraṃ
  jānāti kastvadadaparaḥ sadasadvivekam //522//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Viśvanātha</s>'s <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 10.82)

{What is a firm ornament here? Fame — not a gem. What is a worthy deed? Noble conduct — not meritorious ritual. What is the [true] eye? Unfailing intellect — not the [physical] organ of sight. Who else but you knows the discrimination of real and unreal? //522//}

children.text:
{kauṭilyaṃ kacanicaye karacaraṇādharadaleṣu rāgaste /
  kāṭhinyaṃ kucayugale taralatvaṃ nayanayorvasati //523//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 7.81)
{Crookedness dwells in [your] mass of hair; redness in [your] hands, feet, and lip-petals; hardness in [your] pair of breasts; and fickleness in [your] eyes. //523//}

children.text:
{bhaktirbhave na vibhave vyasanaṃ śāstre na yuvatikāmāstre /
  cintā yaśasi na vapuṣi prāyaḥ paridṛśyate mahatām //524//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{Devotion is in the Lord (<s>Bhava</s>), not in wealth; passion (<s>vyasana</s>) is in scripture, not in the arrow of desire for young women; anxiety is about fame, not about the body — such is what is generally observed of great souls. //524//}

children.text:
yathottaraṃ cet pūrvasya pūrvasyārthasya hetutā /
tadā kāraṇamālā syāt ...
children.translated_text: When, successively, each prior meaning serves as the cause of the subsequent — then that is <s>kāraṇamālā</s> (causal chain) ...
Successively — each subsequent [cause operating] toward the next subsequent [effect]. Example —

children.text:
{jitendriyatvaṃ vinayasya kāraṇaṃ guṇaprakarṣo vinayādavāpyate /
  guṇaprakarṣeṇa jano 'nurajyate janānurāgaprabhavā hi saṃpadaḥ //525//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vallabhadeva</s>'s <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s>; <s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 162)

{Mastery of the senses is the cause of modesty; excellence of qualities is obtained through modesty; through the excellence of qualities, people become devoted; for prosperity arises from the devotion of the people. //525//}

children.text:
{hetumatā saha hetoravhidhānamabhedayo hetuḥ /}
iti hetvalaṅkāro na lakṣitaḥ / āyurdhṛtamityādirūpo hyeṣa na bhūṣaṇatāṃ kadācidarhati vaicitryābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: {'The statement of a cause along with its effect — the cause of [their] non-difference — is <s>hetu</s> (cause [as a figure]).'} Thus the figure called <s>hetu</s> has not been separately recognized [here]. For this [type], being of the form 'life is sustained' and the like, never merits the status of an ornament, since it lacks aesthetic charm (<s>vaicitrya</s>).

children.text:
{aviralakamalavikāsaḥ sakalālimadaśca kokilānandaḥ /
  ramyo 'yameti saṃprati lokotkaṇṭhākaraḥ kālaḥ //526//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 7.83)
{The lotuses bloom profusely, the bees are all intoxicated, and the cuckoos are delighted — this season is now delightful, [yet] causes longing in the people. //526//}

children.text: ityatra kāvyarūpatāṃ komalānuprāsamahimnaiva samāmnāsiṣurna punarhetvalaṅkārakalpanayeti pūrvoktakāvyaliṅgameva hetuḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the status of being poetry has been attributed solely to the power of the soft <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), and not to the conception of <s>hetu</s> as a figure — thus it is the <s>kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason) described earlier that constitutes the [true] <s>hetu</s> (causal figure). //
... but [when the causation is] mutual, through action — // <s>MKpr-K</s>_120 //
When two things mutually generate each other ...

children.text: arthayorekakriyāmukhena parasparaṃ kāraṇatve sati anyonyanāmā alaṅkāraḥ / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: When two meanings are mutually causal through the medium of a single action — that figure is called <s>anyonya</s> (mutual [causation]). Example —

children.text:
{haṃsāṇaṃ sarehiṃ sirī sārijjai aha sarāṇa haṃsehiṃ /
  aṇṇoṇṇaṃ via ee appāṇṇaṃ ṇavara garuanti //527//}
[haṃsānāṃ sarobhiḥ śrīḥ sāryate atha sarasāṃ haṃsaiḥ /
children.translated_text: [The beauty of swans is enhanced by lakes, and then the beauty of lakes by swans;
mutually indeed, these merely glorify themselves. //]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s>, Nirnaya Sagar Press, 953)
{The beauty of swans is enhanced by lakes, and then the beauty of lakes by swans —
Here, the mutual generativeness of both [swans and lakes] is through the medium of mutually enhancing each other's beauty.
... from merely hearing the reply,

children.text: praśnasyonnayanaṃ yatra kriyate tatra vā sati // MKpr-K_121 //
children.translated_text: where the raising of a question is inferred — in that case, that is [the figure called <s>uttara</s> (reply)]. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_121 //
When the reply is repeatedly of an unimaginable nature, that [too] is <s>uttara</s>.

children.text: prativacanopalambhādeva pūrvavākyaṃ yatra kalpyate tadekaṃ tāvaduttaram / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: Where the preceding statement is inferred merely from encountering the reply — that is one [type of] <s>uttara</s> (reply). Example —

children.text:
{vāṇia_a hatthidantā kutto amhāṇa vagdhakittī a /
  jāva luliāla_amuhī dharammi parisakkae soṇhā //528//}

children.translated_text: [O merchant, ivory tusks? Where would we get them? And tiger-skins?
So long as the daughter-in-law with disheveled locks embraces [her husband] at home, the young wife... //]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 951; <s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s> 3.17)
{O merchant, ivory tusks? — Where would we have them? And tiger-skins? —

children.text: hastidantavyāghrakṛttīnāmahamarthī tāḥ mūlyena prayaccheti kreturvacanam amunā vākyena samunnīyata //
children.translated_text: 'I want ivory tusks and tiger-skins; give them to me for a price' — this statement of the buyer is inferred from that sentence [of the reply].

children.text:
na caitat kāvyaliṅgam uttarasya tādrūpyānupapatteḥ / nahi praśnasya prativacanaṃ janako hetuḥ / nāpīdamanumānam ekadharminiṣṭhatayā sādyasādhanayoranirdeśādityalaṅkārāntaramevottaraṃ sādhīyaḥ /
praśnādanantaraṃ lokātikrāntagocaratayā yat asaṃbhāvyarūpaṃ prativacanaṃ syāt tat aparamuttaram / anayośca sakṛdupādāne na cārutāpratītirityasakṛdityuktam / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text:
And this is not <s>kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason), because the reply would not be of such a form [if it were]. For the reply to a question is not a generating cause.
