Nor is this inference, since the subject (<s>sādhya</s>) and the proof (<s>sādhana</s>) — being confined to a single locus — are not separately indicated. Thus <s>uttara</s> is indeed a distinct figure, and more effective.
When, following a question, the reply is of a form that transcends ordinary [expectation] — that is the second [type of] <s>uttara</s>. And since a single use of both [types] does not produce the perception of aesthetic charm, [the text says] 'repeatedly.' Example —

children.text:
{kā visamā devvagari kiṃ labdhaṃ jaṃ jaṇo guṇggāhī /
  kiṃ sokkhaṃ sukalattaṃ kiṃ dukkhaṃ jaṃ khalo lo_o //529//}
[kā viṣamā daivagatiḥ kiṃ labdhavyaṃ yat jano guṇagrāhī /
children.translated_text: [What is adversity? The course of fate. What is to be gained? That people appreciate merit.

children.text: kiṃ saukhyaṃ sukalatraṃ kiṃ duḥkhaṃ yat khalo lokaḥ //]
children.translated_text: What is happiness? A good wife. What is sorrow? That the world is full of rogues. //]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s>, Nirnaya Sagar Press, 975)
{What is adversity? The course of fate. What is to be gained? That people appreciate merit.

children.text: praśnaparisaṃkhyāyāmanyavyapohe eva tātparyam / iha tu vācye eva viśrāntirityanayorvivekaḥ //
children.translated_text: In the <s>praśnaparisaṃkhyā</s> (enumerative question), the purport lies precisely in the exclusion of everything else. But here, the purport rests in the expressed meaning itself — this is the distinction between the two.
When a subtle meaning, perceived from some [sign], is revealed to another — // <s>MKpr-K</s>_122 //

children.text: dharmeṇa kenacid yatra tat sūkṣmaṃ paricakṣate /
children.translated_text: where it is conveyed through some property — that is called <s>sūkṣma</s> (the subtle).
Perceived from some [sign] — from a gesture, hint, or the like; subtle — apprehensible only by a keen intellect. //
Example —

children.text:
{vaktrasyandisvedabinduprabandhairdṛṣṭvā bhinnaṃ kuṅkumaṃ kāpi kaṇṭhe /
  puṃstvaṃ tanvyā vyañjayantī vayasyā smitvā pāṇau khaḍgalekhāṃ lilekha //530//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{Seeing the <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron paste) on the neck broken apart by streams of sweat drops flowing from the face — a certain female friend, revealing the manliness of the slender one [i.e., that her friend had been with a man], smiled and drew on her palm the outline of a sword. //530//}

children.text: atra ākṛtimavalokya kayāpi vitarkitaṃ puruṣāyitam asilatālekhanena vaidagdhyādabhivyaktimupanītam puṃsāmeva kṛpāṇapāṇitā yogyatvāt //
children.translated_text: Here, the sexual union (<s>puruṣāyita</s>) was surmised by some [friend] from observing the appearance; it was brought to expression through the skillful drawing of a sword-line — because wielding a sword in hand is appropriate only for men. //
And as follows:

children.text:
{saṃketakālamanasaṃ viṭ.am jñātvā vidagdhayā /
  īṣannetrārpitākūtaṃ līlāpadmaṃ nimīlitam //531//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s <s>Dhvanyālokalocana</s> 2.36)
{Knowing the lover to be absent at the appointed time, the clever woman, with a hint barely placed in her glance, playfully closed a lotus. //531//}

children.text: atra jijñāsitaḥ saṃketakālaḥ kayācidiṅgitamātreṇa vidito niśāsamayaśaṃsinā kamalanimīlanena līlayā pratipāditaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the appointed time was inquired about by some woman; [the answer] was known through a mere gesture; and it was playfully conveyed by the closing of a lotus, which signals the nighttime. //
When there is a successively ascending excellence, the climax is the ultimate limit — // <s>MKpr-K</s>_123 //

children.text: paraḥ paryantabhāgaḥ avadhiryasya dhārādhirohitayā tatraivotkarṣasya viśrānteḥ / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: The ultimate limit is the final point, because the ascending excellence comes to rest precisely there. Example —

children.text:
{rājye sāraṃ vasudhā vasudhāyāṃ puraṃ pure saudham /
  saudhe talpaṃ talpe varāṅganānaṅgasarvasvam //532//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 7.97)
{In kingship, the essence is the earth; on the earth, the city; in the city, the palace; in the palace, the bed; and on the bed, a beautiful woman — the very all of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Love). //532//}
When two properties that stand in the relation of cause and effect,
despite being in entirely different locations, are manifest simultaneously — that is <s>asaṃgati</s> (incongruity). // <s>MKpr-K</s>_124 //

children.text: iha yaddeśaṃ karaṇaṃ taddeśameva kāryamutpadyamānaṃ dṛṣṭam yathā dhūmādi / yatra tu hetuphalarūpayorapi dharmayoḥ kenāpyatiśayena nānādeśatayā yugapadavabhāsanaṃ sā tayoḥ svabhāvotpannaparasparasaṃgatityāgāt asaṃgatiḥ / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: Ordinarily, a cause produces an effect in the same location — as smoke and the like. But where two properties, though in the form of cause and effect, through some extraordinary [poetic power] are manifested simultaneously despite being in different locations — that is <s>asaṃgati</s> (incongruity), because [the properties] abandon their naturally occurring mutual connection. Example —

children.text:
{jasse_a vaṇo tasse_a ve_aṇā bhaṇai taṃ jaṇo ali_aṃ /
  dantakkha_aṃ kavole bahu_e ve_aṇā savattīṇaṃ //533//}

children.translated_text: [Whoever has the wound, that person alone has the pain — so says the world falsely;
The bite-mark is on the bride's cheek, [but] the pain is felt by the co-wives. //]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 981)
{Whoever has the wound, that person alone has the pain — so says the world falsely.

children.text: eṣā ca virodhabādhinī na virodhaḥ bhinnādharatayaiva dvayoriha virodhitāyāḥ pratibhāsāt / virodhe tu virodhitvam ekāśrayaniṣṭamanuktamapi paryavasitam apavādaviṣayaparihāreṇotsargasya vyavasthiteḥ / tathā caivaṃ nidarśitam //124//
children.translated_text: And this [figure] overrides [apparent] contradiction — it is not [mere] contradiction (<s>virodha</s>), because the contradictoriness of the two is perceived precisely through their being in different substrata. In [actual] contradiction, the contradictoriness resides in a single substratum — though unstated, this is the established conclusion, since the general rule holds after setting aside the domain of the exception. And thus it has been illustrated. //124//
<s>Samādhi</s> (resolution) is [when] a difficult task is accomplished through the conjunction of an additional means.

children.text: sādhanāntaropakṛtena kartrā yat akleśena kāryamārabdhaṃ samādhīyate sa samādhirnāma / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: When an agent, assisted by another means, commences and accomplishes a task without difficulty — that is called <s>samādhi</s> (resolution). Example —

children.text:
{mānamasyā nirākartuṃ pādayorme patiṣyataḥ /
  upakārāya diṣṭyedamudīrṇaṃ ghanagarjitam //534//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Daṇḍin</s>'s <s>Kāvyādarśa</s> 2.299)
{To remove her pride, my feet are about to fall [at hers] — fortunately, this thunder of clouds has arisen, to [serve as] an aid! //534//}

children.text: samaṃ yogyatayā yogo yadi saṃbhāvitaḥ kvacit // MKpr-K_125 //
children.translated_text: When a conjunction is imagined of those that are equal in fitness — // <s>MKpr-K</s>_125 //

children.text: idamanayoḥ ślāghyamiti yogyatayā saṃbandhasya niyataviṣayamadhyavasānaṃ cettadā samam tat sadyoge 'sadyoge ca //
children.translated_text: When, regarding 'this [pair] is praiseworthy,' the decisive conclusion is that their connection is confined to a specific domain of fitness — that is <s>sama</s> (equal pairing), whether the conjunction actually exists or does not exist.
Example —

children.text:
{dhātuḥ śilpātiśayanikaṣasthānameṣā mṛgākṣī
  rūpe devo 'pyayamanupamo dattapatraḥ smarasya /
  jātaṃ daivātsadṛśamanayoḥ saṃgataṃ yat tadeta-
  cchṛṅgārasyopanatamadhunā rājyamekātapatram //535//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{This doe-eyed woman is the touchstone for the Creator's supreme artistry in form; and this god too, [being] incomparable, holds the credentials of <s>Smara</s> (the god of Love). That by fate a fitting union of these two has come about — this is the unopposed sovereignty of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment) that has now presented itself! //535//}

children.text:
{citraṃ citraṃ bata bata mahaccitrametadvicitraṃ
  jāto daivāducitaracanāsaṃvidhātā vidhātā /
  yannimbānāṃ pariṇataphalasphītirāsvādanīyā
  yaccaitasyāḥ kavalanakalākovidaḥ kākalokaḥ //536//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{How wondrous, how wondrous — truly, exceedingly, extraordinarily wondrous! The Creator, who by fate fashioned [things] with fitting arrangement — [has ordained] that the ripened, abundant fruits of the neem trees are [meant] to be relished, and that the community of crows is expert in the art of biting into them! //536//}
Sometimes, when due to extreme dissimilarity, <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre) cannot achieve a connection,
and when the agent fails to obtain the fruit of the action and indeed incurs misfortune — // <s>MKpr-K</s>_126 //
When the qualities and actions of the effect are contrary to the qualities and actions of its cause,

children.text: krameṇa ca viruddhe yat sa eṣa viṣamo mataḥ // MKpr-K_127 //
children.translated_text: and [this contrariety is presented] in sequence — that is known as <s>viṣama</s> (disparity). // <s>MKpr-K</s>_127 //

children.text: dvayoratyantavilakṣaṇatayā yat anupapadyamānatayaiva yogaḥ pratīyate (1) yacca kiñcidārabhamāṇaḥ kartā kriyāyāḥ praṇāśāt na kevalamabhīṣṭaṃ yat phalaṃ na labhet yāvadaprārthitamapyanarthaṃ viṣayamāsādayet (2) tathā satyapi kāryasya kāraṇarūpānukāre tat tayorguṇau kriye ca parasparaṃ viruddhatāṃ vrajataḥ (3/4) sa samaviparyayātmā catūrūpo viṣamaḥ //
children.translated_text: When the conjunction of two utterly dissimilar things is perceived as itself impossible — (1); and when an agent, upon commencing some [action], through the destruction of the action, not only fails to obtain the desired fruit but even encounters an undesired misfortune — (2); and furthermore, when despite the effect's resemblance to the cause in form, the qualities and actions of the two become mutually contrary — (3/4): this <s>viṣama</s> (disparity), of the nature of agreement and reversal, is of four kinds. //
Examples in order —

children.text:
{śirīṣādapi mṛdvaṅgī kveyamāyatalocanā /
  ayaṃ kva ca kukūlāgnikarkaśo madanānalaḥ //537//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Padmagupta</s>'s <s>Navasāhasāṅkacarita</s> 1.28)
{Her limbs are softer even than a <s>śirīṣa</s> flower — how [can] this large-eyed woman [endure]? And how [can] this fire of passion, harsh as a chaff-fire, [be reconciled with her]? //537//}

children.text:
{siṃhikāsutasaṃtrastaḥ śaśaḥ śītāṃśumāśritaḥ /
  jagrase sāśrayaṃ tatra tamanyaḥ siṃhikāsutaḥ //538//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 303)

{The hare, frightened by the son of <s>Siṃhikā</s> (<s>Rāhu</s>), took refuge in the cool-rayed [moon]; but there, another son of <s>Siṃhikā</s> (<s>Rāhu</s>) swallowed him together with his refuge. //538//}

children.text:
{sadyaḥkarasparśamavāpya citraṃ raṇe raṇe yasya kṛpāṇalekhā /
  tamālanīlā śaradindupāṇḍu yaśastrilokyābharaṇaṃ prasūte //539//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Padmagupta</s>'s <s>Navasāhasāṅkacarita</s> 1.62)

{Wondrous it is — upon obtaining the touch of his hand in every battle, his sword-edge, dark as a <s>tamāla</s> tree, produces fame that is white as the autumn moon — the ornament of the three worlds! //539//}

children.text:
{ānandamamandamimaṃ kuvalayadalalocane dadāsi tvam /
  virahastvayaiva janitastāpayatitarāṃ śarīraṃ me //540//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 9.47)
{O blue-lotus-eyed one, you bestow this abundant and full joy — yet separation, caused by you alone, burns my body all the more! //540//}

Here, the giving of joy is contradicted by the burning of the body.
Likewise:

children.text:
{vipulena sāgaraśayasya kukṣiṇā bhuvanāni yasya papire yugakṣaye /
  madavibhramāsakalayā pape punaḥ sa purastriyaikatamayaikayā dṛśā //541//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Māgha</s>'s <s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 13.40)

{He who, at the end of the cosmic age, with his vast belly, drank up the worlds as they lay on the waters — that same [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] was in turn drunk up by a single glance, not even complete, of a single city-woman, cast with the wandering of intoxication. //541//}
In such [examples] too, the disparity (<s>viṣamatva</s>) should be understood as appropriate to each case. //127//
When, of a great [thing], something still greater — and of the container and the contained, in sequence —

children.text: āśrayāśrayiṇau syātāṃ tanutve 'pyadhikaṃ tu tat // MKpr-K_128 //
children.translated_text: become the container and the contained [respectively], and even in smallness [surpass] to an even greater degree — that is [the figure called] <s>adhika</s> (excess). // <s>MKpr-K</s>_128 //

children.text:
āśritam ādheyam āśrayastadādhāraḥ / tayormahatorapi viṣaye tadapekṣayā tanū apyāśrayāśrayiṇau prastutavastuprakarṣaviavkṣayā yathākramaṃ yat adhikataratāṃ vrajataḥ / tadidaṃ dvividham adhikaṃ nāma /
krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text:
The contained (<s>āśrita</s>) is the thing supported; the container (<s>āśraya</s>) is its support. When, in the domain of two great things, even things that are small in comparison to them become the container and the contained — with the intention of expressing the excellence of the subject at hand, [the small things] successively attain the status of being even greater. This [figure called] <s>adhika</s> (excess) is of two kinds.
Examples in order —

children.text:
{aho viśālaṃ bhūpāla bhuvanatritayodaram /
  māti mātumaśakyo 'pi yaśorāśiryadatra te //542//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Daṇḍin</s>'s <s>Kāvyādarśa</s> 2.297)
{Ah, vast indeed, O king, is the belly of the triple world — yet your mass of fame, though incapable of being measured, shines within it! //542//}

children.text:
{yugāntakālapratisaṃhṛtātmano jaganti yasyāṃ savikāśamāsata /
  tanau manustatra na kaiṭabhadviṣastapodhanābhyāgamasaṃbhavā mudaḥ //543//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Māgha</s>'s <s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 1.23)

{The worlds, whose forms had been withdrawn at the end of the cosmic age, found full expansion within his body — yet even there, the joys born from the arrival of the ascetics did not find room in the body of the enemy of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>). //543//}
When one who is unable to retaliate against an adversary resorts to disparagement,

children.text: yā tadīyasya tatstutyai pratyanīkaṃ taducyate // MKpr-K_129 //
children.translated_text: and [the disparagement] of something belonging to [the adversary] is for the purpose of praising [the adversary] — that is called <s>pratyanīka</s> (adversarial praise). // <s>MKpr-K</s>_129 //

children.text: nyakkṛtiparamapi vipakṣaṃ sākṣānnirasitumaśaktena kenāpi yat tameva pratipakṣamutkarṣayituṃ tadāśritasya tiraskaraṇam tat anīkapratinidhitulyatvāt pratyanīkamabhidhīyate / yathā anīke abhiyojye tatpratinidhībhūtamaparaṃ mūḍhatayā kenacidabhiyujyate tatheha pratiyogini vijeye tadīyonyo vijīyate ityarthaḥ / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: <s>Pratyanīka</s> (counter-troop): when someone is unable to directly defeat an adversary who is supremely humiliated, [and so] in order to exalt that very opponent, the disparagement of something associated with [the adversary] occurs — this is called <s>pratyanīka</s>, because of the analogy with [attacking] a substitute in battle. Just as in battle, when the [actual] foe to be engaged cannot be [fought], someone else — a substitute — is foolishly attacked, so here, when the rival [who deserves to be] conquered [cannot be conquered], another associated with him is [instead] defeated — that is the meaning. Example:

children.text:
{tvaṃ vinirjitamanobhavarūpaḥ sā ca sundara bhavatyanuraktā /
  pañcabhiryugapadeva śaraistāṃ tāpayatyanuśayādiva kāmaḥ //544//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 306)

{You have conquered the form of <s>Manobhava</s> (the god of love), and she, O handsome one, is enamored of you — yet <s>Kāma</s>, as if out of regret, torments her with all five arrows simultaneously! //544//}
Or alternatively:

children.text:
{yasya kiñcidapakartumakṣamaḥ kāyanigrahagṛhītavigrahaḥ /
  kāntavaktrasadṛśākṛtiṃ kṛtī rāhurindumadhunāpi bādhate //545//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Māgha</s>'s <s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 14.78)
{Unable to do anything to him, whose body is restrained by bodily austerity, <s>Rāhu</s>, skilled [as he is], now afflicts the moon — whose form resembles the lovely face [of the hero]. //545//}
Here, the connection of the moon [to the hero] is through the relation of a relative's relative. //129//
When a thing is concealed by another thing through a mark (<s>lakṣmaṇā</s>) that is equal [to both] —
whether inherent or adventitious — that is known as <s>mīlita</s> (concealment). // <s>MKpr-K</s>_130 //

children.text: sahajam āgantukaṃ vā kimapi sādhāraṇaṃ yat lakṣaṇam taddvāreṇa yat kiñcit kenacidvastu vastusthityaiva valīyastayā tirodhīyate tat mīlitamiti dvidhā smaranti //
children.translated_text: When some inherent or adventitious characteristic that is common [to both] serves as the means by which some thing is, by the very nature of things, concealed by another thing more powerful [than it] through that [shared characteristic] — that is known as <s>mīlita</s>, and is of two kinds.

children.text:
{apāṅgatarale dṛśau madhuravakravarṇāgiro
  vilāsabharamantharā gatiratīva kāntaṃ mukham /
  iti sphuritamaṅgake mṛgadṛśaḥsvato līlayā
  tadatra na madodayaḥ kṛtapado 'pi saṃlakṣyate //546//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{The eyes with darting sidelong glances, speech with sweet, curved syllables, the gait heavy-languid with the weight of coquetry, the face exceedingly lovely — thus the signs that manifest spontaneously upon the limbs of the doe-eyed one through her own playful nature — so here, even though the intoxication of love has taken hold, it is not perceived [as such]. //546//}

children.text: atra dṛktaralatādikamaṅgasya liṅgaṃ svābhāvikaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ ca mahodayena tatrāpyetasya darśanāt /
children.translated_text: Here, the darting of the eyes and the like — these are inherent and common marks of the limbs, since they are observed even in the intoxication of love [and so the cause is concealed].

children.text:
{ye kandarāsu nivasanti sadā himādres
  tvatpātaśaṅkitadhiyo vivaśā dviṣaste /
  apyaṅgamutpulakamudvahatāṃ sakampaṃ
  teṣāmaho bata bhiyāṃ na budho 'pyabhijñaḥ //547//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>)

{Your enemies, their minds terrified by the fear of your attack, who dwell always in the caves of the <s>Himālaya</s> — though they bear limbs bristling with horripilation and trembling — even the wise, alas, cannot identify [these signs as those] of fear! //547//}

children.text: atra tu sāmarthyādavasitasya śaityasya āgantukatvāttatprabhavayorapi kampapulakayostādrūpyaṃ samānatā ca bhayeṣvapi tayorupalakṣitatvāt //130//
children.translated_text: Here, however, the coldness — inferred from the context — is adventitious, and therefore the trembling and horripilation produced by it also have that character; and since trembling and horripilation are also observed in [the context of] fear, there is equality [of the marks]. //130//
Where one thing after another is either established or removed

children.text: viśeṣaṇatayā yatra vastu saikāvalī dvidhā // MKpr-K_131 //
children.translated_text: in the capacity of a qualifier with respect to each preceding [thing] — that is <s>ekāvalī</s> (single strand), of two kinds. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_131 //

children.text: pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ prati yathottarasya vastuno vīpsayā viśeṣaṇabhāvena yat sthāpanaṃ niṣedho vā saṃbhavati sā dvidhā budhairekāvalī bhaṇyate / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: Where, with respect to each preceding [thing], the establishing or negating of the succeeding thing in the capacity of a qualifier occurs through reiteration (<s>vīpsā</s>) — that is called <s>ekāvalī</s> by the wise, of two kinds. Examples in order:

children.text:
{purāṇi yasyāṃ savarāṅganāni varāṅganā rūpapuraskṛtāṅgyaḥ /
  rūpaṃ samunmīlitasadvilāsamastraṃ vilāsaḥ kusumāyudhasya //548//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Padmagupta</s>'s <s>Navasāhasāṅkacarita</s> 1.22)

{In that [city], the dwellings [are adorned with] beautiful women; the beautiful women have their limbs distinguished by beauty; beauty has elegant grace fully unfolded; and grace is the weapon of the flower-armed one (<s>Kāma</s>)! //548//}

children.text:
{na tajjalaṃ yanna sucārupaṅkajaṃ
  napaṅkajaṃ tad yadalīnaṣaṭpadam /
  ca ṣaṭpado 'sau kalaguñjito na yo
  na guñjitaṃ tanna jahāra yanmanaḥ //549//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhaṭṭikāvya</s> 2.19)

{That is not [true] water which has no beautiful lotus; that is not a [true] lotus which has no bee settled upon it; that bee is not [a true one] which does not hum melodiously; and that humming is not [true] which does not steal the mind. //549//}

children.text: pūrvatra purāṇāṃ varāṅganāḥ tāsāmaṅgaviśeṣaṇamukhena rūpam tasya vilāsāḥ teṣāmapyastramityamunā krameṇa viśeṣaṇaṃ vidhīyate / uttaratra pratiṣedhe 'pyevaṃ yojyam //131//
children.translated_text: In the former [example], the beautiful women are the qualifiers of the dwellings; beauty is [the qualifier] of their limbs, through the medium of the body-part qualifier; graces [qualify] beauty; and weapons [qualify] the graces — thus, in this sequence, the qualification is made. In the latter [example], the same pattern should be applied with negation. //131//
The recollection of a thing as experienced — when a similar one is seen —

children.text: yaḥ padārthaḥ kenacidākāreṇa niyataḥ yadā kadācit anubhūto 'bhūt sa kālāntare smṛtipratibodhādhāyini tatsamāne vastuni dṛṣṭe sati yat tathaiva smaryate tat bhavet smaraṇam / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: An object that was once experienced at some time in a particular form — when, at a later time, a similar thing that awakens recollection is seen, and it is remembered in just that way — that is <s>smaraṇa</s> (recollection). Example:

children.text:
{nimnanābhikuhareṣu yadambhaḥ plāvitaṃ caladṛśāṃ laharībhiḥ /
  tadbhavaiḥ kuharutaiḥ suranāryaḥ smāritā suratakaṇṭharutānām //550//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 310)

{The water flooding the low navel-hollows, agitated by the waves of the moving-eyed [river] — through its gurgling sounds, the celestial women are reminded of the throat-sounds of lovemaking. //550//}
Or alternatively:
[Salutations to the horripilation of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who has placed his lip upon the mouth of the breast of <s>Yaśodā</s>, grasped by his pair of hands —
he who has remembered the conch <s>Pāñcajanya</s>!]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 974)

{Salutations to the horripilation of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who has placed his lip upon the mouth of the breast of <s>Yaśodā</s>, grasped by his pair of hands — he who has remembered the conch <s>Pāñcajanya</s>! //551//}
... <s>bhrāntimān</s> (the deluded) — cognition of another [thing] upon seeing something similar [to it]. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_132 //

children.text:
taditi anyat aprākaraṇikaṃ nirdiśyate / tena samānam arthādiha prākaraṇikam āśrīyate / tasya tathāvidhasya dṛṣṭau satyāṃ yat aprākaraṇikatayā saṃvedanaṃ sa bhrāntimān /
na caiṣa rūpakaṃ prathamātiśayoktirvā tatra vastuto bhramasyābhāvāt iha ca, arthānugamanena saṃjñāyāḥ pravṛtteḥ tasya spaṣṭameva pratipannatvāt / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: 'That' — another, non-contextual [thing] is indicated. By 'similar' — the contextual [thing] is intended here. When that [similar thing] is seen, the cognition [takes it] as the non-contextual [thing] — that is <s>bhrāntimān</s>. This is neither <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) nor the first [type of] <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) — because in the former there is in reality no delusion, and in the latter [there is delusion only figuratively]; while here, the designation [<s>bhrāntimān</s>] is established by following the course of the [stated] meaning, since [the delusion] is clearly presented as such. Example:

children.text:
{kapāle mārjāraḥ paya iti karān leḍhi śaśinas
  tarucchidraprotān bisamiti karī saṃkalayati /
  ratānte talpasthān harati vanitāpyaṃśukamiti
  prabhāmattaścandro jagadidamaho viplavayati //552//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhoja</s>'s <s>Sarasvatīkaṇṭhābharaṇa</s> 3.38; <s>Subhāṣitaratnākara</s> 905)

{The cat licks the skull-cup thinking 'it is milk'; the elephant gathers the tree-filtered [moonbeams] thinking 'these are lotus stems'; and at the end of lovemaking, the woman snatches from the bed [the moonbeams] thinking 'these are garments' — the moon, intoxicated with its own radiance, ah, throws this whole world into confusion! //552//}
The <s>ākṣepa</s> (repudiation) of the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) — [is when] the <s>upameya</s> (comparandum) is treated as the [true] standard;

children.text: tasyaiva yadi vā kalpyā tiraskāranibandhanam // MKpr-K_133 //
children.translated_text: or if that very [comparandum] is to be fashioned [as inferior], it serves as the basis for disparagement — [this is] <s>pratīpa</s> (reversal). // <s>MKpr-K</s>_133 //

children.text: asya dhuraṃ sutarāmupameyameva voḍhuṃ prauḍhamiti kaimarthyena yat upamānamākṣipyate yadapi tasyaivopamānatayā prasiddhasya upamānāntaravivakṣayānādarārthamupameyabhāvaḥ kalpyate tat upameyasyopamānapratikūlavartitvāt ubhyarūpaṃ pratīpam / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: When the <s>upameya</s> (comparandum) alone is more than capable of bearing the burden [of the comparison], and the <s>upamāna</s> (standard) is repudiated as superfluous; or when the well-known standard of comparison is to be treated with disdain through the intention to replace it with another standard, and is therefore fashioned as a comparandum — in both cases, since the comparandum operates contrary to the standard of comparison, it is <s>pratīpa</s> (reversal) in both forms. Examples in order:

children.text:
{lāvaṇyaukasi sapratāpagarimaṇyagresare tyāgināṃ
  deva tvayyavanībharakṣamabhuje niṣpādite vedhasā /
  induḥ kiṃ ghaṭitaḥ kimeṣa vihitaḥ pūṣā kimutpāditaṃ
  cintāratnamado mudhaiva kimamī sṛṣṭāḥ kulakṣmābhṛtaḥ //553//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{O abode of charm, bearing the majesty of valor, foremost among the generous, O god, you whose arm — capable of bearing the burden of the earth — was fashioned by the Creator: was the moon fashioned [for anything]? Was this sun created [for anything]? Was the wish-fulfilling gem produced [for anything]? Alas, were these hereditary mountain-kings created in vain? //553//}

children.text:
{e ehi dāva sundari kaṇṇaṃ dāūṇa suṇasu vaaṇijjaṃ /
  tujjha muheṇa kisoari cando uamijjai jaṇeṇa //554//}
[ayi ehi tāvat sundari karṇandattvā śṛṇuṣva vacanīyam /
children.translated_text: [Come, O beautiful one, first give me your ear and hear what must be said —

children.text: tava mukhena kṛśodari candra upamīyate janena //]
children.translated_text: O slender girl, by your face, the moon is compared by people!]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 972)
{Come, O beautiful one, first give me your ear and hear what must be said — O slender girl, by your face, the moon is compared by people [to you]! //554//}

children.text: atra mukhenopamīyamānasya śaśinaḥ svalpataraguṇatvāt upamityaniṣpattyā 'va_aṇijjaṃ'; iti vacanīyapadābhivyaṅgyastiraskāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, since the moon — being compared to the face — has far inferior qualities, the comparison itself fails to materialize; and the disparagement — suggested by the word 'what must be said' (<s>vacanīya</s>) — [is the point].
In some cases, however, the act of comparison is indeed accomplished — [and] the disdain is the [resulting] foundation. For example:

children.text:
{garvamasaṃvāhyamimaṃ locranayugalena kiṃ vahasi mugdhe /
  santīdṛśāni diśi diśi sarassu nanu nīlanalināni //555//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 8.78)
{O innocent one, why do you carry this pride in your pair of eyes, so great as to be beyond massage? There are, in every direction, such things as blue lotuses in the ponds! //555//}

children.text:
ihopameyīkaraṇamevotpalānāmanādaraḥ /
anayaiva rītyā yat asāmānyaguṇayogāt nopamānabhāvamapi anubhūtapūrvi tasya tatkalpanāyāmapi bhavati pratīpamiti pratyetavyam / yathā
children.translated_text: Here, the very act of making the lotuses a comparandum constitutes the disdain. By this same method, it should be understood that even when something that has never before been experienced as a standard of comparison — due to the possession of uncommon qualities — is yet fashioned as one, that too is <s>pratīpa</s>. For example:

children.text:
{ahameva guruḥ sudāruṇānām
  iti hālāhala tāta mā sma dṛpyaḥ /
  nanu santi bhavādṛśāni bhūyo
  bhuvanesmin vacanāni durjanānām //556//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

{O <s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison), father, do not be proud [thinking] 'I alone am the foremost of the terribly cruel!' — for indeed, there are plenty more in this world like you: the words of wicked people! //556//}
Here, the comparison-standard status of <s>hālāhala</s> is utterly inconceivable — yet it has been composed [as such].
When the subject at hand is, through the intention of [showing] equality of quality with another,
bound in identity with [that other] by virtue of [their] connection — that is known as <s>sāmānya</s> (generality). // <s>MKpr-K</s>_134 //

children.text: atādṛśamapi tādṛśatayā vivakṣituṃ yat aprastutārthena saṃpṛktamaparityaktanijaguṇameva tadekātmatayā nibadhyate tat samānaguṇanibandhanāt sāmānyam / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: When something that is not actually of such a nature is, with the intention of presenting it as such, bound in identity with a non-contextual thing — without abandoning its own qualities — by virtue of connection, that is <s>sāmānya</s>, because it is founded on a common quality. Example:

children.text:
{malayajarasaviliptanavo navahāralatāvibhūṣitāḥ
  sitataradantapatra kṛtavaktraruco rucirāmalāṃśukāḥ /
  śaśabhṛti vitatadhāmni dhavalayati dharāmavibhāvyatāṃ gatāḥ /
  priyavasatiṃ prayānti sukhameva nirastabhiyo 'bhisārikāḥ //557//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vāmana</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 4.3.10)

{Freshly anointed with sandalwood paste, adorned with new pearl necklaces, their faces beautified with white <s>dantapatra</s> (tooth-decoration), wearing radiant white garments — when the hare-bearing moon diffuses its extensive light and whitens the earth — having passed beyond perception, the <s>abhisārikā</s> heroines go happily to the dwelling of their beloved, free from fear. //557//}

children.text: atra prastutatadanyayoranyūnānatiriktatayā nibaddhaṃ dhavalatvamekātmatāhetuḥ / ata eva pṛthagbhāvena na tayorupalakṣaṇam / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, whiteness — bound as neither deficient nor excessive between the contextual and the non-contextual — is the cause of identity. Precisely for this reason, they are not separately perceived [as distinct]. Or alternatively:

children.text:
{vetratvacā tulyarucāṃ cadhūnāṃ karṇāgrato gaṇḍatalāgatāni /
  bhṛṅgā sahelaṃ yadi nāpatiṣyan kovedayiṣyannavacampakāni //558//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 311)

{If bees had not playfully alighted upon the <s>campaka</s> blossoms, fresh and arrived at the cheek from before the ear, with a luster equal to that of <s>vetra</s> (cane) bark — who would have recognized the new <s>campakas</s>? //558//}

children.text: atra nimittāntarajanitāpi nānātvapratītiḥ prathamapratipannamabhedaṃ na vyudsitumutsahate pratītatvāttasya pratīteśca bādhāyogāt //
children.translated_text: Here, even though the perception of difference is generated by another cause, the non-difference that was first apprehended cannot be dislodged — because it has already been cognized, and because a cognition [once arisen] is not subject to sublation.
The situation of the superimposed [attribute] without its well-known substratum;
the existence of one thing as identical [with another]; the occurrence of one thing in multiple loci — // <s>MKpr-K</s>_135 //
when another thing accomplishes the deed of something that is [otherwise] incapable [of doing it];

children.text: tathaiva karaṇaṃ ceti viśeṣastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ // MKpr-K_136 //
children.translated_text: and likewise the instrumentality [of another] — thus <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularity) is recognized as of three kinds. // <s>MKpr-K</s>_136 //

children.text:
prasiddhārdhaparihāreṇa yat ādheyasya viśiṣṭā sthitirabhidhīyate sa prathamo viśeṣaḥ /
udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: The first <s>viśeṣa</s> is when, by the removal of the well-known substratum, a distinctive situation of the superimposed [attribute] is described. Example:

children.text:
{divamapyupayātānāmākalpamanalpaguṇagaṇā yeṣām /
  ramayanti jaganti giraḥ kathamiha kavayo na te vandyāḥ //559//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 9.6)

{Even of those who have gone to heaven, the words — possessing no small host of qualities — delight the worlds until the end of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age); how then should those poets not be venerated here? //559//}

children.text: evamapi vastu yat ekenaiva svabhāvena yugapadanekatra vartate sa dvitīyaḥ / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: The second type is when a single thing, by its very nature, exists simultaneously in multiple loci. Example:

children.text:
{sā vasai tujjha hiae sā ccia acchīsu sā a vaaṇesu /
  ahmārisāṇa sundara osāso kattha pāvāṇaṃ //560//}
[sā vasati tava hṛdaye saivākṣiṣu sā ca vacaneṣu /
children.translated_text: [She dwells in your heart, she herself is in your eyes, and she is in your words —
O handsome one, where is there room for wretched ones like us?]
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 947)
{She dwells in your heart, she herself is in your eyes, and she is in your words too — O handsome one, where is there room for wretched ones like us? //560//}

children.text: yadyapi kiñcidrabhasena ārabhamāṇastenaiva yatnenāśakyamapi kāryāntaramārabhate soparo viśeṣaḥ / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: The third type of <s>viśeṣa</s> is when one who begins something with a certain impetuosity, by that very effort also undertakes another task that would [otherwise] be impossible. Example:

children.text:
{sphuradadbhutarūpamutpratāpajvalanaṃ tvāṃ sṛjatānavadyavidyam /
  vidhinā sasṛje navo manobhūrbhuvisatyaṃ savitā vṛhaspatiśca //561//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 315)

{While creating you — of wondrous, radiant form, blazing with fiery valor, of faultless knowledge — the Creator [simultaneously] created a new god of love, a new sun, and a new <s>Bṛhaspati</s> upon the earth! //561//}
Or alternatively:

children.text:
{gṛhiṇī sacivaḥ sakhī mithaḥ priyaśiṣyā lalite kalāvidhau /
  karuṇāvimukhena mṛtyunā haratā tvāṃ bata kiṃ na me hṛtam //562//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa</s>'s <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 8.67)

{Wife, counselor, friend, confidante, skilled pupil in the graceful art [of the <s>kalās</s>] — by Death, cruel and devoid of compassion, taking you away, alas, what has not been taken from me? //562//}

children.text: sarvatra evaṃvidhaviṣaye 'tiśayoktireva prāṇatvenāvatiṣṭhate tāṃ vinā prāueṇālaṅkāratvāyogāt / ata evoktam

children.translated_text: {This very <s>vakrokti</s> (indirect/crooked speech) is present everywhere; through it, meaning is illuminated;

children.text: yatnosyāṃ kavinā kāryaḥ ko 'laṅkāro 'nayā vinā //} iti //
children.translated_text: effort should be made by the poet in this regard — what <s>alaṃkāra</s> exists without it?}
In all cases of this kind, <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) stands as the very life-force — because without it, there would generally be no [status as an] <s>alaṃkāra</s>. Therefore it has been said:
When a thing, through proximity to [another thing of] exceedingly brilliant quality, abandons its own quality

children.text: vastu tadguṇatāmeti bhaṇyate sa tu tadguṇaḥ // MKpr-K_137 //
children.translated_text: and attains the quality of that [other thing] — that is called <s>tadguṇa</s> (possessing the quality of another). // <s>MKpr-K</s>_137 //

children.text: vastu tiraskṛtanijarūpaṃ kenāpi samīpagatena praguṇayā svaguṇasaṃpadoparaktaṃ tatpratibhāsameva yatsamāsādayati sa tadguṇaḥ / tasyāprakṛtasya guṇotrāstīti / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: When a thing, its own nature eclipsed, is, through the nearness of something else, colored by the superior splendor of that [other thing's] qualities, and comes to appear as that very [other thing] — that is <s>tadguṇa</s>. For 'that non-contextual thing's quality is present here' — [hence the name]. Example:

children.text:
{vibhinnavarṇā garuḍāgrajena sūryasya rathyāḥ paritaḥ sphurantyā /
  ratnaiḥ punaryatra rucā rucaṃ svāmāninyire vaṃśakarīranīlaiḥ //563//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Māgha</s>'s <s>Śiśupālavadha</s>, Nirnaya Sagar Press, 4.14)

Of various hues, by the elder brother of <s>Garuḍa</s> [i.e., <s>Aruṇa</s>, the sun's charioteer], all around — of the radiant path of the sun — the gems, with their brilliance, again mimicked their own luster with the deep blue of their bamboo-thickets. || 563 ||

children.text: atra ravituragāpekṣayā garuḍāgrajasya tadapekṣayā ca harinmaṇīnāṃ praguṇavarṇatā //137//
children.translated_text: Here, in relation to the sun's horse [<s>Aruṇa</s>], the elder brother of <s>Garuḍa</s>, and in relation to him, the emeralds — [there is] a superior color. || 137 ||
If there is no imitation of that form by this — that would be <s>atadguṇa</s> (absence of the quality of that).

children.text: yadi tu tadīyaṃ varṇaṃ saṃbhavantyāmapi yogyatāyām idaṃ nyūnaguṇaṃ na gṛhaṇīyāt tadā bhavedatadguṇo nāma / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: If, however, even though the capacity for taking on the color of that [other entity] exists, this one does not take on the inferior quality — then it would be the [figure] called <s>atadguṇa</s>. Example:

children.text:
{dhavalosi jahavi sundara taha vi tue majjha rañjiaṃ hiaaṃ /
  rāabharievi hiae suhaa ṇihitto ṇa rattosi //564//}
[dhvalo 'si yadyapi sundara tathāpi tvayā mama rañjitaṃ hṛdayam /
children.translated_text: [Chāyā:] You are white, O handsome one; yet even so, my heart has been colored by you.

children.text: rāgabharite 'pi hṛdaye subhaga nihito na rakto 'si //]
children.translated_text: Even though placed in a heart filled with passion, O dear one, you are not red.
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> [665, 7-64])
You are white, O handsome one; yet even so, my heart has been colored by you. Even though placed in a heart filled with passion, you are not red. || 564 ||

children.text: atrātiraktenāpi manasā saṃyukto na raktatāmupagata ityatadguṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, though united with a mind that is exceedingly impassioned, he has not attained redness — thus [this is] <s>atadguṇa</s>.

children.text: kiñca taditi aprakṛtam asyeti ca prakṛtamatra nirdiśyate / tena yat aprakṛtasya rūpaṃ prakṛtena kutp'pi nimittāt nānuvidhīyate so 'tadaguṇa ityapi pratipattavyam / yathā
children.translated_text: Moreover, 'tat' (that) designates the non-contextual [entity], and 'asya' (of this) designates the contextual [entity]. Therefore, when the form of the non-contextual [entity] is not followed by the contextual one for some reason — that too should be understood as <s>atadguṇa</s>. As in:

children.text:
{gāṅgamambu sitamambu yāmunaṃ kajjalābhamubhayatra majjataḥ /
  rājahaṃsa tava saiva śubhratā cīyate na ca na cāpacīyate //565//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s>)
The water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is white; the water of the <s>Yamunā</s> is dark as collyrium — O royal swan, bathing in both, that very whiteness of yours neither increases nor decreases. || 565 ||
When what has been established in one way by one [element] is [shown to be] otherwise by another — || Kpr-K_138 ||

children.text: tathaiva yadvidhīyeta sa vyāghāta iti smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: that is remembered as <s>vyāghāta</s> (contradiction) when the same [thing] is so treated.

children.text: yenopāyena yat ekenopakalpitam tasyānyena jigīṣutayā tadupāyakameva yat anyathākaraṇam sa sādhitavastuvyāhatitetutvāt vyāghātaḥ / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: When something established by one means is made otherwise by another, desirous of conquering — that making-otherwise of the very means — that is <s>vyāghāta</s>, because of being the cause of the contradiction of the established fact. Example:

children.text:
{dṛśā dagdhaṃ manasijaṃ jīvayanti dṛśaiva yāḥ /
  virūpākṣasya jayinīstāḥ stuve vāmalocanāḥ //566//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rājaśekhara</s>'s <s>Viddhaśālabhañjikā</s> 1.4)

Those who burn <s>Manasija</s> (the Mind-born, <s>Kāma</s>) with their gaze, yet revive him with that very gaze — I praise those beautiful women with sidelong glances, who are victorious over <s>Virūpākṣa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). || 566 ||

children.text: seṣṭā saṃsṛṣṭireteṣāṃ bhedena yadiha sthitiḥ // MKpr-K_139 //
children.translated_text: The desired [figure] is <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination) of these — when [they] abide here as distinct. || Kpr-K_139 ||

children.text:
eteṣāṃ samanantaramevoktasvarūpāṇāṃ yathāsaṃbhavananyonyanirapekṣatayā yat ekatra śabdabhāge eva arthaviṣaye eva ubhayatrāpi vā avasthānam sā ekārthasamavāyasvabhāvā saṃsṛṣṭiḥ /
tatra śabdālaṅkārasaṃsṛṣṭiryathā
children.translated_text: Of these — whose natures have just been described — when, as applicable, they stand mutually independent in a single location, whether in the domain of word, or in the domain of meaning, or in both — that, having the nature of the co-occurrence of a single meaning, is <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination). Therein, the combination of word-figures, as in:
(<s>Māgha</s>'s <s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 6.14)

By another [maiden] — whose beauty was enhanced by the agitation of bees wandering in greed for the fragrance of her face, who moved with swaying [gait], with a girdle of bells tinkling, with eyes playfully rolling — he was entertained. || 567 ||
The combination of meaning-figures, however:

children.text:
{limpatīva tamoṅgāni varṣatīvāñjanaṃ nabhaḥ /
  asatpuruṣaseveva dṛṣṭirviphalatāṃ gatā //568[=417]//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śūdraka</s>'s <s>Mṛcchakaṭikā</s> 1.32)
It is as if darkness smears the limbs, as if the sky rains collyrium — vision has gone to futility, like the service of wicked men. || 568 [= 417] ||

children.text:
pūrvatra parasparanirapekṣau yamakānuprāsau saṃsṛṣṭiṃ prayojayataḥ uttaratra tu tathāvidhe upamotprekṣe /
śabdārthālaṅkārayostu saṃsṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: In the former [example], <s>yamaka</s> (chiming) and <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), being mutually independent, produce <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>. In the latter, <s>upamā</s> (simile) and <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) do likewise. The combination of a word-figure and a meaning-figure:

children.text:
{so ṇatthi ettha gāme jo e_aṃ mahamahantalā_aṇṇaṃ /
  taruṇāṇa hiaalūḍiṃ parisakkantīṃ ṇivāre_i //569//}
  [sa nāstyatra grāme ya enāṃ mahamahāyamānalāvaṇyām /
  taruṇānāṃ hṛdayaluṇṭhākiṃ pariṣvakkamāṇāṃ nivārayati /]

children.translated_text: (<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 997)

There is no one in this village who can restrain her — so greatly abounding in beauty — from roaming about, stealing the hearts of young men. || 569 || [Chāyā:] There is no one in this village who can restrain her — so greatly abounding in beauty — from roaming about, stealing the hearts of young men.

children.text: atrānuprāso rūpakaṃ cānyonyānapekṣe / saṃsargaśca tayorekatra vākye chandasi vā samavetatvāt //139//
children.translated_text: Here, <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) and <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) are mutually independent. And their conjunction [is saṃsṛṣṭi] because they are co-present in a single sentence or metrical unit. || 139 ||
<s>Saṃkara</s> (intermixture) is [the state] where those [figures], not resting independently within themselves, relate to each other as principal and subordinate.

children.text: ete eva yatrātmani anāsāditasvatantrabhāvāḥ prasparam anugrāhyānugrāhakatāṃ dadhati sa eṣāṃ saṃkīryamāṇasvarūpatvāt saṃkaraḥ / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: These very [figures], where they have not attained independent status within themselves [and instead] mutually assume the relationship of that-which-is-to-be-supported and that-which-supports — that, because of their natures being intermixed, is their <s>saṃkara</s> (intermixture). Example:

children.text:
{ātte sīmantaratne marakatini hṛte hematāṭaṅkapatre
  luptāyāṃ mekhalāyāṃ jhaṭiti maṇitulākoṭiyugme gṛhīte /
  śoṇaṃ bimboṣṭhakāntyā tvadarimṛgadṛśāmitvarīṇāmaraṇye
  rājan guñjāphalānāṃ sraja iti śabarā naiva hāraṃ haranti //570//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

When the emerald crest-jewel of the parting has been seized, when the gold ear-ornament leaf has been snatched, when the girdle has been stripped away, when the pair of jeweled scale-weights have been suddenly grasped — reddened by the luster of their bimba-fruit lips, O king, the women of your enemies in the forest — the <s>Śabaras</s> (forest-dwellers) do not steal their necklaces, [thinking them to be] garlands of guñjā berries. || 570 ||

children.text: atra tadguṇamapekṣya bhrāntimatā prādurbhūtam tadāśrayeṇa ca tadguṇaḥ sacetasāṃ prabhūtacamatkṛtinimittamityanayoraṅgāṅgibhāvaḥ / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, <s>bhrāntimān</s> (delusion) has come about dependent on <s>tadguṇa</s> (having the quality of that), and by its support, <s>tadguṇa</s> becomes the cause of great aesthetic wonder in sentient beings — thus there is a principal-subordinate relationship between the two. Or as in:

children.text:
{jaṭābhābhirbhābhiḥ karadhṛtakalaṅkākṣavalayo
  viyogivyāpatteriva kalitavairāgyaviśadaḥ /
  paripreṅkhattārāparikarakapālāṅkitatale
  śaśī bhasmāpāṇḍuḥ pitṛvana iva vyomni carati //571//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura</s>'s <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)

With the matted locks as his rays, with the blemish held in his hand as a string of prayer-beads, pale as if from the effect of the sorrow of separation, adorned with stars as a retinue of skull-ornaments on his circle-marked surface, the moon — ash-pale — wanders in the sky as if in a cremation ground. || 571 ||

children.text:
upamā rūpakam utprekṣā śleṣaśceti catvāro 'tra pūrvavat aṅgāṅgitayā pratīyante /
kalaṅka evākṣavalayamiti rūpakaparigrahe karadhṛtatvameva sādhakapramāṇatāṃ pratipadyate / asya hi rūpakatve tirohitakalaṅkarūpam akṣavalayameva mukhyatayāvagamyate tasyaiva ca karagrahaṇayogyatāyāṃ sārvatrikī prasiddhiḥ / śleṣacchāyayā tu kalaṅgasya kalaṅkasya mūrtyaiva udvahanāt / kalaṅko 'kṣavalayamiveti tu, upamāyāṃ
kalaṅkasya, utkaṭatayā pratipattiḥ / na cāsya karadhṛtatvaṃ tattvatostīti mukhye 'pyupacāra eva śaraṇaṃ syāt /
evaṃrūpaśca saṃkaraḥ śabdālaṅkārayorapi paridṛśyate / yathā
children.translated_text: <s>Upamā</s> (simile), <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), and <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre) — these four are perceived here as before in a principal-subordinate relationship. When the blemish itself is identified as a string of prayer-beads through <s>rūpaka</s>, the fact of being held in the hand alone attains the status of supporting evidence. For when this is a <s>rūpaka</s>, the form of the hidden blemish is primarily apprehended as the prayer-beads themselves, and of those very [beads], the well-known fitness for being grasped in the hand [is established]. But through the shade of <s>śleṣa</s>, because of bearing the blemish in its very form as blemish. 'The blemish is like prayer-beads' — with <s>upamā</s>, the blemish would be apprehended in its full prominence. But the fact of holding in the hand does not truly belong to [the blemish] — hence even in the primary [sense], figurative usage alone would be the recourse. Such <s>saṃkara</s> (intermixture) is also seen among word-figures. As in:

children.text:
{rājati taṭīyamabhihatadānavarāsātipātisārāvanadā /
  gajatā ca yūthamviratadānavarā sātipāti sārā vanadā //572//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ratnākara</s>'s <s>Haravijaya</s> 5.137)

The bank shines, with cries arising from the incessant falling of rain-streams dropping the rut-fluid; and the herd of elephants also [shines], with [those same words rearranged:] heroically, incessantly, spiritedly, as forest-dwellers. || 572 ||
Here, <s>yamaka</s> (chiming) and the <s>citra</s> (pictorial) variety of forward-and-reverse [reading] are mutually dependent in the pair of half-verses.
And when, upon accepting one [figure], there is no ground [for it] nor fault [in the other], there is indeterminacy. || Kpr-K_140 ||

children.text:
dvayorbahūnāṃ vā alaṅkārāṇāmekatra samāveśe 'pi virodhāt na yatra yugapadavasthānam na caikatarasya parigrahe sādhakam taditarasya vā parihāre bādhakamasti yenaikatara eva parigṛhyate sa niścayābhāvārūpo
dvitīyaḥ saṃkaraḥ samuccayena saṃkarasyaivākṣepāt / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: Even when two or many figures are co-present in a single location, where — because of mutual conflict — there is no simultaneous existence, and where upon accepting one there is no supporting evidence, nor upon rejecting the other is there any invalidating [evidence], by which one alone would be accepted — that, in the form of the absence of determinacy, is the second [type of] <s>saṃkara</s>; since mere aggregation implies the intermixture of the <s>saṃkara</s> itself. Example:

children.text:
{jaha gahiro jaha raaṇaṇivbharo jaha a ṇimmalacchāo /
  taha kiṃ vihiṇā eso sarasavāṇīo jalaṇihī ṇa kio //573//}
[yathā gabhīro yathā ratnanirbharo yathā ca nirmalacchāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Chāyā:] as deep, as gem-laden, and as clear in reflection —

children.text: tathā kiṃ vidhinā eṣa sarasapānīyo jalanidhirna krṭaḥ //]
children.translated_text: why was this one, with sweet waters, not made by the Creator as an ocean?
(<s>Hāla</s>'s <s>Gāthāsaptaśatī</s> 976)
As deep, as gem-laden, and as clear in reflection —

children.text: atra samudre prastute viśeṣaṇasāmyādaprastutārthapratīteḥ kimasau samāsoktiḥ kim abdheraprastutasya mukhena kasyāpi tatsamaguṇatayā prastutasya pratīteḥ iyamaprastutapraśaṃsā iti saṃdehaḥ / yathā vā
children.translated_text: Here, since the ocean is the contextual [subject], and from the equality of the qualifying attributes the non-contextual meaning is cognized — is this <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression)? Or is it <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) — since through the face of the non-contextual ocean, someone who possesses equal qualities and is the actual [intended] subject is cognized? — this is the doubt. Or as in:
(<s>Kṣemendra</s>'s <s>Aucityavicāracarcā</s>)
This orb of the moon, giver of delight to the eyes, is shining — even now, this unbreakable, undissipated darkness [remains]. || 574 ||

children.text:
atra kiṃ kāmasyoddīpalaḥ kālo vartate iti bhaṅgyantareṇābhidhānāt paryāyoktam / uta vadanasyendubimbatayā adhyavasānāt atiśayoktiḥ kiṃ vā / etaditi vaktraṃ nirdiśya tadrūpāropavaśāt rūpakam / athavā tayoḥ samuccayavivakṣāyāṃ dīpakam /athavā tulyayogitā / kimu pradoṣasamaye viśeṣaṇasāmyādānanasyāvagatau samāsoktiḥ / āhosvit mukhanairmalyaprastāvāt aprastutapraśaṃsā iti bahūnāṃ saṃdehādayameva saṃkaraḥ /
yatra tu nyāyadoṣayoranyarasyāvatāraḥ tatra ekatarasya niścayāt na saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, is it <s>paryāyokta</s> (circumlocution) — because it is stated indirectly, [meaning] 'the time that excites desire is at hand'? Or is it <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) — because of the metaphorical identification of the face as the moon-orb? Or is it <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) — because, having designated the face by 'this,' through the superimposition of its form [as the moon]? Or, with the intention of aggregating both, is it <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination)? Or <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction)? Or, at evening-time, from the equality of qualifying attributes, is it <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) — when the face is cognized [as the subject]? Or is it <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) — on the occasion of the purity of the face? — Thus, from the doubt among many [figures], this is the very [form of] <s>saṃkara</s>. But where the evidence of propriety or impropriety [clearly] favors one — there, from the determination of one, there is no doubt.

children.text: nyāyaśca sādhakatvam anukūlatā doṣo 'pi bādhakatvaṃ pratikūlatā / tatra
children.translated_text: And 'propriety' means supporting evidence, favorability; 'impropriety' also means invalidating evidence, unfavorability. Therein:
(<s>Śrīvatsalāñchanācārya</s>'s <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 321)
The radiance of her laughter spreads the charm of her moon-face like moonlight. || 575 ||

children.text: ityatra mukhyatayā avagamyamānā hāsadyutirvaktre evānukūlyaṃ bhajate ityupamāyāḥ sādhakam / śaśinā tu na tathā pratikūleti rūpakaṃ prati tasyā abādhakatā /
children.translated_text: Here, the radiance of laughter, being apprehended primarily, belongs favorably to the face alone — hence it supports <s>upamā</s> (simile). But the moon does not [receive it] in the same way — unfavorably — hence there is no invalidation of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) by it.
(<s>Harṣa</s>'s <s>Ratnāvalī</s> [3.23cd])
In your face-moon — truly, another cool-rayed [moon] has risen. || 576 ||

children.text: ityatrāparatvamindoranuguṇaṃ na tu vaktrasya pratikūlamiti rūpakasya sādhakatāṃ pratipadyate na tūpamāyā bādhakatām /
children.translated_text: Here, the 'otherness' is favorable to the moon, not unfavorable to the face — thus it attains the status of supporting evidence for <s>rūpaka</s>, but not that of invalidating <s>upamā</s>.
(<s>Udbhaṭa</s>'s <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasārasaṅgraha</s>)
O king, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> [or: the best among men] — <s>Lakṣmī</s> embraces you unreservedly. || 577 ||

children.text: ityatra punarāliṅganamupamāṃ nirasyati sadṛśaṃ prati parapreyasīprayuktasyāloṅganasyāsaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: Here, however, the embracing invalidates <s>upamā</s> — because an embrace with respect to a merely similar entity, like another's beloved, is impossible.
(<s>Kālidāsa</s>, <s>Pañcastavī</s> 3.1)
May the lotus-foot of <s>Ambikā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), beautiful with the enchanting tinkling of anklets, be for our victory! || 578 ||

children.text: ityatra mañjīraśiñjitam ambuje pratikūlam asaṃbhavāditi rūpakasyabādhakam na tu pāde 'nukūlamityupamāyāḥ sādhakamabhidhayate vidhyupamardino bādhakasya tadapekṣayotkaṭatvena pratipatteḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the tinkling of anklets is unfavorable to a lotus — because of its impossibility — hence it invalidates <s>rūpaka</s>; but it is not said to support <s>upamā</s> — because it is favorable to the foot — since the invalidating [evidence], which overrides the supportive, is perceived as more prominent in relation to it.
Thus should the wise examine other cases as well. || 140 ||
When both word-figure and meaning-figure are manifestly established in a single locus and determined...

children.text: abhinne eva pade sphuṭatayā, yat ubhāvapi śabdārthālaṅkārau vyavasthāṃ samāsādayataḥ so 'pyaparaḥ saṃkaraḥ / udāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: When both word-figure and meaning-figure manifestly reach a settled state in a single, undivided word — that too is another [type of] <s>saṃkara</s>. Example:
(<s>Ratnākara</s>'s <s>Haravijaya</s> 19.1)

The day-lotus — with the sun-disk as its broad pericarp, with its clearly blazing rays as filaments, and then the disk of day as its wide pollen — contracted, with the swarm of bees [of darkness] fixed upon the surface marked by the petal-cluster of the eight directions, its entrance bound by darkness. || 579 ||
Here, <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) have entered into a single word.
... therefore, it is proclaimed as having three forms. || Kpr-K_141 ||

children.text:
tadayamanugrāhyānugrāhakatayā saṃdehena ekapadapratipādyatayā ca vyavasthitatvāttriprakāra eva saṃkaro vyākṛtaḥ / prakārāntareṇa tu na śakyo vyākartum ānantyāttatprabhedānāmiti pratipāditāḥ
śabdārthobhayagatatvena trividhyajuṣo 'laṅkārāḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus, this <s>saṃkara</s>, being established in the three forms of principal-subordinate relationship, doubt, and co-presentation in a single word, has been analyzed as precisely threefold. It cannot be analyzed otherwise because of the infinity of their sub-varieties. Thus, the figures of speech have been set forth as threefold — pertaining to word, to meaning, and to both.

children.text:
kutaḥ punareṣa niyamo yadeteṣāṃ tulye 'pi kāvyaśobhātiśayahetutve kaścidalaṅkāraḥ śabdasya kaścidarthasya kaściccobhayasya iti cet / uktamtra yathā kāvye doṣaguṇāḷaṅkārāṇāṃ śabdārthobhayagatatvena
vyavasthāyāmanvayavyatirekāveva prabhavataḥ nimittāntarasyābhāvāt / tataśca yo 'laṅkāro yadīyānvayavyatirekāvanuvidhatte sa tadalaṅkāro vyavasthāpyate iti /
children.translated_text: But why is this rule [established] that — given that their capacity to produce the excellence of poetic beauty is equal — some figures are of word, some of meaning, and some of both? It is said that just as, in poetry, the determination of faults, qualities, and figures as pertaining to word, meaning, and both is [established] — it is only positive and negative concomitance (anvaya-vyatireka) that prevails, since no other criterion exists. Accordingly, whatever figure follows the positive and negative concomitance of whichever [element] — that figure is determined as belonging to that [element].

children.text: evaṃ ca yathā punaruktavadābhāsaḥ paraṃparitarūpakaṃ cobhayor bhāvānuvidhāyitayā, ubhayālaṅkārau tathā śabdahetukārthāntaranyāsaprabhṛtayo 'pi draṣṭavyāḥ / arthasya tu tatra vaivitryam utkaṭatayā pratibhāsate, iti vācyālaṅkāramadhye vastusthitimanapekṣyaiva lakṣitāḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus, just as <s>punaruktavadābhāsa</s> (apparent tautology) and chain-<s>rūpaka</s> (extended metaphor) belong to both [word and meaning] because they follow the nature of both, so too should word-caused <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) and the like be regarded. But since, in those cases, the variety of meaning appears more prominently, they have been listed among the meaning-figures without regard to the actual state of affairs.

children.text: yo 'laṅkāro yadāśritaḥ sa tadalaṅkāra ityapi kalpanāyām anvayavyatirelāveva samāśrayitavyau tadāśrayaṇamantareṇa viśiṣṭasyāśrayibhāvasyābhāvādityalaṅkārāṇāṃ yathoktanimitta eva parasparavyatireko jyāyān //141//
children.translated_text: The principle that an <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) dependent on another is an <s>alaṅkāra</s> of that other — even in such a construction, one must resort to <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) alone, for without relying on those, the distinguished status of being a dependent [figure] cannot be established. Thus the mutual distinction of <s>alaṅkāras</s> through the stated criteria alone is the superior [method]. ||141||
Some defects of these [figures], occurring as appropriate,
are subsumed under those already stated, and hence have not been treated separately. || MKpr-K_142 ||

children.text: tathāhi ---- anuprāsasya prasiddhyabhāvo vaiphalyaṃ vṛttivirodha iti ye trayo doṣāḥ / te prasiddhiviruddhatām apuṣṭāthatvam pratikūlavarṇatāṃ ca yathākramaṃ na vyatikrāmanti tatsvabhāvatvāt / krameṇodāharaṇam ----
children.translated_text: That is to say: the three defects of <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) — absence of established usage (<s>prasiddhyabhāva</s>), futility (<s>vaiphalya</s>), and conflict with style (<s>vṛttivirodha</s>) — do not go beyond contradiction of established convention, unsupported meaning, and adverse phonemic quality, respectively, since they are of that very nature. Examples in order:

children.text:
{cakrī cakrārapaṅktiṃ harirapi ca harīn dhūrjaṭirdhūrdhvajāgrān
  akṣaṃ nakṣatranāthoruṇamapi varuṇaḥ kūbarāgraṃ kuberaḥ /
  raṃhaḥ saṃghaḥ surāṇāṃ jagadupakṛtaye nityayuktasya yasya
  stauti prītiprasannonvahamahimaruceḥ sovatātsyandano vaḥ //580//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Mayūra's</s> <s>Sūryaśataka</s> 71)

{The discus-bearer [tends] the discus, <s>Hari</s> the horses, <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) the tips of the pole-flags, the lord of the stars (<s>Soma</s>) the axle, <s>Varuṇa</s> the dawn-redness, <s>Kubera</s> the yoke-tip — the host of gods, with delight-gladdened faces, daily praises the lustre and glory of that [sun's] chariot, always yoked for the benefit of the world. May that chariot of his protect you! ||580||}

children.text: atra kartṛkarmapratiniyamena stutiḥ anuprāsānurodhenaiva kṛtā na purāṇetihāsādiṣu tathā pratīteti prasiddhivirodhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here, the praise [is constructed] with a fixed assignment of agent and object solely for the sake of conformity with <s>anuprāsa</s> — [but] such [an assignment] is not known in the <s>Purāṇas</s>, <s>Itihāsas</s>, and the like. This is a contradiction of established convention.

children.text:
{bhaṇa taruṇi ramaṇamandiramānandasyandisundarendumukhi /
  yadi sallīlollāpini gacchasi tat kiṃ tvadīyaṃ me //581//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Rudraṭa's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 2.22)
{Tell me, O young woman with a beautiful moon-face dripping with the nectar of joy, dwelling of the beloved — if you go with playful prattle, then what [is there] of yours [that is] mine? ||581||}
(<s>Rudraṭa's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 2.23)
{The tinkling of minute jeweled girdle-ornaments, the incessant jingling of charming anklets, the movement of reddened feet — makes a rattle-sound without cause. ||582||}

children.text: atra vāvyasya vicintyamānaṃ na kiñcidapi cārutvaṃ pratīyate, ityapuṣṭārthataivānuprāsasya vaiphalyam //
children.translated_text: Here, upon reflection, no beauty whatsoever of the expressed meaning is perceived — thus the futility of the <s>anuprāsa</s> is merely unsupported meaning.

children.text: akuṇṭhotkaṇṭhayā iti atra śṛṅgāre paruṣavarṇāḍambaraḥ pūrvoktarītyā virudhyate iti paruṣānuprāso 'tra pratikūlavarṇataiva vṛttivirodhaḥ //
children.translated_text: In '<s>akuṇṭhotkaṇṭhayā</s>' — here, in a <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) [context], the parade of harsh phonemes conflicts with the previously stated style. Thus the harsh <s>anuprāsa</s> is precisely adverse phonemic quality, constituting conflict with style.
Of <s>yamaka</s> (chiming), the defect is futile chiming (<s>yamana</s>) extending over three quarter-verses [i.e., unfit usage]. For example:

children.text:
{bhujaṅgamasyeva maṇiḥ sadambhā grāhāvakīrṇeva nadī sadambhāḥ /
  durantatāṃ nirṇayato 'pi jantoḥ karṣanti cetaḥ prasabhaṃ sadambhāḥ //583//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{The pride-bearers (<s>sadambhāḥ</s>) — like the jewel of a serpent — like a river infested with crocodiles — even while determining the endlessness of a creature, forcibly attract the mind. ||583||}

children.text: upamāyām upamānasya jātipramāṇagatanyūnatvam adhikatā vā tādṛśī anucitārthatvaṃ doṣaḥ / dharmāśraye tu nyūnādhikatve yathākramaṃ hīnapadatvamadhikapadatvaṃ ca na vyabhicarataḥ // krameṇodāharaṇam --
children.translated_text: In <s>upamā</s> (simile), the defect is when the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) is inferior in genus or magnitude, or when it is superior [to the thing compared] in a way that is inappropriate in meaning. As for the common property (<s>dharma</s>), inferiority or superiority in its locus corresponds to deficiency of words or excess of words, without deviation. Examples in order:
(<s>Vāmana's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 4.2.9)
{The greatest outrage has been committed by you — as by <s>caṇḍālas</s> (outcasts)! ||584||}
(<s>Vāmana's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 4.2)
{This sun shines like a spark of fire! ||585||}

children.text:
{ayaṃ padmāsanāsīnaścakravāko virājate /
  yugādau bhagavān vedhā vinirmitsuriva prajāḥ //586//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhāmaha's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 2.25; <s>Vāmana's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 4.2.11)
{This one, seated on a lotus, shines like a <s>cakravāka</s> bird — like the Blessed Creator (<s>Brahmā</s>) at the beginning of the age, as if about to create beings. ||586||}

children.text:
{pātālamiva te nābhiḥ stanau kṣitidharopamau /
  veṇīdaṇḍaḥ punarayaṃ kālindīpātasaṃnibhaḥ //587//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vāmana's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 4.2.11)
{Your navel is like the netherworld (<s>pātāla</s>), your breasts are like mountains; and this braid of yours resembles the cascade of the <s>Kālindī</s> (river <s>Yamunā</s>). ||587||}
Here, with <s>caṇḍālas</s> and the like as the standard of comparison, the subject being praised is excessively disparaged — hence it is inappropriate in meaning.

children.text:
{sa munirlāñchito mauñjyā kṛṣṇājinapaṭaṃ vahan /
  vyarājannīlajīmūtabhāgāśliṣṭa ivāṃśumān //588//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Vāmana's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 4.2.9)
{That sage, marked with the <s>mauñjī</s> (muñja-grass girdle), wearing a garment of black antelope skin, shone like the sun embraced by a portion of blue cloud. ||588||}

children.text: atropamānasya mauñjīsthānīyastaḍillakṣaṇo dharmaḥ kenāpi padena na pratipādita iti hīnapadatvam //
children.translated_text: Here, the property corresponding to the <s>mauñjī</s> in the standard of comparison — namely, the lightning — is not conveyed by any word. This is deficiency of words (<s>hīnapadatva</s>).

children.text:
{sa pītavāsāḥ pragṛhītaśārṅgo manojñabhīmaṃ vapurāpa kṛṣṇaḥ /
  śatahradendrāyudhavānniśāyāṃ saṃsṛjyamānaḥ śaśineva meghaḥ //589//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhāmaha's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 2.58)

{<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, wearing yellow garments and holding the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, assumed a form that was both pleasing and fearsome — like a cloud at night, joining with the moon, bearing a rainbow and a hundred lightning flashes. ||589||}
Here, since things like the conch [of the <s>upameya</s>] are not indicated, the mention of the moon [in the <s>upamāna</s>] is superfluous — this is excess of words (<s>adhikapadatva</s>).

children.text:
liṅgavacanabhedo 'pi upamānopameyayoḥ sādhāraṇaṃ cet dharmamanyarūpaṃ kuryāt / tadā ekatarasyaiva taddharmasamanvayāvagateḥ saviśeṣaṇasyaiva tasyopamānatvamupameyatvaṃ vā pratīyamānena dharmeṇa
pratīyate iti prakāntasyārthasya sphuṭamanirvāhādasya bhagnaprakramarūpatvam / yathā ----
children.translated_text: Even a discordance of gender and number between the standard of comparison and the thing compared — if the common property is such that it would assume a different form [due to the discordance], then only one of the two would be understood as possessing that property. [Whether it serves as] the standard of comparison or the thing compared is perceived through the [actually] perceived property — thus, since the intended meaning is not clearly conveyed, this has the nature of a broken sequence (<s>bhagnaprakrama</s>). For example:
(<s>Rudraṭa's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 11.20)
{Like a wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāratna</s>, neuter), you (masculine) have fallen from [my] hand — alas for my wretched fate! ||590||}
(<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 334)
{The rice-cakes (<s>saktavaḥ</s>, masculine plural) have been eaten, O lord — pure, like the women of a noble family (<s>kulavadhūḥ</s>, feminine singular)! ||591||}

children.text: yatra tu nānātve 'pi liṅggavacanayoḥ sāmānyābhidhāyi padaṃ dvarūpabhedaṃ nāpadyate na tatraitaddūṣaṇāvatāraḥ ubhayathāpi asya anugamakṣamasvabhāvatvāt / yathā
children.translated_text: But where, even when there is a difference of gender and number, the word expressing the common property does not undergo a change of form [i.e., remains invariable] — there, this fault does not apply, since it is by nature capable of following both [genders/numbers]. For example:
(<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 335)
{Celebrated for his priceless qualities, like the great ocean [celebrated] for its gems. ||592||}

children.text:
{tadveṣosadṛśonyābhiḥ strībhirmadhuratābhṛtaḥ /
  dadhate sma parāṃ śobhāṃ tadīyā vibhramā iva //593//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 336)
{Her coquetries (<s>vibhramāḥ</s>, masculine plural), assuming a form resembling his appearance, possessing sweetness, bore supreme beauty — like [the coquetries themselves]. ||593||}

children.text: kālapuruṣavidhyādibhede 'pi na tathā pratītiraskhalitarūpatayā viśrāntimāsādayatītyasāvapi bhagnaprakramatayaiva vyāptaḥ / yathā
children.translated_text: Even when there is a difference of tense, person, mood, and the like, the cognition does not come to rest in an unobstructed form — thus that too is subsumed under the broken-sequence [defect]. For example:

children.text:
{atithiṃ nāma kākutsthāt putramāpa kumudvatī /
  paścimād yāminīyāmāt prasādamiva cetanā //594//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa's</s> <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 17.1)

{<s>Kumudvatī</s> obtained from <s>Kākutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) a son named <s>Atithi</s> — like consciousness (<s>cetanā</s>) obtaining clarity (<s>prasāda</s>) from the last watch of the night. ||594||}

children.text: atra cetanā prasādamāpnoti na punarāpeti kālabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, consciousness 'obtains' (<s>āpnoti</s>, present) clarity, but does not 'obtain' (<s>āpa</s>, past) it — this is a discordance of tense.
(<s>Harṣa's</s> <s>Ratnāvalī</s> 1.20)

{With your body purified and distinct from a recent fresh bath, beautiful with the radiance of a gleaming <s>kusumbha</s>-red garment — you shine while worshipping the god of the <s>Makara</s> banner (<s>Kāma</s>), like a creeper born from a young coral tree. ||595||}

children.text: atra latā vibhrājate na tu vibhrājase iti saṃbodhyamānaniṣṭhasya parabhāgasya asaṃbodhyamānaviṣayatayā vyatyāsāt puruṣabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, a creeper 'shines' (<s>vibhrājate</s>, third person), but not 'you shine' (<s>vibhrājase</s>, second person with direct address) — since the latter part, which pertains to the addressee, is not applicable to the non-addressed [creeper], there is a discordance of person due to the transposition.
(<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 339)
{May your fame flow forth forever, like the <s>Gaṅgā</s>! ||596||}

children.text: ityādau ca gaṅgā pravahati na tu pravahatu iti apravṛttapravartanātmano vidheḥ / evañjātīyakasya cānyasyārthasya upamānagatasyāsaṃbhavādvidhyādibhedaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here and in similar cases, the <s>Gaṅgā</s> 'flows' (<s>pravahati</s>, indicative) but not 'may it flow' (<s>pravahatu</s>, optative/imperative) — since the imperative involves causing something not yet in progress to commence. And since such another meaning is impossible for the standard of comparison, this is a discordance of mood and the like.

children.text:
nanu samānam uccāritaṃ pratīyamānaṃ vā dharmāntaramupādāya paryavasitāyām upamāyām upameyasya prakṛtadharmāmisaṃbandhānna kaścitkālādibhedo 'sti / yatrāpyupāttenaiva sāmānyadharmeṇa upamā
avagamyate yathā {yudhiṣṭhira ivāyaṃ satyaṃ vadati} iti tatra yudhiṣthira iva satyavādyayaṃ satyaṃ vadatīti pratipatsyāmahe / satyavādī satyaṃ vadatīti ca na paunaruktyam āśaṅkanīyam raipoṣaṃ puṣṇātītivat
yudhiṣthira iva satyavadanena satyavādyayamityarthāvagamāt / satyametat kiṃ tu sthiteṣu prayogeṣu samarthanamidaṃ na tu sarvathā niravadyam prastutavastupratītivyādhātāditi savetasa evātra pramāṇam //
children.translated_text: Now, when a common property — whether expressed or implied — is taken, and when a simile is concluded [through it], there is no discordance of tense or the like in the thing compared, [precisely because] the thing compared is not connected with the property of the subject [of the standard of comparison]. And even where the simile is understood through the expressed common property itself — as in '<s>yudhiṣṭhira ivāyaṃ satyaṃ vadati</s>' ('this one speaks truth, like <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>') — we shall understand it as: 'like <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, being truthful, this one speaks truth.' And there is no tautology to be suspected in 'a truthful one speaks truth,' just as in 'he nourishes with nourishment' — since the meaning understood is: 'this one, being truthful like <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> in truthfulness.' This is correct. But while this justification works for existing usages, it is not entirely unobjectionable in every case, since it disrupts the cognition of the intended subject. Therefore, usage alone is the authority here.
Dissimilarity and impossibility in <s>upamā</s> also ultimately resolve into inappropriate meaning (<s>anucitārthatā</s>). For example:
(<s>Vāmana's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> 2.4.16)
{I compose a poetry-moon with extended meaning-rays. ||597||}

children.text: atra kāvyasya śaśinā arthānāṃ ca raśmibhiḥ sādharmyaṃ kutrāpi na pratītamityanucitārthatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, the similarity of poetry with the moon, and of meanings with rays, is not perceived anywhere — hence it is inappropriate in meaning.

children.text:
{nipeturāsyādiva tasya dīptāḥ
  śarā dhanurmaṇḍalamadhyabhājaḥ /
  jājvalyamānā iva vāridhārā
  dinārdhabhājaḥ pariveṣiṇorkāt //598//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Govindaṭhakkura's</s> <s>Kāvyapradīpa</s>)
{From his mouth fell blazing arrows, occupying the middle of the bow-circle — like burning streams of water from the sun's disc at half-day, shining brilliantly. ||598||}

children.text: atrāpi jvalantyombudhārāḥ sūryamaṇḍalāt niṣpatantyo na saṃbhavantītyupanibadhyamāno 'rtho 'naucityameva puṣṇāti //
children.translated_text: Here too, burning water-streams issuing from the sun's disc do not exist — thus the meaning being composed only nourishes inappropriateness.

children.text:
utprekṣāyāmapi saṃbhāvanaṃ dhruvevādaya eva śabdā vaktuṃ sahante na yathāśabdo 'pi kevalasyāsya sādhārmyameva pratipādayituṃ paryāptatvāt tasya cāsyāmavivakṣitatvāditi tatrāśaktirasyāvācakatvaṃ doṣaḥ /
yathā
children.translated_text: In <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) too, it is only words like '<s>dhruva</s>' ('certainly') and '<s>iva</s>' ('as if') and the rest that are capable of expressing supposition — not the word '<s>yathā</s>' ('as') by itself, since it is sufficient only to convey similarity, and since similarity is not intended here. Thus the incapacity [of <s>yathā</s>] is its non-denotativeness, [which is] a defect. For example:
(<s>Śrivatsalāñchanācārya's</s> <s>Kāvyaparīkṣā</s> 340)
{A dark blue lotus bud rose from the womb of the pool, contracted as though from the suspicion of the skill of a woman's eye. ||599||}

children.text: utprekṣitamapi tāttvikena rūpeṇa parivarjitatvāt nirupākhyaprakhyam / tatsamarthanāya yat arthāntaranyāsopādānam tat ālekhyamiva gaganataletyantamasamīcīnamiti nirviṣayatvametasya / anucitārthataiva doṣaḥ / yathā
children.translated_text: What is supposed [in <s>utprekṣā</s>], being rejected in its actual form, becomes a semblance of resemblance devoid of [true] resemblance. And the use of <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) to justify it — like 'a painting on the surface of the sky' — is entirely improper. Hence [the figure] has no valid subject. The defect is [simply] inappropriate meaning. For example:

children.text:
{divākarādrakṣati yo guhāsu līnaṃ divā bhītamivāndhakāram /
  kṣudre 'pi nūnaṃ prapanne mamatvamuccaiḥ śirasāmatīva //600//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Kālidāsa's</s> <s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 1.12)

{<s>Himālaya</s>, who protects the darkness hiding in caves by day, frightened as it were by the sun — surely, even toward the lowly who have sought refuge, an exceedingly lofty one has affection. ||600||}

children.text:
atrācetanasya tamaso divākarāttrāsa eva na saṃbhavatīti kuta eva tatprayojitamadriṇā paritrāṇam / saṃbhāvitena tu rūpeṇa pratibhāsamānasyāsya na kācidanupapattiravataratīti vyartha eva tatsamarthanāyāṃ yatnaḥ /
sādhāraṇaviśeṣaṇavaśādeva samāsoktiranuktamapi upamānaviśeṣaṃ prakāśayatīti tasyātra punarupādāne prayojanābhāvāt anupādeyatvaṃ yat tat apuṣṭārthatvaṃ punaruktaṃ vā doṣaḥ / yathā
children.translated_text: Here, for insentient darkness, fear of the sun is simply not possible — how much less, then, is the protection afforded by the mountain motivated by that [fear]? But this [darkness], appearing in a supposed form, admits of no logical impossibility — therefore the effort to justify it [through <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>] is pointless. In <s>samāsokti</s> (compressed expression), since the shared qualifier alone reveals the unexpressed specific standard of comparison, there is no purpose in its further mention [through an explicit simile-word] — and such purposelessness is [the defect of] unsupported meaning or tautology. For example:

children.text:
{spṛśati tigmarucau kakubhaḥ karairdayitayeva vijṛmbhitatāpayā /
  atanumānaparigrahayā sthitaṃ rucirayā cirayāpi dinaśriyā //601//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Ratnākara's</s> <s>Haravijaya</s> 3.37)

{The sun, with its hot rays, touches the directions with the fingertips of the charm of its sustained radiance — with a beautiful embrace possessing a degree of honor, established for a long time. ||601||}

children.text: atra tigmaruceḥ kakubhāṃ ca yathā sadṛśaviśeṣaṇavaśena vyaktiviśeṣaparigraheṇa ca nāyakatayā nāyikātvena ca vyaktiḥ, tathā grīṣmadivasaśriyo 'pi pratināyikātvena bhaviṣyatīti kiṃ dayitayeti svaśabdopādānena //
children.translated_text: Here, just as the identity of the hero and heroine is revealed through the shared qualifiers and the selection of a particular referent — so too the beauty of the summer day would function as the rival heroine. What need, then, for the explicit mention 'like a beloved' (<s>dayitayā</s>)?

children.text: śleṣopamāyāstu sa viṣayaḥ yatropamānasyopādānamantareṇa sādhāraṇeṣvapi viśeṣaṇeṣu na tathā pratītiḥ / yathā
children.translated_text: But in <s>śleṣopamā</s> (punning simile), the domain is precisely that in which, without the introduction of the standard of comparison, even the shared qualifiers do not produce the [intended] cognition. For example:
{She, reddish-coppery as young shoots, radiant with brilliant rays, granting the desired fruit to the one eager for the fruit of waking — shone like the twilight of dawn. ||602||}
(<s>Udbhaṭa's</s> <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasārasaṅgraha</s> 4.15)

children.text: aprastutapraśaṃsāyāmapi upameyam anayaiva rītyā pratītaṃ na punaḥ prayogeṇa kadarthatāṃ neyam / yathā
children.translated_text: In <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) too, the thing compared, cognized by this very method, should not be dragged into disrespect through explicit usage. For example:

children.text:
{āhūteṣu vihaṅgameṣu maśako nāyān puro vāryate
  madhyevāridhi vāvasaṃstṛṇamaṇirdhatte maṇīnāṃ rucam /
  khadyoto 'pi na kampate pracalituṃ madhye 'pi tejasvināṃ
  dhik sāmānyamacetanaṃ prabhumivānāmṛṣṭatattvāntaram //603//}

children.translated_text: (<s>Bhallaṭaśataka</s> 67)

{When the birds are summoned, a mosquito — none prevents it from coming first; in the midst of the ocean, a piece of straw-crystal bears the lustre of [true] gems; a firefly does not hesitate to move about even among the luminaries — shame on the commonplace insensible [world], which, like a king, does not discern the true nature of things! ||603||}

children.text: atra acetanasya prabhoraprastutaviśiṣṭasāmānyadvāreṇābhivyaktau na yuktameva punaḥ kathanam //
children.translated_text: Here, since the insensible [being] has been revealed through the door of the distinguished general [category] pertaining to the irrelevant, restating it explicitly is indeed not appropriate.

children.text: tadeta alaṅkāradoṣāḥ yathāsaṃbhāvinonye 'pyevañjātīyakāḥ pūrvoktayaiva doṣajātyā antarbhāvitāḥ na pṛthag pratipādanamarhantīti saṃpūrṇamidaṃ kāvyalakṣaṇam //142//
children.translated_text: Thus, these are the faults of ornaments. Other faults of this kind too, as they may arise, are subsumed under the very same class of faults stated earlier and do not merit separate treatment — thus this definition of poetry (<s>kāvyalakṣaṇa</s>) is complete. //142//

children.text:
{ityeṣa mārgo viduṣāṃ vibhinno 'pyabhinnarūpaḥ pratibhāsate yat /
  na tadvicitraṃ yadamutra samyagvinirmitā saṃghaṭanaiva hetuḥ //1//}
children.translated_text: {'This path of the learned, though diverse, appears as if uniform — and that is not surprising, for the cause here is indeed the well-constructed arrangement.' //1//}
Thus ends the tenth chapter (<s>ullāsa</s>) of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, entitled 'The Determination of Figures of Meaning' (<s>arthālaṅkāranirṇaya</s>).
// Thus the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> is concluded. //
// Thus this treatise is complete. //
